product_title: Cruising Companion Pawprint Car Seat Cover
review_headline: Fits my 2015 Honda CR-V - great for trips!
review_body:
I purchased this pet seat cover to protect our new vehicle, when I need to travel with our pets (dog and cat). After searching around at local pets stores I was unable to find anything this stylish and fitted. I kept coming back to this one, and I finally decided to purchase it, even if it was a little more than I wanted to spend for one. I purchased Camel color. It fits my back seat really well, looks very stylish with the cute paw print pattern. It's very easy to put on and I don't even tighten the bottom straps, since my dog doesn't weigh all that much. If your dog weighs more than 10 lbs then you might have to secure the bottom straps to keep it smooth and from getting creases when the dog moves around. I also love the seat belt slits, which allows me to easily use my dogs seat belt harness. (if interested in one, I purchased it at [[ASIN:B00AO1VK8Q Leegoal Nylon Harness]]
I clip to his collar and keeps him from trying to claw my doors or climb between the front seats. It keeps him put in one spot, for his safety and mine. This cover does hang down the sides, or front very much and that is fine with me. I like the way it fits my seat, and has a clean tailored look. Everyone compliments me on this seat cover. I am adding a photo that shows a close up and also how it looks in my vehicle.
It is not waterproof however I think that it's thick enough to protect your seat if your dog just has wet paws and not soaking dripping wet. I have not had that experience yet, but may come back to update my review at some point regarding it's water durability. I hope my review will help others who are contemplating purchasing this item.

review_body: I am leary of all dog conditioners and their residues.  Get this one.  Rinse well.  Use their shampoo.  Leave it on for a few minutes and follow up with this rinse.  Always make sure you get the mats out of your dog BEFORE the bath.  Getting mats wet sets them in stone.  Small knots can come out in the bath if you use a course metal comb.  Get the dead hair OUT of your dogs coat and it will shine and stay mat free.  COMB your dog with a coarse to medium and medium to fine tooth metal comb every day...EVERY DAY.  They can't do it for themselves.  If you have domesticated your animal, comb his/her dead hair out.

product_title: Bark Control Pro - Dog Bark Collar - The Quick and Effective Small and Large Breed Shock Collar – Adjustable Sensitivity – Seven Levels of Feedback – Guaranteed
review_body:
I will admit, I was very skeptical over this whole Bark Collar idea. When my Lab mix puppies decided that they wanted to start barking in the middle of the night, I was very happy that Bark Contol Pro was there to give us the sleep that we were in need of.

After several nights of dogs barking at nothing in the middle of the night, I used the bark control pro, in hopes that it would settle them down. I was very discouraged, when my male dog, ignored the collar altogether, and still continued to bark. I questioned whether it was him or the collar, however, after putting it on the female, I can tell you that it does indeed work.

Our boy tends to be a follower and tends to repeat actions the female does, so the bark collar not only ended up helping us train her not to bark when it wasn't necessary, it also helped our male with his barking because, since she wasn't, he didn't see the need to.

Now, if there was a reason to bark, like someone at the door, or someone in the back yard who didn't need to be there, our dogs still let us know regardless of the collar or not. So now, we are able to get a nights sleep and actually know that if the dogs bark, it isn't just for fun, there is something we need to check out!

product_title: Pet Memorial Jewelry Set- Necklace, Pendant for Ashes, Funnel - Stainless Steel Cremation Urn Kit Gift Boxed
review_headline: Heartfelt necklace made with top quality design and materials
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:a5bf267e099922c8e9a09f254b2ab303]]This review is for the Pet Memorial (Heart, Small).

This is a touching, well made pet memorial necklace. I never knew something like this existed. Then my best friend lost her cat of 16 years and I knew I had to get her something because I felt so bad. She had her cat cremated and put it in an urn. This necklace is perfect for keeping a tiny bit of those ashes close to your heart so you can still be with your precious fur baby even when they are gone over the rainbow bridge.

The pendant is not too large or too small, it is perfect to keep on 24/7. It is good quality metals and is slightly heavy which is perfect because it doesn't flip around or move all over the place. It is attached to the chain with an O ring. The chain is absolutely beautiful. It is box links that hold together well and are very fluid around the neckline. The lobster claw is firm and opens and closes easily but is very secure so nothing will happen to this necklace when you least expect it.

The set comes beautifully boxed in a white box with a special saying to remember your pet glued inside the black velvet. There is a miniature funnel for putting the ashes in the top of the pendant. There are also instructions. It is easy to do and the screw top on the pendant is easy to take off and put back on. The only thing I would recommend is definitely putting a bead of glue on the screw when you put it back in after you have filled this with ashes just to be EXTRA safe.

5/5 stars for design, functionality and materials.

product_title: Vet's Best Flea & Tick Pet & Home Spray
review_headline: Not working great for us unfortunately
review_body: I was looking for a natural alternative to potentially dangerous flea medicines, this product had good reviews so I tried it. I had also tried a similar product but one that contained a large amount of cedar oil. The other product did not work and I read some information that cedar oil might be harmful for cats. Anyway, my dogs had a very minor flea problem. I would find, at max, 5 fleas on them when I would flea comb them every other day or so. I used borax for my carpet and I was vacuuming regularly. I sprayed this as directed, massaged it in and flea combed the dogs. The next day I flea-combed them again and I found there to be no reduction in the number of fleas. I tried this for several days, I also sprayed them right before we went outside and I sprayed the whole house with it. I tried bathing them, drying and then starting fresh with the product and still I saw no reduction in fleas. I am giving up now and getting a traditional product from the vet. I tried. I am giving it 3 stars because the fleas I sprayed directly with it did seem distressed and it had a really nice smell, it also seemed to repel mosquitos. I also did not catch any fleas on a flea trap on the carpet where I sprayed it but that could have also been from the borax. I live in Florida so maybe we have more resistant fleas?

product_title: OxGord 48-Inch Animal Playpen for Pets with Pop up Mesh Kennel Fence Tent Soft Sided Cage
review_headline: It comes in a nice carrying bag
review_body:
I was in need of something that would allow me to leave my dogs out while I am away, but not allow them to roam the entire house since we have one with bladder issues. This playpen gives them enough room to romp and play without giving access to her to have accidents. It comes in a nice carrying bag, which will be great for trips where we are able to take them along. There are even some included ground stakes to affix it when using it outdoors. It comes out easily and has a nifty stretch strap to keep it folded up until your ready. It pops up super easy, almost with a flick of the wrists. The mesh sides and top keep the pooches in, but allows them to see what is going on around them. The bottom attaches with velcro, but it isn't quite effective and pops off a majority of the time. I tried placing their bed on one side hoping it would at least keep that side secured, however it didn't. I plan to permanently sew the bottom to the pen so it will no longer be an issue. After about a week of use and many bites and scratches, the screens are still in place and in one piece. It's even allowed me to take my house cats outdoors for a bit of fresh air and no one has yet to escape or break the mesh. I love this playpen and it will open up a lot of doors for my pups, they won't have to be locked in kennels all day and I don't have to worry about pet urine. My cats have loved the outdoor time they've been getting, even if it's just from inside the pen (with the bottom off), they get to feel the grass under their feet, sniff the air and watch the birds. I'm only giving 4-stars because of the velcro-bottom, but I've experienced no other issues with it when using it with my cats or dogs (pug & chihuahua).

I love that it included both tops so that I can use the traditional top or the pump handle, depending on our location or mood. The shampoo provides an amazing scent that is sure to please. It's light, but distinct. The oatmeal and aloe vera combination is great for pets of all sizes/breeds/coat types. My dog, Rocco, is a hound/beagle mix and it keeps his coat feeling super soft for days! I love that Rocco doesn't experience any irritation when using this shampoo. It's made of natural ingredients and is paraben free, dye free, and alcohol free, making it a perfect shampoo for your furry friend.

The shampoo is a creamy pearl white color and is thick. A little goes a long ways so it saves you money in the long run as well. I love that it lathered up nicely, providing Rocco with a shiny clean coat.

I'll definitely continue to use Fifi & Fido pet shampoo. It's one of the best on the market and it's offered at such an affordable price!

If this mat didn't have something securing it and you have a cat who will paw at it, I think it would easily turn over on itself and get litter everywhere. product_title: Kararantula Interchangeable Cat Toy - Attachment Only
review_headline: Easy favorite for interactive cat toy
review_body:
I have several other rod and attachment style toys such as Da Bird, some other mice-like lure products, and even made an investment in the bird catcher pro. I think this one has a lot to offer and added benefits the others do not. I would start a new cat owner with this toy, as well as start a kitten on this toy.

Some thoughts:
1) These small bug-like lures are much smaller than the whole da bird range (guinea and regular) and less hard. This makes them less intimidating for any cat.
2) The legs as other reviewers have mentioned have a lot of dynamic movement which is very stimulating and realistic in a bug-like way.I also can't believe they haven't come off yet the way my cat has chewed on them, but they seem very well-made so far.
3) The attached cord is much thicker than other rod toys which makes the movement slower but easier to control. You can accidentally end up surprising or running into your cat with some of the faster flying toys as they have a more whip-like action. This one has no whipping motion in it. It also doesn't tangle the way the the thinner wires do.

I will be buying this again and suggesting it to friends. I hope in the future major pet stores start stocking more of these interactive cat toy products instead of excessively stocking standard static toys, but for now, you can only try them out here.

I'm sure if I could understand her barking she would say "Thank you OxGord for making my old self a very lovely and comfortable bed! WOOF". I would definitely recommend this OxGord Elevated Pet Bed!

review_headline: They both fit fine inside and they like it
review_body:
I used this to travel internationally with my yorkie and my chorkie. They both fit fine inside and they like it. They esch had their own carrier.
Pros:
1- It has retained its shape. I have found that with some pet carriers, they loose shape and become uncomfortable for both the carrier and the pet.
2- Pet gets enough ventilation.
3- Removable bottom insert is easy to clean.
4-The door on the top has 3 securities so pets can't open it. Velcro, zipper and buckle. I found this really great because my pets can open if it is just the zipper.
5- It has a feature to secure the carrier to a suitcase handle which was very usefull during our trip.
Cons:
1- The door is on top so you have to lay it on its side so the dog can get in.
2- It does not fit under the seat of the plane unless it is on its side....this was actually the only real negative thing for me. But my pets survived it, they just moved when I layed it on its side. But they are really small so if you have a chubby or tall pet I suggest you find another carrier.
3- They say you can secure the carrier with a seat belt in the car but I have not been able to figure it out. You can buckle it but it bends the carrier and with time it will lose shape.
I hope this was helpful.

product_title: Petflect Reflective Dog Vest
review_headline: Large vest is too small for an 80 lb German Shepherd
review_body:
The Petflect website has a sizing chart that says the Large size will fit dogs 61-130 lbs. My dog is an 80 lb German Shepherd, and the Large vest is too small. I can get the ends of the velcro to connect with about 1" overlap, but the cut of the vest is for a smaller animal, so it makes his body shape look strange the way it sits on his shoulders and torso. If he is standing upright, the straps do not cut in to him, but if he curls up in his bed or does any other dynamic movement, the straps cut into him and look very restrictive. German Shepherds are very barrel chested and have very long torsos, so this might have something to do with it. It would be nice if they made an XL size for these types of dogs (with a longer cut on the vest, as well as longer straps). I'm not going to return the vest because I don't want to deal with the hassle, and I also don't see another vest for this good a price.

9/9/15 UPDATE:
When my dog goes for a hike his chest actually expands (probably because of the increased breathing) and the lower strap no longer reaches around his chest. It busts open, the vest spins around to the front (like a bib) and he trips on it. Solution?: I cut one side of the strap off, sewed in a 6 inch piece of webbing, and attached the velcro strap to the end of that webbing, thereby lengthening the belly strap.

9/10/15 UPDATE:
Having added a length of webbing on only one side of the belly strap caused the vest to fall to one side (difference in weight on one side). To remedy this I removed my webbing addition, cut it in half and inserted webbing on BOTH sides of the vest where the vest meets the belly strap. The front strap is still too short but I'm not going to mess with it because it doesn't bust open.

CONCLUSIONS:
Modifying this vest has really become a hassle, and I recommend that if you have an average sized (80 lb) male German Shepherd you search for a vest made by a different company that offers an XL size for large dogs.

review_headline: Couldn't be happier with this product!
review_body:
We've put this product to a slightly different use to most of the other reviewers - but with the same, excellent result.
We moved house about 6 months ago and almost immediately started having trouble with a very territorial and aggressive Burmese cat living next door. He was constantly approaching both our front and courtyard screen doors and challenging our cats. As our cats were inside and couldn't fight back, the Burmese would continuously hurl himself at the door - yeowlling and spitting until one of us stopped him with a spray from the hose. This would leave two of our cats hiding under a sofa or a bed for hours but stressed the other one so much - obviously concerned about his territory - it resulted in him spraying around the house!
My girlfiend living in the US found this on Amazon and as nothing else had worked, I decided to give it a go. Two mats, an extension mat plus post to Australia wasn't cheap but we were pretty desperate by then.
I am thrilled to report that after encountering the mat on just two occasions, the Burmese has rarely been sighted. He has approached the front door a couple of times but stops 6 feet short of the mat and then retreats.
After a couple of weeks of deliberation, he decided to try accessing the upstairs balcony doors ... so we hung one of the mats over the balcony at his access point and he hasn't been spotted there since. He didn't even come into contact with the mat - the sight of it was enough to deter him!
Sossij, Charlie and Kipper wholeheartedly endorse this product! :-)
It's worth noting that the product is intended for internal use - we were able to use them externally as our screen doors are protected from the weather by deep verandahs.

product_title: Orijen Alberta Wild Boar Singles Freeze-Dried Dog Treats, 3.5-oz bag (approx. 85 treats)
review_headline: May work as a "pill pocket" for your cat!  (or dog)
review_body:
My elderly cat has started needing more meds, including some that come only as pill form (and not as liquids or topicals)---he is darn near impossible to pill, and the process results in high stress for both of us and most of the time, also results in the pill not getting in. I've tried Greenies pill pockets (he will not eat; he is about the fussiest cat on the face of the earth---doesn't eat about 2/3 of the different foods that I buy for him, and ALWAYS detects the presence of medicine in his food), a pill shooter (even more trauma for both of us), etc etc with no luck.

However, he loves the Orijen cat wild boar treats with a wild fanaticism, so I originally thought that maybe I could cut those in half and put part of the pill inside, cover with butter to cover up yucky pill residue, and then repeat until he got his full dosage. But unfortunately, the cat version of these treats is just too small and crumbly---so I checked out the pic of the dog version, and ordered.

The dog treat is about 2.5x bigger than the cat treat, and I was able to cut one in half, insert a portion of a pill, and then "frost" the seam with Kong Salmon paste. The first time that I did this, he wolfed the treat down, and I was ecstatic, thinking I'd finally cracked the problem! But the 2nd time, it took him 2 hours to eat it, the 3rd time he refused it altogether, the 4th time it took him 6h to eat it, and the 5th time, he refused it altogether.

I should note that I don't feed my cat the dog treats as a normal treat, since the dog recipe has boar liver as its first ingredient (it's 2nd on the cat treats), and cats shouldn't be fed liver as a normal component of their diet since they can get vitamin A toxicity from too much liver---but in my case, I'm trying to use these treats to pill the cat maybe 2x a week, so amounts are quite low.

One last note--the dog treats, on a per-ounce basis, are substantially less expensive than the super-expensive cat treats ($8+ for 1.25 oz), which makes me think that Orijen has duly noted the top price cat owners are willing to pay for treats, and has set their price as high as possible. How about a price break, Orijen? My cat would eat his cat-specific wild boar treats day and night if I let him, but just like an addictive drug, I have to cut his Orijen treat consumption with less expensive brands so I don't go broke!

product_title: Petiner Dog Training Electric Shock Control No Bark Collars
review_headline: Great because it gives warning tones first!
review_body:
If you are looking for an electric shock collar to train your dog to stop barking, this one will do the trick. What I like about it is that it uses tones first before the shock to either warn your dog not to bark or to reinforce what he's already learned from the collar. At the first bark it sounds a short warning tone, and if there's a second bark within 30 seconds it sounds a longer tone. Even on the third bark it sounds a longer warning tone. Some dogs will stop barking after the tones and so it won't even shock them at all. But if there are more than three barks, it delivers a short mild shock and the intensity builds only if the barking continues. After a while, the dog will recognize the warning tone (if they ignore it initially) and won't continue barking. You can also tune it so that it is more or less sensitive to your dogs bark frequency.

This is easy to take off and on, which makes it nice to use only in certain circumstances (ie. only when your dog is in the yard or at the park). It's not meant to be used as a collar with a leash or to hold your dog's tags. The adjustable collar will fit any size dog. It comes with a battery and two lengths of electrodes so you'll have all you need to use it right when you get it. product_title: RUGGED RANCH RATTR The Ratinator Multiple Catch Live Rat Trap , 21 Rats in One
review_headline: Rats are curious and smart so I was worried they would figure out how ...
review_body:
So far I've caught two wood (pack) rats. 1 living in my attic and 1 living in my grill on the back patio. The rats both got in the trap overnight so they had to hang out until the morning. Rats are curious and smart so I was worried they would figure out how to get out but neither of them did. There is an area to put the bait food in middle of the cage that the rats can't get to. I didn't put the food in this portion, but rather inside the cage so they would have something to eat for the multiple hours they were in the cage. The purpose of buying a live trap was to provide a more humane way to get rid of them, not to starve them. I have been giving the rats to friends of mine who have a boa snake that needs larger rats than what our local pet store sells. Since these are wild rats they put the live rat in the freezer for 5-10 min before giving it to their snake so that it is a little numb and not injure the snake. Killing anything bothers me in general but I'd rather the rats death go toward feeding another animal instead of just poisoning/killing them. You could also relocate any rats you catch but be sure you release them next to a water source. The cage came with a handy Tupperware type container that you can put the cage in to transport.

The only reason I'm giving 4 stars is that they could have done a little better job with their marketing, in terms of the picture on the front of the box. I hesitated in purchasing this because the picture on the box looks like a random picture of a prison inmate looking dude next to the cage. It made me wonder if this cage was legit or if it was just something being made out of someone's garage and he had his buddy pose for the picture.

product_title: Zack & Zoey Blue Prince Royalty Robe Soft Terry Bathrobe for Dogs Medium
review_headline: Cute but sadly doesn't fit...4 Stars...
review_body:
This is very cute but I had to take off 1 star for sizing issues. This "Royalty Robe" seems best suited for SMALL dogs in the 15 lb range. I read other reviewers who indicated this is on the "Large" size but I suppose I should have realized they were speaking about much smaller dogs than mine. Our dog, Bogart, is 16" down the back, and he is 23 lbs., but this Robe is too tight/small for him and his proportions. I was able to get the Robe on him but it is way too tight in the chest and arm area and he didn't look happy or comfortable.

As for the quality...it seems, "top notch", good quality, as it seems to be made of plush, durable, terry/ cotton fabric...kind of like a luxury towel. The Robe has a cute hood and a tie. Although I find the hood and tie to be cute, it seems to be purely for fashion as I do not find it to be functional or purposeful since it is sewn to tie on the bottom, or belly area of the dog. This leads me to believe some dogs will just chew on the bow, or find it uncomfortable. Perhaps if the Robe was larger the tie would serve more of a purpose if the Velcro gets loose? But again for us this Robe was super tight on so the Velcro was sticking quite fine. In addition the Robe also has a hood to indicate it is a "Royalty Robe" (again adds to the Fashion of it but I am not sure it is purposeful...just cute!!) It also has an embroidered Blue Crown on back with the word "Prince" just adorable! It is nicely finished as it is all trimmed up in a Blue Fabric/Cord that accentuates the idea of a "luxury" bath robe.

Sadly, the only options when I ordered were Blue/Medium so I am disappointed as I can't even return it for a bigger size. Again I took the chance since I read other reviews and the price was so reasonably priced at 7.99. Free shipping is a bonus! Overall, I recommend only if you have a small dog. Otherwise you will waste your money.

product_title: eCOTRITION Snak Shak Treat Stuffer for Hamster/Gerbil
review_headline: It's very attractive.  It's exciting to the gerbils.  But is that enough?  ~~~
review_body:
I've kept gerbils over the years, a great many in fact. With the possible exception of sunflower seeds, they generally are pretty sensible little noshers. With standard hamster-and-gerbil foods, they ignore most of what's of greatest appeal to hamsters (seeds like milo and millet, usually) and concentrate on what appeals to them the most (whole grains, wheat middens, vegan kibble). This log was introduced to a pair of gerbil brothers about eight months old, pretty much full grown. They fell on the "log," ate out the insides, and started on the exterior. This leaves me with some unresolved issues: if it is a "treat" then why is it designed to stay in the cage all the time? If the log and its contents are 100 percent edible, then why is the leading ingredient made of pine?

I can't judge this irrevocably but I'm just not comfortable with an item with such great human curb appeal that may not be best for gerbils. I can tell you that gerbils don't needed added sugars, whether they come in the form of honey, corn syrup or cane sugar, and that a young pair like mine will develop caries (tooth decay and cavities) if exposed to too much sugar. Gerbils like a treat, as do we all. But our gerbils also go nuts for tiny shavings of fresh carrot that they can get in their mouth, and limited doses of nuts and striped sunflower seeds that are not a part of their regular diet. Once in a while a little bit of orange or apple isn't going to kill them, but I can find no reason to think that added sugars and potentially indigestible pine shavings are going to be good for them. This item is made in China. As far as I'm concerned it can stay there.

review_headline: Our Tails Are Waggin' Over the Pet Feeder!
review_body:

He has a quirk of hating to hear his tags clink against metal bowls, so we had used small plastic dog bowls found in every pet store across the nation in the past. His tags do hit the rim of this feeder, but the sound doesn't bother him like metal on metal. The collapsible bowls in this set are narrower (4" across the inside) and deeper (2" from the top) than his old standard plastic bowls (plus they are raised, of course). The height (3-3/4" to the top rim) is good for him. It's very attractive, folds up and collapses easily for travel, and fits dogs his size generally, give or take five pounds.

All four colors are bright and cheerful, even the green is gorgeous. It can look washed out online.

The materials seem to be sturdy. The frame is a hard plastic, and the bowls a more flexible plastic. The company also makes a nice matching rubber grippmat that acts as a placemat for your fur child. We will be buying a second set -- the elevated feeder and grippmat -- to put on our boat home, too. What better endorsement than to buy the product again?!

review_body:
I love waking up every morning and taking a walk around my neighborhood. Unfortunately, it has become increasingly difficult with the numerous stray dogs that have moved in. They've started becoming more aggressive and I've been walking with pepper spray, but I'd hate to ever have to use it. When I seen the Hoont Electronic Dog Repeller and Trainer with LED Flashlight I was hoping it would be the solution to my issue and I was right! This thing works great and humanely.

I received a small box with the Hoont device, which comes with a convenient wrist strap, and a user manual. It requires a single 9V battery, which is not included, but easy to install. I have included product pictures for reference.

The Repeller works by transmitting a high pitched, ultrasonic sound that I can't hear, but the dogs can. It will work within a 50ft radius and has a button for repelling and another for training.

The Hoont Repeller has a built-in LED flashlight that can be turned on and off with a switch on the side of the device. When the light becomes dim I know it's time to change the battery. I enjoy being able to walk in the early hours of the morning and after sunset having the security of the flashlight. I even use the Repeller and light while walking to my car.

Because the device is lightweight and compact, measuring only 4x2.5", it's easy to take with me wherever I go. It fits in my povket, purse and hike pack, but I prefer the sense of security having it around my wrist, especially in high-risk areas.

product_title: Purina Tidy Cats LightWeight 24/7 Performance Clumping Litter for Multiple Cats - (1) 17 lb. Pail
review_body:
I don't normally buy the Tidy Cats brand because in the past I've found their litter to be poor quality (poor clumping and odor control) so I normally buy more expensive cat litter. I saw this on a great sale at my grocery store, so decided to try it out. And I love it. Best cat litter I've ever used, hands down. It clumps amazingly well, is really clean, and I don't smell anything. As long as the regular price is not too expensive, I'll be buying this from now on.

I came online here to see if I could buy more of it from Amazon for a good deal, and then found all these negative reviews. I was shocked. I've had an entirely positive experience with this Lightweight cat litter. My litter box is in our laundry room (decent-sized) so maybe that is part of it, as all the mess tends to stay in there anyway. But that said, I still don't see any more tracking on the floor than normal. And I definitely haven't noticed any dust. In fact, this product is much less dusty than the cat litters I've used previously.

I really like this cat litter. I figured Tidy Cats would be taking over the market with this cat litter, as it is so good plus it is lightweight. Clearly, others haven't had the same experience. So, I guess it just depends on your personal situation and preferences. I'm sure glad I tried it.

review_headline: Awesome Best! Much better than my last one
review_body:
I purchased this premium microfiber quilted dog car seat cover from The Pristine Lola 700 and installed it in my Nissan Maxima's back seat. It fits perfectly just like custom made for it and the installation was quick and easy.

I love the extra adjustable long straps that fit securely around the head rests unlike the last cover I had, and I have not seen a seat cover that comes with it. The best thing about this dog seat cover is that it is a good large size with 63” length so it does completely covers the entire back seat to ensure no dog hair is left anywhere. The non slip backing ensures that the cover stays in place and I have never had a problem with this.

There are two storage pockets that are deep enough to store a leash and collapsible dog water bowl. As well there is a zipper that can be used to allow for seating of passengers without removing the seat cover.

We bought this the other day to try with one of our cats who gets very stressed out and territorial when we have company staying with us. He's a very high strung cat he will only eat his dry food, doesn't like treats, doesn't like wet food, and can't be tricked into taking pills with pill pockets which he will chew apart and spit out the pill. Since we moved to our new place over a year ago he started marking, but only when we had guests staying with us or immediately following, and was visibly stressed during their visits.

We found this at our local pet store and decided to give it a try, we weren't particularly hopeful it would work, but we thought the putting it on their paw thing was great. We figured at least we wouldn't have to force feed him and pill we knew he'd lick it off just to clean himself. It did seem to help, he's still anxious, but his anxiety doesn't seem as bad after we give it to him. The first time I gave it to him I put it on his paw and while he did lick it off, be really was not happy about having gel put on his paw and ran and hid. product_title: Cat's Pride Fresh and Light Ultimate Care Premium Unscented Hypoallergenic Multi-Cat Scoop Litter
review_headline: So-so litter may work better when there's only one cat
review_body:
With four indoor cats, I go through a lot of litter and am always interested in trying new types. My cats, OTOH aren't always as game.

My current favorite has been SmartCat litter, which is made from grass seed and which has no dust, is renewable and clumps exceptionally well. It's also very lightweight. Unfortunately, one of my cats doesn't share my appreciation for it and demonstrated her opinion in a decidedly unacceptable way, by peeing on the bed when I changed over the last litter box to it. So it was back to the Costco stuff (Litter Purrfect), at least for that box, and there haven't been any accidents since.

Enter Cat's Pride Fresh and Light Ultimate. I took a chance and filled one of the boxes with it, and it was a big hit with the cats from the start. Unfortunately, over time I found I was not nearly as fond of it. It tracks a lot worse than the other litters I've used (most notably Litter Purrfect, which I've used the most; also SmartCat and Petco's house brand) probably because of its fine texture. Despite using a very good mat , I was finding it EVERYWHERE, even after sweeping it up again and again. I have no complaints about odor--it's no better or worse than conventional litters. (I loathe scented litters and only use unscented, which this is.)

Unfortunately, it also seems to lose some of its clumping ability pretty quickly, so I had to deal with some broken clumps. And that, inevitably, will lead to odor.

I initially rated it four stars, but I bought two more jugs, and by the time I was down to the last one, I had grown to actively dislike it and couldn't wait to use it up and move on to another brand--one that clumps better and tracks a lot less. It's worth noting that I use a LARGE litter box, and the jug it comes in really only filled it once.

It may be that it will work better for single-cat households, since the litter box where I was using it (I have four) gets a lot of use. But for my situation, I'm done with this product and won't be going back.ng back.

product_title: SturdiBag Extra Large Flexible Height Pet Carrier.
review_body:
As the name suggests, this is a quality, sturdy pet carrier. I was pleased to find a bag that can carry pets above 22 pounds, as our french bulldog is on the bigger side at 32 pounds.

However, I had to return the extra large and purchase a large because it was simply TOO big. Although I'm sure our pup appreciated the extra leg room, I'm not sure how anyone can carry around the XL. It's simply too tall, long, and bulky.

Although the large is a little cozier, it's the only way to go and will work for short trips. However, there are a few design flaws.

Our dog needs to be able to stick his head out the carrier, otherwise he gets anxious if he doesn't have a good view of what is going on. Our old pet carrier (which he outgrew) had a flap that unzipped part of the way on one side so that he could stick his head out, and unzipped fully on the other side so that he could step into the bag. This bag only unzips on ONE side. Although it has a top flap that you can open, our dog has to be standing up in order to poke his head out--that isn't comfortable for him and it's a lot harder to carry/balance the bag when he is standing (keep in mind that our dog is quite tall for a frenchie).

Also, the only parts of the bag that unzip are all on the same side. In order to get our dog to go in, we usually hold a treat at one opening as he walks in through an opening on the opposite side. Our dog does not like to walk into a dark closed bag--neither would I!

Unfortunately, most manufacturers don't make bags that can support the weight of our large french bulldog, so it looks like he and his owners will just have to adjust to this one.

product_title: Wagner's 57075 Safflower Seed, 5-Pound Bag
review_body: In my yard safflower seed actually works much better than black oil sunflower to attract desirable birds. Why? Sunflower is adored by those pesky European house sparrows who mob the feeder when it is served, crowding out other birds. Grackles also love it (and also drive away smaller birds), as do squirrels, who can't get to the feeder but loiter constantly under it for any discards. Granted, the sparrows are not picky and do eat safflower, too. But they (and the grackles) do not like it as much as sunflower so they leave more room for other birds. The squirrels are uninterested, too, and I rarely see them under the feeder when I serve safflower instead of sunflower (chipmunks, on the other hand, do like it but they are much less obtrusive than squirrels). on the other hand, the desirable birds (cardinals, chickadees, nuthatches, finches, etc.) seem to like both types of seeds equally well, so in the end I see them a lot more when I serve safflower.

review_body: And so here I am, just another upset client adding to the pile of disappointing complaints on what I had hoped to be a great product. Myself being a vet tech at a vet office have known of the product for some time now and have many clients that use it and have no reports of any problems as of yet. Lucky for them. So I thought I'd give it a whirl on my 4 year old perfectly healthy 75 pound female pitbull. Highly active and happy and bouncy as can be, just a few days shy of a week my dog started to grow lethargic. She was eating and drinking normally but she wouldn't run to the door the moment she heard the knob jiggle. The pink color in her ears and gums grew pale and, living on the second floor of an apartment, as she would typically book it down the stairs to head outside, instead she was hesitant going down each and every step, hopping from foot to foot a few times before taking another step and whining and whimpering in the process as if it were physically painful for her. The collar was the ONLY thing we had changed for her since the day we got her at 8 weeks and just two days after removing the collar she bounced right back to her usual crazy self. I don't reccommend this product for anyone with highly active dogs or any pets in the elderly stages of life as they are weak and it seems to cause a multitude of issues in them as well. So now I will try to get my $60+ dollars back that was wasted on this collar that lasted me a whopping 4-5 days rather than a whole 8 months.

product_title: ProSelect Empire Dog Cage
review_headline: Has helped with our dog's anxiety!
review_body: We purchased this crate about 2 weeks ago.  Our dog suffers from separation anxiety and we have tried everything with the exception of hiring a behaviorist for treatment. We have tried Prozac, Xanax, Thunder shirt, lavender oil, exercise, things in crate to keep busy - basically everything that was affordable to try to help him but nothing worked.  He is a Beagle with very powerful jaws and was destroying his wire cage.  He bent many of the wire bars together, popping loose the welding.  My husband then put zip ties to hold the bars in place - only to find all of them bitten off lying on the floor.  He got to where he was able to pull the door loose and escape.  We then purchased little padlocks to put around the door and this helped to keep the door in place.  But he kept squeezing the bars together and the vet said that it was possible for dogs to break those wires loose and swallow them.  We were really worried about this happening.  We video recorded him one day  and saw him actually getting the corner of the door bent open enough to squeeze his head through!  It must have hurt him because he quickly pulled it back.  I later checked his neck and it was scratched up from this.  We were on the verge of finding him a home that we felt he would do better but with the exception of the separation anxiety, he is a perfect companion to us.  Based on good reviews We then decided to give the proselect empire cage a try.  My husband put the crate together and the next day we tried it.  We video recorded him again - he started getting anxious but when he tried to bite the bar on the cage it was too hard for him and he just looked at it and barked.  After that he never tried to escape.  He is now very calm in his crate.  He lays down and is very comfortable in it.  We think he really likes it.  He has went into it on his own and it is hard to get him up and out of it in the mornings.  For our dog this crate has been excellent in keeping him calm and he no longer reaches that'high anxiety' point to where he cannot calm back down.  Now when we come home he only starts whining and panting a little at us.  Nothing like before. My father has occasionally had to come and let him out when we could not and he even notices the difference in him.  He says that he just seems happier.  It seems that once he learned he could not mess around with the bars and the door - why bother.  This cage is pricey but so worth it for us because it has been a life saver - keeping our little guy safe and happy therefore allowing us to enjoy our time with him.  We are so happy that we finally found something that has worked!

product_title: Replacement Dog Tether
review_body:
I use this and another tether from a different brand to secure and keep each of my dogs safe in the car in conjunction with harnesses that they wear (I wouldn't want a collar to choke them if we had to slam on the brakes suddenly). After having been seriously injured in a car accident I wanted to ensure that my dogs were as protected as possible while in the car in case someone else did something that created a hazardous situation. My sister got a tiny dog several months ago and borrowed one of my tethers and has returned it. Since the one I had is no longer available, I had to get a different kind. Thankfully there are a lot more on Amazon now than there were when I originally purchased my other tethers and this one is so much better, that I may buy even more.
My other tethers are very short strap loops with one carabiner attached. They work by wrapping the loop around the seat belt and threading the carabiner through the loop. You then attach the carabiner to the D ring in the dog's harness. Unfortunately, this makes a very short tether even shorter. This is fine if I only have one dog on my lap, but being that my dogs are tiny, they often like to be together and the short tethers frequently cause one of them to have to sit on the other or not be able to get comfortable. The adjustable tether solves this problem, but also makes it easy to ensure that they can't go farther than you want them too. I used to "daisy chain" a couple of my old tethers to gain extra length, but one of my dogs was able to go a bit farther than was safe and ended up hanging from the headrest after attempting to get onto my husband's shoulder. (He was in a harness, so it didn't hurt him, but it can be quite distracting)
This tether seems well made and the carabiners don't feel cheap or chintzy and the strap is a softer fabric so it won't burn and scrape skin like cheaper strap material if it should be pulled forcefully (like in a crash or hard stop). Being that my dogs are tiny, there's never any concern that the strap will break, but this looks and feels strong enough to restrain large dogs well. Overall, I really, really like this tether and will choose this one over any of the other ones I own. I definitely recommend this.tiny, there's never any concern that the strap will break, but this looks and feels strong enough to restrain large dogs well. product_title: Tagg Pet GPS Plus - Dog and Cat Tracker Collar Attachment
review_body: First off this is a great idea at an affordable price.  I have a young Great Pyrenees and I live in the country with him with a large amount of surrounding woods, but with excellent cell coverage.  The home zone feature is great and it will let you know if the dog/pet leaves this area.  This was obnoxious at first when my wife and I would walk him but we hit the snooze button when we receive the first alert and no longer have an issue.  If he were to get away on the walk we could simply pull up the app and ping his location.  The temperature sensor is currently not activated but will be later this summer with a change in the outdated app.  I believe the entire app is going to be revamped.  Honestly, this should have happened prior to the release but I can wait.  Yes you do have to pay a subscription plan but this works off of cell towers and gps which I'm sure Tagg has to pay a rental fee to use.  Besides, $79 for the unit is not a lot of money for peace of mind.  This device is also water resistant so I have never had to worry about it while hosing my dog down.  As far as the battery, at first it was not lasting very long and this was when we were taking him for walks and it was constantly telling us that my dog was outside of the home zone.  The continuous location pinging runs the battery down pretty fast(within a few days).  But now that the snooze seems to be functioning well we are getting around 3 weeks out of it.  We also take our dog to doggy daycare so he can burn some energy off while my wife and I are at work while it is so hot out and with one press of the snooze button there are no alerts received during the 8 hours he is there.  Overall I'm very satisfied with the product but definitely looking forward to the app upgrade and temp sensor being activated.  on a side, I did contact Tagg with suggestions and they responded and stated that they were looking for suggestions and that they would forward them to their software team, particularly snoozing the Tagg from the app.

review_headline: Buyer beware.  Dangerous machine!  Do NOT buy.
review_body: I've purchased hundreds of items on Amazon within the last few years and this is my second review ever.  I felt compelled to write one for this purchase, due to the possibility of an animal being harmed.  Before purchasing this item, I read most of the reviews thoroughly.  Most definitely, the good outweighed the bad, so I decided to go for it and give this dryer a try.  I have been using a human blow dryer to groom my 2 Goldendoodles for the past 2 years.  It takes me 3 hours each dog, which was becoming daunting, so I searched and searched for a good and reasonable dog dryer.  2 days after receiving it, I washed one of my dogs, I decided to give it a go. About 5 minutes into drying, I noticed a burning smell and the dryer started to get really, really HOT.  Just as I was about to turn the hose away from my dog, it blew out a huge plum of black smoke/powder directly on my dogs chest.  My dog is cream, so it was very noticeable.  I used it for all of 5 MINUTES!  If I wouldn't have been paying attention, or left the dryer attached to the cage, it would have definitely burned or killed my dog.  I would not recommend this product to anyone!  Don't be fooled like myself by the good reviews.  This machine is dangerous and should be taken off the shelves!!  It is going back to Amazon immediately.

product_title: Petco Auto Fish Feeder
review_headline: Needs practice to get it oriented.
review_body:
I have this in a 10 gallon tank, raising tilapias, ultimately for sale. The trick with mounting the clear hopper is to get it oriented correctly with the black insert that connects the hopper to the body of the unit. Play with the the black insert until you get it to click onto the hopper. The correct orientation is to have one of the raised fastening ridges next to the HINGE on the clear hopper. Try it on your tank. The hopper should rotate and then come to rest with the hopper door closed. When you have this orientation figured out, scratch the black insert with an H at the hinge so you can line up the fastening ridge with the hinge easily any time. Yes, this is hard to describe, but play with it and then make your scratch mark for future filling.

Works well so far (3 months) and is equal to but cheaper than the eheim that I have on another tank.

review_headline: All 5 of our dogs, from 2 pounds to large breed, love them!
review_body:
I WAS NOT COMPENSATED for this review.

We have four chihuahuas (two are tiny, at 2 and 3 lbs. and the others are regular size) and one puppy Standard Poodle.

I bought the tiny ones at first but because of the shape, the chihuahuas had a hard time getting a grip with their teeth. They kept stealing the Large one from the puppy. I bought them a package of Large ones and these dogs have never been happier. They have never been interested in chews because of their tiny teeth and weak jaws.

These treats have absolutely no odor, even when slobbered on and chewed on for hours. Absolutely no diarrhea, either.

To finally see our little ones have a treat they truly enjoy has been incredible. I will admit, I was quite skeptical. I would have never guessed my dogs would show any interest in these, but they go crazy for them. We've had them a week and they are almost finished.

Our two little guys have terrible plaque and bad breath. They won't allow us to brush their teeth and have refused every single kind of chew. These treats have also eased the anxiety of my largest chihuahua, combined with her Thundershirt. She has something on which to focus and the chewing has helped get out her nervous energy.

The puppy, of course, loves it. He is in that nightmare teething stage and these have saved my furniture and my sanity.

I was most concerned about Wawa. She has the weakest jaw strength and already needs a dental cleaning at age 2. When I found she had stolen the puppy's treat (she is 3lb and he is 35lb) I was amazed. She was just SO happy!

product_title: Grandma Lucy's Grain Free Freeze Dried Dog Food
review_headline: Fantastic for those seeking a low phosphorous food
review_body:
My 14-year old basset was recently diagnosed with kidney failure (CRF). The vet 'prescribed' a kidney-formulated (low protein, low phosphorous) diet that left Wellington lethargic and very grumpy. Five years ago he had significant back surgery. Keeping him fairly active is key to maintaining muscles and thus stability around his spine. But once he started on the RX food, he kept to a 10-foot radius around the house and slept the other 23 hours a day. Honestly, I thought we were nearing the end. I didn't even know he was in CRF until the bloodwork came back, and in trying to fix the kidneys it seemed like the vet broke the dog.

I did *extensive* research and found that lowering phosphorous is critical with CRF, but lowering protein is controversial. And given his back issues and the known tendency of seniors to lose muscle, I thought losing dietary protein would result in losing even more muscle, and thus the back would go long before the kidneys. In my research, I found Grandma Lucy's Artisan has very low phosphorous and modest protein. And just one look at the ingredients sold me. The first three ingredients in the RX food were corn and gluten. Fourth was byproduct meal. Grandma Lucy's could be fed to your mother (smile). And one bag in? He went for a hike with us this morning. Plays with this toys again. And wags his tail incessantly. If the kidneys go a day or two sooner, it was worth it for him.

Added bonus: the RX food was dry. Once reconstituted, GL ensures the dog is getting lots of water with his food.

The difference here lies with the way that each type of DE is treated. Pool grade DE is calcined, meaning that is treated with very high heat. This turns the silicon dioxide that is present in the DE into crystalline silica. Pool grade diatomaceous earth has more than 1 percent 1% (in fact, it can it can range from 60-70 percent) crystalline silica. Food Grade Diatomaceous Earth, on the other hand, has less than 1% crystalline silica and is not calcined.

review_headline: Not just for dogs - can be used for cats/kittens too!
review_body: This is a great little pet stroller, I purchased it for the animal shelter I work for. Our main purpose for wanting a pet stroller was to allow us to take cats/kittens to our major fundraising events. At our events, our adoptable animals selected to attend and stationed with their handlers at the entrance of the facility to greet our donors as they arrive. Being stationed out in the open, bringing cats/kittens always posed the problem of getting loose. We needed something to contain the cats/kittens that was stylish and appropriate for the event. A traditional carrier would not fly at these types of events. So we typically opted to bring only dogs to these events until we ordered this pet stroller. It is working wonderfully! It's a very secure stroller that is encloses completely. There is very little worry of anyone escaping, although there are  very small openings where the zipper meets in the corners. But only the smallest of kittens could fit through these holes, and they'd have to have a pretty good go at it. We are very happy with this stroller, and so are our cat lover donors who now get to snuggle with kittens at our events.

review_headline: Waste of Money, Worm Segments aka proglottid still present
review_body:
We bought this at a local pet store after seeing worm segments peeking out of the anus of our cats. We thought we would give it a try. We followed the directions to the T making sure they got their daily doses. After a while we thought there were gone when we finished.
However, after treatment days later there were still tapeworm segments peeking out. We went to the vet instead and got some actual dewormer pills (which aren't that expensive). I have yet to see any worms peeking out or in stool.

It would be wise to follow up later with more worm pills, but not with this stuff. This is just over-glorified "natural" (it really isn't because of how much it is diluted {research what the 6x actual means}) water. I know we are in the age of trying to save money and be "natural", but honestly there are many inexpensive medicines that really do not have many side effects. Not all, but the rare few.

review_headline: great reviews, and the fact that the pack can ...
review_body:
After reviewing several doggie backpacks, I decided on this one because of the large pockets, great reviews, and the fact that the pack can come off but keep the base layer strapped on. We have a black lab, 85-90 lbs. I ordered the large size in blue. I apparently mis-read the sizing guide, apparently I should have ordered an XL. I thought the L fit OK, but my husband felt she should have the XL, so we'll be ordering that instead. Color is great, looks exactly as depicted. Pockets are VERY large, you can fit a lot in here. The straps are decent quality, and the handle on top is nice, though it's likely more useful for smaller dogs. I really like the feature about taking the pack off but keeping the base layer strapped on - I think it's really smart design. After trying it on, our dog liked it! She didn't seem to mind the pack at all, or after I loaded it with a few items to test for weight. Keep in mind she is an 11 year old dog, so it was a pleasant surprise she didn't mind this and actually seemed to like it! (first time she's ever worn a pack).

The only con for me is that the pockets on the side are so large that it is difficult to keep the weight balanced as items moved around. I tested one can of food and one 16oz water bottle on each side, and as she waddled around the items shifted around making the pack off kilter. I think this can probably be managed depending on what and how you pack.

product_title: AmazonBasics Soft-Sided Pet Travel Carrier
review_headline: Nice and light, cat seems to enjoy it
review_body:
WEIGHT IS MINIMAL
Having a 20+ pound cat, this carrier appealed to me on 2 fronts.
It did not add to the weight I had to carry, that a large plastic carrier would.
It has a shoulder strap. This helps distribute the weight or allows you to use your hand to open a door. I can see how much easier this would be if you had 2 cats to carry around.

EASY TO STORE
Also to those of you, that have limited storage space, this carrier folds flat and does not take up space when stored. You can pop it into the back of a closet.

TWO WAYS INTO THE CARRIER
Using the carrier, you have a front door and a top door. I would have liked to have a 3rd door on the opposite end, but this is okay. I know on a few of my cats the top door is essential as often they have no inclination to get out, once they realize they are at the vets.
The non-opening ends rigidity, keeps the carrier square, such that you can easily leave one end opened and setting on the floor. This is my successful technique to get one of my cats into a carrier. Falls for it every time.

REMOVABLE BOTTOM PAD
The bottom pad is hard and has a removable faux lambswool pad on top. Since the pad is removable, it appears it can be washed. This can be essential if your pet has an accident.

USAGE
I have carried around my heaviest cat in this. At 20+ pounds in weight, Cisco can be hard to transport, he is fluffy as well. This carrier did not seem to tight for him. Also the see-through sides added to his sense of space. I’m thinking of getting a few more for my other cats (I have 4) as this carrier is easier to store and smaller than some of my large plastic ones.

TRAVEL
I’m assuming since this carrier is soft-sided it is not suitable for buses or planes.

One of our dogs is a puppy and he got car sick 3 times during the trip there and back. It was easy to just wipe up with a wet paper towel. Very easy to clean. The dogs also knocked over the water dish a couple of times and it was great that the water didn't absorb into the car seats.

I would highly recommend this for anyone with dogs. It kept them safe in the back and kept us safe with the dogs not trying to crawl up to the front. Great product, easy to wash, and easy to set up.

product_title: Taste of the Wild Cat Food
review_body: I bought this cat food as a change of pace from the Blue Diamond I had been feeding my 3 kitties.  Blue Diamond is an excellent food, but more expensive and the flavor range is limited.  I thought the kitties deserved a change and this venison and salmon formula seemed just the ticket.  It's also less expensive by about $5 (and every dollar counts).  The ingredients are excellent and on par with BD.  About a year or so ago, I decided that my felines deserved better food than the grocery store junk I had been feeding them.  I settled on BD because, frankly, it was on sale at the time and they had a weight loss formula.  Once they started on it, I was extremely happy to discover that my kits were no longer having issues with ugly, gross hairballs.  They simply disappeared.  This was the biggest change that occurred when I switched their diet.  Their coats also looked better and were really shiny, and they shed less and generally ate less of the good food, which was obviously filling them up for a longer period of time (they ate constantly when fed the cheap stuff).  I originally picked Blue Diamond because they had a weight loss formula and my cats looked more like lion cubs, so some stricter feeding measures were in order, lol!  However, it's been a year and they haven't lost an ounce between them, but no matter.  I have been feeding them TOTW for about a month and I'm pleased with the results thus far.  There have been no hairballs, so on this score, the two brands are even.  The kibbles are also the same small size.  TOTW smells really good, like real meat and once the transition was complete, my lion cubs seemed to like it a lot, maybe even better than BD.  I will try feeding them TOTW for the foreseeable future. I buy the largest size bag, which lasts about a month.  Cats are obligate carnivores, meaning they don't need any carbohydrates in their diet.  However, both BD and TOTW have carbs, which I understand aid digestion.  I would prefer an all meat formula, something that replicates their diet in the wild.  However, it appears that all cat food brands contain some measure of carbohydrates so that is out of the question.  Although it's a pinch on my pocketbook, I feel better giving them a more wholesome diet than Purina Meow Mix (yes, I know, bad kitty mommy, lol).  I guess I'll have to give up on them losing weight if the weight loss formula didn't have the slightest impact, but they do appear to feel better now that their diet has improved.  They are certainly eating less, which is good.  Although this is a review of TOTW Rocky Mountain formula, I have to say that it is comparable to Blue Diamond in every way.  I will stick with it and save myself some precious dollars and hopefully, give my felines a delectable dining experience (I would actually like some venison myself, with a red wine reduction, thank you, lol)! product_title: Good Pet Stuff Company Hidden Cat Litter Box
review_headline: Decent - but started holding odors after 6 months
review_body:
Like many cat owners---I've been on the hunt for the perfect litter box. I used this box for about a year then had to move on to something else. Overall - I liked the fact that it didn't seem to look like a litter box & that it was covered. It is a little big to fit into a corner or a space due to its round size - but not too big.
For the first 6 months or so it was great --- Even with the top on, it hid the litter box, and there was no smell. While I don't change it every day, I do change it every other day, and do a complete litter change every two weeks & scrub out the box. It was great for awhile, then slowly it got to the point where, even with daily changes, it smelled so much in the litter box my 2 cats didn't want to use it. I ended up having to leave the top off because the odor that was trapped in there was just too much. I know it does happen after awhile it just seems as the plastic absorbs the odor & even with daily changes my cats didn't want to use the box. I ended up getting them a new box and they are quite happy & content with it.

So - while this isn't a bad litter box - It isn't something that I was able to keep around over a year. Would I buy it again----not for the price.

review_body:
Pros:
Adjustable lighting angle
Easy to install

Cons:
Cord clips interfere with glass canopy

The Marineland hidden LED strip light is an innovative approach to aquarium lighting. Since the light is mounted on the front edge of the aquarium, light can be directed towards the rear of the aquarium instead of the bottom, resulting in fewer shadows on the fish. The only issue I've had with this product is that the cord clips are made of rather thick plastic, which prevents the tank's glass canopy from resting evenly on the frame. The LEDs produce pleasantly colored light that is at least (if not more) as bright as the light produced by a standard fluorescent aquarium fixture. I especially enjoy using the blue moonlight feature to illuminate my tank at night.

product_title: NEOGEN RODENTICIDE 45-Pack Ramik Rat and Mouse Bait Pail
review_body:
Wow! This is a day two report, but I'm impressed so far - I'll do an update as time goes on.
Rats seem to like it OVER thrown-out human food! My problem with baits in the past has been that mice and rats turn their noses up at the D-Con, etc. baits and prefer the little scraps they can retrieve from my garbage cans, etc. They were clearly attracted to the and went for the unopened plastic packages pf Ramik Green.

Our usually mice-and-squirrels-and-rabbits-only neighborhood was besieged by rats after collapsed sewage pipes recently created a "sink hole" in the road and apparently provided them with access from a distant connection to the sewers. Some homes were apparently entered through toilets!
I heard noises in my house and saw a darting rat a couple times. Bread and other on-the-counter foods were attacked quickly. Snap and electrocution traps caught a couple but they learn quick. I decided to flood the inside and outside with bait and tried these Ramik baits.
Wow! I first set up two, putting the unopened plastic packages on top of empty leftover packaging from chicken and an eaten frozen meal's bowl with a tiny amount of food left - I thought the smell would draw them and placed them in semi-hidden locations. Within a couple hours both plastic packages were gone - taken away - hopefully to wherever they nested. The noises disappeared during the night. I heard a couple, apparently from a lone rat/mouse.
Today, I'll be setting out many more of these up in places inside and outside, basement, and first floor and attic in places where the the rabbits and visiting friends and neighbors cats and dogs won't be able to get to them.
Rats are very smart, but I don't think they'll be able to identify the packages as having killed their buddies before they themselves get poisoned, but I'll update this later!

product_title: IRIS Open Top Cat Litter Box Kit with Shield and Scoop
review_body:
I've just ordered a third one of these litter boxes and realized it was time to finally write a review.

Concisely:
- most importantly, keeps the litter in the box
- still in good shape after 2.5 years of use
- easy to scoop and clean
- big enough for most cats
- for my needs, very high-value at $10

Verbosely:

I purchased the first one two and half years ago after adopting a medium-sized female cat (10 lbs, spayed) who has very good litter box habits, but vigorously covers after using the box, and had been kicking the litter out of a smaller, low-sided "pan"-style box. The IRIS box absolutely does the trick--she can cover as much as she wants and the high sides of the shield prevent the litter from getting kicked out of the box. I purchased a second one for my sister's much larger male cat (16+ lbs, neutered) who tends to spray and be a bit messier with the litter box. He still manages to kick some litter out sometimes, but the IRIS box is a huge improvement over the low-sided box this box replaced. I've been totally satisfied in both cases and have just ordered a third one for a cat I'm fostering.

I would recommend this to anyone who is looking for an open-top-style litter box. No litter box is going to be the perfect solution for every cat and every pet parent, but for the cats in my life it has worked very well. With it I use Precious Cat clumping litter (multi-cat, in the blue bag).

A (theoretical) disclaimer: this box is large enough to hold many pounds of litter. If you wanted to move the box while over-filled, I could see how the box could become damaged by its own weight, as some reviewers have reported. This has not happened to me, though. (Other disclaimer: the included scoop is mediocre, but works. The "hang-on-the-box" part is nice, but I use a larger scoop that I bought separately.)

The top pieces slide very easily and she really doesn't have to move them at all to be able to slide her tongue in and get all the kibble out. They move in the process but there isn't much thought that she has to give this toy in order to get her food. Another thing I don't like as much about this one compared to other toys is that there are only the 4 openings and they really don't hold much food, maybe half a cup at the most. With all that said, I think this puzzle would be a good intro to food puzzles for a dog to build their confidence or for a smaller dog that just needs to slow down when they eat. product_title: Hill's Science Diet Adult Minced Canned Cat Food, 24-Pack
review_headline: Great food if you get the right batch
review_body: My cat with urinary crystal issues loves this food and it is almost as balanced in nutrients as the prescription food. It helps with his water intake since he will eat most of a can and it has a runny consistency. Unfortunately the consistency varies by batch. He wouldn't really eat the food from certain cases and the texture is obviously different than the other cases (less runny). Since the shipment prior to this had a later expiration date (3/2017) and my cat liked those cases I thought it was safe to order more than one case this past time to avoid the expiration date he didn't like but, I received the older lot expiration date (12/2016). Since it is all he will eat I guess I have to buy one at a time until they are past this particular date of cases or get it from the store until they are past sending out this particular date of food.  The store has 5/2017 date and the food is like the original food my cat liked so it seems the 12/2016 lot is an odd bad batch. So it might be worth a try again down the road for your cat if they didn't like the first batch. I wish it was possible to request skipping over a certain date of cases since I know they will be going into the donation box. Also as the other reviewer mentioned the shipping is a problem and I have to throw out about 2 of the corner cans per 24 pack because they are dented and leaking everywhere. Some are sneaky leaks you don't notice until they start to smell horrible and go in search of the smell. Maybe shipper should use bubble wrap or something or smaller box. Still cheaper than at the store even minus 2 cans per case.

review_headline: like a Shiba Inu or a Schnauzer
review_body:
I had some issues with this product, but after some hassles, the product seems to be working. I bought one used from Wayfair, and after about ten times of use, the front wheel fell off and one of the screws connecting the frame to the carriage came loose. The used model also came without the rain cover. After several weeks of emails with Wayfair, they sent me a new model. Wayfair was cooperative just hard to communicate with them since their message system is so anonymous, and they forgot to inform me that they sent a new model to my old office address. I was able to repair the old model by calling the manufacturer (I had to look them up online), who politely and promptly sent me new bearings and even photographs on how to repair the front wheel. They sent the parts without charging me and via Priority Mail. Overall it's stable, just had some issues getting set up.

Note: the product is advertised to carry dogs up to 70 pounds. The stroller can indeed carry 70 pounds, if divided the top carry case and the bottom case, but the volume of the top case is only large enough for a 35-pound dog, like a Shiba Inu or a Schnauzer. product_title: Sleepypod Atom In-Cabin Pet Carrier
review_headline: Simple, Smart Construction, but not as Difficult as Splitting an Atom
review_body:
Previously, I have owned a Sherpa carrier and have used it only when necessary for hurricane evacuation, etc. It is huge, and fit both pets I once had. The Sherpa is great if you have a larger pet and no real carry-ons. (I believe it's the largest carrier that is allowed on the major airlines; the dimensions are bigger than what is stated on their websites, but Sherpa is the only carrier that is mentioned as bigger yet an allowed exception.)

I now have a kitten and I wanted something that would be discreet and fit with my rollerboard suitcase.

The Atom is a perfect size for my kitten. She can sit or stretch out with no problem. Right now, she's only 2.5 pounds. To compare, I put my sister's 11 pound cat in the carrier. She fit snugly. Although she couldn't sit up, she was able to stretch out slightly and seemed comfortable. I think it would be great for flights 3 hours or less.

When I received the carrier, I put it on the floor and placed some toys in it to get my kitty used to it. She wandered into it and was even found napping at one point.
The Atom slipped easily onto the handle of my roll-aboard. In this position, I liked how my pet was raised nearer to my eye, which allowed me to be very aware of how she was doing.
I purchased the black Atom, and it blended well with my other black luggage. The zippers seem sturdy and the bag feels well-constructed. There is a clip on either side of this bag which can be hooked onto a seatbelt. This is a great feature, in addition to the handle sleeve, for seamless transfers between car, luggage, and plane.
Cons: Pockets are nice, but they close only with a small velcro tab. Things may easily fall out. The shoulder strap is nice, but there is no way to disconect it. For my purposes, I used the handle slide when walking through the terminal and I used the handle located on the top of the carrier to carry the bag. The shoulder strap only got in the way.
I would definitely suggest this carrier to others who have a small pet.

product_title: PetSafe Basic Remote Dog Training Collar for Dogs 8 lb. and Up with Tone and Static Stimulation, Water Resistant, Up to 75 Yards
review_body: I have been using the Basic Remote Trainer for a couple weeks and my dog has adjusted wonderfully to it, with one exception - the reward/positive 'A' tone.  My dog is generally very well trained but she can get excited and distracted occasionally.  This collar reminds her to listen and obey. So far, I have used this to walk my dog without a leash in our quiet neighborhood.   Several years ago I trained my dog on the PetSafe Wireless Pet Containment System to keep her in the backyard. That product uses a series of beeps as a warning as the dog approaches the boundary line. I haven't used it in several years because she is trained to stay in the yard.  However, I believe because of that wireless fence product, my dog had a bad reaction to the "A" tone in the PetSafe Basic Remote Trainer.  I followed the directions repeatedly: had her sit, gave her a treat, verbally affirmed her behavior, and pushed the 'A' button, however, she became very frightened of the 'A' tone and eventually wouldn't even sit out of fear of the 'A' tone.  I would have liked to be able to use the 'A' tone as positive reinforcement, but it just didn't work since she was afraid of it.  Instead I stopped using 'A' and began using the 'B' tone as a negative warning.  Her initial reaction upon hearing the 'B' tone is to get startled and run a 5-6 feet.  She is previously trained to come stand/walk next to me on the commands 'come' and 'heel' so I use those and have had good results with the 'B' tone.  Again, I have not used the shock feature of this collar yet, as I have found that she listens to me more attentively when she has this collar on because of her previous experience with PetSafe training collar products. I will update this review if my experience with the product changes.  Note: I purchased this product from another site.  Update: This has been a wonderful training tool for my dog.  I've been using it for several months now, and have never had to shock her, just use the 'beep' button occasionally as a warning.  Of note, after a few months of ownership, the remote stopped working.  I contacted PetSafe and they sent me a new unit, which I haven't had any problems with to date.

review_body: After reading many reviews I decided to order a bottle to try on my recently adopted Springer spaniel who is suffering from extremely dry skin due to malnutrition. I'd already tried coconut oil in his food, oatmeal baths and a dry skin treatment at the groomer but nothing seemed to be helping or getting rid of the dander and itchy skin. It's only been two days since we've started using the Salmon oil on his food but I can already see a decrease in the dander. I'm very hopeful that the salmon oil will get his skin healthy again. Like other reviews have said it does smell fishy but I think that's a small price to pay for all the positive benefits that this oil offers. My springer also loves the taste of it on his food, even my little Chihuahua/terrier mix who is extremely picky when it comes to food enjoys a few drops on her own food. I haven't had any problems with the pump yet and to keep the oil from spoiling I have been refrigerating it since I live in California and the weathers been on the warm side. I'm so glad that I gave Grizzly a shot. I really think this is just what we need to get my dog's health back on track.

product_title: Halo Holistic Dry Cat Food, Wild Salmon and Whitefish, 6 LB Bag of Natural Cat Food
review_body: I have a healthy 2-year cat who eats since i got her at 3 months non-grain healthy products, mostly, wet food. I provide kibbles for snacking between meals and for that I chose mixing 3/4 wellness and 1/4 halo. Since i started giving her this dry food she had an occasional hairball ( she is a short hair cat), however i decided to give her only halo ( progressively changing her in 2 weeks). After this, she started to have between 2 and 3 hairballs per week!!! It took me a while to identify the culprit. 2 visits to the vet with clear check, more water, different bowls, humidifier in the house, special comb for short-hair cats without change. The poor chiki was in distress until i thought it may be the food. I stopped giving halo food and give her only the orher brand. The hairballs stopped almost immediatly and it has been like that for 6 months now. I think it is a high-quality food that may have this reaction to some cats, just to be aware of it.

I have a 15 pound Maltese-Bichon mix. I live in a very tick infested part of the Northeast. After one walk in the park near my house, my dog would have a dozen ticks in him or on his fur. The ones in him would be almost impossible for me to remove without losing the head. After last year struggling with topical medicines, I decided this year I would try seresto.

The results after 2 weeks have literally amazed me. I find far fewer ticks crawling in his fur, and the very few that I've found actually in him have been either dead or so close to death that I can remove them with a gentle pull.

So far he has no rash or irritation around the collar, he behaves exactly the same, and there is no odor at all.

If the collar works for 8 months like the package says, I'll be thrilled. If it works for 3 months, I'll put a fresh one on him. At this point, I have to say that the collar is almost too good to believe. I will immediately revise my review if he has any medical side effect that I can attribute to the collar (he has zero history of seizure, he rarely vomits and has never been sick).
