product_title: BLUE for Cats Adult Dry Cat Food
review_body:
When I first started feeding Blue my 5 indoor only cats were dining on Purina Cat Chow, which was at most times all I could afford for them to eat. Then I decided to try Blue and a 15 lb bag of dry kibble lasted a whole month for my boys, which is great. At first I noticed that some were having some stomach upset and a couple would throw up after eating and then as each month went by the one throwing up did it more frequently after eating. I'm not sure why he was throwing up after eating this food but he didn't do it when all I fed was Cat Chow.
It took my cats about 3 months of eating Blue for their coats to start becoming very soft, shiny and the poops in the litter box to be less and slightly less smelly. The kibble is small and almost all my cats would rather inhale the food than chew it. I've tried the Turkey, Chicken and Multi cat formulas and noticed that the Multi Cat formula caused the most stomach upset among all 5.
The ingredient list is decent for the price of this cat food and I do notice each month the price either goes up a few dollars or back down to a more reasonable price, but then right back up again. I've done some research on Blue and saw the recalls, also them being sued by Purina for not disclosing their full ingredient list on the packages of cat/dog foods, or should I say lying about what is really in their pet foods.
That right there concerns me because I've lost a canary and hamster years back from a pet food brand that should have been recalled but wasn't and the food was all manufactured in a place where pesticides are also being manufactured. This wasn't a cheap brand either and I was able to buy one for hamsters and another bird seed for canaries. Within 2 weeks of each other my hamster and canary died.
Since then I am more cautious of what foods I buy for my cats and other fur babies. Blue was a choice I made at the time thinking it was safe and also knowing there had been recalls. Finding out that Blue hides ingredients and lies about what really is inside their pet foods is disturbing.

I like that my cats all have shiny coats, lots more energy and seem happy enough eating Blue but after this last bag and seeing my poor cat throw up almost every day right after eating (TMI I know, it was all undigested cat food, nothing else) I feel bad and want my boys to at least have a cat food that won't make them so sick. Even if it means going back to Cat Chow which I am against, I want my cats to be happy.
Needless to say we won't be coming back for more Bluedients and lies about what really is inside their pet foods is disturbing.

I like that my cats all have shiny coats, lots more energy and seem happy enough eating Blue but after this last bag and seeing my poor cat throw up almost every day right after eating (TMI I know, it was all undigested cat food, nothing else) I feel bad and want my boys to at least have a cat food that won't make them so sick. Even if it means going back to Cat Chow which I am against, I want my cats to be happy.
Needless to say we won't be coming back for more Bluekibble get halfway down the bowl and they free feed when ever hungry. A 15 lb bag will last a whole month with 4 cats. For the price the ingredients are decent, except the "natural flavor" added into the mix- which like I've said could literally mean any part of the animal is used for flavor. Compared to the other top dry kibble on the market Blue has about the ingredients including the "natural flavor", except some others also include grains for a much smaller bag tagged with a much larger price. I'm going to go out on a limb here and say that possibly Blue has such a bad reputation because Purina filed a lawsuit back in 2014 or so over 'false advertising' claiming that Blue lied about adding by products into their dog food line. Honesty is always better and you'd think both animal and human foods would be safe and honestly labeled with the complete list of ingredients, but then again we live in a society that lies to get what it wants. My point is to trust what you believe is right and what you want to feed your animals and don't go by what I or anyone else say for that matter. In conclusion I will note that after reviewing all the other dry kibbles for cats and thoroughly being exhausted from finding the same ingredients in all of them, but some with a much higher price (due to them being a larger company with more elite customers) I am satisfied feeding my cats Blue Indoor Chicken kibble. In the past I've fed exclusively Purina Cat Chow and my boys all loved their kibble and now they eat Blue and love this kibble. If my cats are healthy, then I am happy. Simple as that. P.S. For those wondering how much I actually do feed a day- I separate the entire large bag into 3 one-gallon bags and 1 one/half- gallon bag, then feed 2 measuring cups full of kibble into 2 bowls that are left out all day (usually I top off the bowl in the evening because my boys are most active either early morning or evening time). I go through 1 one-gallon bag a week andwhen I get down to the 1 one/half gallon bag I reorder on Prime so that the kibble will be here within a few days before running out of food. The gray cat pictured below weights 13 lbs, the white one is 12 lbs, the tabby is 10 lbs and the kitten is 4 lbs. All my cats are neutered and have core plus Rabies shots annually (except the Rabies is a 3 year vaccine and I don't let my boys have the Feline Leukemia vaccine or FeLV because they each have a severe reaction to the vaccine and it is known to cause sarcoma in cats).

product_title: Merrick Grain Free Dry Dog Food
review_headline: Great food for a shiny coat, less skin itching and reduced shedding.
review_body: I'm the owner of two collies.  A 1 year old and a 4 year old.  I was using Royal Canine for the puppy at the vet's recommendation and both dogs loved it. We were  happy with that brand as well and still consider it a great dog food.  My groomer asked me to switch to Merrick Grain Free Salmon, Duck or Chicken to help the puppy's coat, which was very thick, but dry.  Not wanting to feed two dogs two different foods, I put both dogs on Merrick.  Since Merrick is for dogs of all ages no more having two different tubs of food, first benefit.  Second benefit, I couldn't believe the difference in the shine in both dogs' coats!!  Noticeable after just a month-6 weeks.  Third and most important benefit......my 4 year old suffered from what we all thought was an allergy to grass.  Each spring he'd chew his feet until they were so irritated they required medication.  No more!!!!  Now we're thinking he was allergic to grain and this is a grain free food.  They love this food, all of the flavors!  The flavors recommended by my groomer are a bit higher in Omega 3s but I wouldn't hesitate to try any of the flavors.  The kibble is quite small about the size of a large pea.  The salmon flavor has a pretty strong odor, but no long lasting after effects (if you know what I mean!).

product_title: HEALERS Urban Walker Dog Boots-Silver/Neon Yellow-2 ct, Small
review_headline: Thoughtful details make these boots work as promised
review_body: Our dog is a senior dog who struggles to gain footing on our hardwood floors. When I put his Urban Walkers on, I see his personality change! He brightens up and happily trots across the floor. He seems to know the boots help him gain traction. We've tried three (maybe four) different styles of boots on him before we found the Urban Walkers. Each of the previous boots had a design flaw -- either they flipped around on his paws, slipped off, or wore out quickly. Urban Walkers are thoughtfully designed, with a sticky surface inside each boot to prevent it from flipping around on the dog's paw, vented material that "breathes," and a cleverly designed Velcro wrap that accommodates the dew claw and wraps diagonally around the paw to keep the boot secure while spreading the pressure across the top of the paw rather than tightly around one part of it. I don't have to worry that they're fastened too tightly, possibly cutting off circulation. It's obvious the designer of these boots really thought the details through and tested them. In my experience, that's rare with many pet products like this. I liked them so much, I bought another set as a spare. I highly recommend these  boots.

product_title: Outward Hound Kyjen  Dog Backpack
review_body: I purchased this dog backpack primarily because I have been reading about how backpacks are worth a try for behavior issues and exercise purposes. My dog has energy for days, and I get tired out on our walks way before he ever would. I started walking him with just the harness part, then added the backpack, then added very light weights (tuna can on each side), and now a small bottle of water on each side. While I haven't noticed as big of an improvement as I've read from some other reviews, I think it does help a little, and seems to calm him down a bit on walks. As for the bag itself, I think it is really good quality and better than I expected it to be. I have the size small, and the side pouches have tons of room. It's a two part deal, there's a harness that fits over the dog that is very adjustable and seems to fit comfortably, and the backpack velcros over top of the harness, which makes removing the bag very quick without having to take the whole thing off. There is no real place to attach a leash, but I added a small carabiner clip to the "handle" and his leash attaches just fine to that. It is nice to be able to pack some water, the matching collapsible travel dish, some treats, and some baggies with easily. It is a nice looking pack as well, and very reasonable in price. The only real con I have found is that the pack tends to slide to one side of my dog while he is walking (with or without a leash attached), not slide on the velcro but the whole harness gets off center, even though it is adjusted as best as it can be. Other than that minor issue, I am pleased with this pack, and my picky dog doesn't mind it either and it didn't take much time to get him used to it.

product_title: MisterMax Anti Icky Poo Odor Remover (1) Pint
review_body:
I never write reviews. I am of the belief that if a product works as advertised, it should. And if a product doesn't perform, I just don't buy it again and tell my friends how much it sucks. I was compelled to provide a quick review of Anti Icky Poo because of how great it really works.

My dog is getting up there in age, and randomly peed in our basement one day. After basic cleanup, we assumed this was a purely isolated incident, and chalked it up to her old age. Of course, she took to her own scent, and started a trend. After a handful of deposits, we stopped letting her in the basement, and it seemed to solve the problem.

After a short bit of time, we started to experience what was the worst smell we had ever experienced. Obviously, we cleaned all of the soiled areas thoroughly, and repeated as needed. Yet, the stench of old dog piss remained. Finally, we paid the $50 to rent a carpet cleaner, and thought this would end our woes.

Two days later, the stank returned, and we started to consider replacing our carpet. At this point, each "incident" had been spot treated with a trusted carpet cleaner as soon as the piss was discovered. Also, we vacuumed the entire basement, and re-treated the problem areas multiple times. Still, the foul odor remained, and was still very noticeable.

Finally, I decided to do a bit of research online, and found Anti Icky Poo. Even though I thought it had a really stupid name, I decided to give it a try. I ordered the pint bottle, and it arrived 2 days later. I quickly sprayed the product all over our previously soiled areas, using half the bottle, and let it sit. At first, it had a fruity, sweet smell to it, but I figured it would be better than the stank dog piss. The next day, I repeated the application, using the remainder of the bottle (over about 20 sq. feet?). I never had to remove, or lift up any of the carpet to expose the pad or the subfloor. The next day, after everything had dried, the sweet smell of the product had passed, AND SO DID THE PISS SMELL. I thought it was too good to be true.

I has been 3 weeks now, and the basement has no lingering odor of ANYTHING. IT SMELLS JUST LIKE IT DID WHEN WE MOVED IN. We are supremely pleased with this product, and would recommend it to anyone who is suffering from stank ass pee smells in their carpets. BUY THIS STUFF, you wont regret it.

Received the item, exterior looked as advertised. From the outside, it was exactly what I wanted. Fountain like in appearance, large reservoir with pumped water, backlit, etc.

Opened it up and it smelled like an auto body shop. I washed it under hot water and Dawn for about an hour but the smell didnt come out, only flakes of spray paint and particulate resin and fiberglass. Not a snowballs chance in hell this was going down in front of my dogs. My gut feel-o-meter was off the charts, so I had to box it back up and send it back. This led to a considerable search for knowledge, and ultimately led me to FAQs for Glacier Point for Cats.

For what its worth, I haven't purchased the Glacier Point product either. Instead, I made it a point to not be a lazy bum and now I change out my dogs water frequently.

To end, this fountain looks great and would be a nice conversation piece, but I can't recommend it for consumption, which helped bump it up from 1 star to 2 stars.

product_title: 1 Giant Golden Sulawesi Rabbit Snail (Tylomelania sp. - 1 to 3 inches long) from Indonesia- VERY seldom available! by Aquatic Arts
review_body: EDITED 10/2015- I've learned a lot about rabbit snails since I bought this one for my community tank so I thought I would share. They require a higher PH than most other snails. If the PH is below 7.8 their shells will start eroding. The one I received had very serious erosion on her shell. I've been supplementing with calcium and it hasn't gotten much worse. They like water temperatures between 80-84. They love to munch on cooked carrots, peas and zucchini. There is a great website with tons of info on these guys rabbitsnails.com. Also I do not recommend keeping them with mystery snails. My male mystery snail was constantly looking for loving from my rabbit snail and it wore her down. When I separated them she was much more active. I've gotten 11 babies from this one female I ordered (which is pretty amazing considering I don't have a male in the tank)!   I was really excited to get this snail and she is cool looking but doesn't look nearly as cool as the one pictured. She's more of a dull yellowish gray on her body and half her shell is covered in white. As far as being part of the clean up crew I rarely see her move. I've seen her on the glass once but mostly she just buries herself in the gravel. I'm saying she because the coolest part about her was about a week after we got her I noticed a little baby version of her cruising around. I'm assuming she had a baby. Hopefully junior will be a little more active and she is just recovering from "child birth";-)

review_headline: Just in time for shedding season!
review_body:
(Full disclosure: I received a free product in exchange for an honest review. This review is for the PINK PET BRUSH, not the Blue Grooming Tool Set.)

I have five rescue dogs and also foster, so I’ve owned my share of grooming supplies over the years. Since my dogs are all short- to medium-haired (rat terrier/fox terrier/Jack Russell terrier mixes), I usually stick to combs over brushes (shaking some of the loose fur off with my hands before I start); this is my first time using a “rake.” In fact, prior to writing this review, I’d never heard of a Furminator, but the Flatworld® Rake looks to be a more affordable version of it.

The first thing I noticed about the rake is how short the teeth are – less than half as long as those on my current comb. Thus, the brush fills with hair much more quickly, necessitating in more frequent stops. (Not a big deal, unless your dog hates to be brushed and tries to use the distraction for escape. Jayne, I’m looking at you!) However, the rake does an excellent job of gathering shed and loose hair. All in all, it seems to remove a greater volume of fur than a traditional comb.

I even noticed an improvement on Mags and Finnick, who have very short hair and don’t shed a whole lot. Whereas I brush the other dogs once or twice a week (even more during peak shedding season), I usually skip those two altogether; there just doesn’t seem to be a point, unless they’re obviously dirty or have gotten something stuck on their fur. So imagine my surprise when I tested the Flatworld rake on Mags and actually came away with a small hairball! (For her part, Mags was less than amused.)

I’ll probably work the Flatworld rake into my regular routine going forward, perhaps starting with it and ending with a comb. The design isn’t terribly flashy and the package is written in broken English, but my dogs don’t care and neither do I. The package seems to indicate that it comes in different sizes (50, 66, and 100mm), but I can’t seem to find any others online.sizes (50, 66, and 100mm), but I can’t seem to find any others online.

review_headline: Just, Eh. Worked for Awhile. Cheap Plastic.
review_body: First, product quality. Cheap plastic. It took me quite awhile to get the top "locked" into place, because everything was crooked. The plastic was cheap and flimsy. Once it was in place, albeit crooked, it did work. I filled it with Precious Cat litter to start (when I ran out I switched to Tidy Cat Instant Action and both worked great) and waited for my cat to use it. I didn't have a large area to roll it, so I had to roll, drag, and complete the roll onto it's top and then roll back. The clumps all went in the little scoop as promised. Perfect! This worked quite well for the first few two weeks (as well as the Cat Genie to put them in) and then the scoop started to not only fill with clumps, but whatever space was left, with litter. A lot of litter got wasted, because there was no way I was going to try and "filter" it. I bought so I wouldn't have to scoop it like a regular cat box and touch anything, hence I also bought the Cat Genie!  I never had a problem with the inside/walls getting dirty, but I only had one cat and he tended to go in the same spot and I cleaned it daily and never let it go more than two days. After a few weeks I did notice small clumps of waste in the litter itself that would go into the sifter and then come back out, at this point it was probably time to dump the litter and put in fresh entirely, but as I was away from home on business for two months, this wasn't really an option for me. I was lucky to find a place I could even take/keep my cat! There was absolutely no lingering smell (except directly after his highness would have a blowout) from the litter box, even if I let it go 48 hours. Beware, they will kick litter out of that open door everywhere! Keep a broom handy, you will need it. By the end of the two months I could see this litter box was wearing out and decided to just donate it to a local shelter than trying to ship it home. They can use it as it is, as a regular box, or simply recycle the plastic. If you need a quick, cheap solution for a few months, buy it, otherwise, don't expect to use it long term. review_headline: Would be decent if it didn't separate in the tube and get all over everything....
review_body:
This is good stuff but the production is bit sketchy. First off the positive stuff.

1) Our cat LOVES the stuff and eats it up.
2) It does help with hairballs but the result is that our cat ends up puking them up every few weeks. After that, he seems much happier so anything that helps the problem move along is okay by us.

Now for the problem:
By the time the tube gets about 40% used up the contents seems to separate and when you squeeze it, you get this nasty oil that spurts out and gets all over everything. It's gross and makes using the solution very messy and dramatically more of a hassle.

I find i throw it away by the time it gets about half full because the problem is just too messy to be effective. It's a planned product defect to get us to buy more, it's a bit lame. If it's something else, they should really work on it. I had thought it was either just me or just a bad batch but we have ordered this several times and every tube and every user in our household has had the same experience.

review_headline: Why all the hate. Works great for me.
review_body:
I would recommend this product. I purchased it a few weeks ago because my Yorkie needed to be fed 4 times per day for regulating his gastroenteritis. Coming home from work at lunch was not very efficient. We got this an have no complaints for the operation. I put the time on military time so that it is easier to understand the exact hours that he is being fed and haven't messed with it since. He is now fed every 4 hours from 8am to 8pm.

I can understand that if you have a very motivated cat or dog, that they can get into the other compartments since it is simple plastic pegs that attach the cover to the base. My dog is pretty well behaved and smart and hasn't tried to get at the other food compartments. I have a feeling that if I put chicken in there he might, but I wouldn't leave chicken in there all day. Although there is an ice reservoir, I only used it the first couple days, and then figured that it isn't worth the cleanup of the melted ice.

If given the chance again, I would buy it. I really like it and it has made feeding our dog the right amount of food at the right time much easier. Now if I can one get one for humans so i can eat at regular times too.

review_body: I've been using this product for about 3 years now and i'm about to purchase for the first time from amazon, i usually get it from my local feed store (sorry local feed store, prime is so convenient!). First, I give 4 stars because I don't feel that any spot treat repellent is a bug management system alone, i rely on a good fly spray weekly as well. So, this isn't a strike against freedom 45, just spot treat repellents in general. I rely on freedom 45 for their week long pasture time and supplement with a good fly spray for when i trail ride on the weekends. Southern Michigan, horse flys, deer flys, mosquitos and goodness know what else in a warm wet spell. This keeps the ticks off! I probably apply once a month, when tick season is especially heavy. I do believe this helps with the flys - I apply freedom 45 in dots along the spine and below their 'knees' on all fours but I also apply by hand to groin areas where i otherwise feel many fly bites as well as by hand to the ears, trying to rub some into the interiors. i apply to the top of their eyes, being careful that it doesn't drip into. my mare gets many bites on her chest at the base of her neck so i apply by hand there. each of my animals seems to have a 'special' place where they get attention from the biter bugs so by hand, i treat it. These special area spot treatments seems to minimize the bug bite bumps so I assume this is keeping other biting insects at bay. my horses love to see me coming with the bug treatments, they know i will give them some relief!!

review_headline: A truck full of cream-sickles exploded in your home.
review_body: It's hard to expound much beyond the reviews already here. We can offer some insight into it's 'other' applications, however.  Our Resort features oversized condominium-styled Villas and keeping them smelling and looking clean is a hefty task. They feature full kitchens and multiple full-baths so there are plenty of places for odors to accumulate and hide. The extensive furnishing and deep carpet also prove to be especially adept at absorbing the unique and changing smells of our perpetual Guest flow.  From the overzealous perfumer, to the bacon-grease-left-on-the-counter-all-weekend Guest, this eliminator is incredible at destroying the smell and putting the Villa atmosphere back to neutral.  We most especially like that it doesn't remotely smell like a chemical. It simply exudes the aroma of 3,000 oranges; as if a truck full of cream sickles exploded in your home. It is fairly strong, and as folks have already said, a little goes a long way. 4 misted-puffs into the air of a 2,000sqft Villa can overpower the sinuses for up to an hour after the spray, but eventually fades and creates what's best described as a 'nothing'. Which is precisely what we want!  We have never used the product directly on a surface; instead we put our sprayers on the tightest setting and fumigate the atmosphere.  We can highly recommend this product. And may even suggest you can actually get more than 4- 32oz bottles out of the concentrate, because the solution could be diluted substantially and still pack a punch. Of course, we are using it differently, where we are aerosolizing the spray straight into the air. Perhaps the dilution recommendations are ideal for surfaces.  Don't ever spend another dime on the expensive, worthless and fleeting air fresheners for anything. Use this instead!

She wasn't overweight, but these other issues got me worrying, so I started looking into natural diets for cats and was recommended this by a local PetCo employee. The price initially made me reluctant but I've tried more expensive foods recommended by the Veterinarian that didn't solve her problems, so I figured why not.

I weened her off by having a few pellets of the old food on top of this for about a week. Now she's 100% eating this.

In roughly a month since the switch, her hair has started to clear of the matted fur naturally (but I'm also assisting in removing these by pulling them off when they've become loose enough - as I always have), she's drinking more water, her coat is softer, cleaner, shinier, and overall healthier, and her recurring UTIs have cleared. Her demeanor has actually improved and she's become more friendly and less recluse. I'll continue feeding her this premium food until otherwise.

product_title: Penn-Plax Hamster House - Medium
review_headline: Gerbils Like it But it Won't Last Long
review_body:
It arrived very quickly and was packaged well to protect against breakage. It's almost blanched wood - not sure if this is pine but even so it's very pale. I failed shop class and drafting but the measurements of the medium size using a tape measure are: height roughly 4", length across the back and front is nearly 6 1/2", front to back it's about 5". You can easily fit two adult gerbs inside. Maybe even three.

The only issue for us is that the material is extremely thin. If you've had small animals for awhile now and have been buying this product for years you'll be shocked at how thin the wood is. Having owned gerbs for decades, there's a serious decline in both safe and interesting chew toys. We don't buy plastic (PVC's), try to avoid products from China (eek), and are concerned about pesticides and insects that may inhabit bark toys.

A lot of people complain that with these types of safe wood toys the urine stains are gross. That's fine. I'd rather my babies live long lives by avoiding plastic. But, just as you can wash a wood cutting board in your kitchen, you can wash a wood toy using non-toxic soap. A lot of dish soap has ammonia and bleach is toxic so rinse with safe dish soap and dry thoroughly. Sanding the stains down is another option. I do not recommend and wont purchase again. It's just too thin.

product_title: Nekton S Multi-Vitamin for Birds, 375gm
review_headline: I started my bird on Nekton about one month before he usually molts and I was very pleased with the results
review_body:
My cockatiel bird would lose all of the feathers on his chest and in other spots every winter when he molts. I did research on a few websites for caged birds and an aviarian stated that the mistake bird owners make is not knowing to purchase vitamins that also have amino acids and trace minerals in them along with regular vitamins.

This product has everything in it as one. I started my bird on Nekton about one month before he usually molts and I was very pleased with the results. He didn't lose nearly as many feathers on his chest or other areas of his body, and he was less cranky during his molting.
I have used Nekton daily for about 3 yrs. During molting, I add just a little bit more powder to his daily water and when molting is done, I go back to normal dose.

The powder will leave a residue in the water, which I do not want my bird to drink. To fix this problem, I get out an extra bowl and press two paper towels down into it, pour the mixture over the paper towels, raise the papers out of the bowl and then pour the mixture into the bowl that fits in the bird cage. It's a very simple process and my bird gets to drink granual free water.

review_body: I wasn't expecting a whole lot when we bought this, but we were pleasantly surprised by the quality and ease of this travel kennel. It also has a top opening too so if you have smaller dogs you can just reach in through the top to take them out/put them in and/or place food, water, toys, etc into the kennel. Overall I am VERY satisfied with this kennel and it was well worth the price. It was also shipped quickly, although it is not in a cardboard box and just open to view and the box was a little damaged when we received it but the product was not. I've already got family members with dogs asking about where to buy it for themselves. We'll see how it lasts durability-wise and how it stands up to heavy/frequent usage, but so far things are looking good.

product_title: Dog Leash - Pet Supplies for Dogs Leashes - Dog Leash 2 Handles - 1 Leash 2 Handles - Dog Training Leash - Extra Strong Large Dogs
review_headline: If you want some more range without using the retractor type, this is your huckleberry.
review_body:
This leash is as advertised. Has two handles (both padded) and is extra long. Its exactly what I wanted. I do have two small knocks on it however.

1) The leash material is a little thinner than I am used to, and its more stiff/tough. I'm sure it allows it to be as strong as others without being as thick. The issue for me is, I don't trust the stitching where the handle wrap re-attaches (not on this, but just in general), so when I wrap a loop of leash around my hand, its strong sharp enough to be very uncomfortable. My 4' and 6' leashes I've got at pet stores previously never did this. That's probably a "me" thing, since it has to do with trusting the stitching. Probably not an issue for most folks.

2) Of bigger complain to me was that the black in the leash is still coming off in my hand after repeated use. First time... ok, maybe. Days later? I'm annoyed by that. And its hard to get off your hands - soap doesn't do it, you have to scrub with a brillo pad. May be related to me wrapping the leash around my hand - but I think its actually the soft part. I bought the black one, may not apply to other colors.

Those two aside, to get a 8' leash is awesome. This lets my pooch have a little more range (but allows me to keep her short when I need with the 2nd handle). Pooch loves it. She's getting to explore new ground on our route that she's previously not been able to cover.

product_title: Current USA 18"-24" Satellite Plus PRO LED Light
review_headline: high light and customizable, wonderful fixture!
review_body:
This light has gone beyond exceeding my expectations. As you may well know, choosing a light fixture for a planted aquarium is an extremely arduous task. There's a multitude of opinions, varied reports on PAR ratings, and the list goes on.

I chose this light for my high tech 40 breeder. The light is phenomenal! My e. Belem immediately began to pearl within thirty minutes of swapping the fixture out. My rotala enie is vibrant and bursting with new nodes. My ludwigia repens is thriving. My rotala green is lush and vivid.

Coverage from front to back is exceptional, even on a tank with a depth of 18". This fixture will provide you with medium to high light without issue. It all depends on the height of your tank. On anything 15" or less, high light is a given and you will be able to grow that carpet of HC you've been wanting to(assuming other parameters are in check)

The dynamic effects are cool, though not too practical. I very much enjoy the 24 hour timer. My show tank is in my bedroom, and the gradual ramp up is very pleasant should I be sleeping in. Rather than the lights coming on full strength, it gradually ramps up over 15 minutes. Same thing when shutting down to moonlight, except it ramps down. Very pleasant.

The colors are infinitely adjustable, and you can certainly achieve a variety of looks to suit your personal needs. The instructions are clear and simple.

A wonderful product, worlds ahead of the standard Satellite+. I'm quite happy I opted for this light as opposed to two finnex fixtures.

product_title: Dog Dazer II Ultrasonic Dog Deterrent
review_headline: twenty five pounder) because something that even approached the idea of looking or sounding like an animal appeared on the tv
review_body:
Two puggles - both very healthy - argue about the effectiveness of this one. Both bark excessively, for different reasons. One (five year old, twenty five pounder) because something that even approached the idea of looking or sounding like an animal appeared on the tv. The other (one year old, thirty pounder) because he is super friendly and has to bark his introduction in an attempt to meet all the dogs, everywhere, preferably all at once. If he can't he's certainly going to bark at them until their owners run away in fear.

On the first? I might as well buy earplugs. He has less than zero cares to spare for this thing. He turns back to me and sings the song of his people while this is on. Obviously, this is merely a tuner for him.

The other? Worked like a charm. He now stops and looks back at me to be sure he has permission to meet another dog, rather than tugging and pulling and choking himself while scaring other dogs and owners.

Neither of them get freaked out by it, but neither of them are really calm dogs to begin with (one is super anxious. The other is picking up on that and starting to become so, despite my best efforts to assure him I'm only taking out the trash and I most certainly will return in time for him to eat. I am not, in fact, leaving them alone, forever).

If you've got similarly minded dogs, this could work for you. If they're smaller than thirty pounds, I'd be hesitant.

This was worth it for me, since it's 50% quieter now. I'd five star this in a heartbeat if they'd both hush.

review_headline: I purchased this probiotic with the goal of helping my ...
review_body: I purchased this probiotic with the goal of helping my nearly 14 yr old beagle have an easier time going potty. The probiotics seemed to help her and make things easier outside however there is one thing I need to note that brings up the safety of the product. Shelly has had fatty tumors develop all over her body over the last 4 years. In January I switched her to an organic dog food and I was surprised to see after two weeks many had significantly shrunken and softened for the first time ever (YAY!) She had been on the organic food for a couple of months before I tried the probiotic and her tumors/lumps had been continuing to shrink or lie dormant. I kept watching her for any changes in her condition, after starting the probiotic, and I began to see them rapidly grow after a couple of weeks on this probiotic. This brings me to question where they derived the enzymes from or what could be in this product to promote rapid lipoma growth? The growing stopped and inflammation of some skin tags and fatty tumors went down shortly after stopping the probiotic. If you have a sick dog that may have any cancer or tumors or anything, I would not buy this product because I believe it aided in the growth of the fatty tumors my dog suffers with.

product_title: SunSun-China HW-304B 5-Stage External Canister Filter with 9-watt UV Sterilizer, 525 GPH
review_headline: Incredible value from a huge aquatic company
review_body:
Overall a really good canister filter, with a welcome UV light to help control algae. Algae is the number 1 enemy of fish enthusiasts. Anything that can help control it is worth it. The filter itself is ultra quiet, you have a hard time hearing it. When you first start it up, you will notice it burps a lot. This is caused by all the dead air being misplaced by water. This dead air can be minimized by filling the filter with water prior to starting it up. One thing that will blow you away, is just how much water this filter displaces after all the water is equalized. The tank went down a good inch! NO kidding! I opted to buy the filter with the media, you will get bio balls, boney looking things which help grow beneficial bacteria, felt pads, and carbon media. Most of the media is enclosed in mesh bags, so the mess factor is minimized. Setup is really easy, you just stack one on top of the other. You want to start with the bio balls on the bottom, then the bones, then the carbon. So largest to smallest. The blue felt pad goes on the top. If you get the filter with the media, use the felt pads that come with it, they are bigger and more dense. I'm sure they trap more micro particulate matter.
So far so good, no leaks. I might suggest using some KY jelly to help get the hoses on the fittings, they seem to be really tight and hard to get on. Check for kinks and leaks. You should have no leaks is you connect everything right.
As one other reviewer stated, don't hesitate on buying this filter based on not knowing the maker of it. I did a bit of research and found that sunsun is a enormous aquatic company. They are on par with say Marineland in the USA. Perhaps even bigger. Check them out yourself, I think you will be blown away by how much they actually make. This filter is great value compared to other stuff on the market, less than half the cost of what's in the pet stores. I am including a before and after photo with just 24 hours filtering. Also a picture ofthe filter itself in use.
Bottom line is, if you use the right media the water will get crystal clear. Once you start using the sunsun you won't go back to hang over the tank type.

review_headline: Beautiful, but not an adequate home for Betta Fish.
review_body:
Bettas are tolerant fish, but they need more care & a better environment than most people realize.
They are curious fish that enjoy exploring and people watching. I'm surprised as to the difference in personalities that they have. Heck, I'm surprised they have any kind of personalities at all!
I bought this tank on Amazon, but asked my local fish store about it prior to setting it up. They said that since it's a filtered setup that it should be okay for 3 fish, but to start with 1, and go from there.
That's exactly what I did. I set up the tank with Seachem Matrix filling the pump chamber about a quarter of the way, then took a half of an AquaClear 110 Foam Insert and let that fill the rest of the pump chamber, put a heater in the base of the tank & let it cycle for a couple of days.
When I bought my 1st betta, a Female Dragonscale Crowntail, I put her in the center chamber. Immediately I could tell she was NOT enjoying the water flow. I double checked that the pump was as low as it could go, which it was. So I got creative with silk plants to try to reduce the flow and allow her to have places to be able to relax in her chamber. But even though I keep trying to adjust it, she is Not comfortable in this setup. She will pace, sometimes frantically, back and forth along the front of the tank. Oddly though, she seems to enjoy flitting back and forth along the out flow on the right side. I catch her doing it often enough that I'm sure it's not just an accident that she gets caught in the flow. I truly think she enjoys this activity. Sometimes she sticks her little face up in there for a little bit too.
A week later I bought a Male Black Orchid Crowntail, and put him in the 3rd chamber. He seems to do okay, but he doesn't like having to twitch his fins off of the plants when he turns around. It'll work for him for a while, but he definitely needs more room to roam.
Then I noticed that, even though the left sides of these chambers are frosted THE FISH DO SEE EACH OTHER WELL ENOUGH THAT THEY WILL FLAIR. This is not okay in the long run.
I am going to have to get different tanks for my 2 Bettas. That's all there is to it. In the meanwhile I covered the right side of the center chamber with post-its covered in packing tape so that they won't get overly stressed while I get a 5 gallon cycled for my little girl.
I'm considering turning this into an aquatic planter and maybe put a couple of shrimp & possibly an African Dwarf Frog so that it won't just be a waste of money. It really is a beautiful tank, and I enjoy the sound of the water falling into the base of the tank, but it is NOT a good setup for Betta fish.ELL ENOUGH THAT THEY WILL FLAIR. product_title: Taste of the Wild, Canine Formula
review_headline: Significantly Improved, but Didn't Cure Allergy Problems
review_body:
My dog has horrible allergies. She constantly has yeast infections in her ears, urinary tract infections, and hot spots. We've tried everything: different foods, different shampoos, sprays, oils, etc. We tried this food because it doesn't have grain, corn, beef, chicken, lamb, and we weren't sure exactly what she is allergic to.

While on this diet, she did not get any ear infections or urinary tract infections (which she had perpetually before, just one after the other). She's had high energy levels, loved the food (but she'll eat anything), takes regular poops, and her coat is looking really nice and shiny. So the food seems to have helped tremendously with most of her issues, though not all of them. Her skin is still itchy, though it hasn't progressed to hot spots yet. She likely has grass or other external allergies that no food will cure.

I think people searching for a food that will work for a dog who is allergic to literally everything may find some success with this food, like we did. It seems with severe allergies, there is no magic cure, so you have to just take what you can get. And for the price, you really can't beat it.

One of my cats will eat anything but the other two are fairly picky about what they eat so I thought I'd give this a try and see what happened. They seem to love it. product_title: Pro Plan Focus Sensitive Skin & Stomach Lamb & Rice Adult Cat Food
review_body:
My cat had been vomiting almost every day for the last six months, and had terrible itchy red bumps all over her skin. They bothered her so much she was literally ripping her coat out in chunks. My vet said she was allergic to fleas, but I haven't found a flea on her or anywhere in my home since last summer, so I was skeptical. He offered no tips on how to alleviate her obvious discomfort; basically just told me to live with it. I was heartbroken for her, and I tried everything I could think of to soothe her skin and get her to stop itching, but it just got worse and worse. I was afraid I was going to have to eventually have her put down; I just didn't see how she could go on living when she was so miserable.

I decided to start switching up her food to see if anything helped. I went through three or four different brands with no luck; I even tried giving her fish oil, apple cider vinegar, and olive oil. But within a week of trying this product, the vomiting dropped off significantly and her skin started to noticeably clear up. She has now been on the Pro Plan for almost six weeks, her itchy bumps are completely gone, and she hasn't thrown up in weeks! Her coat is nearly grown back, and softer and shinier than I have ever seen it. She's also more playful than she was even before she got sick. She even tries to wrestle around with my dog, and that NEVER happened before!

I can't believe how quickly she improved; I wish I'd found this months ago! I'm so grateful for this product!

product_title: Chef Michael's Grilled Sirloin Steak Flavor Dog Food 11.5 lb. Bag
review_body:
As a rule, food like this is marketed more for the owners than the dog. The colors and textures are supposed to approximate meat with potatoes and vegetables. And it does that adequately.

But my dogs don't really care about looks. They seem to worry about texture and I've seen them turn up their nose at certain foods. This is not one of them though.

To be sure, it's not the same as that whole-food-no-grains-made-by-midwestern-virgins style food. The ingredients list does show pearled barley, brewers rice, soy protein, and various other things. And yes, those other things include some colorings. So if that's a dealbreaker for you in any amount, look elsewhere.

For me I haven't had any problems giving this to my dogs They seemed to enjoy it. The bag itself is sealed and the food has more moisture than typical dry dog food. So while it's not gourmet, I don't think it's on a par with some of the REALLY horrible stuff out there. It's a decent food.

product_title: Ruffwear Climate Changer Fleece Jacket
review_headline: Required sewing modifications for male and arm rubbing
review_body:
I think this is a really cute, well constructed jacket for my aging male fine-boned fine-haired dog, BUT I needed to sew modifications.
First, I pinched small pleats in the fabric covering the abdomen and sewed them together at the center. This prevented my dog from soaking the underside when he urinated. I was pleased with this easy solution to the first problem.
Then, I noticed the upper part of his arm, in front of the elbow, was being rubbed raw as he stretched his leg forward during movement. I hoped that his skin would adapt to the friction. His skin did adjust after a few weeks, but he lost the hair on his upper arm. To decrease the rubbing I cut a slit in the front of each arm hole. I sewed a seam around the edge and sewed a tack at the top of the V to strengthen it and prevent tearing of the fabric. This has stopped the rubbing and my dog's hair is growing back on his upper leg. I am less pleased with this fix because it is noticeable.
I recommend this jacket for a female dog with coarse fur that will protect her upper leg. I will not purchase a second Climate Changer jacket for my current dog.

product_title: Standard Process Canine Adrenal Support 100 grams
review_headline: Worst instructions ever--main ingredient is liver
review_body:
Like many self-righteous merchants these days, they print in BIG letters that 'minimizing impact the planet...is a core value' but then print the directions and ingredients in what looks like tiny, tiny 4 point type on a box big enough for 12 or 14 point type. The also do not tell you the size of the scoop that comes with it. Instead they say serving size 1/2 tsp., when the rest of the label describes 6 serving sizes, all in tiny 4 point type.

Thinking that the tiny 4 point type was designed for dogs with really good eyesight, I asked my dog to read the instructions, but she was not able to make them out any better that I was.

When I finally took out a powerful magnifying glass to read the directions and ingredients, I saw to my surprise that the first one listed is bovine liver, which means there is more liver than anything else. Now I am not a doctor, but I do know that the adrenal glands are not on or in the liver. AFAIK dogs do not suffer from a shrunken liver and need supplemental liver, nor does the liver affect the adrenal glands, which are on top of the kidneys. But I may be wrong--who knows?

review_headline: New Formula doesn't hold up to Old Reputation
review_body:
This stuff sucks. If I could give it a zero, I would. We bought this to clean up the messes of our new Labrador Retriever puppy. Firstly, the shipping was terrible. The large bottle came wrapped in a clear plastic bag and closed with a twist-tie, and it was just stuffed inside of a cardboard box. When it arrived at our door, the box was visibly wet and torn from where the cardboard had become soggy, and it looked like UPS tried to fix it with some duct tape, but it still had a hole in the box.

Moreover, this stuff doesn't even work. I have tried every method of using it and it doesn't seem to get rid of the smell of pet urine. I sop up the urine with a towel, spray a heavy layer of this product and even let it soak for a good 15 minutes but no matter what once it dries the odor still lingers. It seems to spread the stains around more than "eliminate" them. I wish we hadn't bought such a large amount, because now I feel wasteful dumping it out. I will be looking into getting a different product. It's not fair to amazon purchasers that this new formula is still listed under the same product name and reputation. Look somewhere else for your pet cleaning products.

review_headline: Sarah is doing OK, I have high hopes, only been 3 weeks.
review_body: I started using the Citykitty with my 6 month old rescue kitten.  She did very well for the 1st  few weeks.  No accidents until the final 2 rings were left. I decided to return to the beginning(replacement ring) for a few days and all was well. No problem.  Then I removed 2 rings of the replacement, going back to just before her 1st accident.  She would pee in the toilet and do her business on the floor. I had her watch me clean it up and I piled the kitty litter in the rings.  She is rather regular and does her business about midnight every night so I waited until I knew it was about time and just camped out in the bathroom with her. She peed just fine, and I knew she wanted to do her business and she started to go to the same spot on the floor and I just picked her up then put even more kitty litter on the rings, she got it and did her business on the rings.  I am so proud of her.  Now she knows what I want.  I will slow down on the removal of the final rings as I read others have done and only remove a 1/2 a ring at a time. I am so looking forward to no bathroom messes, kitty litter or otherwise. I forgot to say, cleaning the citykitty tray is a bit easier now that I use the emptycardboard toilet paper rolls.  They work quite well in scraping the kitty litter from the rings and I just toss them in the garbage afterwards.

product_title: PetSafe Simply Clean Self-Cleaning Cat Litter Box, Automatic, Works with Clumping Cat Litter
review_headline: Best Thing I Ever Bought As A Pet Owner
review_body:
This litter box has made such a huge difference in my tiny one bedroom apartment. I have two cats and getting a good electric litter box has been a problem from day 1. Call me lazy, but I didn't want to scoop every day, which is necessary with traditional litter box in the aforementioned tiny apartment. (Having one extra meticulous cat who will pee just outside of it if it's even remotely dirty doesn't help). I've been through two Litter Maids and they both had performance issues. I'd still have to scoop about twice a week and changing out the trays was a hassle - and expensive.

I'd done some research and ultimately decided to go with this one. Most of the negative reviews were about mechanical issues. It has a one year warranty, so if it did what I wanted it to, I felt it would be worth buying a new one in a year if it broke outside of warranty. My other concern was that it wouldn't fit inside the litter box furniture I have. I have the Merry Products Cat Washroom Bench, which is meant to fit most traditional rake electronic litter boxes, and it fits perfectly.

As for performance, it's been amazing. A little noisy, but not enough to be a real nuisance. I empty the bin once weekly and that's it. It takes maybe a minute or two. Couldn't be easier. I line the bin with a plastic bag so I don't have to clean it regularly. It took me about two months to completely change out the litter, and I probably didn't need to (I have a boyfriend who's "allergic" to cat urine, so if it smelled, he wouldn't hesitate to tell me). I started using Ever Clean premium litter and it worked really well. Since I changed out the litter, I used Arm and Hammer, and it doesn't seem to clump as well, so I'll be switching back.

Not having to constantly worry about the litter box has made having cats so much more enjoyable (Fun fact: litter issues are the number one reason cats are returned to shelters.). I'd definitely recommend the Simply Clean Continuous-Clean litter box to anyone anyone looking for a hassle-free litter solution.

He howls, whimpers, and barks whenever we go out (problematic with neighbors) and started ignoring even his kong. He's never done this before, although he is very much a people dog. We started working with a behavioralist who diagnosed him with mild separation anxiety (doesn't seem mild to us considering we haven't been able to leave him alone for more than 1/2hr in months - but I get that he isn't destroying our home or anything in our absence so clinically mild) and she recommended Virbac. We did it for a full 7 weeks and he did not improve at all. We had high hopes because of how helpful Composure was but, for us, it was a no go. I don't necessarily blame the meds - I think it depends on the problem and it's severity. We had friends for whom Composure did nothing, while it was revolutionary for us with his problems last year. We've since moved on to Clomicalm which we are only in the second week of and are continuing our behavioral training. There has been an incremental improvement thus far but it can take 6 weeks to 2 months so we'll see. As for Virbac, I think it's worth the try. Our dog has a unique problem where he doesn't get upset until he finishes eating what's in his kong and frankly I think he just needs more significant help right now than Virbac can provide. It has been a really tough series of moves for him. The vet says he's had as much success with this as with prescription meds, just depends on the issue. Good luck to all!

review_headline: If You Own a Puppy, This is a Savior!
review_body:
We bought the 30 x 30 exercise pen for our German Shepherd puppy. He is now 16 weeks old and as with most puppies, wants to wander everywhere and get into things that he shouldn't. We didn't buy this at first thinking we would do fine without it, and eventually gave in. I would never try to raise a puppy without a pen like this again. We don't specifically use it as a pen like the picture portrays, but more so use it to keep our pup in a specific section of the house that we "puppy proofed". Keep in mind that we have been thoroughly training our pup so he doesn't jump on the pen or try to get out. He is more than capable of pushing the pen over if it's not linked together as a pen. Although our GSD is well trained, without this pen our dog will wander, with it, he stays where we want him. The pen is built well and has a nice finish to it. The welding has been done right with very few sharp edges for the puppy to cut themselves on. We are very happy with this product.

Update: 05/26/2016

We found this pen so useful that we bought a second one. We still use it even though our GSD is 1 1/2 years old. We don't use it exactly the same way as we did when he was a puppy since he can be trusted pretty much everywhere now. But there is one area he will not leave alone and that includes the cat domain in the basement. This this is where the cat food and the worst doggie "snack" of all, cat litter, is found. So we use this pen to surround the cat area allowing them to get in, and the dog to be stuck out. The second one was used to surround the Christmas tree. Our pups first Christmas involved a large curiosity of the lights which he chewed through... on an expensive pre-wired tree. So we decided not to risk it again and protect the tree, but more importantly, the dog from shocking himself. Seriously, this pen is well worth the money and will be of use throughout the years despite the age of your dog!

product_title: Sporn Halter
review_headline: Good at first, but looses effectiveness fairly quickly.
review_body:
I was actually surprised that, at first, the Halter worked as advertised. I was fairly sceptical, even after reading the mostly glowing reviews. The clerk at the pet store recommended it and said they used it in their puppy classes, so I figured I'd give it a try.

And the very first time the pulling stopped. It was actually pleasurable to walk the dog. You could tell he wanted to pull, but every time he put his head down the straps tightened and his head came back up again. The leash was loose(ish). He would still pull when stressed, which for him was every time he passed a bin on the kerb, an open gate, or people on the street. So for easily stressed dogs, like ours, they will still pull regardless of how tight the restraints become (which makes sense, since he was chocking himself when just on a collar).

I was a bit worried about the thin straps being too fragile, or that his short fur would lead to irritation in the armpits as others have mentioned, but that hasn't been an issue. However the "Sherpa Sleeves" don't stay in the one spot and come off too easily and are a pain to put back on, making it difficult to put the halter on the dog. It's also not designed for general off-leash play as it's either too loose for running, or if you tighten it after the leash is off too tight for comfortable play. I still worry that the halter will catch his knee and trip him when he's playing, but it's too difficult to take the whole thing off and put back on when he's excited at the dog park

The collar itself is also very wide and bulky. For a small or medium-sized dog it is too big and looks uncomfortable for the dog when they're laying down. We wound up leaving on his regular collar, just loosening it so we can push it up his neck, and putting the halter's collar on underneath. Not a huge deal but it is another aspect to coordinate when fitting the halter every day.

It also isn't useful as a training tool, not even for loose-leash walking. Without the halter he went straight back to pulling. With the halter we're struggling to make any headway on sitting, staying, or heeling (including stopping yo-yoing). In fact I think we've gone backwards in many ways. The design of the halter means you cannot effectively guide the dog's body with it: there is some play in it which can give the dog the wrong idea about what you want it to do.

Now, a few weeks later, it doesn't even have the same effect on loose-leash walking. He seems to be getting used to the pressure under his arms and on his chest as the collar pulls down. It's still better than just a neck collar as it doesn't choke him when he pulls—though neither does a regular harness—but it's not nearly as effective at stopping pulling as it was originally. I still worry that his greater tolerance to the pressure will end up abrading his armpits.

For that reason I don't think the Sporn Halter is any better, and in some ways worse, than a regular harness. review_body: Now it may seem strange to "love" a flea comb, but this little gem is really easy to use and is helpful when your flea treatment is nearing the end of its effectiveness.  It has a slight curve to it, rather than being perfectly flat, which enables you to kind of slide it over your pet's skin, going with the grain of the fur, without hurting them.  I use it more on my cats than dogs, as the thin tines do not really glide through coats as dense as Rough Collies. Be sure to hold loose skin taut with one hand while combing with the other, that way you don't pinch the skin.  The fact that there is no handle makes it easy to hold in either hand. You can drown any fleas you capture in a small container of soapy water, alcohol or vinegar and water solution, or you can just squish them with your thumbnail where the tines meet the plastic (takes a little bit of dexterity).  You can also get dirt and loose hair off your pet with this comb, just work through tangled areas slowly, from the ends back toward the body until the comb slides freely. They may take a little time to get used to it, but if you're gentle, your pet should enjoy a good grooming with this comb. (Once the tines begin to show wear, you can use it on your air conditioner to straighten the cooling fins that can get bent when you clean them).

review_headline: Essential for Turtle Tank Crud Clearing
review_body:
Turtles are messy critters, especially if you feed them a varied diet with some plants. Differently, give a turtle a live feeder fish, and it's gone in seconds without a trace. However, turtles need plants in order to be healthy, despite the mess. Roughly, half of the plant they will eat, and the other half they will rip to shreds! This makes it such that turtles need a foam filter to catch the larger particles, which in this case are stirred up by the Fluval U3 water jet for easier collection via the Fluval U3 holster. Without Filter Foam Pads and a Fluval Underwater Filter, it is difficult to be vigilant to get waste particles siphoned. It is such that in my experience more waste particles will settle bottom of a tank without Fluval Underwater filtration.
What is great about these pads is that they can be washed and reused many many times. They don't need replacing every time, just cleaning. I rinse them until they come clean when I siphon/clean the tank.

product_title: Hill’s Science Diet Indoor Dry Cat Food
review_headline: A review from my cats...Subscribe and save, saves me!
review_body:
I am writing this post on behalf of my kittens.
Their names are peanut-butter and Jelly.

When the brown suited stranger leaves the monthly offering box on my humans threshold we know we have succeeded in our mission of dominance, for it has been many months since we have left our vomity offering on the cold kitchen floor to warn her of the coming doom.

Unfortunately our human still thinks they are the master and we are the pets, they display this defiant act by only bringing the box in from the stoop and placing it on the kitchen floor.
We know what is inside, we must show our human this by yowling and attempting to scratch our way into the impenetrable corrugated prison that our offering is being held.

After several failed attempts at tripping the human by pretending to be cute and circling her feet we have been understood and the box is opened... alas! the offering is presented awaiting it's official presentation!

Yet again the human is distracted by the smaller version of herself, the one she calls baby Alex... we are sure this is an attempt at cloning the human species that has not yet matured...but cannot be bothered to delve into this further. We use this to our advantage and display the fortitude of our wolverine like claws and shark like teeth to tear into the offering and display our bounty on the cold tile floor... look what we have done, what we can do...

Let this serve as a warning to you, human; we will not be made to wait, this is only a display of what we can do...keep the offerings coming on a monthly basis and we will continue to tolerate your presence in this house.

This crate is a win.

product_title: Pawz Water-Proof Dog Boot
review_headline: They stay on better than other boots we've tried, but they are not perfect
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:dc338ab0bb2c52313869a4501f8aeec7]] This is a review of the Pawz rubber dog boots, size large, for 3-4\\" paws.

We've tried several brands of dog boots that use velcro straps to hold the boot on the paw. All of them were continually falling off our dogs paw while walking and our dog seemed to be bothered by them. Someone suggested the Pawz rubber dog boots to us so we decided to give them a try. These also might be a consideration for dogs that have had surgery or injury to their paw. The Pawz boots could help prevent the dog from licking or biting the paw.

It took some time to get the hang of how to get these on our dogs paws. At first it seemed to be a 2-person operation... one person holding the dogs' paw while the other person help open the rubber boot. But eventually our dog learned to hold her paw up in the air and it was relatively simple for one person just to hold open the Pawz boot and slip it over her paw.

These are pretty secure on the dog's paw. Essentially it is like putting a balloon over your dog's paw. The top is much smaller and closes over the leg of the dog. Almost to the point of making you wonder if it could impede the circulatory system. But it is that tightness that keeps these from pulling off the paw at inopportune times.

So after a few weeks, our dog has \\"lost\\" 4 of the Pawz (they fell off at some point as she was bounding through deep snow) and 6 more of have just worn through or developed holes/tears from her toenails or stones.

They work, but are an ongoing expense as they do fall off under certain circumstances or rip through (and they do rip through quite easily.)

These are the most effective boots insofar as not falling off all the time. When we use these for taking our dog for a walk, they never fall off. It's only when we let her loose to run like the wind that the can fall off. But they tear and rip very easily.

So until something better comes along these seem to be doing a pretty good job. But the long-term costs will ultimately prove to be more expensive than buying a more expensive, but good fitting alternative boot... which we have not found. So it's a good tradeoff for the moment.g-term costs will ultimately prove to be more expensive than buying a more expensive, but good fitting alternative boot... which we have not found. product_title: FURminator deShedding Tool for Dogs
review_headline: A must have for shedding dogs! Tips/ pics
review_body:
Our papillon (long haired/ medium dog) just went through his first shed. We woke up to hair clumps everywhere and an itching dog who wouldn't stop picking at himself. My husband's allergies were horrible, and it was a huge mess we didn't around around our kids.

The regular "cheapie brush" took forever, and didn't remove a lot of hair. For three days I brushed the pup, and he continued to scratch/chew and my fingers got sore from picking out stuck brush hair. Plus, who has the time with 5 kids and full-time work?

I ordered this out of desperation, and am so glad I did. It works great!!! I am uploading a pic of the hair removed during my first use, and a pic of him so you can see his hair type. I have used it three times total and he looks great, stopped itching, and is barely shedding. The "furjector" is so much better on my hands!

Tips: Make sure the dog has no tangles because this is a fine comb that will snag easily. You have to push down harder than a normal brush to get it down near the skin. I had to get used to that and was afraid to hurt him, but he loved it (kept tapping his feet happily.) It removed so much loose hair the first time, it almost sounded like tape peeling. The hair was not breaking off, but just coming out from the shed. I wouldn't use it on long hair on tails, etc because it snags instantly and will rip out hair. I used a wide toothed cheap comb to brush that as usual (he has thick hair 6 inches long on his tail). Long strokes seem to work best, and if skin is bunched, it helps to pull it tight to remove hair and avoid hurting the pup. Also, have a bag handy because you will need it!

product_title: Chris Christensen Ice on Ice Conditioner with Sunscreen
review_body:
I have nothing to compare this to, as I headed straight to the most recomended brand, in order to avoid the headache of trying a bunch of cheaper brands and spending a lot of mobey on products that don't work. I guess you should keep that in mind but.....

I really like this! Especially after a bath. A groomer used a slicker brush on my (then) 4 month old Havanese puppy, and damaged some of his fur, making it feel sort of rough instead of silky soft. I was hopibg this would help smooth his hair back out. It has helped a little in that respect, but no miracles. :( It is fabulous at getting rid of his static, which he has in abundance as the air in my house is really dry! It also helps with smothing out the brushing process. It helps get through the tangles! (If you have a long haired dog, I would also recomend a Chris Christensen wooden pin brush.)

Also, the bottle is way larger than I thought. Thank goodness. It looks like a large pump hair spray bottle. And it doesnt take a whole lot to do the job, so the bottle should last a while. Of course, my puppy only weighs 6 pounds and will probably only get to 10-12 pounds, so if you have a bigger dog you will obviously need more.

There is very little scent to this, so you needn't worry that the smell will be too strong either. And it is very light, so it won't weigh the fur down. It also doesn't seem to leave any sort of build up. I use it every time I brush him, which I do often, trying to get him used to it so he grooms easily when he grows up, :) and haven't noticed a build-up at all!

When this bottle runs out I will probably just reorder rather than try something else, and that seems to be the best recommendation a product can get!

product_title: SmithBuilt Folding Metal Dog Crate - Double Door Cage - Multiple Sizes Available
review_headline: Spend the extra money on a better quality item
review_body:
Bottom line, spend more money. I bought this because I figured all wire crates must be about the same, and they probably all come out of the same factory in China, so why not save a few bucks? I bought this to have a crate for my 80lb Labradoodle at a second house where he spends a lot of time. I have the same size wire crate at my house (different brand) that I've had for over six years that my dog uses almost every day.

When the SmithBuilt crate arrived, I assembled it next to my existing (DreamCrate) crate, and the differences quickly became obvious. The Smith Built crate is immediately rickety. In fact, it shook and wobbled so bad that the first thing I did was get a bag of zip-ties out of my basement and shored the crate up in 24 spots. That has stopped the wobbling, but then I noticed even more troubling differences. The way the SmithBuilt crate is designed, the doors do not overlap the body of the crate. Combined with thinner wire and substandard latch design, this allows for the doors to bow out from the slightest of pressure, and it's very easy to see a paw getting stuck between the door and the body of the crate. The way my older crate is constructed, this is impossible. I zip-tied the wider of the two doors shut because my dog tends to lay against the side of the crate, and I can just see that ending in disaster if I didn't cinch the wide door both at the latch opening, and in the middle. Overall, this crate is sub-standard. My dog is a lazy loaf, not an escape artist, so I will keep this to use with the door open, more as a den for the dog than a cage. If you want to contain an animal, please either spend the extra $$ on a better designed and sturdier product, or try to buy a used one locally.

If you look at what used ones sell for and you think, "I can get a new one for that!", be warned that while you most certainly CAN get a new one for a similar price, it will not be as good of a product.

I really, truly believed all wire crates were created equal, but I can now promise you, they are not.

In fairness to the supplier, the SmithBuilt crate is by far the most cost effective wire crate I could find. But in this case, you do get what you paid for. I am keeping this product because it's my own fault that I was trying to be cheap. If I paid what other crates cost and received this crate I would rate it one star and return it. Since I got what I paid for though, it's my own dumb fault, and I'll rate it three stars based against it's cost.

review_body: Update 2 years later: Well, everything started out fine with the betta fish and this tank. It got to a point he seemed stressed...I learned fish have their ways of showing that. We added almost 10 lb of gravel to the bottom, 3 medium sized silk plants, 1 small silk plant, and his leaf hammock inside. Very pretty, and fish has plenty of room to swim still. The led light is great! If you are new to owning a fish as we are...do your homework. I found the videos on the Tetra website to be helpful. So far so good. Update: It has been a month now...still working as expected. As stated in other reviews, the half moon opening could pose a problem with fish jumping out. I do keep this covered with a piece of cardboard (in half moon shape) that I wrapped in foil (to keep it dry), and just taped it so that I could lift the lid it created to feed him. review_headline: THINK TWICE.....TOXINS KILL TINY KITTY BODIES!
review_body: Here's my story of cheap cat furniture. We have one older cat (about 8 years old) and one youngster (3.5 years old). I purchased this in Sept. of 2014 and primarily because, well, it's inexpensive, and what's the difference anyhow? The younger cat loved this furniture and was on it almost all the time, the older one sniffed around, maybe used it once or twice and then steered clear. Here we thought our youngster was being a cat tree piggy, but in reality, our older and wiser cat didn't like something about it.....fast forward to the end of November when we noticed our youngest was yellow around the ears and mouth....jaundice! We took him to the vet and the prognosis was very poor. He had a pre-hepatic condition, meaning his liver was failing, but not because of a failing organ, but as a reaction to something else. We thought, what the heck could cause this? The vet was not sure, then my wife pointed out the cat tree. I'm not saying it was definitely the cause because we will never know, but the boards in this tree are made of MDF, probably bound with formaldehyde resins and other VOCs, this stuff is TOXIC. Do some research and decide if your pet is worth the risk, in hindsight, I would have gone green.

review_headline: Just buy it - you won't regret it.
review_body: This is a fantastic crate for the houdinis out there. The built-in handles make it easier to carry (it is pretty heavy - about 45 lbs), and reassembling it isn't too difficult - about 2 minutes - though, be prepared for some noise, it *is* metal, after all. The interior is spacious (my GSD is only 65 lbs and she fits very comfortably) and there aren't any sharp edges or corners. I love the latches on this thing - spring-loaded and impossible for my dog to mess with, even if she could get at them (which she can't). The only shortcoming I've seen is that it's a tad too small for a standard 45 inch kennel pad - it runs up the back an inch or two, but it doesn't interfere with anything. review_headline: I like it but my some of my kitties don't
review_body: I love this cat bed and if I could fit in it I'd sleep in it myself...HOWEVER, I can't so I don't and neither do most of my cats.  I may be considered a crazy cat lady but I feed anywhere from 14 to 20 feral cats a night.  In the winter, I try to set up shelters and beds so that they can get a little break from the elements on the coldest nights so I bought a few of these self warming cat beds.  Size and quality wise they are nice.  The stitching is good and the materials are a good quality.  They've withstood the outside elements for several months now with no problems.  Minus a little dirt they still look awesome and don't appear that they'll fall apart anytime soon.  Self warming wise, I'm pretty sure that'd work too but this is where my idea ran aground, most of the cats are afraid of the crinkle/crackle sound that the self warming insides make.  I put them in places that I know some of the cats bed down for the night but with no luck  The beds spent the first two months unused, it wasn't until this week that one of them finally has an occupant.  Maybe the others will catch on?  So notes if you get this bed...1) They're well made  2) they'll withstand outside use 3) they're priced nicely  and 4) Don't get them if your kitty doesn't like stepping on things that make crinkling noises.

review_body: This item serves its purpose perfectly. I live in upstate NY where winter lasts half the year and the temp is frequently hovering at or below 0F. It does stay warm for quite a while if heated to the max so I often bring it in to work or home with me after the ride. It feels great on my back and preheats my bed at night. My cats know when I've put it under the covers and they'll huddle over it as well. I've used it twice daily, five times a week for more than two months now and have had no problems. UPDATE: now developed a leak which is impossible to find, much less fix. product_title: Feliway Behavior Modifier Spray 75 ml
review_headline: Xclnt alone and in concert with Feliway Plug-Ins
review_body:
Purchased 2 yrs ago & we still have a bit left, still viable: used for seasonal cat aggression issues.

Highly recommend this purple label spray version (as opposed to pink label Feliway 'Comfort Zone', see below) either alone or in accompaniment to an initial installation of the plug-ins (purple label Feliway 48ml Plug In Diffuser). During 'angry season', our schedule is every other day: upstairs 3 shots of Feliway spray on our bed & one in each sleeping perch a few hours before bedtime, to let propellents diffuse. Downstairs: one shot in perches, napping & grooming areas, and particularly in any doorway/narrow passage where cranky kitties lurk to 'guard' litter boxes or just assail a sibling. When the plug-ins are in place for 7-10 days the spray is seldom necessary, but we do still sometimes use it in one small hallway where the plug-in doesn't quite reach.

The Behavior Modification spray is stronger than the Comfort Zone; we use the B-Mod every other day in smaller doses & achieve a better result. The Comfort Zone we tried had to be sprayed daily in the same locations to achieve the same results (we were comparing them at the same time, with the same aggression levels in the cats). Our indoor cats' behavior issues are worse in the cold months when the windows can't be opened & there's less 'kitty TV' going on in the yards (birds, squirrels, etc.).

Aside from the Feliway our other measures are litter boxes in two locations to mitigate 'guarding' behavior, two separate water/dry food stations, and daily laser light chase playtime to burn off extra energy. We also use flat-bottomed Sterlite sweater boxes (without lids!) as litter boxes since two cats are very large Maine Coons: changing to these has also helped with aggression issues around the boxes themselves, enough space maybe? Total of 3 boxes as we have 3 cats, but they'll use different boxes according to cat logic we haven't quite figured out.

Hope some of this helps with your cat(s) behavior issues - good luck!s with your cat(s) behavior issues - good luck!

I ran into my reptile room and this Exo Terra bracket had fallen into her enclosure and was sitting on top of her paper towel substrate. My other enclosures have Exo Terra Brackets as well that are being anchored to the glass with regular packing tape, however I have removed them all today. You should do the same.
