review_headline: A truly great harness for pulling dogs.
review_body: This is a really, really great harness. I have a 1 year old French Bulldog x American Bully mix, and he was/is quite the puller. When I first got him, I used a flat buckle collar (Fail). Then I switched to a rear attaching harness (Fail). Then, I went to the prong collar (literally the best thing ever made, don't care what everyone says). After training him to walk beside and behind me on the prong, I really wanted to look for a more comfortable alternative for him. It's extremely rare that he pulls on the prong collar, and barely ever needs a correction for anything anymore. I do live in NYC with tons of distractions on walks, so I do still use it (especially in the cold months when he needs a little tension to get moving when he doesn't want to walk). But, like I said, I want him to be as comfortable as possible. This harness is actually kind of similar to a prong collar. Not in design, obviously, but in terms of function it's the same concept...walk too far and the dog will essentially correct itself, since the harness will force him to trip in his steps by turning him around to face me. If he is getting too far but not to the extent of the leash, a simple pull back on this harness pretty much does the trick. I really love it, and by the way, it's super easy to put on.

product_title: Nina Ottosson DogTwister Interactive game
review_headline: Most stimulating dog toy I've ever gotten for my dogs.  They LOVE it!
review_body:
Initially, my dogs weren't very interested and then I realized they weren't feeling well. I've got them back in good health and when I take the puzzle down, they get really really excited. I tried to start off easy for them and only began with 3 bones in place and treats in all pie pieces. That was the wrong way to go. It was easier for the dogs to understand when I used all 10 bones and put a small treat under each bone and in each pie piece. The dogs must take turns. One waits patiently while the other does the puzzle and then the other dog goes. They learned some skills from each other but each has their own way of doing things. This really is amazing!!! The positive brain chemistry that working on this puzzle creates for the dogs is fantastic! It's as exciting for them as chasing a small rodent and digging in the ground after it. Pretty impressive for a dog toy. My dogs can solve this in 5-6 minutes each. It's exciting to see the problem solving they go through.
One of my dogs is a toy destroyer so I don't leave this on the floor and I don't leave them unattended with it. That being said, it is an extremely durable toy. It takes a beating when they are biting it and using their feet to manipulate the pieces. It's also easy to wash, but some water stays inside this toy. It takes extra time for air drying (important depending on your flooring choices).
I'm looking forward to adding more of Nina's puzzles to my dogs' toy chest. The mental stimulation is unsurpassed by any other toy I've ever given them. It's great to see them perk up on days when I'm unable to take them for our walk. Another bonus is that the treat portions are small and a little goes a long way. My dogs maintain a perfectly healthy weight.
I do wish they made these on a smaller scale for tiny dogs. My Chihuahua has to sit on the sidelines and watch my two big dogs have a blast...

product_title: Soft Paws Nail Caps for Cats - Blue & Pink Combo Sparkle Pack - Original, Authentic Soft Paws. Veterinarian Developed Safe & Effective Alternative to Declawing. Nail Caps Made in the USA. Accept No Imitations!
review_body: I can't believe these worked, but they did.  The cats are already used to having their nails clipped regularly, which probably helped.  You just fill the caps with glue, have someone hold the cat, and stick them on.  Then you have to distract them with toys or cuddles for a few minutes while the glue sets.  They tried to pull them off for a little while after they were put on and then just left them alone and seemed to forget they are there.  We have two cats so the two colors are helpful, that way when I find one I know which cat needs to be captured and have a cap replaced.  It's been a week and they've each lost two, but it seems like they actually lost them because the claws shed their sheaths, not because they pulled them off.  Seems like it will be a weekly check-in to see if they need any replaced and they will probably need a couple at a time done. The glue actually lasts too, you can re-cap it and use it again which was a nice surprise.    **Update** After using these for a few weeks they have saved my upholstered furniture but at the cost of my looped rugs.  These softpaws seem to give my cats super strength when it comes to hooking their capped claws into one of the rug loops and unraveling the rugs so they have done a lot more damage than back when they just scratched on the rugs because now there are big gaping holes in my rugs where they have pulled out all the yarn.  If you have rugs that are cut pile or woven then you're safe.

product_title: Natural Balance Original Ultra Whole Body Health Dry Cat Food
review_headline: Trying A New Dry Food for the Kitty
review_body:
I feed my cat a different food for the dry portion of her diet. But who can resist something new? My kitty became a guinea-cat for this new Natural Balance dry food, \\"chicken meal and salmon meal\\" formula. I followed the directions of dry food and introduced it a little at a time, mixing it with the other dry food over about a week. Then I fed it without mixing. Kitty loves the food and eats it with relish.

This is a \\"natural\\" grain free food. competition in the pet food industry is fierce and there is much disagreement, including litigation, about the value of grain free. The packaging hypes the food as promoting digestion, providing antioxidants, and promoting brain health as well as meeting the cat's nutritional needs. So perhaps I will have a smarter kitty.

Of the five first listed ingredients, three are forms of chicken, with salmon meal as number six. Thus this is primarily a chicken product. I didn't know what \\"meal\\" meant in the title of this food. A look at Wiki indicated that \\"meal\\" was a common component of dry cat food, made by compression and was valuable for its increased protein content. That helped me feel better about the food.

I had two other small issues. The bag neither opens nor seals easily. This may be more of a result of the way I tore it open, but the fact remains that I had to tie the bag shut to keep the food fresh. I was also concerned about feeding my kitty too much fish as some of the sources I have read state that fish should be only a small part of the pet's diet. I doubt that this is a large problem given the predominance of chicken in the food. However, I have stopped giving my kitty wet fish food during the time I am using this product.

Variety is good for pets and their humans. My kitty liked this food and I am sure it is nutritionally good for her. I prefer and trust the dry food I was using earlier. Thus, while I enjoyed getting to know this brand, I don't think it will form the regular part of my cat's dry food diet.

Robin Friedmanry food diet. Robin Friedman

product_title: Natural Balance Perfect Bites Cat Treats
review_headline: Perfect fish treat bites for your kitty
review_body:
I have a kitty cat Jake. He used to have brother Elwood, who passed away of old age last year. So you can imagine the infinite, divine love that Jake gets from his Mommy every second of the day.

Most recently, Jake had treats that were in the shape of fish and had some catnip in it. He would abandon all activities when he heard me making \\"here is the treat, Jake!\\" announcement. So it was interesting to find out how he is going to like Natural Balance bites with salmon flavor. I was worried - when it come to cat food, Jake really preferes white fish. Salmon he eats, but it is more like \\"eh - if you have nothing better I will eat it\\". So I was curious to find out if he will love the treats. Treats are really small, and I usually give him 2 of them in the morning. They must be really chewy, because he savors them one at the time. After several days of of having salmon bites, I tricked him into having catnip fish treats. He was confused. He hesitated and then when he realized that is it for the day, he took it anyway, but I could tell he was disappointed. The next day I gave him salmon treats again. Not only was he greedy in getting to eat them both as quickly as possible (I guess he was afraid I might change my mind and not give them both to enjoy), but after he ate both little treats, he kept sniffing the floor in hopes there were more that may have come out of the bag.

Based on this experiment, I say \\"Perfect Bites\\" are perfect for my kitty. Salmon is this form is something he cannot wait to eat. This brand also offers chicken and rabbit flavors. I am planning to give him rabbit flavor next because he never ate rabbit before. And if he likes it, I will start calling him Jaques - little French food lover. Boy - I love that cat too much!

product_title: SportDOG Rechargeable Bark Control Collar
review_body:
Best thing ever. My poor Doggy with massive separation anxiety would howl whenever I left the house. I could view him on the security cam and it was so sad. He would work himself up with his howling. I was hesitant to use it on him thinking the anxiety might get worse, but a few other reviews on here made think it would be worth a shot. Tried this on myself and it's not bad. Level 0 is like someone tapping your neck. The higher levels aren't pleasant. I first tried this collar on the dog when I was with him, using the escalating function. I could tell he got shocked pretty good twice. Then he got it and was quiet. I left him alone and he stared at the door for a while, silently, before getting bored and falling asleep! Amazing. The collar has almost become like a security blanket to him. Whenever he needs to calm down, I put the collar on, even if it's off, and he knows it's relaxing time.

I've had this collar for over a year now and it's still going strong. He wears it every day when I'm gone. I'm not sure how some dogs apparently got injured with it as I've never had an issue. I do make sure never to put it on him when he's wet and I switched him to a harness with his tags so no other metal can touch the prongs.

review_body: love these little diapers. my little dog went into heat for the 1st time.  i was looking to find cheap diapers since i didnt even know if she would keep them on.  needless to say these were wonderful.  absorbent, PERFECT FIT and not a bank breaker.  since i am pretty frugal, i do only use 1 diaper a day.  shes an inside dog so she only goes out to potty/poop.  what i do is i cut up a maxi pad into 3 sections and stick 1 piece to the are in the diaper that she will use. through out the day she wears it and if she needs to go out we take off her diaper so she can handle her business.  if her "pad" needs changing we will change it and replace it with a new "pad" using the same diaper and put it on her when she comes back inside.  my dog sleeps overnight with her diaper on.  the people who are complaining about the tabs sticking and tearing the diaper obviously are NOT putting the tabs where they go.  these diapers will last the whole day if used right.  only reason i gave 4 stars instead of 5 is because there is a gap in padding where the tail goes so it leaves a small room for leak/mess.  this was fixed right when i decided to add my own "pad" for her inside the diaper so i can make them last longer :)  i would definitely be buying them again

review_headline: So this product was actually super nice for about two weeks
review_body:
So this product was actually super nice for about two weeks.
Unfortunately for me, I own a Maine Coon and he likes to get his water everywhere. Within about a month, I started to notice a really nasty odor coming from this mat. Upon closer inspection, it was growing mold on it. I went ahead and cleaned it with some color-safe bleach (and rinsed it out well), and let it dry out in the sun, but every few days this mat would have mold growing back on it. I noticed it never completely dried when he spilled water on it. Since the bottom is rubber and the top is this carpet-ish material, I assume it just can't dry from his messiness. In addition, it discolors and stains really easily, which for a messy cat... not really great.

After about a month and a half of this, I ended up throwing it away and going for a standard rubber mat. If you have a non-messy animal/one that doesn't do three-point dives into his water dish, this would probably work fine, and it is quite pretty.

review_headline: Used this on a cat.  No blood lost!

I put this on wrong the first time (the logo goes on the belly side, not on the animal's back), but after flipping it around found it put NO pressure on my cat's neck, but held her fairly securely.  Once it was on it didn't seem to bother her (this is the cat who's chewed up collars to make sure we didn't put them back on), and I was able to keep her contained in a moving vehicle, without the screaming we usually get when using a carrier.  I'd like to note here that I was NOT the driver, just the cat-wrangler.  She did manage to wriggle out at one point, so if I ordered again, I'd get a smaller size, though I ordered the correct one, going by the measurements here.  Otherwise, no problems, and we'll use it again.  Oh, and the blue was more of a royal blue than baby blue.  Not a problem, just an FYI.  Overall, very happy with this.

product_title: Watermelon/Mango Pangea Fruit Mix Complete Gecko Diet 1/2 LB
review_headline: If our crestie loves it, we love it!
review_body:
I discovered Pangea Crestie food by being too busy prior to vacation and realizing 2 days before went out of town that I had insufficient Repashy left for the pet sitter to use while we were away. Frantically, I jumped on Amazon to find Repashy that could reach me through Prime and on-time. Finding none that offered guaranteed delivery by the day we left, I noticed the Pangea food popping up on my search pages. After reading several of the reviews and seeing the product could be delivered by our leave date, I jumped on it. Sadly, it did not arrived on the "guaranteed by" date and I had no choice but to track down a pet store that carried our tried-and-true Repashy an hour before we left. Would you be surprised if I told you my fortune cookie fortune that day read "lady who wait until last minute to buy pet food must buy double pet food for punishment"?

The package was delivered one day late and sat waiting for our return several days later. My double-food purchase shame aside, I was excited to give Bond, James Bond (our Crestie...he likes his crickets shaken, not stirred) his new food. WOW! He absolutely LOVES this watermelon/mango mix! The consistency kind of had me freaked out (more "yogurty" than the smoothie-like appearance of Repashy), and I couldn't decide how I felt about the smell, but I am not the one eating it so my opinion doesn't really matter there. Bond devoured it, finishing his entire serving for the first time ever. What I really love about the Pangea mix is that it is far easier to "see" what has been eaten when compared to Repashy, which is extremely helpful when trying to gauge their general appetites. The high presence of tongue-tracks in the food is sure sign of happy eating, and Bond has definitely put on a healthier weight over the past month from his new food.

While I am not prepared to part with our 3 years of trust in the Repashy products, I am prepared to purchase "double food"for a bit as I fully intend to keep the Pangea mix in the pet pantry as well. We are very excited to try another flavor when watermelon/mango runs low!

review_headline: nice large pads, good absorbency & they don't leak
review_body:
O.M.G. These pads are great!!! They have saved my back & my sanity....We recently took in two strays and now have eight cats. Things have been getting messy lately. I use these under my kitty litter boxes because we have one or two that sometimes like to go near the box but not in it. They seem to be doing it more since the arrival of the new kitties. I try to scoop & clean the boxes several times a day to make sure they have a nice clean place to go, but it never seems like enough. and sure enough every day now i find pee pooling up under the box. after two weeks of this i got REAL sick of having to mop up the tile and clean the floor and underneath the boxes every day....

Initially i tried out some puppy training pads from the dollar store that are standard 20 X 20 size. they worked ok. but with those smaller pads i needed four overlapped to cover the area properly and the cats were always managing to scoot them around. With these larger pads i only need two pads overlapped to get the job done. they provide a lot of coverage and they never rip or leak. less trouble with the cats scooching them out of place too. In my experience they hold the urine very well. If one of the kitties lets loose very near the edge of the pad then there might be some spillage, but otherwise they work fabulously.

Looks like some people saying they leak while the majority of us don't have that problem. I've only ever had a problem with the pads holding when one goes near the edge, and i've never had the bottom leak or break on me. I was thinking that perhaps it has to do with the volume of liquid the pads have to hold. I only have cats, no dogs, but two of my boy kitties are well over 20 lbs. The Biggest is 24.5 lbs and he makes quite a large puddle when he goes. If he goes too close to the edge of the box it sprays out over the edge. These pads holds his mess just fine. Maybe for large dogs they are not heavy duty enough, but i think for small & medium sized animals they should work well.s they should work well.

product_title: All Natural-All American Beef Ears
review_headline: my dog thought this was the best thing ever
review_body:
I think these things are absolutely disgusting. However, what is important is not what *I* think of them, but what my dog thinks of them. And she thinks they are awesome.

My dog is a 2-year-old, 95-pound Rottweiler. One of these ears (received in a recent Petbox) seems to be a good size for her. I think slightly larger dogs could also safely have these, and probably even dogs down to 50 or 60 pounds. (Wouldn't go a whole lot smaller than that -- the ear was pretty big and a smaller dog would have a hard time chewing one of these.)

I have never given this particular dog rawhides or ears as treats before, so she took a minute to figure it out. Once she understood she could chew on it, she went to work and did not stop until I took it away. She had managed to consume about 1/3-1/2 of it in an hour, usually by breaking off little pieces and chewing them further. (My previous dog, on the other hand, would have had this thing gone in about 15 minutes flat. It totally depends on the dog.) I'll give her the rest of it tomorrow and let her work on it some more.

So for slow chewers, these are great because they'll last a few days. Also, for what it's worth, these are made in the USA. Mine came shrink-wrapped in rather thick plastic, which was a little bit hard to remove.

review_body: I started training my 6 year old cat, Walter, in October and now, two months later, he is completely Toilet trained! When we first started he was slightly hesitant, but each step he got more and more comfortable with the process. The kit comes with a toilet training seat insert and an extra training insert, just in case you move too fast for your cat, which can be very very useful. When I punched out the first hole Walter was a little afraid of the water, so I set a single square of toilet paper over the hole until he realized it was nothing to be scared of. During the entire training process I took him into the bathroom often and showed him the training insert and the water while praising him so he would see the toilet and bathroom as a good place to be. I am very happy with this product and now I will never have to use litter or clean cat 'business' out of a smelly, dusty box again! Also, Walter is a very large lazy kitty and the training seat held his weight with now issues at all.

review_headline: Has been wonderful for our arthritic dog.
review_body: We bought this for our 80 lb GSD that is suffering from severe arthritis in her front legs.  She is having trouble standing up and walking and sometimes she falls unexpectedly.  We received this harness on Thursday and it has been a life saver.  The handle on top is perfect for guiding her and giving her extra support when she needs it.  It is sturdy and our girl feels supported when she wears it.  It is also really easy to get on.  The front strap is velcro that you set once to your pup's size and then never have to reset it.  To put the harness on, you slip it over your pup's head and then loop the other strap around their middle.  The plastic latch seems really sturdy and feels very secure so far.  Measurement wise, our girl was right at the low end of the XL size range.  I'm glad we chose XL--this size fits perfectly on her.  It is not too baggy and there is room to cinch it smaller if we need to.  I took the advice of some other reviewers and bought car seatbelt strap protectors to avoid any chance of chafing from the straps.  For ordinary use, this probably wouldn't be necessary, but since we are using it to give her support when her legs fail, I think its a good idea to put in the extra padding.  For the XL size, I used three of these: http://www.amazon.com/Auto-Expressions-Sheepskin-Shoulder-Pad-Grey/dp/B000CAINRK/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1418662131&sr=8-1&keywords=sheepskin+car+seatbelt+cover. product_title: Baby Tears Plant – 2 Bunches – Live Aquarium Plants by Aquatic Arts
review_body:
My online shopping experience with Aquatic Arts has been nothing short of exceptional. I recently purchased and received the following:
Ivory White Mystery Snails, CPO Dwarf Mexican Crayfish/Mini Lobsters, Blue Mystery Snails, Thai Micro Spider Crabs, Black/Purple Mystery Snails, Orange Giant Sulawesi Rabbit Snails, Baby Tears, Hairgrass, Cholla Wood, Moneywort, Dark Red Ludwigia, Green Cabomba, Hornwort, Anubias Barteri, Amazon Sword Plant and extra-large bunch of Hornwort.
I will not go into each individual purchase as there are too many to go into each; however I will make some points on items I think are worth pointing out:
First, Aquatic Arts is appreciative of customers and have a live arrival guarantee. Should any critters not make the journey, they compensate in advance by sending extras (not to mention they also give shipping discounts and provide coupon codes when certain dollar amounts are spent). I’m sure what and how many depends on the order, but I have seen on previous reviews that AA has done the same for them. As for me, they sent me lots of extras and I couldn’t be happier with my order. They were responsive when I emailed them and were willing to work with me when I requested to modify my order and best of all they were HONEST. When I asked they gave me an honest answer about tank mates not getting along so they weren’t concerned about the sale, but about the best interest of the critters and customer satisfaction. They tracked and showed concern about the delay in the package delivery (heavy Christmas traffic; bad timing on my part), but they were boxed to survive up to a week in the box if necessary- I will go into more detail later.
In regards to the little critters, here are my reviews; the mystery snails are beautiful, bright and fun to look at. The rabbit snails however, are captivating and are difficult to take your eyes off of. Their shells are beautiful and they themselves are brightly colored. It’s interesting to watch them grazing peacefully around the aquarium. The CPO’s are my aquarium’s pride and joy. They are ADORABLE and perfectly sized for an aquarium with non-aggressive fish. I ordered three and received four and one of the females was pregnant! I love watching them wander around the aquarium grabbing at all the little bits under the gravel. As for the Micro Spider Crabs- the disclaimer “(FOR EXPERIENCED NANO AQUARISTS AND SHRIMP HOBBYISTS ONLY!)” is there for a reason! I have a 75 gallon and they are tiny! Probably about the size of a pencil eraser. If you’re really interested in these please make sure the aquarium is designed for something this small otherwise you’re probably not going to see them very often. I noticed some previous reviews made a complaint about this; I’d say it’s kind of like baby proofing a house, except you have to build your aquarium to accommodate these little creatures.
All the plants I received came in great condition and made my aquarium look 10x’s better and livelier. The fish and critters love them too, I can’t wait to see them grown and fully established. I will note that the extra-large bunch of hornwort was EXTRA LARGE. A little much for my aquarium, but I have an outdoor pond so I put some of the hornwort in there as well.
As far as the shipping, like I said my deliver was delayed due to heavy holiday mail. Otherwise it was sent two day expedited shipping through USPS. My large order came in a large box and within that box was a thick Styrofoam container. That container was full of recycled and recyclable cardboard-like insulation- perfect for cold weather so I like that much better than packing peanuts. The critters and plants themselves were in plastic baggies, much like the ones you get when you go to a pet store. The CPO’s and crabs had little bunches of java moss in them to make the trip more comfortable.
So as I stated above, this has been a great shopping experience. I very much look forward to shopping from Aquatic Arts in the future and I highly recommend them for their variety of aquatic creatures that most often can’t be found at your local pet store, their courtesy, honesty and professionalism.rience. review_headline: My dog's favorite toy, but really looks like a dildo
review_body:
If my dog (30 lb corgi/lab mix) were to review this item, he would give it a 5+, however I would give it a 3. The replacement just came in today and he is so happy to have something satisfying to chew on again. I had to laugh at the description, though" "Best for strong chewers 40 lbs and up" since my pup is barely 30 lbs and is at least 5 years old. Needless to say, I'm very happy with the replacement policy with this company!

I would personally give this item 3 stars because it doesn't last as long as the ring form and because it really looks like a dildo. I have to explain this toy whenever I send him to a pet-sitter or whenever he wants to chew on this toy outside of his crate. The toy is worth it to give my dog something appropriate to chew on, but it would be nice if it was a little less dildo-shaped. I'd recommend buying the ring shape if you are particularly shy about your dog chewing on a dildo, but I know that I will always have one of these around my house. Thanks Goughnuts!

review_headline: If my VERY picky cat likes it, it must be good!
review_body:
I have a VERY PICKY cat. So picky that I have to put his cat food in a blender to take out the lumps or he won't eat it. And even then, he only eats one flavor and brand. Did I say PICKY?!

So, I was curious to see if he would he this food, especially since it's a good quality food. I put some of this on his plate along with his normal pureed food. I thought I would try it first without putting it through the blender. He ate it and I thought, \\"Well, maybe it's just a one time thing.\\" So, the next day, I tried it again, and he ate it again! Still no blending required! I have been feeding him this food for the last four days and he eats it every time. I'm impressed! If my cat likes it, it must be good! And, better yet, it's good for him. All natural ingredients. I am VERY Happy!

UPDATE: Unfortunately, he decided he didn't like it after all. After a few days, he just started putting his nose in the air and leaving it. I DO have a PICKY cat, so this might not be the case with everyone. The only canned food he likes is [[ASIN:B002CJASQ8 Friskies Cat Food Savory Shreds with Salmon in Sauce, 5.5-Ounce Cans (Pack of 24)]]; and, even then, he has to have it run through the blender until it is pureed into pudding. I tried this with Beyond, but it doesn't work. It was a nice try.

product_title: Vetri-Science Laboratories Glyco-Flex II Bite-Sized Cat Chews
review_headline: It helped my kitty move easier, but only the one that would eat them.
review_body:
I have a couple older cats and have noticed that they are starting to slow down. With the advice of my vet I have been told to add in a joint supplement to help them move. I have given them a capsule before, which was not fun for any of us. After taking the supplement for about a month I notice that they do seem to be moving better. So, when I saw these treat I figured that I would try them.

The first thing you will notice is the smell, rank! But I have tried other supplements or treats and I have come to the conclusion that if they didn’t stink the cats won’t eat them. Well, only one of the cats eats the treats which is no surprise, my other kitty isn’t much of a treat kitty. The other one likes them and doesn’t mind eating two treat a day (2 treats a day per 10 pounds of body weight).

It is hard to determine if the treats are working. I think he is moving better but it is hard to tell with cats since they are the masters of disguising pain. I would make sure to ask your vet before giving them to your kitty. But I think they have helped, at least for the cat that will eat them. It is definitely less stress giving a couple treats than a capsule.

Shawn Kovacich
Author and Creator of numerous books and DVD's.

product_title: Pioneer Pet Raindrop Style Drinking Water Fountain, 96-Ounce
review_headline: Well-received by my cats who turned up their noses to the Big Max
review_body:
We recently adopted a kitten (in addition to a 6 yo cat) and decided to get a second fountain for the house. I had previously been using a Drinkwell Original with great results, but just wanted something different for variety.

I had purchased the Pioneer Pet Big Max and both cats sort of snubbed it. The older one is just conditioned to like the free-fall stream of the Drinkwell and the kitten was a little overwhelmed by the size of the Big Max. They both used the Big Max but no more than a stationary bowl of water.

I decided to exchange it for the Raindrop model and I could not be more pleased. Almost immediately both cats took interest in it. The design gives them more options to drink: at the bubbler, down the ramp, a small (very small, but reachable by a curious tongue!) free fall area at the edge of the ramp, or just the well itself. I had it set up for 5 minutes and both guys wanted to try it.

As an added bonus, it uses the same pump as the Big Max, but moves less water, so the net result is faster motion, which attracts both cats. With the Big Max I had the pump at full power and it was a ho-hum affair with almost no motion past the ramp. The Raindrop at half-speed moves the water enough to catch the attention of the cats without being noisy at all.
Also- the Raindrop design is more accessible to the cats. The ramp on the Big Max was centered and the older cat could reach it with a lean but the kitten had to step into the bowl to get to it. The angled design of the Raindrop is just ideal for cats of all sizes.

I would recommend this to any cat owner looking for a solid, easy to clean water fountain.

So far, he's had this toy for about a month. I would caution that it is no where near indestructible to an aggressive chewer. product_title: Outward Hound Kyjen  Dog Backpack
review_headline: Awesome pack! Durable and Lightweight! Great for arctic breeds! Needs Leash attachments.
review_body:
I don't understand what these negative reviews are complaining about! I use one with my 120lb American Akita and have had ZERO issues!

Here are pics of him LOVING it! https://www.facebook.com/media/set/?set=a.505757982889275.1073741861.379285572203184&type=3

"It's too thin and rips easily!"...I got this pack precisely BECAUSE it is thin because my double-coated dog over-heats easily! It is also very lightweight on its own! I have also never had a single stitch rip! When we aren't hiking, I use it on walks with a frozen 2 liter of water in each side! No issues!

"It falls to one side if it isn't balanced well!" BOOHOO! It's called PHYSICS! Balance it! Of course if I put all of the water in one side, it'd lean to that side! DUH! Even if it didn't slide to one side, why would you want to do that to your dog?! As much as some of you complain and want it to be comfortable to your dog, you certainly don't sound like you are trying to make him comfortable! You should always try to put the same amount of weight in each side FOR the COMFORT of your dog! THINK!

The pack is obviously designed with the dogs comfort in mind. The pouches are designed so that the majority of the weight will rest forward over the dogs shoulder rather than over their back. I know many other packs that aren't designed this way.

Also, for all of you that say it slides around with nothing in it, you obviously need to tighten it. You put a trail pack on yourself once with loose straps and/or all the weight to one side and see how YOU feel!

If your dog is chafing, try tightening it. If it is fitted properly and it still chafes, this pack isn't for your dog. Not all packs fit all dogs. This pack is perfect for a deep-chested double-coated dog like mine. Too much padding or too thick of material would be uncomfortable for him and cause him to over heat more easily.

The ONLY reason I did not give this pack 5 stars is because it has no leash attachments.
I have to use an Easy Walk Harness between the harness and removable packs instead.

Definitely recommend this pack! Don't listen to the few haters at the bottom!

Here are a couple of pics to show it in use. In one, you can see how the Easy Walk Harness fits on top of the Outward Hound Harness.

product_title: MidWest Homes for Pets Foldable Metal Exercise Pen / Pet Playpen, 8 Panels Each
review_headline: Great for a Senior Pug - She Likes It
review_body: Our senior pug used to be an expert at using wee-wee pads in the middle of the night but she now has disk disease and can't tell when she's going #2. So, recently, at night she would roam around the house keeping us up with her pitter patter and leaving "presents" in unexpected places. We ordered this pen to give her a fixed place to stay right next to our bed while we sleep. We line it with wee-wee pads so we know she'll hit the mark and we also put a bed, toys and water in there. It's like her house and she's excited every night and runs to the spot while we build the pen around her.  The 24" height is really even more than we need. I was worried it would be a pain to put away the pen every morning but the panels fold easily so we can hide it in the closet and the closure is very easy to close or open. If you open the pen and zig zag the panels you can stand it up as a wall.  We are using the pen on hardwood floor and I am a little worried the pen will scratch the floor if it is slid but I haven't seen any scratches. I wish it came with those little rubber tubes that are cut open that you squeeze around things to prevent scratching or skidding because when I feel the bottom it's not totally smooth. Otherwise, I am very satisfied with this pen. Using it in this way has greatly improved our sleep and made the morning "clean-up" ritual much less annoying.

review_body:
*************I THINK ITS VERY IMPORTANT TO READ THIS PRIOR TO PURCHASING.!!!!!!***************

I had purchased this training collar approximately a month ago. I personally wanted to return this item, Because of a few reasons that I thought were very important.

1.) in order to charge this shock collar, you need to take off the collar because where you plug it into charge is located on the end of the unit underneath the collar. This got to be a huge pain to have to disassemble the collar each and every time just to charge.

2.) my second reason that I wanted to return it is because in order to change the mode from vibrate to shock or sound, you have to hit the mode button in order to toggle back-and-forth. This is not set up well at all. I am one of those people that don't like to use the shock method often, however, imagine if your dog started to go after another animal. You have it on vibrate but it's not getting its attention and it is urgent. You literally have to go into the mode, hit another button to change it, then hit another button to activate. Again, not a good set up.

I have gone on here and found a unit where the charger plug-in is on the side of the unit where you do not have to take off the collar each and every time, and it also has a very basic set up on the Remote control unit. It has three buttons on the left and right side. You do not have to go into any kind of mode to change from sound to vibrate, and so on.

After about two weeks she was moving around like a dog half her age!! She started running and playing. She started coming up to us for attention and actually wanted to be petted and loved on. I never thought I would see this much of a difference in her and can't say enough about these supplements!! It's almost hard to believe. It's worth every penny I spent and then some!!!

review_body:
reading the one star review I feel compelled to write mine.
Lola and Foxy Martingale Collars are a quality product that really give you confidence that your dog will never slip
from their collar. Martingales are also called Hound Collars for that reason.The quality construction of the Lola and Foxy is what I choose for my Ozzie a Dachshund Shepherd mix now 15 yo. I discovered Lola and foxy 4 years ago after Oz had disc trouble and he has worn one ever since.It is a good thing that Lola and Foxys do not have a release snap. The purpose of a Martingale is to give the owner total confidence that their dog is secure. The great feature of a martingale is that it can be adjusted to close to FULL SNUG only and not go so far as to become a "choke" collar as the connector chain slides in a limited range. LOVE them. Lastly Lola and Foxy is the very only company to provide a separate metal D ring hanger for your dogs tags.The large selection of fashion materials is also a plus for most dog lovers.what I am really saying is I have tried them all as to Martingales and Lola and Foxy is a high quality individually made product that merits its pricing. P.S. I just bought another one the first has lasted several years and will be passed on to rescue still very functional.

product_title: VetriScience Vetri Probiotic Every day for Dogs and Cats, 60 Bite-Sized Chews 7.41 Oz.
review_headline: Probiotics are important for us, so why not for dogs and cats?
review_body:
These are the cutest little tiny bone-shaped chews, and unlike a lot of other dog chews I've tried lately, these are clearly made from the good stuff. My little 7.5 lb. chiweenie treated the chew like he does those things he considers precious and not to be lost: He put it far back in his mouth, then picked up one of his bones and wandered around the house crying, looking for the perfect place to bury it and save it until just the perfect moment to really enjoy it. That means he loves it. And that's a real surprise, because I have never seen such a finicky dog in my life. I'm going to make giving this chew his \\"last one\\" treat for the day because I save the most special thing for last. After everyone goes to bed, I'll hear him sneaking in to dig up his lovely treasure and devour it in peace. Little dogs....

For a dog Bingo's size, half a chew a day is recommended. That means this bag will last four months. That should be ample time to see how his gut flora improves. He has a very sensitive little tummy, and so many things upset his digestive tract. Based on my own experience with an uppity gut, I know the probiotics can make all the difference in the world, and I can't imagine it would be too different for dogs. (Cats can take these, too.) Anyway, so far so good. Building up good gut flora doesn't happen overnight. If, over time, this product does not live up to what I expect, I'll post an update.

After looking at ALL the other options, not just on Amazon, I bought this one and we've had it about a month and are completely satisfied. It is plenty strong for the bigger Dog and literally went together in about three minutes, no tools required. Far easier than the other bed. review_body:
This bed is really nice however watch out when you open the box the bed comes in; I used scissors to cut the tape on the box and it also cut the bed. I'm sure that cut down on how anti-bacterial the bed is going to be over time...

Also, my dog is super quirky so it was like pulling teeth getting him to lie on the bed. Whenever any weight is put on the bed the other parts of the bed poof up (kind of like when you step into a bouncy house). It was awkward for me to lie on so I could understand why my dog didn't want to lie on it. But after the air in the bed is pushed out by the weight of me/my dog, it is a fine bed. Just to be clear, this "poof" happens every time weight is put on the bed. So your dog will have to get used to the poof-ness of the bed when he/she initially steps on it.

After over a week of training, my dog finally sleeps on the bed. If you experience this same problem, try jealousy: My parents' dog is not quirky and instantly lay on the bed. I praised their dog, so my dog got jealous and wanted to lie on the bed too. Problem solved.

Just in case you're wondering, yes, I had to Google when to use lie/lay.

review_body: These are so much cuter than their picture! I hemmed and hawed a lot about getting bells for bell training. I've never had a bell-trained dog before, but I work at a zoo, and when you know a lot of zookeepers they have a lot of great advice for training animals. My dog was terrified of going through doors (in, out, didn't matter, did not want to cross any thresholds, even inside doors) so I thought there would be no way to train with bells. In 3 months she has over come her fear of doors, her fear of the sound of the bells, and we are well on our way to being fully bell-trained. She now sits in front of the door and lifts her paw like "shake" so I tap the bells to her foot and she's not afraid anymore. I think we are very close to her doing it on her own, which will be a welcome relief for my husband and I to not have to guess anymore when she wants 'out'! I realize that I could really use any bells, but I think it's important, at least for my dog, to have something that is designated as 'hers' since she has had several fears to overcome.

product_title: Patio Pacific Thermo Panel IIIe with Endura Flap
review_body:
This is a great sturdy secure door. That really sums it up. I have three rambunctious shelties going in and out of it all day. I got the taller one as the dogs are different sizes. I left it set on the lowest height for the smallest one to step over. Since my porch in my new home is about 5" lower than the house, I made a small wooden ramp for outside so they could step equally on both sides of the door and not strain their spines. They are getting older. 8 and 11 at this point.

The one thing that was not as I would have liked was the stick on wide white weather proofing. First, I wanted to put it on both inner and outer parts of the doors. There is only enough for one side. Secondly, it was jammed into the box and all crumbly and when I tried to heat it up with a hair dryer it still did not relax. I put it on anyways as it's getting cold but I found another place online that carried it and ordered two and now it's secure, not drafty and weatherproof on both sides.

The door is nice looking installed and no drafts at all around the flap. I previously had a double flap in the wall of my previous house so I was wondering how the single would work. It does just fine.

The final thing we did was to cut the adjustable burglar bar shorter so now that pushes the existing door hard against the side of the pet door weatherproofing allowing virtually no space in between. I also set it in the track toward the inside edge of the door and used 3/4" plastic filler molding to keep it securely in place around the outer edges.

The dogs had to take a day or so to get used to it even with years of experience in my former home. The flap is cloudy so they can't see where they are stepping and former one was clear. The ramp helped that a lot so they trust it now. The magnets are stiffer too but I left them alone for now to see as it closes quicker and even the smallest one figured out how to push it open after a day or so.

All in all, I'm glad I went for the more expensive door after research as I think it will last a long time and keep the energy bills lower.

product_title: EzyDog Quick Fit Custom Fit Adjustable Dog Harness
review_headline: A little more effort, but worth it (size X-Small and Small)
review_body:
I didn't know quite what to think of this harness, at first. My dogs did not care for wearing it, and it took quite a while to get it dialed in and just right. Using their sizing guidelines, the fit was inconsistent. I had to adjust the Small size to the very maximum for my larger Chihuahua mix, even though his measurements were right in the middle of the sizing guidelines. The X-small harness for my smaller Chihuahua on the other hand, is too large. Set to the smallest adjustment, it gaps at the sides, and she can still get her leg out.
All that aside, these have become great harnesses! Extremely easy to put on and remove. At first, it looked like it was going to irritate my dog behind his legs, but it I have not noticed any redness or rash (he has very short hair and irritates easily), and his gait is normal. I do wish that it came with an additional neoprene sleeve for the underbelly strap. When it comes to walking, these harnesses are set at the perfect location on their backs, not too far up to choke, not too far back to allow for much rebellion.

product_title: FURminator deShedding Tool for Cats
review_body:
I own 2 short haired, indoor cats. One with a very dense undercoat and prone to hairballs. Another whose undercoat is thin and is less prone to hairballs. I have owned this product for about a year.

This works amazingly well. You will get enough fur out of your cat the first time to make another cat! And no, you will not leave kitty bald. My cat with the very dense undercoat looked relieved. He still had a lot of hair but it without so much of the undercoat, his fur felt more "normal". Shedding became less of an issue and petting him does not leave you covered in so much fur. He loves to be combed and so I kept up with it, but he would still have so much excess hair. Now it is manageable. Your cat will still shed as long as he has fur, but this gets it down. His hairball problems dropped too.

For my other cat whose undercoat was not as dense, I could rarely get much hair off of her with normal brushing. This got out much more. That being said, since she did not have as much of a shedding problem, the difference was less noticeable.

When you use it, you need to be prepared to have fur all over. You also need to be careful not to press down too hard with those metal teeth. You do not need to press down. More of a scooping motion as you comb. But it is easy to want to press. Your cat will not love you for that after too much of that. For one cat I can just put down a towel and the hair is well contained. For my dense coated boy, we have to go through walking around and chin rubbing things as part of the routine. So I just plan to get some vacuuming done after.

product_title: Prevue Pet Products Wrought Iron Select Bird Cage Black Hammertone 3151BLK
review_headline: For the price I guess it is an OK cage
review_body:
This review is based only on initial impressions after putting together the cage; however, the most important aspects of it, which are quality of paint, its protection against rust and damage from bird excrement will have to wait for quite a while. The other points to look for in the long term are weld spots and joints of the components.
The first thing to comment is about the packaging, for a bulky and heavy item, the contents are well protected and took the shipping beating fairly well. The second thing one notices after opening the box, is the strong chemical smell emanating from it, mainly from the box with the rubber wheels.
Inside the main box all the pieces are packed tightly and with lots of bubble wrap. If you have wood floors it would be a good idea to cut the box and open it in such a way that it gives a decent size working area where to assemble the cage, especially if putting it together without assistance, as sometimes one of the ends drop to the floor while trying to align the other end to put the screw in.
I ordered the cage in Black Hammertone, the paint looks good and seems to coat all the corners and joints of the frames well.
I agree with the reviewers, the instructions are a waste of the paper they are printed on.
In my opinion, the hardware is more or less at the same level as the instructions, in other words, useless. The screws are barely long enough to catch one or two threads, especially the eight screws holding the walls of the cage together. I ended up purchasing longer screws from Amazon to replace what came with the cage (The Hillman Group 4405 M6-1.00 x 12mm Metric Stainless Steel Socket Cap Screw (10-Pack) if you plan to use the seed guards, and The Hillman Group 45340 M6-1.00 x 35 Metric Stainless Steel Socket Cap Screw, 5-Pack for the cage frame components). I also recommend using stainless steel washers to keep the paint from peeling when tightening the screws and to prevent rust.
When putting the cagetogether, I found that it was easier to align and start the screw on the other side if I didn't tighten the opposite side screw all the way, that way I could wiggle the piece and avoid stripping the threads of the welded nuts in the frame.
The seed guards issues have been already covered by other reviews and I do agree, I will probably end up not using them.
Finally, before moving the bird(s) to the cage, and as other reviewers have suggested, it is wise to place the cage outside for few days to take care of the awful chemical smell. This is an important step—in my opinion.

review_body:

Since we fed them crickets when they were younger, it took a while for them to start eating these pellets. However, if you mix the pellets in with some vegetables that they like (e.g., kale) they will eventually become accustomed to eating the pellets.

The only drawbacks to the pellets are that they need to soak for 30 minutes in water before you can feed them to the beardies and they sometimes break apart (there are little bits and pieces of them scattered around the reptile tank after the beardies are done eating). However, this is a much more cost effective and sanitary means of feeding beardies when compared with purchasing hundreds of smelly crickets.

I would not recommend feeding these pellets to young beardies as the pellets are too large (plus, younger beardies are better off with live food).

product_title: Go Pet Club F2093  Cat Tree Furniture, 61-Inch
review_headline: My Ideal Cat Tree: Simple Design, Unique Touches, Quality Construction
review_body:
I actually ended up purchasing this through Overstock.com with a ten percent off coupon, making it about two-thirds the price as here and everywhere else. Delivery was within two weeks, but considering it was free shipping, that was more than satisfactory.

The tree was simple and easy to put together. You may have to finagle the platforms' and posts' pre-drilled holes to get everything aligned, but it isn't a hair-pulling experience. Everything attaches with bolts using the hex-wrench that is included. The end result is beautiful (in terms of cat trees!) and on day one I was complimented by how attractive it was. The vine (included) really sets it off nicely so that it appears to be a *part* of the décor, not a cat toy that is just in the way of it.

I really like the compact size (width), and it is quite stable with my 10+ lbs cats jumping on and off. The smaller platforms are big enough to hold each without danger of them falling off, and the largest platform on top is currently holding my two large males together with room to spare. The layout allows for cats to climb up the platforms like stairs, making it easier on the older felines. I also like what it doesn't have: loads of barrels and top-heavy condos that my cats won't use. There is a tunnel on the base, but that works well both in appearance and structural balance. The faux fur combined with the rough rope (I forget the proper name) is aesthetically better (in my opinion) than the carpeted trees, and as it's softer has less appeal to my cats for clawing and more for lounging. I've bought an inexpensive cardboard scratcher to place next to the tree for their nail tendon stretches (much cheaper).

I'd hesitated at the price, but now I'm glad I held off and bought this over something half the price but not quite what I had wanted. This is definitely a very nice cat tree and - though it's only been a few days - I'm very pleased with it. So are my cats. :)

review_headline: Hands Down The Best Pet Stroller with Functional Design Features
review_body:
I did a lot of research for six months prior to purchasing this stroller seven months ago. I wanted to test this stroller for few months before writing this review. For the record, I do not work for this company and do not get paid for writing reviews. So here it is...

Pros (must haves)

1. I bought this stroller for my 10LB indoor cat. The stroller is quite large and sturdy. It can accommodate few cats or puppies. My cat can sit or stretch comfortably and still has quite a lot of room to roam around and enjoy the 360 view. It also has plenty of head space. The interior dimensions are 30\\"L X 13\\"W X 22\\"H.

2. Stroller can be used for walking, jogging and in rough terrain/hiking. It could be folded with one hand easily and placed in the car trunk. The length is about 4 feet long and 3.25 feet high once folded. I can take the stroller out without having to fold it or remove the big wheels so this was a huge factor for me.

3. The handle bar is easy on the hands for long walks. It sits high with stroller height to handle at 42 inches so you do not have to bend your back to push the stroller easily.

4. The stroller has a basket on the bottom for storing few things such as an air pump or pet stuff. I would not recommend putting heavy things in the basket as it might tear.

5. The terrific rear safety breaks feature will keep your pet safe if you need to stop uphill or downhill however I would not leave my pet unsupervised since I am never comfortable with the forces of nature/gravity! The rear safety break is next to the wheels and could be engaged with your foot. No need to bend down!

6 The No Zipper Easy Lock feature is a must have. You do not have to worry about cheap plastic zippers breaking. The No Zipper feature makes it very quick and easy to open or close the hood. Great for folks with joint pain.

7. The air-filled wheels are the best I have seen in pet strollers. They are large so your baby will relax and enjoy a smooth ride. The front wheel can either be fix or swivel. The stroller comes with an air pump (bonus) so you do not need to worry about the wheels breaking like some of the cheaper strollers with plastic wheels which can crack or break so easily. When low on air, you simply pump some air and continue your stroll. The other advantage is that the inner tube could be repaired or replaced if torn. In addition, you do not have to lift the front up to maneuver over the large uneven surfaces.

8. The stroller is made with durable and thick water resistant material including the nice mesh all around accommodating air flow and visibility for your pet. The stroller's airy and spacious design allows your pet to enjoy the front and back view while sitting or standing. The back view allows your pet to see you and the wide front view eliminates the blind spots so for cats this is a plus. The stroller has a top window as well.

9. The inside of the stroller has two bottoms which accommodates the folding. The one side is a bit higher than the other side. My cat does not seem to have a problem with it. The stroller has a comfy pet bed. I have placed a pet blanket to keep my cat more comfortable during our outings.

10. The stroller comes with a rain cover (bonus). This is a plus since you have to pay extra for a rain cover when you purchase other strollers.

11. The stroller was delivered on time. The packaging was intact. It included all the pieces and the stroller was not damaged. It took me (female) about 10 minutes to assemble the stroller. I did not have any problems with the instructions. The stroller is more expensive compared to the other strollers however given all the features; I consider the price to be reasonable. This stroller will last you a very long time.

Cons

1. The stroller has a small tray and two bottle holder cups which arevery shallow (about 1.5-1.75 inches deep) on the handle bar. I tried placing my water bottle and it tipped over. It can probably hold a very small size water bottle about 3-4 inches tall.

Nice to have / wish list

1. Pet bowl and pet water container and parent water container to fit the cup.

She has not tried to chew through the mesh to escape. It would be great if Pet Gear can offer the Cat Harness as a safety feature. My cat can easily get out of the harnesses I have tried so far. Please drop me a note if you know of a safe and good quality Cat Harness for a small 10LB cat.

If you purchase this stroller for your indoor cat, start slowly. Place your cat in the stroller and get her used to it inside your house first. Be patient and reward your cat after each stroll. Put your pet's blanket inside the stroller so she knows it is a safe area. The next step is to take her in the stroller to your backyard and let her smell the plants and flowers and watch the birds. I do this when I attend to my garden. Do not leave her unsupervised as she might get excited by the birds and attempt to break loose. The final step is to take her out of the house on quiet streets. It is best to go out when the streets are not as busy(early in the morning or dusk) and definitely not on Trash days. Cats are afraid of dog barks so try to make the stroll an enjoyable experience for your pet when dogs are not around. Talk to your cat and let her see you. Your voice and presence would calm her down as she gets used to this stroller. It took my cat about a week to get used to her stroller. Be patient.

review_headline: The Best Flea and Heartworm Preventative, bar none!
review_body: I'm a huge supporter of this product and here's why:    I have several wonderful dogs and have given them the best care possible.  One of them is a toy breed and only weighs 3lbs.  Many years ago, I was using the top heartworm preventive on the market to protect her, at the advice of my vet.  That product was Heartgard, which is a chewable tablet.    Like most people at the time, I used Heartgard for all my dogs and had already had one diagnosed with heartworms, despite that he received his regular doses on time.  The chewables were almost as large as my toy breeds daily meal, so I found it very difficult to get her to eat it all.  When she was also diagnosed with heartworms, I wasn't surprised one bit.  The first time may have been that 1%, or whatever percentage it is that Heartgard claims might catch heartworms anyway, but the second was likely a result of not being able to get a small dog to eat the chewable prescribed to her.  And, yes, I did protest to my vet and Heartgard about the struggles I had feeding a large chewable to a small dog.    Later I began having money problems, and decided that I'd either need to get rid of my dogs, or figure out a way to lower the budget to care for them.  After doing a lot of reading, I discovered that Ivermectin was the active ingredient in Heartgard and could be purchased with little money at any Farmer's Co-Op.  So, I did just that, and I found it much easier to drop a small dose of liquid Ivermectin into the toy breed's mouth, rather then force her to eat an apparently not-so-tasty dog treat, that had been infused with this same ingredient.    For fleas, I had used Frontline Plus -- the leading flea preventative at the time -- since it was introduced on the market.  But over the years, it had become increasingly ineffective and stories began circulating that fleas had become immune to it (I suspect this is why Merial allowed the patent to expire, so you now have all sorts of no-name products that now use the same activeingredient, Fipronil.)  Finally it got to where it wasn't working at all and I had fleas everywhere, so I began looking for a new flea preventative, and that's when I discovered Revolution!    All the reviews for Revolution were overwhelmingly positive, which I thought was strange, since there wasn't a single vet that sold it in the large town where I live (several do today, but I suspect they were forced to carry it by customer demand, and most still push other brands that I believe give them bigger kickbacks.)  Not only did revolution kill fleas, but it also killed heartworms, which I loved, because even though Ivermectin worked, it still didn't protect against everything, and I just prefer using a product that's actually made for dogs.  It basically served the purpose of two preventatives, but at the price of one.  I've now used it for around 5 years without any heartworm problems, and the fleas disappeared immediately, and I haven't seen one in my house, or on my dogs, since.    Probably because Revolution was so great, everyone seems to have come out with a topical multi-preventative and most of them don't seem to be much different.  Topical treatments are great, because they're so simple to apply.  Unfortunately, I recently decided to try Frontline Multi, at my vet's insistence, because it was apparently undercutting the price of Revolution (which mysteriously went up a little after all the others were released.)  So far, it has worked okay, although my dogs do seem to scratch more lately, which is more likely due to an allergy, then fleas.    My main problem with Frontline Plus, however, is that it's more difficult to apply.  I'm still on a budget, and to save money, I buy the largest dose and split it appropriately between the dogs, using the guidelines for dosage volume per weight.  Frontline Plus seems to make this purposely difficult, with the main thing being how they made the tube more difficult to use with a syringe to draw out the dosage.  I've already decided to go back to using Revolution when I'm through with my stash of Frontline Plus, but after getting frustrated while treating my dogs this evening, I decided to write this review to help Revolution, which has been nothing short of wonderful.  While other pharmaceuticals work hard to drain your pocketbook while caring for your dogs, I have to hand it to Pfizer for giving dog owners a break, since Revolution seems to be the multi-preventative that drove down the price to treat heartworms and fleas.  And because Revolution is just easier to apply when using for multiple dogs.  As a result, I'll support Revolution by only buying their product in the future, because they earned such loyalty from me.

product_title: Aqueon Mini Bow 2.5 Gallon Desktop Aquarium Kit
review_headline: Why all the hate?  Decent tank!
review_body:
-1 star because the incandescent lamp is just wretched. I ended up going to Lowes and getting a custom sized piece of Acrylic cut and using an LED light on top. The one thing I like about the filter is that it allows the acrylic to sit flush onto the aquarium and no fish are ever going to escape this tank! My other gripe is the rim is loose on the front. That's a bit worrisome, but not much. I just have to make sure when I move the tank to grab from the bottom.

But the rest of the kit is great. I don't get some of these reviews. People saying the filter sucks up the food and causes cloudiness. Dude... if you're feeding so much that your filter is sucking up the food... it's not the filter causing cloudiness, it's the fact that you're WAY overfeeding. You feed ONLY ENOUGH that the fish eat in 5 minutes or less. If there is food floating about and not getting eaten... feed less. That's not the filter's fault. It has one job, and it's doing it.

And why all the hate on the filter? I'd heard so many negative reviews on it that I was fearing the worst. But it's awesome! It is so powerful that it pushes the fish and plants all around. It might take longer than a Fluval to filter all the gunk out when you first set the tank up, but honestly, for an Aqueon filter, it's pretty good! I've got another Aqueon filter on another 10 gallon tank and it does a good job. I only knock on Aqueon filters because I've had one bust after a month and a half's use. So they're not as dependable as say, Fluval. But there is no problem with power on this filter.

Yes, the acrylic/plastic scratches, and mine (which I won free from my LFS so I'm not looking a gift horse in the mouth here) was scratched a bit in the packaging. I expected that, because of the reviews, and well... it's plastic. It's to be expected. Just be careful, don't rub it with anything scratchy like those glass cleaner scrubbers, and don't use gravel, use sand instead.

The bow front does distort it a bit, and that's a little disheartening. But hey, I got it free, I'm not complaining.

Bonus though is... it's plastic. Unless you damage it or crack it yourself, it'll last forever. It'll never leak. There is no silicone to give way. I'm good with that. It's my 5th tank, my other 4 are all glass, and let me tell you, I have nightmares of my 40 gallon breeder busting.

Now, onto the complaints about the filter power cord getting wet. Aqueon reinforces their filters so it's ok if they get wet. I know your fear... electrocution... not fun. When I bought my first tank, an Aqueon 10 gallon kit, I was putting it together and had to call the store and ask "Is the power cord that hooks to the filter SUPPOSED to go in the water?" Yes, it's fine if it gets wet. If it's getting too wet or your having it leak down, what I hope is your drip loop, then you have filled the tank too full. It says in the directions to leave at least an inch from the top. I actually have left an inch and a half, and it barely gets wet at all.

I think most of these complaints are from people who clearly do not read the directions, and user error. It's people like that, that are the reason McDonald's has to put "Caution... Coffee... Hot" on their coffee cups. I mean, c'mon! It's a 5 gallon tub of plastic... how hard can it be?

TLDR: I like the tank. I like the filter. The light sucked, but a quick trip to Lowes fixes that.

review_body:
The ChemiPure Elite 11.74oz media bags came bulk in a sealed zip-locked bag. However, the media bags inside were not charcoal, but a discolored brown. The media bags were wet with water drops inside of the zip-locked bag. They appeared to be holdovers from a post-Katrina pet supply or dumped from a cargo carrier and salvaged.

I am immediately returning these for replacement. If the next shipment's ChemiPure bags are not as dry as they are inside a retail container (reference [[ASIN:B00BUFTTE2 Boyd Enterprises Chemi-Pure Elite for Aquarium, 11.74-Ounces]]), I'll advise and update my rating.

NOT RECOMMENDED AT THIS TIME

UPDATE 23 October 2014
Received replacement shipment - Bulk package shipped with other items. The top of the bulk package was torn or cut and carbon powder from the ChemiPure was inside the shipping box. Returning this shipment for replacement. I will give it one more try for a three star max-eval, due to the two 'damaged' shipments. NOTE: Per product description and instruction: \\"Keep Chemi-pure sealed in container until ready for use. Rinse lightly under running water....\\". There is no indication that Boyd is now shipping the media wet, or pre-rinsed, or open to air. Maybe the third time will be a charm.

STILL NOT RECOMMENDED AT THIS TIME!

review_headline: Kitty-pretties love it and eat A LOT
review_body:
I've been happy with Kirkland brand cat food for years. My oldest cat, not so much: she throws up a lot. So I was happy to try out another type of cat food, the results were mostly positive.

Happy:
My 11-year-old cat did not throw up once while eating this food.
All 4 of my cats (Siamese, 5-11 years old) LOVED this food like kitty treats.

Not happy:
The cats ate a lot of this food. I got the feeling it wasn't very filling -- the ingredients may have something to do with that.
At the rate they went through it, this food ends up being rather pricey. I'm not averse to getting my cats good food, but there are so many options I'd rather try something else before switching to this completely.

Conclusion:
I'll try some other brands first, but it's good to know there is at least one option that works for me and my cats.

product_title: Big Barker 7" Pillow Top Orthopedic Dog Bed for Large and Extra Large Breed Dogs (Headrest Edition)
review_body: We used to think our lab, Shiloh, was the Big Barker but then my son and his girlfriend adopted Abby, a Bouvier de Flandes, and now we know what a Big Barker truly is!  Abby is enjoying her senior years and with that comes a bit of soreness in the hind quarters.  She deserved a Giant orthopedic bed and Shiloh needed a large one.  We could easily accommodate Shiloh, but poor Abby always had a head or a rump hanging off her not-quite-large enough bed...until I found the BIG BARKER GIANT SIZED bed.  Ahhhh,  the absolute comfort for my weary bones, said Abby!  Yippee, said her human family!  Finally ALL of her could rest in the supreme comfort she has earned over her 13 years!  Both the Giant and the Large Big Barkers are well made, easily plumped, and magically comfortable.  We know this to be a fact, since we tested them for comfort ourselves before we offered them to our pups. The attached bolster is a favorite with both Abby and Shiloh and watching them relax on their Big Barkers reminds me of carefree Romans in ancient times lolling about just waiting for someone to pass the peeled grapes.  Very LUXE, indeed!  Thinking that both covers with their three-sided zip will be a breeze to remove and launder, never again having to struggle to pull out or stuff in an egg crate mattress through a single opening. That'll save our backs as well!  The 7" loft is higher than any other orthopedic bed we've tried and yet the step up is not so great as to cause any discomfort in mounting the mattress.  Abby, who has always been a world class sleeper--even if she was half on, half off her other beds, now looks as though her dreams have been achieved at both ends!  Our thanks to you, Big Barker folks, we are well pleased with our purchase and are very glad our search (often disappointing AND expensive) has ended in total satisfaction!

product_title: Marina Decor Polyresin Cave, Medium
review_headline: Realistic Looking Cave Is Great Addition To Aquarium!
review_body:
I bought this cave for my two baby red-eared slider turtles. I put it in a 10 gallon tank. My one turtle loves hide and would sleep in the cave all the time. Unfortunately, he outgrew it. Later on, my husband and I got two fish. The fish absolutely LOVED hanging out in the cave. However, they were feeder fish, so the turtles ate them about 1 year later when they were old enough to catch and eat the fish. I don't have fish and don't plan to get more unless I get more feeder fish for my turtles. As for my turtles, they have long outgrown this cave. They used it for about a good 1.5 years. It made the tank look very pretty, but I had to get rid of it to get other ornaments for the turtles - ones that made more sense.

I liked the design of the cave and how it was made - it looked very realistic and it was very easy to clean. I would just use a toothbrush to brush off any gunk that got stuck on the inside/outside of the cave. Because of the material the cave is made of, the whole cleaning process was easy and took less than 5 minutes, if even.

I know that this company sells different size caves. However, I wish they would sell one that is roughly the same size/height as the medium, but with a bigger opening. That way, I would've gotten more use out of it. I looked into getting the large cave, but for some reason, the hole looked shorter, and I wasn't sure if it'd be appropriate for the turtles. However, for the amount of time I got use out of it versus the price, I still feel it was worth it.

My dog did run off within a day of getting the Gibi and I was able to track her very accurately, though with a 10 min delay on her escape. (No real time alerts ever happened, always delayed.)
Pros: Custom safe zones (as opposed to the despised Tagg circle), low profile design, waterproof, 30 second tracking frequency (way better than the 3 minute for Tagg), multiple custom safe zones, friendly and excellent customer service.
Cons: Inaccurate locations, erratic notifications, NO app (on a phone the website is slow to respond and constantly logs you out), no activity tracking, crappy battery life (same as Tagg)
I would have swapped out Gibi for Tagg if Gibi had activity tracking and dealt with the other annoyances. After all, Tagg has them too. But as it is, Tagg showed itself to be slightly better off here overall. After Gibi irons out the kinks and gets an app up and running I will probably try them again. The custom safe zones and close to real time tracking is a big plus, however until then, gotta stick with what works (mostly) and offers more.

review_headline: but if you are thinking about using it to remove urine odors from something like a basement floor that is pourous
review_body: I paid $60.00 for a bottle of concentrate of this stuff and I just may as well have set a match to the money. My dog had an accident on the basement floor (urine) so I scrubbed it with my usual floor cleaner. The urine smell did not come out so then I used a bleach combination, still odor. After several attempts with various concoctions failed to get the odor out I decided to try this stuff. I followed the directions and as soon as it dried, still urine odor. I tried again using more of the product; still odor. I have even tried dumping this stuff directly on the spot, and it still didn't work. I ended up going to my local animal shelter and asked them if they could suggest anything that would get the odor out, and they were kind enough to give me some of the product they use at the shelter, and voila! Odor gone after the first use. I asked them about the odorxit and they told me they had sent them some to try at the shelter, but it didn't even work in the viewing area where they only view dogs, but do not house them there. So, if you are looking for an expensive air freshener this might work, but if you are thinking about using it to remove urine odors from something like a basement floor that is pourous, forget it and save your money. One reviewer said it worked on a berber carpet and they had saturated the carpet with this. My guess is that the carpet never actually dried, and my bet is if they ever pull it up the odor will still be in the subfloor.

product_title: SENTRY Flea Comb for Cats
review_body:
I can't even guess how many flea combs I've purchased during my life, well since I was old enough to have pets of my own anyway. I've tried double row combs which I don't like (because fleas tend to get caught between the rows and simply drop out), I've had super fancy squishy handled combs that have teeth covered in something so slick, the fleas just slide right off. But hey, at least the handle makes a great a stress relieving tool!

All that being said, this comb is by far my favorite! It does best on finer coats, cat or dog (but really fine dog hair). The one thing that makes this comb stand out from a LOT of other combs is that the part of the comb in which the teeth are inserted is not BLACK!!! I've yet to figure out why ANY flea comb manufacturer thinks grabbing super dark brown to black fleas using a comb with a black background is a good idea! The brighter the area where the teeth insert, the better. I almost bought a different comb that was displayed in the picture as being yellow but then I read the "small print" and saw that the comb was actually a blue darker than this! Grrr!

So anyway, I definitely recommend this comb and this color to cat owners in particular. I usually add water to a container like an old sour cream bucket or something similar and THEN only AFTER I put water in it I put dish soap into it (you don't need to use harsh chemicals). Why not the other way around? Flea circus anyone? Fleas are amazing at escaping as we all know, but MAN! Can they ever jump off soap bubbles! Nasty little beasts! Most of the time I'm able to simply tap them (especially males and young ones) off the comb (QUICKLY!!!) but sometimes the big mommas (literally the big female fleas) get stuck in between the teeth of the comb and I have to pinch the comb on each side to get her out. But at least they stay there stuck and don't jump away! Oh! This comb is also fantastic at picking up flea "dirt" which is really our pets' dried blood and the fleas' um...end product, on which I've recently learned eggs can be laid upon.

This is completely irrelevant flea trivia but if fleas weren't so disgusting, I would almost admire their ability to adapt and survive. Did you know it's only the females who feed on blood? And what really blew me away is that fleas actually pupate! They actually spin a cocoon....A COCOON!!! That's just one reason they're so hard to get rid of. They are able to stay tucked away dormant in our yards and homes for a LONG time until a nice meal comes by!

Sorry if I grossed you out too much!

Overall, this is an amazing flea comb!ur pets' dried blood and the fleas' um...end product, on which I've recently learned eggs can be laid upon.
