product_title: Brentwood 4-Inch Gel Memory Foam Orthopedic Dog Bed, 100-Percent Waterproof
review_headline: Definitely the preferred bed at our house
review_body:
I have purchased 3 of these beds in the last year. Each of my German Shepherds has one in their crate. In my opinion, the large (which I believe is around 46") fits very well in a 48" long wire crate. The first was purchased close to 11 months ago when my dog had ACL surgery. I needed something that would offer great support and comfort while maintaining structural integrity (no one wants a dog bed that goes flat). I also wanted it to be low maintenance and not cost $200-$300. I am confident in stating that it is absolutely worth the $100. The reason I have 3 is because all the dogs love them. That being said, there are negatives to almost everything and I want this review to be helpful to others. I will list the positive and negative aspects below for easy viewing.

Pros👍
Ships flat but plumps up within a matter of hours after opening
No weird chemical smells
Nice and thick gel foam/memory foam offering good support (hasn't lost its thickness after almost a year)
Lightweight and easy to move/perfect for a crate
Dogs really like them
Covers are tight over the bed and made of easy to clean materials (doesn't hold dog hair)
Outer cover is easy to unzip and is machine washable/dryer safe
Inner cover is made of a water resistant nylon type material and zips off
Very reasonably priced
Water resistant inner cover protects the foam core to make cleaning easier
When necessary you can clean the foam core

Cons👎
Inner cover zipper is junk and broke the first or second time I took it off
Inner cover is NOT waterproof....just resistant. If your large dog has an accident you will be stripping the bed down and cleaning the foam
It takes quite awhile for the foam to dry
Outer cover zipper is not top quality however mine has not broke
If you have more than one dog you'll have to buy enough beds or you'll feel guilty 😉

product_title: Nature's Variety Pride by Instinct Grain Free Dry Cat Food
review_headline: Expensive! Read Review for Great Alternative
review_body:
My cats normally eat grain-free [[ASIN:B004QW11EW Pure Vita Grain Free - 15 lbs]] by Nurti-Source, and like it just fine. It's a high end cat food, with very similar ingredients to Pride by Instinct Chesire's Recipe.

I placed a bowl of Pride next to their Pure Vita food. They ate it, but didn't demolish the bowl, like they might with a bowl of crappy but delicious Friskies. After about a week, they seem to like it as much as their old food, Pure Vita. They eat both at the same rate.

The biggest difference is the PRICE. Pricewise, Pride by Instinct Chesire's Recipe is about $4 per pound, while Pure Vita runs about $2.53 per pound. Right now, Pride runs $19.99 for 5 lbs, and Pure Vita Chicken is $38 for 15 lbs.

The ingredients are so very similar, although Pride's first ingredient is Chicken Meal, and Pure Vita's is Chicken. Other than that, the other ingredients are quite similar, just in mixed up order.

I wouldn't dissuade friends from buying this, but I'd recommend Pure Vita Chicken first.

product_title: StarMark Bob-A-Lot Interactive Dog Toy
review_headline: Fun, attractive toy with healthy benefit!
review_body:
Love this toy! Needed something to slow my rescue puppy down when she eats and this toy looked interesting. Watched a review on YouTube that sold me on the product, so I bought it. It took about two tries and she figured it out. Went from her eating her 1 cup of food in 5 seconds flat to it taking a few minutes, and that's only because I still have the dispensing door wide open while she learns the toy. It's fun to watch her paw at the toy and bump it with her nose to get it moving, and then she hoovers up the food as she goes. She's a coonhound/shepherd mix and very motivated to learn and play. She's heavily into chewing right now and has tried to use the toy for chew, but since it's heavy (weighted at the bottom) and rounded (moves) she gets frustrated quickly and moves onto more appropriate chew toys and bones in her artillery.
Pro's:
- Increases time it takes to eat her meal, even with small pieces of puppy food.
- Adjustable dispensing door will allow me to increase the feed time even more.
- Doesn't hold interest as a chew.
- Entertaining to watch her play and eat.

Cons:
- Doesn't seem like an easy product to wash (to be honest I've not really looked into how to clean the outside).
- Can be loud on hard floors (the few times she's tried picking it up and dropped it, it's rather loud on the tile with the weighted bottom and hard plastic).

All in all I think this is a fun toy and has the added benefit of slowing feed times a bit. The price is also very attractive. I've already recommended this toy to friends and family with dogs.

review_headline: Don't inflict this product on your pet.

I asked my brother if the dog has fleas and he said he shouldn't I just gave him some anti flea medication from the pet store. I looked at the dogs belly and he had fleas. I asked my brother for the brand of anti flea medication and where he bought it.

I went to the pet store and said this Zodiac product didn't work and the clerk said yes many people have had the same complaint. I asked why they sell it and the lady said it is cheap and works for some.

I then went to the Vet and asked about Zodiac and they said we don't sell it because it is dangerous and doesn't work. I bought a recommended anti flea medication from the vet. After using the vet recommended medicine Max was fine that day.

Max the dog spent 3 weeks in discomfort thanks to this garbage product and according to the vet it could have been worse. Don't inflict this product on your pet.

product_title: 2-Pack PetSafe Basic Bark Control Collar
review_body: Works like a charm.  My 4-year old female went to bark several times in a row, yelped once as it kicked in, and then over the next hour the barks got less and less.  It only took one session for her to be quiet in the house, and she's remained that way when the collar is off.  I'm sure she'd pick up the habit again, and so will be using the collar off and on when needed, but the collar worked as advertised: barking is greatly reduced.    I tried it again on a very barky, rambunctious 1-year old that was visiting the office and that one took longer to figure it out.  It went on a loud barking streak, and after about 20 seconds jumped straight up in the air as the collar kicked in hard.  This quieted him down for about a minute before he launched into a long barking session again and got zapped hard again.  He basically would ignore the collar until it got to the highest levels and then yelp like crazy.  I had to intervene and calm him down so that his barks about being scared wouldn't trigger more zaps, and then he settled down and is now quiet when at the office.      The bottom line is this is a training tool, not a magic collar, and you have to adjust how its used to the personality of the dog.

product_title: SeaChem Safe Water Conditioner 250g / 8.8 Oz
review_headline: Great Product for Removing Chlorine From Your Aquarium
review_body:
I was originally using Seachem Prime to treat my aquarium water and then reading some forums I discovered Safe and decided to do some research on this. It's essentially the same product as Prime just in dry powdered form and more concentrated so you save money in the long run. This product should last me years even with weekly water changes.

I have a 30 gallon tank so whenever I do a water change I usually siphon out about 15% of my water. I then put the dose of Safe into my tank as my bucket isn't very large. If you are changing water in a larger tank, you can also treat each individual bucket as you want but I find it easier to just dose the entire tank and then start adding in the new water after making sure it is the same temperature as the water in my tank. This is especially true if you are using a siphon that hooks up to your sink or hose for quick water changes.

I follow the instructions from Seachem's website:

Directions for all other sizes (this is different if you buy the 50g or 100g sizes!)

Use 1.25 g (1/4 tsp.) for every 1,250 L (300 gallons) as needed to reduce chlorine and chloramine or use 1.25 g (1/4 tsp.) for every 300 L (75 gallons) for ammonia.

Since my tank is only 30 gallons I use (1/10) of that dose to treat the entire tank. That ends up being 1/40 of a teaspoon so I had to buy some smaller measuring spoons. I use 1/32 of a teaspoon and have seen no ill effects with using this slightly higher dose as you would be using more for ammonia anyways.

I've been using Prime for years and now been using Safe for over a month and have had no issues with my fish and chlorine and they seem very happy and healthy. You can also double or triple this dose in an emergency if you and need to quickly detoxify nitrites and nitrates.

It keeps coming loose as my dog is swimming and causes the straps to rub against her belly and sides.  I keep noticing little bald spots where the hair has been rubbed off.  It doesn't seem to bother her, but she would never dream of complaining, so I get a little obsessed about readjusting the underbelly velcro straps so they don't cause any chaffing to start.  It's just annoying to me thinking that something she loves doing so much, swimming, could possibly cause her any hurt or discomfort.  If she had a more natural ability to swim on her own, maybe I wouldn't be so concerned about the velcro coming unfastened.  But, Boxer's are not known for their swimming abilities because of their very muscular athletic bodies, and they seem to have to work especially hard to keep afloat, so a life jacket is a must. review_body: As others have said, I was pretty skeptical about the effectiveness of the thundershirt. However, I was pleasantly surprised from the very first time I put it on our dog. The one area that the thundershirt has not helped our dog with is crate anxiety, hence the 4 stars. The poor thing about has a heart attack if left in the crate without a human in the room with her.  I really hoped the thundershirt would make a difference, but so far it has not. I'm going to try letting her sleep in the crate with thundershirt on, as someone else suggested, and see if that helps.  I'll update if it does.

product_title: EHEIM Quick Vac Pro Automatic Gravel Cleaner and Sludge Extractor
review_headline: Best investment I ever made for my tank
review_body:
I almost didn’t buy this based on a customer review that mentioned a lot of debris blowing out of the filter and issues with possible leaking into the battery compartment. But I REALLY needed something like this and since I couldn’t locate any other item even remotely similar, I ended up ordering it anyway.
Let me say I feel it is one of the better investments I have made for my aquarium. Wish I had something like this on a bigger scale for my pond too!
As for the customer video showing debris blowing out, I did NOT have that problem. The filter material is very fine and I had no debris or bubble issues while using it. The batteries that came with the unit were cheap batteries not Duracell as another customer mentioned. But that’s ok with me. The battery compartment did not leak and fit very snug. The filter was easy to remove and clean. I also sucked up some gravel and small plant material up into the impeller area and no issues with it clogging, I just gave it a hard shake and they came back out. It did a great job of picking up debris. At first I didn’t think it was doing much but then looked at the filter and was surprised at how much it picked up. A few of my fish came too close for comfort to the inlet while in use and I was happy to see that there was not enough power to suck them up. NOTE: they only came close, I do not know what would happen if they came right up to the opening and I wasn’t about to experiment with them.
However, there are a few down sides. For larger tanks this is great, but for smaller tanks or for tanks with a lot of decorations there are some things that can be improved upon. The bottom part is too large for smaller tanks and for trying to get around decorations. A smaller inlet would make it easier to vacuum around decorations. Also, if the entire filter area must be summered while using, then the unit is too long for an average 10 gallon tank. I have a 16 gallon tall aquarium and I couldn’tuse the extension part, which I would rather use since it has the cutout edges. I had to use it just with the impeller cover, which did work fine, but a shorter model with a smaller inlet would have been an improvement. Perhaps they could make a couple different versions of this.
Even so, I was very happy with this purchase and highly recommend it.

product_title: DOGTEK Sonic Bird House Bark Control Outdoor/Indoor
review_body:
I was very skeptical about the effectiveness of this product before I bought it. After reading many reviews, as many bad as good, I decided to try it. We have a large breed dog, Great Pyrenees, and three small dogs, Lhasa Apso/Maltese mix. I was afraid that if this product did work it would only work for the large dog as I have read some poor reviews from small dog owners.

review_body:
I read somewhere that a small percentage of dogs are not affected by these and was dreading that my neighbor's dog might fall into that percentage. I purchased it anyway and hoped for the best. This thing works like a charm on both my neighbor's dogs! After talking to my neighbor and reporting them to the HOA, they still do not care about their dog barking. It is such a lack of respect and consideration that it makes me so upset. It is like a slap in the face because we have two dogs and we make sure they are behaved and do not incessantly bark out of respect and consideration to them. Dogs do not bark just because. I do not want to hear that rubbish that dogs are dogs and they will bark. Unacceptable! Bad, irresponsible, lazy dog owners who lack common sense are the cause of misbehaving dogs.

About 90% of the time I am in my backyard, their dog runs out there and starts barking. Or sometimes when they hear a noise out in the front yard/street, it is out there barking. And the worst part, my bedroom is right next to their back gate! Now, my neighbor does keep the dog from barking in the evening, but there's been occasions where it is 6 a.m. and it is out there barking. I know they can hear their dog barking, because I can hear it barking from even the farthest part of my house.

So, anytime I hear their dog barking, I like to go right up to the wall, stick my arm over, aim in its direction, and daze it with this. The first time I used it, the dog took off running to the other end of the yard. It barked some more, I hit the button again, and it ran through its doggie door and back into the house. WOW! Amazing! Since then, I've only had to use a handful of times and now I don't hear their dog anymore.

Now, I heard some reviewers saying that after awhile, dogs will get used to this and it becomes less effective. I even read one reviewer saying that they purchased a mega phone and used it in conjunction with this and it solved the problem. I try to use this sparingly so their dog doesn't get used to it. But after using it only several times, I haven't heard the dog barking at all in awhile. Such a wonderful thing!

Hopefully this continues to work out for me! Peace at least... for now anyways (fingers crossed).

review_headline: Great for extra small pets. I wish it accommodated my dog better.
review_body:
Attmu, maker of several odds and ends products have made a budget friendly Pet Carrier for small dogs and cats.

▶ Package Contents
• Attmu Pet Carrier
• Shoulder Strap

▶ Hardware
This nylon pet carrier is 12” x 9” x 17” inches, about an inch less than the product dimensions. I understand that you could consider each side as an inch longer when flattened, but when unfolded, the overall product is an inch shorter. The product is very simple, with a zipper to open the carrier on the front and back, an additional small zipper pocket (3.75” x 9” inches) on the side for any leashes or collars, and four tabs to change the position of the adjustable shoulder pad.

What I really like best about this pet carrier is the build of the product, as it is an open concept soft carrier; allowing pets to not be scared because they aren’t in a closed environment. I would, however, not use this product if your pet finds closed spaces hostile. I could easily see it being abused. That being said, I find this product sturdy for the material it is made out of.

▶ Testing
I used this pet carrier while taking my Pompeian “Jax” to the vet. He is under 10 pounds and a beautiful fluffy white and black spotted coat (like a cow). Although he is able to stand in this carrier, he is very uncomfortable. His hair would make it out of the holes, making him adjust himself often. This carrier should state it is for extra small pets, preferably cats.

▶ Final Thoughts
It does its job as a carrier, but I wouldn’t use this as a long term solution. The last thing I need is an agitated pet when going to the vet. I would recommend this pet carrier, but because my under 10 pound Pompeian was uncomfortable I see the size of this carrier could be a tad wider, which is why I give this a 4 star rating. Honestly, this is perfect for most cats and extra smaller dogs.

Pros:
+ A very smart design. Well vented and comfortable (for pets that would fit).

Cons:
- My less than 10 lb Pomeranian was very uncomfortable in the carrier. I would have preferred a little larger carrier.

review_headline: I really can't say that I 'personally' love 'em, but my beautiful Golden Retriever gal
review_body:
Okay, I really can't say that I 'personally' love 'em, but my beautiful Golden Retriever gal, Molly sure does! What I do like/love about them is that they are made here in America of seemingly very good ingredients. After so many incidences of pet foot products produced in a particular other country containing toxic contaminants, I WILL NOT, NOT EVER feed any foreign made products to my precious girl.

That being said, I have bought this brand of treats many times over the years, but had never purchased the LARGE size. And boy, are they really LARGE! I guess I didn't envision their size until I opened the box. Well, I like to give Molly a nice little treat when she has been a good girl, but really don't want to give her such a big treat that it will add too many extra calories to her daily intake. So, what to do? Well, I talked my 'other half' into taking a bunch of them down to the basement and cut them up into smaller pieces! Hey, it worked wonderfully! As a bonus, when he brought them back upstairs, he was covered in 'treat dust' which made Molly cling to him, wanting to lick all of the crumbs off of his shirt! See, this is a very versatile product to get your dog to adore you in many fun ways!

Seriously, buy this product in whatever size/flavor you like. I bet your dog will love them (and you), too!

review_headline: Dog Appeasement Pheromone Helps, isn't a miracle cure.
review_body:
My dog: A 100 lb, 12 (ish) year old, rescued black lab with severe separation anxiety, along with a nice case of thunderstorm/fireworks anxiousness to round out her quirks.

We've tried Thundershirts, calming chews, tabs and sprays of all kinds, essential oils, food additives, lovies (she has a dozen), Kong with special treats, nearly tried it all. The Pet Naturals of Vermont Calming Chews seem to work best, though they tend to make her pretty groggy and wear off pretty fast.

So, I thought I would try DAP. Although the instructions indicated it would take up to 4 weeks to see improvement, within 6 hours she was mellower than I've ever seen her. Happy even.

This lasted for a couple days before she seemed to level out and the effects became less noticeable.

We found that combining the DAP - we plug it in a few hours before we leave her - with calming chew(s) administered an hour before leaving seems to work best.

When we return fewer lovies are sopping wet and scattered in front of the door (which is where DAP is plugged in) and fewer indications of her pacing, climbing the stairs, pacing, panting and drooling all over the place.

Which is a win in my book.

I'm here buying more, plus the spray, will let you know how the spray works.

product_title: Fluval C Power Filter
review_headline: Fluval C3 Will not Last - Hagen Blames Customer for Defects
review_body: I bought the filter 2 years ago.  The filter worked fine for 2 years.  But last week, I was washing the filter and motor assembly in my sink.  After I was done, I noticed the metal shaft that secures the impeller was gone!  It turns out it went down the drain.  A new motor assembly with the shaft is nearly as much as a new filter. So I wrote Hagen to see if they will send me a new metal shaft.  After a lengthy period, I was finally told that their warranty does not cover \\"physical loss\\".  So they want me to buy a new shaft at a cost with shipping of $21!  That is nearly half the price of a new filter.  The fact the metal impeller shaft fell out of the assembly is a leap to say it was \\"physical loss\\".  The only reason there was a \\"physical loss\\" was because the impeller shaft was not secured inside the motor assembly.  I recommend that when you wash the filter, to do it in a bucket to avoid losing any parts.  The cost to replace those parts if you lose them will be high.    9/13/14 - I wrote back to Hagen and they decided to send me an impeller shaft under warranty rather than saying I lost it.  I never knew it would come out and on my larger Fluval, I see a rubber washer in the bottom of the impeller compartment that also came out when washing the filter in a bucket.  So be warned, these parts can unexpectedly fall out and you may not get them replaced without a cost. I moved my review to 3 stars because they agreed to replace the part.  The filter itself works well, but I am unsure of how long it will last.

product_title: Kaytee Complete Dwarf Rabbit Kit
review_headline: Reasonably good quality/value like most SuperPet (Kaytee) cages, but WAY TOO SMALL for most buns &the food included is unhealthy
review_body:
I purchased this for usage when we go on vacation as I take my rabbit everywhere and needed something to put her food and litter pan in (she free roams my house and wherever we go, so I didn't need anything big since she only eats and poops inside of it...) I was really surprised by the size as I did not realize how small this would be. My rabbit's main litter pan actually does not fit in this, and so the cage itself became a big litter pan filled with CareFresh and timothy hay. As she's a somewhat bigger bunny, the cage is not long enough for her sprawl laid out and her head almost touches the top of the cage when she is sitting up. Since this was mainly to house the litter pan and some hay, it wasn't a big deal. However, if I was going to lock this cage with her in it, I would have serious reservations over the size not being suitable for her. If this is the primary living quarters for your rabbit, I strongly urge looking at larger sizes!

The build quality is similar to the extra large SuperPet (now Kaytee) habitat I have. It's reasonably good quality for the price. By using the wire top and solid bottom, this is safer for rabbit feet, helps prevent bedding/pellets from being scattered everywhere, and allows adequate air ventilation. It also allows bunny to get a good view of his/her surroundings. The metal wire top is coated with a white paint. This coating helps to prevent rust and on my main one I have had for 6 years it held up well for 3-4 years. It uses the same friction locking mechanism of other Kaytee cages. On my main cage, this lock broke after about a year and a half of daily usage (which is what made me decide to allow Lilly to free roam since I no longer had a cage that locked and did not want to spend the money on a new one.) The door uses a sloped ramp when it opens, which I have always liked. Overall, it's a good build quality for the price, and uses build characteristics that make it a safe habitat. I personally like the design of the Living World cages much more, but they are generally a little more expensive than SuperPet.

.
.
So why am I giving this three stars? Because:
1) the size is not suitable for rabbits; and
2) the food that is included is not formulated for optimal rabbit health & contains ingredients of questionable safety

First, I do not feel the size of this cage is at all appropriate for most rabbits and that labeling this as a rabbit cage is not responsible marketing. If you are thinking about this as the primary living habitat for your rabbit, I do not think this size is a good choice because it is too small both in terms of width/length and not nearly tall enough for even standard-sized rabbits. This may be a better match for the smallest of dwarf rabbits whom are kept inside of this cage for only a small portion of the day, but if bunny is going to spend a significant portion of his/her life in this, your bunny will greatly appreciate something significantly longer and taller.

The other reason is because of the food that is included (Fiesta Max) and how someone buying a starter set for their first bun may not know that Fiesta Max is notorious for having ingredients of questionable safety while simultaneously lacking certain trace minerals that are needed for optimal health (which is also not responsible marketing in my opinion.) Kaytee makes some high quality foods such as FortiDiet, but Fiesta Max is among the worst foods made (on the healthy side, Oxbow Bunny Basics is considered by many [myself and my Vet included] to be the best commercial rabbit food on the market.)

You as the pet parent are the best judge of if this cage is suitable for your rabbit in your situation. But given Kaytee (AKA SuperPet), PennPlax, and LivingWorld (LW makes SUPER nice rabbit habitats!) all offer rabbit cages that are longer, wider, and taller, I think you will find that a larger cage from one of those makers is a better habitat for your pet-family member.r your pet-family member.

product_title: World's Best Cat Litter
review_body:
We have been using this for almost a year now. It has it's pros and cons which I believe may be the same for most cat litters. On the plus side, it does clump very well and it is perfectly safe to throw the clumps in your toilet and flush. This alone is a great convenience over run-of-the-mill varieties. Another positive is that it is made of purely natural materials, making it safe to handle by both your cat and yourself. It also does a good job at absorbing bad odors. It does not mask them with some perfume-y scent. It just does away with them.

On the negative side, it can sometimes be a bot dusty. Kitty's paw prints may show up on darker-colored furniture. And since the granules are lightweight, they are easily carried away with kitty, leaving a little debris around the litter box. While these are both issues, they are not HUGE issues and can easily be compensated for by modifying your litter box setup. I recommend a covered litter box if your cat is particularly messy when covering up. We are also considering trying out those tacky surfaces that will hold on to debris that is carried out on kitty's paws.

Another negative is that the litter can attract insects. In our case, small flies, gnats, and the like. We found this to be a problem more with keeping the unused litter in a bag nearby with a clothespin to keep it shut. The insects found their way into the unused litter and it became a nuisance. I recommend keeping your unused litter in an airtight container. This improved our situation immensely.

All-in-all, a very good litter that is kitty-, human, and environment-safe.

product_title: Taste of the Wild Canned Cat Food
review_headline: Great Ingredients, But Just Lacking The Quality I Hoped For
review_body:
When it comes to companies who truly care about the health of the animals they are providing food for, Taste of the Wild is among the best. They are magnificent. But- unfortunately, their cat food is lacking. My dogs like a few of their canned dog food varieties, and don't mind their dry dog food. But this canned cat food is definitely not up-to-par in my cats opinions.

I have four cats, all eat all kinds of foods regularly. We supplement a lot of their diet with chicken, turkey, tuna, and salmon. So they are spoiled on real meat and that does tend to make them a bit more picky when it comes to what they will eat. With that being said, they do easily delve into a few of the cheaper canned cat foods I buy- like 9 Lives and Fancy Feast. But they will barely touch this Taste of the Wild formula. Let's way the pros and cons, shall we?

Pros:

Lots of gravy: Two of my cats are gravy lovers. One, very old cat (my old lady- I lovingly call her), is a picky eater who, in her old age, has decided she only wants to eat the gravy of any food she's ever given. Because she's so old, we happily oblige to her commands and try to give her gravy-filled foods. This food does have a lot of gravy, which makes it easy for her to eat and she loves slurping it up.

Easy-open can: As with most cat foods now-a-days, the can of this food has a pull-tab that allows you to easily open it. Always a plus in my mind. Can't pass up convenience!

Great ingredients list: Taste of the Wild is notorious for putting a lot of focus on all-natural ingredients and leaving out the preservatives and additives. This food follows suit and does have a pretty great ingredients list compared to other foods.

Cons:

Not a lot of meat: My two younger boys are only about a year old and they need their meat. They love chewing and often will gobble up entire raw chicken bones! So when canned foods lack any sort of meat in them, my younger cats feel hungry afterwards. Even after they finish a can of this food, they're still whining for another meal. I think this is largely because the food has way more gravy, and way less meat than other brands they eat.

Expensive: This brand is pretty pricey, and the fact that my cats aren't too fond of it, leaves me feeling as though I'm just paying a bit too much. My cats prefer cheaper brands, and typically I wouldn't complain about the price. But because of the high gravy amount, and the minimal meat- I don't quite feel like I'm paying what this food is worth.

One-flavor: I can only find one flavor of canned cat food from Taste of the Wild. Maybe I haven't heard of any others? But animals need variety, nonetheless. One flavor may work for some picky eaters, but most animals require different tastes and textures- which is not only healthy for their body, but it mentally stimulates their mind as well. This one-flavor food would work great when mixed with other foods occasionally, but as a single food I don't think any cat would enjoy it every single day.

Overall, this product was just 'meh'. Definitely great in terms of ingredients and health. But just lacking quality, and my cats didn't care for it. product_title: Interpet Limited Superpet Hay Manger
review_headline: I've used many hay feeders as I am yet to find one I love...so far this is the best, but it still isn't a product I call "great"
review_body:
This is the primary feeder I use to give hay to my rabbit. Overall, I think it is a good product but not a great product...thus far, this is the best product of its type I have used.

Timothy hay is simply messy...there's no way around it. Simultaneously, it's arguably the most important thing for rabbits (beyond air and water, perhaps.) Not offering fresh timothy hay 24-7 really isn't an option, so I needed something to hold the hay. I've used a few of these hay racks. Thus far, all of them spill hay through the sides of cages. And thus far, this one has been the most durable; the plastic models I have used all quickly turn into modified chew toys.

More or less, you stuff hay in here, hang it up on by hooking it on the wires in the cage, and Bunny grabs it whenever he/she pleases. Being metal, it holds up well. Being coated, it resists rust and is easy to clean. Having a lot of openings, it is easy for rabbits to get to. Having openings that aren't too big, it avoids the risk of a rabbit getting her head stuck in the hay feeder (except for possibly the smallest of rabbits.) And for the most part, sharp angles are avoided which reduces the chance of injury. So it works.

But on the less positive side, this is still messy as hay gushes out the side of it and onto the floor, it doesn't hold hay super tight, it doesn't have a very big capacity, it doesn't latch on to the cage (a tugging rabbit can dislodge it pretty easily), and the salt hanger (which I advise against using!) does present a possible poking hazard. Additionally, the angle it holds the hay at (a 'V') makes it so that if bunny wants a piece from the bottom, it's going to spill most of or all the contents. (It is also worth noting that if your rabbit tends to bite hay feeders often, metal MAY NOT be the best choice due to risk of damage to the mouth.) (It's also worth noting that for smaller animals and very small rabbits, this could potentially present an issue for a stuck head and if I had a rabbit like a super-super small Netherlands dwarf I would probably be somewhat hesitant to use this.)

This last part can get really annoying because rabbits LOVE to play with their food (and darn near everything else.) As rabbits are selective feeders rather than outright grazers, one issue you may encounter is that Bunny will more or less pull most of or all of the hay out of the feeder prior to eating most (or any) of the hay, giving the rabbit-equivalent of a \\"foam party\\" in her cage. Sometimes rabbits decide they have found the PERFECT piece of hay, and must either eat that first, or perhaps relocate it to a safe place to enjoy at a later time. With how timothy hay bundles up and how this is held in a \\"V\\" formation, her attempts to extract her favorite strand of hay can result in a ton (or all) of the hay coming out. So this is partly due to the design, but partly due to how rabbits eat!

So here I am today, still using the product, with more satisfaction than from other hay feeders, but still not thrilled. As you want to try to elevate the hay for sanitary reasons, a hay feeder is a must-have. Thus far, this is the best product I have used...and while it is not perfect, it does help make hay feeding a little easier, and it does improve the hygiene somewhat, and at the price, it's reasonably inexpensive and it is reasonably durable. So why not give it a try?

product_title: 8in1 Safe Guard Canine Dewormer
review_headline: Highly effective and easy to administer
review_body:
Two features about this dewormer attracted me: the range of types of worms it treats and the fact that the treatment is spread over 3 days. It worked perfectly for our dog and was a cinch to give her. The medicine comes in three little pouches, and it's a very fine powder. I imagine most dogs would lick it up with their regular food. Our dog was feeling sick enough to turn her nose up at the usual kibble, so we mixed the powder into some plain mashed potatoes. Instant success. The powder blended right in to the potatoes, which are easy on a sick dog's stomach. She started feeling better after the first dose and was completely better the day after the final, third dose. She tested clear of worms at the vet the next week.

This is definitely the kind of treatment you give for a dog that has worms. I think it's overkill as a preventative measure, though. There are cheaper liquid or pill dewormers that can be given in one dose, once a month. That's what we'll start doing from now on, but this brand is great for effectively solving an existing problem.

product_title: AquaTop UV Sterilizing Pump - SP5UV
review_headline: Not a terrible choice but not great either
review_body:
I got this because I have a aquatop 21 gallon aquarium and it was recommended as it isn't that big and fits in the tank without taking up a lot of room. I was surprised at how big it was for a small uv light/ filter. I ordered it and was impressed with how easy to take it apart that it was. But putting it back together is another story. My first time was while it was all dry and I had no issues at all. But when I went to clean it after a week, the filter media wouldn't go back in the grated section. It seemed to stop 3/4ths of the way in. So I let it sit and dry out for a few hours and then tried it dry and it got most of the way in. It would be nice to have other options to pull it in the tube rather than pushing it up. Of course in typical aquatop fashion the directions have something to be desired as they are practically non existent. It does have 2 power lines. One for the uv light and one for the pump. It does come apart easily enough. In fact upon cleaning it the first time I realized my pump was missing the power flow regulation switch on the front. Amazon fixed this by quickly replacing the pump. 2nd device came complete.

Overall, I'm satisfied with it but in no hurry to be cleaning it again and will be keeping an eye out for a different small one for my tank.

(I had just gone to the minimart). I put in a new set and once again, she was much better. It doesn't stop all barking, because the dog has to bark to trigger it, but that's okay. A single bark or two isn't a problem. The batteries seem to go quickly but they are very cheap and the quiet is so very worth it. Note that my dog is very small. I don't know if it would work on a larger dog.

review_headline: Needs to make feather / arm replacements available. (or if avail, better accessible)
review_body: The main problem is that the feather and arm attachment can not stand up for long against standard cat play / abuse. And that SmartyKat does not offer a way to replace the arm or feather. At least not that I have found and I surely have checked. My 4 month old kitten has torn the feather off a couple of times already. The first time i just sewed the velcro / wire hook back on with just a couple of loops of thread. I did the same thing again the next time that she tore it off. The third time I doubled up the thread and it through 4 times. Giving it 8 loops of thread. That lasted about 2 weeks. Then i accidentally stumbled on the best way to fix it. I had placed the thread in a box in the closet when I went to get it out I saw a couple of twisty ties and thought that I would give that a try. I took a twisty tie and stripped off the outer plastic. Then inside very thin wire went through the velco thing very easily. I then attached the leading wire hook and twisted it together. And snipped the wire as close as possible. Made sure that the wire tie would not pose a safety threat in any way and attached the feather. And that fixed it permanently. If SmartyKat offered the feather and arm attachments available separately then it would be better worth it.

product_title: Blackhole Cat Litter Mat - Super Size Rectangular 30" X 23" - Blackhole Litter Mat
review_headline: Does what it is supposed to do (much to my surprise)
review_body: I have 2 Siamese/Ragdoll cats.  I use the Swheat Scoop litter, which I love, but it is very lightweight.  Therefore, it tracks away from the litter box a little bit more than the heavier clay litter.  I have hardwood floors and I've been finding it all over the floor leading from the litter box room, which is a small closet-like room under the stairs. Imagine Harry Potter sleeping there. It's very annoying because the only thing I'm vacuuming up is a little litter that has spread around the room leading from the box. It's really not much at all, but noticeable on the wood floor and annoying. So I did a lot of research and decided that this mat made the most sense.  It was quite large and covered a good size area in front of my oversized litter box.  It is a rubbery type of material and stays in place.  I did put the end of it slightly under the litter box.  The cats investigated it immediately and seemed to love it.  They pawed at it and laid on it.  They weren't bothered by it at all. And now they totally ignore it. And considering it is a rubbery material, it seems to have no smell to it.  At least any that I can detect.  I was quite doubtful that this would work.  Oh, I figured it would catch the litter that was brought out of the box quite well.  But I doubted it would stop the tracking.  I was wrong.  It seems that when they exit the box and hit the mat a great deal of litter comes off their paws and ends up in the mat.  I don't even have any litter slightly off the front of the mat.  Color me surprised.  As far as cleaning it, since I have hardwood flooring everywhere, I use a 2 gal shop vac with a brush attachment to vacuum.  It does a spectacular job on the floors and is great at picking up animal hair.  Much better than those stupid stick brooms.  I just go over the mat with the brush attachment and it vacuums up the litter right out of the little holes.  I really can't find anything to complain about with this mat.  I would recommend it and I would purchase it again.

product_title: FURminator deShedding Tool for Cats
review_headline: Try to enjoy your time with them when doing this
review_body:
It does what it says. It does not provide a hair free home, in fact you will have more hair than before.
I did not think they could have improved on such a chore. but they did with this design AND the
technique you should use to get the most out of each brush stroke.

The design kinda requires you maintain some form of that angle toward the fur (when you come into
contact with skin, angle top of head [not the whole brush. Hold it straight up and down and then
push head a little forward to get the angle] a few degrees forward. This angle is what does it) so to
collect hair ON the brush. It takes hair off so well you will find bails of hair flying away, on the
sheets, the sofa and so on. You cant brush more than a few times, at a time, in order to collect
hair on the brush (it only holds so much at a time), otherwise it collects on your pet and everywhere
else. Flatten pet, angle, brush just a few times and remove hair and start again. Once, or twice a week,
is all you need. I brush 4 times, remove hair, and do over several times until much less hair, BUT
dont overdue, or you will find bald patches (I had to wait three weeks for one of our friends hair to grow
back) and you are done. Takes a few minutes. And when you think you are done, look your pet once
over and you may find tufts of hair brushed away that didnt make it on brush and just get those too.

The button is OK, but you can pull the hair away yourself (your choice).

The pattern would be comb [and hold] edge at an angle, 4 strokes and then remove the hair
collected and place where the cats wont try to eat, or lick it (or try to remove it from the trash to
play/eat) and brush again.

Careful. The handle is heavy (perhaps to aid in the angle motion) so gentle when doing their head
(or thump) and down the body you will have to hope they flatten their hips (rear legs) so you dont
bump into them while brushing (and possibly cause bruising under the skin).

No marking which way to fasten teeth protector (you will need it because teeth will break and may
cause injury so this guard is a must), but the extra space side goes to the bottom of the brush
head (down).

Try to enjoy your time with them when doing this. They do appreciate it and realize it, especially
after noticing a newer form of brushing and the result. I think they can feel the difference with FAR
less hair). You should also realize this isnt your ordinary kind of brushing, so careful. It is new in
weight, style, discipline and result. It will be worth it once you master it. And both female and
male cats have nipples so I havent yet been able to even consider their tummies. Best left alone.
The gentler you are the more they will look forward to the effort which will turn out a way of showing
them your affection.

Brush slow, not fast.Do not press hard against their skin, just to get through coat. The blades are
not really sharp so there isnt a cutting action. It is more of a pull/raking action (test it on an old
towel. It will not cut the threads, but pull them out. That should tell you how effective the teeth
design on The Furminator is.

Problem with AMZN selling counterfeit product. Manufacturer (good customer support) tells me
1. Only get it from Amazon themselves as seller and 2. No hologram (small, paw sticker at upper
left facing of packaging and under platic cover), dont get it. And the newer models have the push
button.

You WILL be impressed with how much hair your pet actually has that it doesnt need and walks
around with (and manages to eat through licking) after using The Furminator. And the AMZN
pricing is $15 less (and no s/h) than locally. But if I couldnt be sure it was the real product, I would
have had to spend the extra money.
Good work,guys ((United Pet Group)! Wonderful product. Thank you.

Now if only I could find a use for the bags of hair collected? Warm material. Maybe filler for stuffed
toys, or comforters, but they would have to be cleaned first (allergens). If you come up with ideas,
let us Amazonites know.

product_title: Back to the Roots Water Garden
review_headline: Fun at first, but a major headache after a while
review_body:
I bought this item fully intending to love it and have my own little aquafarm at home. Unfortunately, this unit has a significant number of flaws and is not suitable for long-term use. Some of the major issues:

- The tank is NOT self-cleaning, in spite of the manufacturer's claims. In the first month or so, yes, the water will clear up and remain more or less clear. However, algae will start to build up over time, and once it's set in, it's hard to get rid of. I tried a Nerite snail, it died, so I bought a small catfish and he helps to scrub the sides, but one little catfish alone can't get rid of all of the algae, and the small tank won't support a larger fish population. One positive thing I can say here is that the tank never stank, and even if you pressed your nose up to the grills you'd only notice a faint \\"earthy\\" odor.

- The tank is a major pain to clean. You must empty out most of the water and scrub the sides to clean off the algae. This is made more difficult by the fact that you cannot remove the top without also extracting the pump and attached optional heater. Re-inserting the pump later is also a pain.

- The tank is not very aesthetically pleasing. Unless you live in a tropical area or keep the heating in your home turned up very high, you'll need to add a heater, and that along with the pump leads to a lot of cables and clutter, since the tank was not designed for it.

- The biggest downside of all: the plants simply won't grow! Yes, wheatgrass can survive 2 or 3 trimmings and grows pretty well, but there's not much use for it unless you like to eat grass. The basil, which would be more useful, unfortunately doesn't grow well at all and doesn't look very appetizing.

- This is specific to me, but I received a scratched up and damaged unit. I was fully refunded for this, but it shouldn't have happened in the first place.

I'm looking to buy a real aquarium so that my beta and catfish can stop swimming in algae and their own filth. This was a nice try, but the product itself is unfortunately flawed and doesn't live up to expectations. product_title: Motorola Pet Scout66 Wi-Fi HD Pet Monitoring Camera
review_headline: Easy-to-setup cloud based security camera - not just for pets!
review_body:
It should be said up front that this needs to be set up using a compatible smartphone or tablet (Android 4.0 or above, or iOS 7.0 or up). You can monitor it through a PC browser, but you CANNOT set it up using a PC. So don't buy unless you have a compatible phone, tablet or ipod.

When I saw this \\"pet monitor\\", I thought, why can't this be used as an indoor security camera in general? In particular, I wanted a camera to set up in the living room window facing our front door, so I could see if the person ringing our doorbell was a friend or just another window salesman. I've had a different camera for more than a year (Trendnet camera, provided by Vine for review) doing that job, but it was a real pain to set up and I can't figure out how to view it remotely or record video. Another camera I got through Vine took very grainy black and white pictures, was battery-operated and required a paid subscription for most features. This Motorola camera seems to have made both of those cameras obsolete.

I set this up in under 15 minutes. I downloaded the accompanying Hubble for Motorola app on both my Android smartphone and my ipod touch, turned on the camera (it plugs into the wall), created an account/password and paired the camera with the app.

The interface is very user-friendly. You can have up to 4 cameras on the account; each one can be given a different name and picture avatar on the app's main menu. Tap the avatar and you'll see a live stream at the top of the screen, and below it, a timeline of events. If a motion or sound is detected (by default, motion and sound detections are on; they can be easily shut off or put in \\"do not disturb\\" mode for up to 3 hours) then it will say when on the timeline, and if motion is detected, a 10-second video w/audio is recorded, hopefully long enough to catch a crook stealing packages from your porch. Motion and sound detection sensitivity can be adjusted; \\"medium\\" is enough to trigger someone moving right outside the door but not if a car goes down the street.

Because these videos are cloud-based, I can view them from other locations, and get alerts on my phone when things happen. It was cool to get alerted from across town when my husband came home! Other remote features: touch the live stream, and you can take a snapshot, turn on the camera's speaker and say something (maybe freak out a burglar? LOL) or even play one of 5 lullaby tunes (just in case they market this as a baby monitor).

The camera also has a temperature detector, which you can set to alert you if the ambient temperature goes above or below a certain number. I suppose that's useful if you have reptiles or other pets that need a certain temperature.

I downloaded the app onto a 7\\" tablet running Android Kitkat, a smartphone also running Kitkat, and an ipod touch with iOS 7.0, and all work well. The tablet is nice to have set up on a counter as a full-screen monitor. Because videos are sent up to the cloud and back again, there is occasional buffering and lagging. The ipod app keeps wanting to update firmware on the camera, and it keeps failing to load - I'm going to ask their CS about that.

In addition to the smartphone apps, the camera can be monitored by logging in to Hubble's website. But again, you need the smartphone app to set it up. (May as well reiterate that at the end of the review.)ight outside the door but not if a car goes down the street.

I downloaded the app onto a 7\\" tablet running Android Kitkat, a smartphone also running Kitkat, and an ipod touch with iOS 7.0, and all work well. The tablet is nice to have set up on a counter as a full-screen monitor. Because videos are sent up to the cloud and back again, there is occasional buffering and lagging. The ipod app keeps wanting to update firmware on the camera, and it keeps failing to load - I'm going to ask their CS about that.

In addition to the smartphone apps, the camera can be monitored by logging in to Hubble's website. But again, you need the smartphone app to set it up. (May as well reiterate that at the end of the review.)

My old cat got motion sick and would sometimes vomit on car rides, but even that he preferred to do inside his litter box. product_title: K&H Cool Bed III Cooling Dog Bed
review_headline: It really works; can be unwieldy
review_body: The bed's cooling mechanism actually works. Also, the exterior shell is tough enough that my 80lb dog who intentionally scratches at it on occasion has never made a tear in it. But there are some real drawbacks to this bed. First of all, it is super heavy - think back injury heavy - thanks to the weight and the fact that it is an awkward and shifting shape. And when you do move it, you have to be super careful not to allow the internal membrane from folding and shifting, because it is not secured. Air gets into the bed when you are filling it, but the air release valve also allows water to escape, so removing the air can be frustrating and messy. Finally, make sure you dry the outside of the bed thoroughly before using, especially the bottom, as mold seems to form readily on its surface and is insanely hard to remove once there. This product works to cool your dog extremely well and is very comfortable for your dog and durable, none of ours have torn yet and we only got rid of one because of mold. My dog would give it 5 stars, I give it 3 for the hassles above, and while the bed is still worth it for the price, if they made one that secured the inside and a better air release valve, I might even buy replacements for the ones I have now.

product_title: Precious Cat Ultra Premium Clumping Cat Litter
review_body: I have ordered this for the past year or so.  The litter is the larger size of chucks, not the fine stuff.  I like that it isn't dusty, compared to all the other brands I've tried, and the best part - no added scent!  I do not like the strong scents of litter, detergent, etc. If you love scented products, this probably isn't for you!  I fill it a few inches deep, and clean it every other day for my one cat. Does a cat box smell?  Of course! This doesn't mask the smell with heavy sickening scents, but rather by containing it in tight clumps.  Clean it regularly, and a covered box helps! product_title: [Upgraded and Unique] Ipow Retractable Belt Pet Dog Leash - 16.5 Feet Long (26 Pound)
review_headline: Good low-cost dog leash, until it broke
review_body:
I had a chance to try out this leash on my buddy Tucker, a 5 year old 20 lb Jack Russel Terrier. He's a city dog. This is my second retractable leash and I like it a lot. It's remarkably light weight and lighter than I thought it would be. The entire outer casing is smooth, shiny black ABS plastic, with a subtle glittery finish. The plastic does not appear to be as heavy duty and as ruggedized as my [[ASIN:B00KMHKOZC Pet Magasin Retractable Dog Leash]], but overall, it looks adequately constructed for a dog of Tucker's size. The handle is not textured for grip, but it didn't bother me the slightest as finger indentations are there instead.

Tucker is quite strong and pulls a lot when something catches his attention, but it's no problem yanking him back with this leash. He's very spazzy, and as a result, he often ends up with the leash between his legs. The ribbon has a tendency to twist during use, but it does not affect the retraction one bit. It's smooth and flowing extending out as well as retracting back in. This is a constant problem for my other leash. Any twists or kinks prevented the ribbon from sliding back into the enclosure.

The part I like the least is the 2 button design. I prefer a 1 button toggle because it is easier and faster to click and unclick one button rather than two. The big button locks. The smaller button releases. Still, this is a very good low cost retractable dog leash.

UPDATE: 8/18/14 - This leash broke after a week of use. An internal piece broke off and the leash no longer retracts. For this, I'm downgrading my rating. The Pet Magasin is holding up nicely.

product_title: Back to the Roots Water Garden
review_body:
Review written 6 weeks after receiving product: I never really had much hope that this thing would be truly self-cleaning, or that it would provide enough greens for more than a garnish or the occasional sprout for a sandwich. I purchased this product mainly for its design, and figured if it grew plants well enough I might be able to add some ornamental plants to the top.

Unfortunately, as other reviewers have noted there are some major flaws. First of all, it is FAR from self-cleaning. Having followed the instructions to the letter, add "sludge remover", added an aquatic plant, added a snail, and fed the fish less (I have a fan-tailed betta) - it is STILL an algae covered mess that requires weekly cleaning.

From the included instructions: "Plants that require full sun, like basil, should be placed near a window that receives direct sunlight" then, in the very next paragraph ""If you place your tank in a sunny spot, consider adding a backing to prevent algae"... um, so put the thing in a sunny spot, but put some backing on it (not included). Thanks guys.

The way the tray attaches to the pump makes it difficult to remove the tray, which is filled with water. As with other reviewers, the tray in mine warped as well, making it a pain to try and fit the thing back together. The tank is heavy so it's a chore to carry over to a sink to begin with, remove the messy top, try and clean the algae and pump, then re-assemble the thing. And enjoy doing this weekly. Yeah - no.

All of the above could be forgiven if perhaps it did one of the things it claims well. It sucks in the "self cleaning" department, and - using the seed provided I have nothing more than anemic, spindly little plants 6 weeks later. Perhaps this system is optimized for wheatgrass - which admittedly is the one thing I did not plant, but basil, mustard, and micro greens have not developed much beyond the seedling phase, and many seedlings fell through and are now floating around in my algae filled tank

At this point I'm going to have to cut my losses and toss the thing. Simon the fish is getting new digs in the form of a standard fishbowl.and many seedlings fell through and are now floating around in my algae filled tank

review_body: I am using these along with another product, Pet-Tabs Plus Advanced Formula Vitamin-Mineral Supplement for Dogs, so I am going to write identical reviews for both as I am not able to review one's efficacy used alone. I have a 14+ year old American Put Bull Terrier with severe arthritis and atrophying of his back hips and legs, along with congenital hip dysplasia. Thank goodness his front legs and chest muscles are still sound enough to get him around. He had gotten where he could barely walk at all with his back legs, and then I found these. OMG. They make such a HUGE difference in his mobility! If I skip even one dose I can see the difference as his back legs get more unstable again. Give him his next dose and he's much improved within hours. Absolutely recommend these for a senior dog. He continues to get worse, but he has, after all, already exceed the life expectancy of a Pit Bull. One negative I have, and I'm not going to deduct a star for it because it's negligible considering how great these are, but for most of you, the dose may be in half tablets so you will have to cut them in half. That is a nuisance. I would rather they reduce the tablet size so you could give 1, 2 or 3 tablets as needed instead of having to cut them. But again, keeping this at five start because they are excellent for my boy.

product_title: PetSafe Gentle Spray Bark Collar for Dogs, Citronella, Anti-Bark Device, Water Resistant
review_headline: Amazing!! Works way more effectively than shock collars!
review_body:
Pros:
- Very effective
- Nicer to dogs vs shock collars
- Can snap a defensive dog into a calmer state
- The citronella spray smells nice or smells like nothing at all (I've had 2 different scents)

Cons:
- Overly sensitive. It can spray from other loud noises near by
- Bulky on smaller dogs
- First one broke after 3 months of use

I have 2 dachshunds, Winnie & Cooper... both extreme barkers. Winnie will constantly bark at the sound of anything... cars, people walking by the apartment, knocks, sounds I can't even hear... etc! She'll run to the door or to a near by window to bark and snarl at everything. Cooper often joins but his main issue is aggression towards other dogs when on walks. The PetSafe anti-bark spray collar helped tremendously with both problems!

I've tried all sorts of training tactics but after years of failed attempts I had purchased the PetSafe shock collars for both dogs. Winnie figured out how to bark and growl without setting it off and even when she would set it off it wouldn't stop her barking. Cooper was terrified of the shock collar and would shriek if it were to ever shock him. :( The saddest thing ever!! So I decided to try the spray collar instead since it seemed nicer, although I doubted its ability to stop the barking.

The spray collar went on Winnie first. One bark, it sprayed her in the face and stopped her dead in her tracks before she could make it to her usual spot on the window. She had a look of confusion. She heard another sound and started growling. It sprayed her again. She immediately went from her aggressive/defensive mode to a calm submissive state. Amazing! The shock collar wasn't sensitive enough to detect growling but the spray collar is. The spray collar also doesn't have a pointy plastic part that protrudes into the dog's neck to pick up vibrations like the shock collars did. It's smooth and flat, much more comfy for the dogs.

Thenwe tried the spray collar on Cooper. We took him for a walk and saw other dogs. Cooper immediately went into his aggressive bark, growl, and attack mode. At the first bark, it sprayed him and he jumped back and immediately backed away from the other dog and went to stand next to my boyfriend in a calm, submissive state. That was the first time in 5 years I've seen Cooper back away from another dog that calmly.

2 cons I've experienced with the spray collar:
1) The collar is sensitive... If Winnie barks loudly next to Cooper, it sets off Cooper's collar although he was sitting there quietly.
2) I've had to purchase a second collar because the first one broke after about 3 month's use. The area where you refill the spray broke and kept leaking out the fluid and eventually the entire collar stopped working.

Overall, this has been an amazing product and I highly recommend it for others with loud barkers. :)

review_headline: It's working - not perfectly, but the barking has lessened

I'm trying to keep it on him all the time in the hopes that he will figure it out and stop barking....except for when someone comes to the door. He is a smart dog and has figured out that he can bark twice and maybe 3 times before he gets the "shock"...and he figured out that he can wooo-wooo-wooo (which is not actual "barking" but is noisy0 and he grumbles a lot now. It's funny as after he barks a couple of times and remembers that the collar will shock him, he'll lower his barks to the wooo-wooo-woo and go upstairs and we can hear him grumble, grumble and the collar will not shock him. He stays there until he hears something (a neighbor coming home, a kid outside) and he'll start the barking....but it honestly is better.
I would recommend this product.

review_body: I have two cats, one DLH and one DSH, and they both shed a lot, especially the DLH. She comes trotting whenever she sees me get it out of the drawer. My DSH cat hates it, but he also hates regular brushes. So I can say it works very well on both DSH and DLH cats and your cat will probably feel the same way about the deshedding tool as s/he does about a regular brush. product_title: ThunderLeash No-Pull Dog Leash
review_headline: Big improvement over a choke chain and leash
review_body:
I must explain that before this leash I was strictly a choke chain and leather leash guy. However I have been doing a lot of reading about corrective vs positive reinforcement and there is a lot to say about the positive reinforcement. I have noticed a difference in this puppy vs others I raised using "correction".

I wouldn't say this leash PREVENTS pulling but it certainly gives better feedback to the dog. The main functioning part of this system is a simple hook which provides a secondary tether that is wrapped around the dogs upper chest. It is then fed through the loop so that when you pull it tightens around the rib cage. That loop is secured to the back of the existing collar.

I have a puppy and obviously they are high powered and lack control. The first couple of days I had lots of pulling but with simple tugs ('corrections') she would come back and walk with me. Now that we have had several tries with it she has stopped pulling as much. When she does pull it causes it to constrict around her rib which causes her to restrict the pulling. She can still pull but much of the pressure is applied to her midsection.

The only issue I have run into is that sometimes the tether that goes around the midsection will fall out of the loop. Not a big deal since the collar is still attached to the leash. All in all a good training tool and I feel much better about not tugging at her neck.

Craftsmanship is evident in the tether and buckle. I regularly inspect my dogs armpits and chest after a walk and I have noticed no irritation after a few weeks.

review_body:

Acts differently on each of my 5 cats. Anyway, within maybe 3-4 days, the pee on the floor stopped. I keep 6 (+1) litter boxes and it seems like I'm always removing their "stuff."

She struggles into the box, does her stuff, paws the litter a couple of time without effect, then struggles out, and makes a hasty departure (as hasty as she can go). One of the younger boys covers it up for her! Is that great or what?

Definitely try this stuff for bad cat behavior. BUT, also keep an eye out for contributing factors, like the litter change.

5 cats in a household is a lot of cats...vet says he rarely hears about 5 different-aged rescues getting along so well...no bloody fights, only an occasional paw swipe, and that just between grandma and the tiny runty female (miss whiney). The big (large) boys do chase and tussle, but it's purely exercise to my eye.

review_body: I can't say enough about this product.  I have a 2.5 lb. chihuahua who has a liver problem that prevents her from having her teeth cleaned (no anesthesia). product_title: Wisdom Panel Mixed Breed DNA Test Kit
review_body: My dog was found wandering alongside a highway and brought home. He was only ~5lbs and I had no knowledge of what his genetic make-up could be. After bringing him in, the vet said he was probably a Labrador/Retriever mix. He's 5 months old now and I always get asked what breed he is. I got this kit because I was really curious (also wanted to know for nutrition/health reasons) and a friend recommended it. It was so easy to use (I just swabbed my pup's cheeks while he was sleeping and he didn't put up a fight). It took about 10 days to be notified it was received in the lab from the time I sent it out, but only 7 days to get my actual results. Turns out there is no Labrador in him at all, but he is an American Foxhound, American Staffordshire Terrier, English Foxhound, Whippet mix! All of these make sense to me from what I have physically observed. He definitely has that hound bark and he LOVES the outdoors. I had an inkling he might be some sort of sight hound because of the way he watched airplanes and birds. I had no idea what his long legs came from and he runs very fast. I am so pleased with these results -- they make so much sense. They even include predicted adult weight range (very helpful, especially since I had no idea how big he might get). I have been showing this to all of my family and friends and will highly recommend this to any dog owners curious about their own dogs!

review_headline: However that sifter still produced those horrible gummy clumps
review_body:
I have a Van Ness sifting cat pan so I WILL NOT scoop manually. However that sifter still produced those horrible gummy clumps. However this product has cured that problem. At first there were issues- the cats had a wonderful time scuffling the plastic, knocking off the lid in their joy. The volume of plastic prevented the lid from locking closed. It looked rather ugly, like it was wearing a tutu!. The volume of plastic also prevented the door from swinging freely. I now use only one liner, the lid locks,the plastic barely rustles and the door swings freely. Amazingly the litter sifts cleanly into the pan, I place it on the bucket lid to transfer to the bucket so it doesn't scatter everywhere. Then the sifter comes out pretty clean and I put it in the second litter box and pour the clean litter in on top of it. Voila!
I would give it five stars except that it is a very dusty and rather lengthy process as it sifts. Maybe a different cat litter would be better. Please also note that my cats are declawed so the ripping effect does not occur. I did not buy these at Amazon but I will be doing that in the future. The price is very good.

review_body:
This is too small for a betta fish (or any fish). And male bettas should not be kept near each other. I know it seems counterintuitive but most pet stores and suppliers are misinformed about bettas. Learn about betta fish and their care from breeders and enthusiasts (like the Nippy Fish site), NOT sellers. To dispel some common myths about bettas:

- They do not live in small dirty puddles in the wild. The recommended tank size is 5+ gallons. They need at LEAST 1 gallon, and 2.5 gallons and up is much better.
- They shouldn't be with or near other bettas unless breeding.
- They are carnivores and need carnivore fish food. They do not eat plants, and they shouldn't eat dried pellets, flakes or freeze-dried food, which bind them up.
- They need heated water (75-80°).
- They need a clean tank just like every other fish.
- A single betta with the correct supplies for living by itself will cost about $100. Or it can live in a larger aquarium with certain types of other fish.

Hope that helps!

review_body:
Freshwater LED+, 24 to 36 inch.
My version does not have a 'bug-eye' I.R. sensor, but instead is equipped with a sensor on the end of a rather long cord -- very smart and convenient. The remote comes pre-loaded with a battery, and a spare is included. The instructions are very clear and concise, with well explained illustrations.
Where do I start? This light is simply amazing!

It actually makes it look as if he was studded with LED's of his own! My Threadfin Geophagus simply glows with silver, emerald and blue! I'm thrilled. 2.) The moonlight settings are very nice, especially since they can imitate Full, Half, and Quarter moon brightness -- plus a rolling cloud effect. 3.) I can now actualy witness my Pleco's nocturnal activities! 4.) Heat output is very minimal. On the daylight settings, the fixture gets very 'warm' but not hot. On all the other settings, the fixture is cool to the touch. 5.) I am constantly tempted to cycle through all the lightning settings -- from severe 'overhead' to fading 'distant'. The only thing missing is actual thunder!

Technology has hit a homer here. Kudos to Current USA for this great product. It's functional. And it's FUN.
It may not be what you want if you have live plants, especially if you spend lots of time with storm and cloud-effects.

Highly recommended

product_title: All Glass Aquarium AAG10005 Tank, 5.5-Gallon
review_headline: Great for Tadpoles - But Buy Locally if Possible
review_body:
This review is written from the point of view of a tadpole raiser.

Tadpoles need somewhere clean to live where they have ample room to swim, nooks to hide in, and places to bask. A 5 gallon aquarium tank can provide the perfect environment for all of this.

Definitely a glass-walled aquarium is key. It might be a bit heavier than acrylic, and you have to use a little more care so you don't drop and break it, but it's well worth it. Glass doesn't scratch easily, meaning you don't get little grooves and nicks in it. For you, it means you can clearly see your pets and observe for any signs of illness or disease. For your pets, it means that algae and other growths won't build up in those grooves, becoming nearly impossible to remove. Glass is far easier to clean and maintain.

The rule of thumb for tadpoles is that you want about 1 liter per 5 tadpoles. A liter is about a quarter of a gallon. With a 5 gallon tank, you can have it 3/5ths full and have about 20 tadpoles in there without any issue. This is probably the most you want to deal with at the same time, anyway. This will keep you going until the froglet stage. At the froglet stage the ratio is 1 froglet per 1 liter of water, so you'd want to have only 12 froglets in there. For most tadpole parents, their intention is to raise the tadpoles to the froglet stage and then let them go into the wild (assuming they are raising local eggs they gathered themselves). So, again, the tank will be fine to handle the remaining tadpoles while the larger onese are set free.

A great size and material for the typical tadpole parent.

A note on the price. I usually avoid price statements since items on Amazon can fluctuate wildly based on who is currently selling it and what the market is. But as I write this review, the price here is fairly high. Be sure to shop around and see if you can get it for less money locally. It could be in a month or two that the Amazon situation will rectify itself and the price will come down to be more in line with local options.rectify itself and the price will come down to be more in line with local options.

product_title: Seachem Renew 1 Liter
review_headline: Perfect for the Planted or Discus Aquarium
review_body:
I've used many Seachem products and all have been exceptionally effective. Renew is no exception.

This filter media is a great alternative to activated carbon. The single greatest advantage is the way this media handles phosphates and PH in the planted or Discus aquarium. Ordinary activated carbon will eventually release excess phosphate back into the water column, upsetting the nutrient balance and potentially causing an algae bloom or other issues. Carbon can also raise the PH, which could have an impact on both plants and the PH sensitive Discus. Renew will become exhausted, much like activated carbon, after a few weeks of use. Once the media is exhausted it won't provide any benefits, but in the case of Renew it won't cause any problems.

Overall, I highly recommend this product. It will help you keep your nitrates low and keep the water crystal clear.

product_title: Proden PlaqueOff Dental Care for Dogs and Cats, 60gm
review_body:
Firstly, do not expect miracle results in 3 days. We are at day 11 of adding this to our 85 lb. greyhound's daily lunch and he is now showing signs of better breath and less yellowing of the teeth. He gets three scoops sprinkled on his dry dog food once a day. I choose to crumble a bit of freeze-dried dog food on top, as well, to make it more appealing. He licks the bowl clean, seaweed and all. He used to have the worst, rotten, fishy breath but it has improved dramatically after 11 days. I was just riding in the car with him, he panted towards my face, and my toes didn't curl.
I will say I was impatient in the beginning, after 3 to 5 days, thinking there was no sign for the better. Judged it prematurely. The bottle says expect results in 3 to 8 weeks. We have been lucky to notice a change just shy of 2 weeks. Good luck to you all fighting the 'breath of death' fight.
PS) There is a scoop included in the bottle, about the size of a dime. So the servings are tiny, really. Three "dimes" a day for my greyhound and it's worked.

product_title: Pebble Smart Doggie Doorbell
review_body:
I don't write reviews and I can't recall ever returning anything back to amazon, but this one had to go.

The rear panel of the sound box wouldn't stay in. It wasn't broken; it just wouldn't stay in. I had to tape it. As far as the adhesive on the controller goes, the sun hit if for an hour and it fell off. I had to buy double-sided tape from the hardware store.

After it was up, it took about 10 min to get him to touch the pad. (He already knew \\"touch\\").
But the pad wasn't reliable. Sometimes it would ring and sometimes it wouldn't. Oh, he pressed it. It just wasn't reliable. (He's a medium size dog.)

Here is a summary of the problems:

1. The back panel is flimsy
2. The volume is too loud. It doesn't have a volume control.
3. It doesn't have a \\"simple\\" ding, just a long tune or a long doorbell. Annoying.
4. Needs better adhesive.
5. It needs a better quality touch sensor; so it's more reliable. It also seems a little flimsy.
6. It needs an \\"off\\" switch. Once he realizes it's going to open the door, he'll abuse it.

The cheap fix for (6) is to take out the battery. But for that see problem (1). LOL.

Having said that, amazon's return policy is excellent. No hassles. And it was picked upped by UPS the next day.

product_title: Java Moss - Live Aquarium Plant by Aquatic Arts – Large 25 Square inch Portion
review_headline: Fast delivery and a quality product with great customer support
review_body:
Now this was my first time ordering live aquarium plants online so I was pretty hesitant myself on if I should buy this or look for a local grower. I received a large portion of this a few weeks ago. It was delivered within three days of the confirmation of my order and was packed in clear plastic zip lock bag which was heavy duty and did not leak. This bag was inside of a thermo cup filled with insulation to help maintain a cool environment. The whole box that the thermo cup was packed in also contained this insulation type material. The temperatures around my area were about 80 degrees and slightly muggy at the time.The plastic bag that contained the java moss was cool to the touch.

Now on to the the actual product itself. There were a few brown strands of java moss when i opened the package but this is to be expected when a plant is shipped in complete darkness. There is definitely more than enough to cover a larger piece of wood that is approximately a foot long and 8-9 inchs wide, that I used inside of my 29 gallon tall tank. I had enough left over that I attached some java moss to a few rocks and placed them inside of my 5.5 gallon tank. It didn't completely cover the pieces but it was enough to evenly place throughout both pieces. That being said the brown strands are begging to turn green and appear to thriving and growing at this time. I would recommend Invertobsession due to the delivery speed, the guarantee that all products will arrive alive, a direct contact number that is provided in a letter, and the quality and quantity of the product.
