product_title: The ORIGINAL Bad Air Sponge Odor Absorbing Neutralant, 14oz(Packaging May Vary)
review_body:
I have roommates that smoke in the house and this has seemed to help keep the odor down.

I used to smell it when walking in my house after being outside for a while, but now when I walk in I dont. So it must work since their habits havent changed much...

product_title: Litter Locker Refill Cartridge 10 pk
review_body: I've used this product for a number of  years now and the refill cartridge together with the Litter Locker have really made taking care of my two rescue cats a whole lot easier.

product_title: Graffiti Print Apron
review_body: We have two cocker spaniel puppies that we groom. Their coats are soft and voluminous and before I bought this apron, we'd wind up wearing most of it and having to change our clothes after grooming. These aprons are light weight polyester and washable and have pockets to hold a brush or scissors or whatever you need to grab quickly.  Beats changing clothes covered in hair.

product_title: Tidy Cats Cat Litter, Breeze, Litter Box Kit System, 1 Kit
review_body: Had a little trouble getting my cat to adjust to it, but after I took away his old litter box, he used it just fine. Much less litter tracking. And no more urine smell. Does nothing to hide the smell of poop though.

product_title: Ruffwear The Beacon
review_body: This clip is sturdy and easy to clip on and off.  The light is bright and I like the blinking feature for extra visibility. However, it does not produce a glow around my dog as some reviews claimed.  I have a large dog and if the light is on one side of her, you cannot see the light at all from her other side.

product_title: FURminator Large Yellow deShedding Tool with 4-Inch Edge
review_body: My cat LOVES this thing! As soon as he sees me with it, he will jump up and start meowing to get my attention. He tries to brush himself with it and grabs my hand if I stop brushing him.

product_title: Petsafe Stay and Play Fence Receiver Collar
review_body: The color itself is a bit cheap and the receiver does not hold a charge very long. I charge them every night.

product_title: 52" Deluxe Cat Tower Tree Furniture with Condo Scratcher Posts US Warranty
review_body: My only complaint is the ramp falls off too easy, other than that it's really sturdy and my cats really like it.

product_title: Simple Solution 6-Layer Dog Training Pads, Absorbs Up to 6 Cups of Liquid
review_body: very absorbant, and scented well, as our elderly small dog seems to find the middle of the pad more often than not with these.

product_title: Vet's Best Aspirin Free Aches and Pains Dog Supplements, Natural Formula, USA Made
review_body: I can tell a noticeable different when I give these to my GSD. He loves to play Frisbee and I mean LOVES it! I have to monitor his Frisbee time because after all that jumping he will start limping so we have to come back inside and give him his pill and I do see it help him. Where as before he might be limping around for days now he takes a pill and in a few hours he wants to go again but I am a mean mommy and I make him rest up.

product_title: Proanthozone 50mg for Large Dogs (120 Caps)
review_body: My dog was limping all the time due to an overreach injury. Nothing helped besides laser light therapy that was very expensive. I tried this product and after she was on it a couple weeks, her limping subsided. Now she only limps a little when she first gets up in the morning. I am very happy with the results!

product_title: Resco Original Deluxe Dog and Cat Nail/Claw Clippers
review_body: I chose the guillotine style clippers b/c the scissor style sounds really uncomfortable. These clippers are really sharp and get the job done very quick! The only downside is that it's somewhat awkward to angle against your pet's nails.

review_body: Plugged the thing in. First thing my cat did was pee all over it. I admit I had been skeptical to start...how would pheromone therapy be helpful to my cat when his problem is territorial? If it simulates the pheromones of another cat, wouldn't he regard that as competition and need to do something about it? And that seems to be exactly what happened.

product_title: FURminator deShedding Tool for Dogs
review_body: My beagle sheds on everything, and his dry skin ensures his hair goes everywhere when he scratches. This helped reduce the problem substantiality. It took me a while to really want to spend the money on this, since it is a tad expensive, but worth every penny.

product_title: Bergan Comfort Carrier Soft-Sided Pet Carrier
review_headline: Perfect for Kitty on the Airplane
review_body: This bag was inexpensive, and perfectly effective.  Our cat is 13 years old and on the small side (She had plenty of room to walk in, turn around, etc), and has rarely had to go in any kind of crate.  She actually curled right up on the pad in this one, although she did cry about it at first.  It was perfect on our Southwest flight, and slid right under the seat.  No one in the airport or plane really knew we had a cat with us!  The side pocket was perfect for in-flight petting (More for me than her!).  Great value- no need to spend more unless your kitty is huge!

product_title: Best Choice Products Sheep Shears Goat Clippers Animal Shave Grooming Farm Pet Supplies Livestock, 320W
review_headline: Not for dogs (nudge, nudge, wink, wink)
review_body:
I have a yellow lab/golden retriever/Husky? mix whose long hair gets impossibly matted.

These shears worked great. Did not take too long to get him rough cut, but then used a fine set of clippers to clean him up.

Drawbacks are they are LOUD, and you need to be really careful, or you can nick their skin.

If you have a animal where the hair gets really matted, these work great.

product_title: PetSafe Busy Buddy Bouncy Bone Dog Toy
review_body: It kept my dog busy. I like it because it made my pup work for his treat. It's also helpful for chewers like my pup!

product_title: Habitrail Ovo Pet Habitat
review_body:
I got my first robo hamster, Murphy, over the weekend. When I got him home, I already had the Habitrail Cristal habitat set up with the den attached. I let Murphy into the habitat through the den and after a quick spin around the rest of his new digs, he went back to the den. I filled the den with bedding almost up to the lid and he LOVES to burrow in there and nap- he spends most of his time in the den and pretty much leaves it just to eat and run around really quick. The lid is easy to open but not so easy that a sly, little hamster could get it open.

I highly recommend this product as an addition to your Habitrail or Critter Trail!

product_title: Flourite Dark, 7 kg / 15.4 lbs
review_body: RINSE BEFORE USE! Excellent product, Ive had multiple planted aquariums. Great results in all of them with Flourite. I like the dark better than the reddish color, just because of the more natural look. Rinsing it will not change how well it works. Its just extremely dusty and will turn your tank to soup if you dont rinse it extensively.

product_title: Customized Military ID Dog Tags - Personalized Metal Tags Matte Set with 2 Chains and 2 Black Silencers
review_body: I ordered these for my son for his Halloween costume. My husband is a soldier, so my son is going to be one for Halloween. The dog tags are very similar to my husbands actual dog tags. This company was very easy to deal with and they arrived MUCH quicker than I expected.

product_title: BYS2012 Pet cat Dog LED Safety Flashing Blinker Light Tag Collar Dog Flash Tag Pendant
review_body: I could be inclined to give this 5 stars pending a test on battery life, it was well worth the price. In an effort, however, to hold the seller responsible for the accuracy of the description, to be fair, mine did not come with extra batteries. There are 3x small hearing aid type batteries but all are required to make it light so ...... no extras really. If the batteries hold up then its clearly less expensive to buy 2 or 3 lights rather than purchase replacement batteries. It is highly visible on dark nights and my dog, while a little surprised at first, seems to like the increased ground visibility. I like it better ...... much easier for me to see where she is. This does the job and appears to be made well from all aluminum housing and clip so save your money, buying a more expensive version (many with lower ratings) is probably unnecessary. The bulb does have to be loosened to turn it off so leaving it on the collar while not in use is not an option.

product_title: JW Pet SkidStop Slow Feed Pet Bowl ( Blue/ White )

product_title: Marshall Ferret Litter Pan
review_headline: Excellent for rabbits:  well made, sturdy, commodious, great value
review_body:
My buck keeps urinating right outside the regular litter box (looks just like this: s6.thisnext.com/media/largest_dimension/7635734F.jpg)

I don't know if it's behavioral or if he just doesn't like having to jump into the litter box because he's lazy or tired or getting arthritis or some other mobility issue.

In case it's a mobility issue, I thought I'd try an easy-entry litter box right where he urinates. So far he's using this and has only urinated on the floor outside both litter boxes once in the past 7 days (which is a BIG improvement).

I am happy to give my rabbits options, especially as they get older and are getting less nimble and mobile.

product_title: Omega Paw Self-Cleaning Litter Box, Large
review_headline: A litter box for people who hate litter boxes
review_body: I have to admit that my husband and I both detest cleaning the litter box and could rightfully be accused of being beyond neglectful in that area.  To that end, the room that we kept our litter box in was a miserable and disgusting place to be in (although the cat seemed to love it there).  I was sorting through some papers and found a $50 Amazon gift card that had gotten overlooked, and then a couple of days later I stumbled across this and decided \\"what the heck?\\" and ordered it.  All I can say is that I wish we had found this little gem a looooong time ago.  Assembly was easy as pie (make sure the locks are securely fastened under the lip to prevent leakage), and the cat took to it right away.  The hood keeps the dust down tremendously, and I can't say enough about how easy it is to clean.  Every morning when I first get up I stumble into the cat room in my bleary eyed state, roll the box, give it a couple of solid thumps on the bottom, and roll it back.  Then I just dump the contents of the drawer into a garbage can with a sealed lid.  It couldn't be easier.  Right now we are using regular clumping litter until it's used up, but then we plan to try to flushable clumping litter so that we can also get rid of the garbage can.    Update: we switched to clumping, flushable litter and it works great and is even easier to use!

product_title: Wellness CORE Natural Grain Free Dry Dog Food
review_headline: Good good, good delivery, happy dogs
review_body:
I need grain-free for my dogs, and they really like this brand. With two large dogs, it can be pretty expensive to get them what they need. I use Subscribe and Save, with the 15% discount. The price becomes very competitive with other, lower quality foods. And I don't need to lug it around.

One comment with Wellness foods is that the dog's stool is drier, so make sure your dog is getting plenty of water. They may increase their drinking compared to other foods. Considering the reason my dogs are on grain-free food, the firmer stool is a plus.

Also be sure to assess your dog's calorie needs. Ask your vet how many calories they may need per day, and adjust your feeding to match that. Be sure to include treats in your calculations! This food has a fairly high calorie density. I found I needed to cut about 1/2 cup out per day compared to their previous food (they now get 2 1/2 cups instead of 3 per day). Fat dogs are not funny, they are at increased health risk.

product_title: Living World Hamster Fluff, 1-Ounce
review_body: After reading the reviews on this product from the decent people warning that this product is highly NOT recommended for your pet and seeing the \\"positive\\" reviews, I realized that these \\"positive\\" reviews are a ploy from either the company or any other sellers of this product who are trying to 'fluff' these reviews into seeming like it's more 50/50. The reality is this product is NOT a good choice for your hamster or other pet and should not be advertised as such. I use non-lotion/unscented tissue and my dwarfs have a field day nesting with it. I would suggest just sticking with that.

product_title: Dog Dazer II Ultrasonic Dog Deterrent
review_body: I have used the Dazer several times and it has worked every time.  Just yesterday,  a little dog was yappin' his brains out next door. He stopped, then paused and barked again, so I hit it again, then he stopped again...One more time and he was finished!  He ran away and I heard him grumbling!  He then came back and just stared at me , I felt kind of bad because he seemed sad he could not bark anymore. Oh well. The point is this thing works on most dogs...

product_title: Comfort Zone Feliway Spray for Cat Calming
review_body:
We have two cats in our house and both are neurotic.

--- Rex, our cat, seems to suffer from separation anxiety and drags my wife's clothing around the house every time she leaves. In addition, he seems to hate, not just dislike, but HATE my father, who lives with us. Dad's always been nice to Rex, but Rex will often swat at him when he walks by. Rex also is very defensive of the house and anytime another cat comes by the outside of the house, he runs from door to door and window to window stalking it, and then sometimes sprays near the doors.

--- Princess, my father's cat, seems to suffer from OCD. Besides being skittish around new people, she will lick herself until she has large bald patches on her legs. The vet has put a couple kids through college with the money she's taken off my father, but Princess never seems to improve.

After being recommended by the new vet my father has found, we decided to give Feliway a shot and bought the diffuser and one refill. Dad has it installed in his bedroom, and from the first night it was in use, he said Princess started sleeping on the side of the bed nearest the diffuser. She seems to be less skittish around visitors. She used to disappear the whole time they were in the house. Now she will come out and sit at a distance and watch people. Dad says Rex seems to be a little nicer to him, and spends more time in his room (Rex used to just go in the room to use that litter box and see if any of Princess' food was left out).

The diffuser didn't stop Rex from spraying, so the vet recommended this Comfort Zone spray and said to spray it everyday in the areas Rex sprayed, as well as by the exterior doors. I could have bought this from the vet for more than twice what I paid here on Amazon, so as usual, this is where I made my purchase. The spray seems to have made a difference in Rex's behavior. As far as we can tell, he hasn't sprayed since we started using the spray, and he seems less compelled to serve on guard duty at the doors. We've used this tiny can for about three weeks and still have a good amount left, so a little goes a long way. Hopefully it will permanently change Rex's behavior for the better.mpelled to serve on guard duty at the doors. We've used this tiny can for about three weeks and still have a good amount left, so a little goes a long way. Hopefully it will permanently change Rex's behavior for the better.

review_headline: Not for "active chewers" ... lasts just minutes; cleanup difficult
review_body:
This is \\"toy disaster,\\" but my dogs weren't harmed in any way. A dog that chews and rips toys will demolish the Loofa ball in a few minutes and you'll have a challenging clean job..

I made a mistake in purchasing a LOOFA Dental Dog Toy Ball (medium) that's part of this set. I was attracted by the \\"Dental Dog Toy\\" subtitle, and suspended my normal skepticism. The toy lasted about 20 minutes with one of my two Scottish Terriers. He totally shredded it (the back label does say \\"For Shredding and Flossing,\\" but I didn't comprehend what \\"Shredding.\\" really meant.

Not only did Jack completely shred the ball in under 20 minutes, but I spent an equal amount of time picking up the bigger pieces and then vacuuming up most of the rest. I had to disassemble the small vacuum cleaner rotating-brush head (air turbine driven) and extract a piece of loofa that jammed the turbine. I'm still picking up pieces a day later. The pieces of loofa are almost like Velcro, they attach to fabric like carpets, dog bed covers, etc, and stick to the dog's coat as well.

Some dogs may take great care not to damage their toys, but I recommend you stay away from the LOOFA Doggie Product toys if you have a terrier.

review_body: This worked! Required two people to apply it, using a towel to wrap the bird gently. I kept it on for a couple months to stop my Africa Grey from feather picking. product_title: Pioneer Pet Raindrop Style Drinking Water Fountain, 96-Ounce
review_body:
My petmate plastic fountain recently burned out after three years of flawless service and I needed to come up with a replacement. After a lot of research, I decided that this was the best fountain for the price and bit the bullet.

I like that this fountain has a removable/cleanable filter which keeps the flowing water clean. The fountain is also made of stainless steel which is much more easy to keep clean than my previous plastic fountain. I replace the water and wipe it down weekly, and give a thorough cleaning every month. With the plastic fountain, I had to clean it every week to keep the water from becoming slimy.

My cats took a day or so to adjust to the new fountain, but now they love it. They seem to alternate between drinking from the moving and still portions of the fountain, and I've found them more interested in this fountain than the previous. As an added bonus, they seem less tempted to play with the water. With my previous plastic fountain, the would stick their paw in the falling stream of water and divert it out of the bowl; I'd come home to a soggy floor at least once per week. Since the water flows in a trough with this fountain, they no longer want to play with the flowing water any more.

Overall, this fountain is an excellent choice for the price, and I like it much more than my previous plastic fountain.

product_title: StarMark Everlasting Fun Ball on a Rope Dog Toy
review_headline: Flimsy - Poor Quality Toy Poses Many Risks
review_body:
Surprisingly of poor quality and for aggressive chews especially this toy poses a myriad of choking and other dire risks.

We have two Old English Bulldogs and both are hard core aggressive chewers. Most of the toys we rely on are nylabone, Kong and a few others. Last year our one year old had a piece of rubber lodged in his lower intestines. Long story short - major surgery and we almost lost him.

The problems I see with this toy is as follows.

* Very small ball - not for large dogs

* Ball is easy to tear and swallow pieces - especially at the opening for treats.

* Flimsy rope poses yet another choking hazard

* Cheap, thin plastic around the base of the rope where is meets the ball.

Perhaps this would be suitable for small breeds, and dogs who are mild chewers. Still I would emphasize that even in that case supervision is 100% critical. As for larger and or hard core chewers this toy is an accident waiting to happen.

review_headline: Good Product, Need to have realistic expectations
review_body:

The behavior and dog itself really determines if this will work. For example, our Sheltie is scared of fireworks, so much she does not come out of the house the week of the 4th. This product does little to help that. Medication and homeowner love is really the only solution there. However, on miniature dachshund this has worked well to calm frightened dogs that then have potty accidents. It does not however, stop a dog from barking. That's not what this product is meant to do.

Near the $50 mark, I feel this is tad overpriced for the purpose and the reason I gave it 3 stars. But for those with loved pets that it works on I can see it being worth the money. Just have realistic expectations when you buy this product.

product_title: Nutri-Vet Hip & Joint Advanced Strength Chewable Tablets for Dogs
review_body:
My Dobie, Max, has a fairly common hip and joint problem. My vet had prescribed Rejuvenate which worked quite well. When the prescription expired I ordered Rejuvenate Plus from Amazon because my vet was no longer available unless I paid an outrageous fee for her to write just a prescription renewal. I mistakenly believed that since the names Rejuvenate and Rejuvenate Plus were similar the results might be similar as well. Was I ever wrong. The Rejuvenate Plus made Max sick and when he started digging through his food to find it and throwing it on the floor I was getting concerned. Then, when he did not find it in his food, where it was mixed with some meat, and he unknowingly ate it and started vomiting I threw the Rejuvenate Plus in the trash. I decided to check out the contents of this Nutri-Vet and noticed that it contained some of the ingredients that were in his former prescription so I placed the order.

I give him the Nutri-Vet every morning with his food. He has no objection to it and does not throw it on the floor but gobbles it down. He seems to be getting up a bit easier especially after he has been laying down for an hour or more. This Nutri-Vet seems to be working as well as the prescription did in aiding his getting up and down. I.will continue to give him these tablets and if all continues to go well I will reorder this product when the current supply runs out. It is sad to see your pet struggle just to get up and this Nutrri-Vet is doing well to assist in that effort.

review_body:
While my Lab loves everything that is round and chewy, this is by far his favorite ball. He loves the feel of it and rolls it in his mouth as he runs back to me. When we're finished playing, he drops it in my backpack for the next day. As solid as this ball is, it should last forever.

The teeth are fun, too. I haven't tried training him to carry it with the teeth showing, but when he does it by chance, it's really funny. But that's not the only reason to buy this ball. It's heavy enough that it throws great and has a wonderful bounce. Sometimes, because it's not a completely round, bounces at irregular angles which keeps the dog more interested. And, depending on how it's put in the Chuckit, it whistles when you throw it.

The color choices are nice. I decided on orange because it's a great color choice for a deep-yellow Lab, and more importantly, it's very visible in grass, weeds, and water.

A Tip: This is not a chew toy. If your dog is a power chewer, you should use this ball only when playing \\"fetch\\" or other supervised play.

Another Tip: Different dogs like different things. If your dog is picky about food or flavors, try putting a treat in the ball before giving it to him/her the first time. Peanut butter or liver treats are favorite with many dogs.

I hope they keep making these balls forever because I want to keep buying them forever.

product_title: 2-Pack PetSafe Basic Bark Control Collar
review_body:
I love this! My poor neighbors probably love this too! I believe my dog is far too scared of the dark, so she loves to randomly bark at odd times throughout the night.

My dog is a MinPin, so she is quite small. Her neck is probably only as big around as my fist. I love that I can adjust this down as small as needed to fit her.

The shock is perfect. She takes it well and never had any sort of panic attacks because of the shocks. Usually she forgets and does a surprise yelp after a bark and goes quiet.

It recommends not to use this all day and night, so I generally only put this on her when we go to bed. She has never gotten any types of sores or rubbing issues. I find it not to be much different than a standard collar, just remember it must be a little snug to get good contact with the skin. My dog has very short hair so I know it gets good contact, but a fluffier dog would require shaving to make it work properly.

The only reason I don't give it 5 stars is because the battery dies faster than I would like. I find it so hard to turn the lock/unlock key that I just have to leave it on. If you don't want to have to order a new battery, you can see if there is a local battery store near you such as Batteries+, which had replacements there. This does not take a standard battery. product_title: Redbarn Ham Bone
review_body:
I have a beagle. He's 6 months old and he has been chewing on my furniture and walls. He has other chew toys, but he still goes for my furniture. So, I got him this bone. He's satisfied and he no longer chews on my furniture. Here's a list of Pros and Cons:

Pros
*Distracts puppy-The first day he got it, he spent the entire day chewing on that thing. He only stopped for his walks, his feeding times, and for drinks of water. He can spend hours chewing it.

*Saved furniture- Whenever he gets the need to chew (which, as a puppy, is pretty much all the time) he just runs over to his bone. He no longer chews on my furniture.

*Lasts long- My puppy gets through his bones fast. It usually takes him 10 minutes to get through a long rawhide bone. However, this bone is HUGE! It's long and thick, so even though my puppy constantly attacks it, it's strong enough to withstand it.

*It's cheap-With my Amazon prime, I only paid $6.18 for this. It's a great deal.

Cons
*Messy-It's coated in something. It's hard and crunchy and my dog loves it but it's messy. So, when I opened the plastic that held it together, a bunch of crumbs started falling out. Also, my puppy made a HUGE mess of crumbs. It was from chipping off the coating on this bone. It's better to open it over the trash can so that you won't have to clean up what falls out. Also, give this to your dog in a place that's easy to clean. Thankfully, my house only has hard floors, so all I had to do was sweep it up. However, carpeted areas would need to be vacuumed.

*Smell-It comes with a smell. It's not a foul smell, but it's noticeable.

All in all, an amazing product. I will definitely be buying it again once he finishes this one up.

review_headline: Seems to work well (Worked great 3-1/2 yrs and then died)
review_body: I have been using this about 3 weeks now with a CHE (ceramic heating element) and it keeps temperature very well.  I should mention that it does NOT  have numbers on the dial, but just a High-Low type of control, so you WILL need a thermometer to get things set up.  I have left my digital thermometer in place and the temp seems to stay within a degree (Maybe two if it's more chilly at night-- I'm in Wisconsin and we haven't turned the furnace on yet) since I've started using this thermostat for my tortoise.  The only thing I find slightly annoying is that they have supplied a safety cover (to make sure you don't accidentally bump the thermostat controls once you have set it) and there are some slots on the bottom to allow for the plug cords.  Well, I have it set up with a ZooMed CHE placed in a ZooMed metal cage clamp fixture... But the slots are TOO SMALL for the plug of their own lamp fixture... You just would think they would've styled this to be used with their own branded products, don't you?  So... I can't really effectively use the safety cover-- But other than that, a fine product.  UPDATE 2-16-17 NOW DEAD.  SO, 3-1/2 YEARS USE. WORKED GREAT AND THEN JUST WOULDNT TURN CHE ON TO HEAT ANYMORE.  NOT SURE HOW LONG THESE SHOULD LAST, WAS HOPING A BIT LONGER,BUT WAS FINE WHILE IT LASTED!! Came to order a new thermostat.  Have decided to try another brand to see how that one is--

Some friends just didn't appreciate my brilliance. Some people just don't understand what love really is.

review_body: I have purchased 5 of these boxes over the course of many years. The quality has definitely gone down over time. I had sworn by them; I never had the frequently cited problems of the cats urine escaping, or the lids not attaching firmly, or problems with gutters and ruts making scooping harder. Well, I moved last year, and ordered 3 new ones, and there is a sea change in manufacturing quality, I am very sorry to report. To do a compare and contrast, the first is strictly cosmetic. The old boxes were green. The boxes are now blue. The old boxes were larger, just enough; these are appreciably smaller. The plastic in the older boxes was thick and durable. The plastic in the newer models is very thin, and I don't see lasting very long. Now to my biggest complaint. The lids do not attach on the new models. Oh, if you're lucky, it'll attach on one side, but don't hold out for both. It starts out attaching, and then you cannot get it off. So clearly, fighting to get it to detach for cleaning, erodes the latches. So, now I have 3 boxes whose tops are in various states of attaching, or not. It's really a shame, because I gave the old model 5 stars years back (because they lasted!), and this is just not comparable. Hopefully they'll read the poor reviews and make some adjustments. It used to be a great product.

product_title: PetFusion SmartGrip Cat Litter Mat. Large (35 x 24 inches). Safe for your cats, free from Phthalates & VCM
review_headline: Litter around the house = Dramatically reduced
review_body:
I have had this mat for several months and I really like it. I used to have a product similar to this mat [[ASIN:B003SLKUA8 Medium Litter Catcher Mat in Blue]]. It worked pretty well, but it was a pain to clean and was too small. Plus, my cats didn't really like the feel of it, so they learned to jump over it on their way in/out of the box (not the product's fault though - just wanted to mention it).

I purchased this mat based on the good reviews. I haven't been disappointed. It is a great size and traps the majority of the litter - it has reduced the amount of litter around the house dramatically. It is also really easy to clean. Whenever I clean the litter box, I lift this up, make it into a tube shape, and dump all the litter on it right into the box. I have never tried washing it before, but I have wiped it down with clorox wipes, or plain water on a paper towel, and it wipes off messes really easily (my cat has vomited hairballs on it a coupe times!). Also, my cats really like the feel of it, so they don't mind walking over it which helps.

The reason for he one star deduction is that it is really light. I have to place part of it under the front of the litter box to hold it in place. And, even with that, it gets shifted around (the same thing happens whether it is on carpet, hardwood, or tile). It isn't a huge deal, but a little more weight to is would be nice.

Also, the colors aren't the most attractive - I got the beige and it is more like a peach skintone color. It's not a reason to deduct any stars (it goes near a litter box, after all!), just wanted to share my thoughts on it.

---

Tip: I have played around with lots of different configurations to reduce the most amount of litter. What I have found to be most useful (in addition to using a litter mat), is to face the opening of the litter toward a wall. I make the distance between the opening and wall just large enough for my cats to getin/out. Then, I place the mat, perpendicular, between the wall and opening. By doing this, it forces them to walk a certain path, where most litter will get trapped on the mat. Just a tip that works well for my furballs. :-)

review_headline: My cat loves the Tidy Cat Breeze system!
review_body: This is such a great system - easy to set up and very easy to clean.  With regular kitty litter there is a lot of mess - no matter how attentive you are about cleaning the box, there's always a mess.  Besides the pee and poo mess (and smell), the litter itself gets stuck to the cat's feet and is then deposited onto the floor.  I've had a completely different experience with the Tidy Cat Breeze system.  As soon as I got it out of the shipping box and was setting it up, my cat wanted to get into it - he immediately took to it.  The urine goes right through the main platform to a pad that's in a pull out tray on the bottom - I've smelled no urine odor in the week that I've been using it (you change the pads once a week).  There is no scooping out clumped litter - you only scoop out the poo.  The other great thing about this system are the pellets.  They stay in the box where they should be - I've only seen a few stray pellets that have fallen out of the box after my cat has been in it. In addition, my cat use to randomly not use his litter box to poo - I could never figure out what his reasoning was, but none the less, it was frustrating.  Since I got this system my cat has used it consistently and hasn't gone poo anywhere else but the Breeze box.  If anyone else has had this problem I'm sure you know how frustrating and upsetting it is.  I'm a huge fan of this system and felt compelled to write a review about how much I (and my cat) love it.

I have a 15 year old Chihuahua, she's been my partner since I was 8 years old. Imagine that, she's been with me through my childhood, puberty, adolescence, and young adulthood.

Sooo, this week I found out how to feed it to her mixed into her dry food, with her eager response to finish the whole thing like never before!
What I do is that I serve her the corresponding portion of dry food, drizzle it with half a tablespoon of OLIVE OIL (Extra Virgin), then crumble half a tablet (what she requires for her size) and then mix it in. WHOAAAAA, I got so happy on how eager she ate all her food like I had never seen before. Plus, olive oil is great for dogs too! (It's good for their immune system, for the brain, for longetivity, and of course for a shinier and healthier looking coat)Then, why not boost a little more goodness to this Vitamin and drizzle some Extra Virgin Olive Oil on top of it all?

product_title: Grannick Bitter Apple Spray for Birds 4oz
review_headline: Works well on symptom - NOT on cause!
review_body:
Most bird owners already know that avian behaviors are sometimes tough to predict and change. Feather plucking, while distressing to see, is usually a symptom of a larger problem and is not the problem itself.

Having said that, this product has been a standby for me for many years. When plucking or chewing behavior is first identified, Bitter Apple helps to deter the behavior while I am finding a solution to the underlying problem. Whether the cause of plucking is loneliness, territorial/dominance issues, boredom, lack of sleep, breeding behavior, skin problems, or other such stressors, the underlying issue must be addressed to stop the behavior.

THIS PRODUCT, BY ITSELF, WILL NOT STOP THE BEHAVIOR PERMANENTLY! It will simply give you and your plucking/chewing bird some \\"breathing room\\" to solve the problem.

You must figure out WHY your bird is plucking, and tackle that issue, while you are treating the behavior. Any other approach is likely doomed to failure.

This is still one of the best anti-plucking agents I have ever used. We commonly keep it on hand at the avian vet clinic as well. The only reason I give it four stars rather than five is that it is simply a \\"bandaid\\" and not a cure for the emotional or behavioral problem in and of itself. I do not want new consumers to believe that a \\"magic spray\\" will make plucking or other annoying activity to cease. It won't. But for the ease and comfort of your bird while you diagnose the problem and correct it, I have never found a better product.

product_title: Flexi Explore Retractable Dog Leash
review_headline: Best Walk Ever with my Stubborn American Bulldog Puppy
review_body:
The experts say that the leash was only invented a 100 years ago and dogs followed their masters because they wanted to.

I've been having problems walking my American Bulldog a 10 week old Puppy on a regular leash. She'll stop and no matter how I pull, or lightly kick, she'd stubbornly stay in one spot. By the end of the walk she'd be better, but the first part of the walk was tortuous.

My dog will end up around 60-100 Lbs even though she's only around 10 Pounds now. My number one goal is that she learn not go in front and pull. I don't need for her to be an automaton walking woodenly by my side. Just that she not walk ahead and pull others who might not be alphas.

Walking her today was magical, we'd walk then she'd stop, I'd keep walking and let the leash play out, at around 10 feet, or with a little pull, she'd start walking and catch up with me. The leash would torsion up and I'd be able to push the button to stop the leash and pull her back if she went ahead. Today she was walking with me because she likes walking with me and not because she's being forced. Big difference.

It's like you are walking your dog without a leash but you have control of her to keep her from trouble.

Kudos to this leash for helping me have the most mutually enjoyable walk every with my Stubborn American BullDog Puppy.

Much has been said about this leash but I want to add.

Buy the 100lb one. It has a flat ribbon that doesn't tangle and won't give rope burns. My 10-12 pound American Bulldog Puppy didn't even notice the tension. Only time I'd buy something smaller might be for a Toy Breed. But for a big breed even at the Puppy Stage the 100Lb is the best.!!

product_title: Four Paws Pet Products CFP01676 Super Catnip Cat Scratching Perch, 24-Inch
review_headline: Affordable tall scratching post with shelf- my cat loves it!
review_body:
I have had this for years, but my neighbor's son was playing around with it and it broke, so I'm buying it again. My cat loved it. Here's why:

- Has a top shelf she likes to lounge on (most posts don't have this)
- 2 feet tall. Most post are only 14.\\" This really allows her to stretch out and scratch like cats do with trees in nature.
- Has sisal rope. Cat scratchers made of only carpet don't do the job. They really need the rope- again mimics scratching tree bark in nature.
- Compact. I live in a studio, so I don't have space for anything too wide. This is slim and I can stow it away if needed, but still wide enough that she can perch on top of it.
- Cheap. I'm sorry, but I'm not paying $70-$100 for a scratching post. This is what a post should cost- totally worth it.
- Plush toy balls. I thought these were stupid when I bought it, but she actually loves them, even years after the catnip smell wore off. They make a slight rattle noise which I think she likes, and anything hanging from a string is irresistible to cats. She played with them so much the strings broke several times but I just tied them back together. This was not due to poor quality but the fact that she played with them a LOT.

Downsides:
Like the other reviewer said, not the most sturdy cat post. But my cat never knocked it over, so not a problem. She is 11 lbs, and fairly active/playful.

Note: I had tried other scratching posts in the past- classic carpeted posts with a spring toy on top- and she completely ignored them and chose to scratch the couch instead. I thought I had one of those cats that just didn't respond to scratching posts, but I just had the wrong kind. I really think it's the rope and the shelf that make the difference.

My tank filters from the top and has a lot of air bubbles coming up. This has worked very well for me. I also put a piece of scotch tape over the hopper door to hold it where I want it to be. This seems to be the only design flaw with the feeder. The hopper door doesn't hold its adjustment that well. Don't let this one flaw keep you from buying this unit. Its not much of an issue I adjusted the feed rate once and put a piece of tape on it to hold the adjustment and never had to deal with it again. You can't even see the tape on it. Also, my food has always stayed dry with no issues whatsoever even with the moisture caused by lots of air bubbles breaking on the surface. I like that I can hear the feeder activate, though it is very quiet. That way I know its still working and I can watch the fish feed. Great product.

product_title: VetriScience Laboratories GlycoFlex 3, Hip and Joint Supplement for Cats, 60 Bite Sized Chews, 4.23 oz
review_body:
Squeaky is a healthy 12 year old female indoor cat whose diet mostly consists of Science Diet Age-Defying 11 Years+ dry food. She has never refused treats such as Temptations MixUps (which I assume is junk food for cats, though I rarely offer her any and when I do I only give her a tiny portion), but she has no interest at all in these Vetri-Science chews. I offered her one every day for nearly three weeks, I tried leaving a couple in with her dry food (she ate around them), and she simply has no interest in them.

Cats are known to be finicky and a bag of these chews are expensive, so I think anyone who wants to try them out on their cat or cats might want to first see if they can obtain a sample. At Amazon's current price, these chews cost about 22 cents per chew, and I think people who want to market such expensive chews would do well to either offer free samples or sample bags for a dollar or so.

I wish Squeaky was interested in them because they seem like they'd be good for her, but as cat owners (a euphemism for humans who are cat servants, for dogs have owners while cats have slaves) know, you can't make a cat do anything it doesn't want to do.

product_title: Northmate Interactive Feeder
review_headline: Dog feeder or Parrot Foraging Feeder, works for both!
review_body:
Affective neuroscience has shown that seeking something, or looking/working for food is even better than getting the food alone, so I was delighted to see this product and excited to try it. It has met and exceeded my hopes! My dog took to it right away and spent a glorious time nosing out her dinner. She gets more excited to see this come down for meals than she did with her food bowls. review_body: Pretty horrible if you ask me. I currently own two aquaclear 110. I never had a problem with those two hob filters. I decided to go into canister filter. Set up was pretty easy. product_title: Ware Manufacturing Plastic Base 6-Level Clean Living Small Pet Cage with Wire Top, Large, White/Blue
review_headline: Not even nice enough for a rat
review_body:
I bought this cage last year. It arrived with a damaged top section with a dangerous \\"bar\\" that was split like two pointy daggars and painted over during manufacturing and which could have injured the rats, myself or my kids. I complained to Ware Mfg. and they replaced the section. Then a few months ago I was rolling the cage across my smooth new laminate floor and the front right wheel snapped off, taking a chunk of the supporting plastic with it. The whole cage nearly toppled over, which would have been a dangerous mess, as I was taking the cage out for a cleaning.

As it is, I have to support that broken corner with all sorts of props and the cage is no longer portable. I contacted Ware about a replacement base and they quoted their 90 day warranty and suggested I try to buy a base from one of their retailers.

I might even have considered such a purchase was the cage not so poorly constructed of cheap material. The sides are difficult to fit back into the base after the first few cleanings, and the grills above the waste tray no longer fit. The worst problem is that the rat's urine erodes whatever kind of plastic they use, etching it deeply and not allowing good cleaning, plus it gets discolored and unattractive. The base plastic in particular cannot hold the load of the cage above it, and it is brittle and cracks without warning.

I will not purchase a Ware product again after this experience. I was sold something supposedly easy to clean and received a major headache to repair more than clean.

On the plus side, this cage's bar separation is fine for large adult rats. When they were little we added a wrap of smaller chicken wire mesh from Tractor Supply over the top 1/3 of the cage and that stopped the escapes.

review_body:

product_title: Don Sullivan's "Secrets to Training the Perfect Dog" (LARGE DOG)
review_headline: Researched many, and this is the best.
review_body: I've researched many dog training techniques, and this is the best-hands down-that I have seen. My dog (a german shepherd lab about 2 yoa) has responded very well. Prior to training she was a "bolter" and very obstinate. She now listens to my commands and stays close to me everywhere we go. Still have some work to do with distractions, but she's lightyears from when we started a couple months ago. I've found that I was really doing her a disservice by not formally training her. When you can be on the same page with your pup, everyone's life is easier and you no longer resort to getting frustrated by their miscommunication with you. I've seen posts about how this training is cruel, etc. and I would say it could be cruel if you're a loose cannon and have no patience. If you can discipline from neutral ground, without anger, make the correction needed, praise the dog and move on, I can't think of anything more beneficial and the dog will love it. 5 stars.

I even let everything setup overnight with a fan on it and it was working great for a few hours until I came into the room a few hours later and saw it broken apart again. I removed all of the glue and Velcro and went to see one last time if I could figure out how to keep this thing together. Finally I came across a review by someone that said to hammer the ever loving hell out of the snaps to get them securely in place. There is no way you will be able to get them secured with just your own strength. After doing that, voila! They finally weren't moving. Do not use Velcro, make sure you screw this thing in otherwise it will just fall. I have a huge window sill which I thought would support this pretty well but the more weight on the free edge, the more the Velcro will come away from the sill. So two things you MUST use, SCREWS and HAMMER!!! It's great and my little lady loves it when now that I manhandled it.

review_body:

product_title: Petmate Compass Plastic Pets Kennel with Chrome Door
review_body: This is my 2nd Petmate plastic kennel so I'm going to compare this one to the first as well as the Petmate Navigator. Several years ago I adopted a senior dog who has anxiety issues and would pee whenever he was left alone. He figured out he could lift his leg and keep his wire kennel dry. I tried taping wee wee pads to the sides like shower curtains but it really wasn't effective. I needed an enclosed crate. I looked around and discovered that the large crates were all held together by screws. Then I found the Petmate Furrarri kennel which has latches similar to small cat carriers. I needed to be able to open it easily to wash it out and put it back together easily also. It is an extremely sturdy crate and one I would recommend if a pet needs to fly or is strong and determined to escape. It's also hard to find now. Petsmart still carries it online. Since it isn't readily available I figured it must have been replaced by something else. I found the Petmate Navigator and the Petmate Compass. It's difficult to tell the difference so I needed to go to a store to see them. They are almost identical. The Navigator has a divider that you can position as the pet grows and it is made out of a slightly stronger (heavier) material than the Compass. The Compass is like 2 laundry baskets latched together. It's very light and easy to assemble.  My puppy is 8 months old and 24 lbs. He's also 24\\" tall and 24\\" long. A lanky teenager so he's not a big strong dog who can chew through it. I wouldn't use it on an airplane, I would be terrified it would come apart but for our purpose it's perfect. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because I think it's stated to be acceptable for airline travel.  Not for my dog, ever, but for home use, it's much lighter than a wire crate and the door is a pleasure to open and close. I would purchase it again for home or auto travel use.

product_title: PetSafe Stay + Play Wireless Fence, Covers up to 3/4 Acre, for Dogs and Cats over 5 lb., Waterproof and Rechargeable, with Tone and Static Correction
review_body:
This is by far the best perimeter fence we have purchased. We had a wired fence and it was a pain in the tush. This one being wireless is amazing and it is worth every penny!

We live on over an acre and the terrain is varied. Some uphills, some downhills. I works very well on uneven terrain. Other reviewers have said that it isn't reliable, ours is working great. We have even taken it camping with us to keep the dogs off the tether and in our campsite. It easily adjusts to different distances, depending on what you have going on.

Some reviewers say that the collars don't hold a charge, I feel that this is due to the amount the dog wearing the collar, is testing the perimeter. If you have an animal that is constantly testing the perimeter then, yes, you will have a battery that doesn't last very long. If you have a dog that you have taken to the edge and he/she were shocked, then I think you'll have a dog that stays within the bounderies! It is important to spend some time with the animal, to make sure they are aware of what happens if they don't come back when it begins to beep. Right now, we could have the collars on "beep only" and they wouldn't leave.

As a note, if you have smaller or thin skinned dogs (we have Schnauzers), there is no need to crank up the shock during training. We did this and it was hard to get them off the porch! I (personally) didn't think this was neccessary but my husband wanted to give them full throttle because they had been huge runners. They don't run anymore. They are happy with the area they have which is the maximum the fence will allow. 210' circumferance.

I can't say enough about this and if anyone has any doubts, you shouldn't. I especially like the part about it being portable as we RV quite a bit. Bottom line?? I LOVE THIS PRODUCT!! Feel free to contact me if you have any questions.

product_title: PetSafe Deluxe Bark Control Collar (PDBC-300) for Dogs 8 lb. and Up, Waterproof, 3 Modes of Static Correction
review_body:
When we moved from our own home to a rented apartment a few years ago, our dogs went through several adjustments. One was that the youngest dog, a rescue, needed to wear a bark collar so he wouldn't howl and bark all day while we were at work. So, we begrudgingly got him a bark collar. He's golden now and very quiet, but he still needs to wear his collar. He doesn't use it and the battery now lasts for years, quite literally. He has the Pet Safe Small Dog Bark Collar, not this one.

Well, suddenly our older dog started barking last month. At first, it was just when the neighbor came in or out of her apartment. Then it was every time she went to the basement. Now, it's any time someone closes a car door on the street. Unfortunately, we're getting complaints about him now. So, we figured it was time to get him a bark collar, too.

Both dogs are jack russell terriers. The baby was only 11 lbs when we got his bark collar, so we bought Pet Safe's small dog bark collar from PetSmart for $100 before tax. It was expensive, but it's been worth the money. I came on Amazon to see if I could get the same collar for my other jack russell, but they're still nearly $100 even on Amazon. Ugh! So, I bought this Pet Safe bark collar because it had decent reviews and was less than half the price of the other collar. Plus, he's a bit bigger than my younger dog - nearly 17 lbs - so I thought this one would do the trick.

Unfortunately, it doesn't. It's just too big. It seems to work fine, but I can't attest to it really because it's simply too big. If you have a small dog, I really suggest investing in Pet Safe's small dog bark collar. The unit is about 1/3 the size of this one, and the collar works well to place the unit. The collar on this unit did tighten to fit my dog, but the unit itself is so huge he found it too heavy. Whereas he wears my other dog's small-unit collar just fine, when I put this on him all he wanted to do was remove this collar because it was weighing him down. It won't work for daytime wear in that case.

I think this could be a great unit for someone with a dog even as small as a beagle, something 25+ or 30+ lbs. But for any dog under 20 lbs, I really think the unit itself is much too big despite the fact that they advertise it for dogs 8+ lbs. Buyers with small dogs beware! Thank goodness for Amazon's excellent return policy. I'm returning this and buying the much more expensive Small Dog Bark Collar from Pet Safe. It sucks that it costs so much more, but it does work. I'm reviewing that product separately, if you're interested.

review_headline: Great toy for TUG and PLAY (not chewing)
review_body:
First off, I'd like to say I don't really know what some people expect here out of products like this. Jolly Balls are designed as toys for your dog to PLAY with- not just something for them to chew on. If you want something that's going to last forever that your dog is going to gnaw at for hours/days, get them an antler or a Kong or something.

I have two German Shepherds and a cattle dog mix, and I can honestly say Jolly Balls (the tug-n-toss in particular) are some of my favorite toys for them. I have several in multiple sizes... my personal favorite is the 4.5, as its light and easy to carry around for training and play sessions. I had my last 4.5 for TWO YEARS with two GSDs that play pretty vigorously before the handle finally was so mangled that it fell off (I still have the ball, which is just as intact as it ever was, and that they still carry around and play with). 2+ years for $8? That's a bargain. My larger sizes, while full of punctures, have held up just fine- handle and all.

So, be reasonable with your expectations with a product like this. I don't just throw one down and let the dogs have at it... I PLAY with them with it, throw it, tug with it, then put it away when I'm done. Extremely happy with how they hold up in that respect, and the dogs are far more enriched for it.

product_title: Andis Professional Animal Clipper
review_body:
This is my first set of clippers, and my first time attempting to groom my dog. All in all I would purchase this set of clippers again.

I purchased these clippers because they are listed as heavy duty, drop resistant, and are supposed to stay cool while you clip. Other clipper reviews I read said that the housing chamber on the clippers broke easily after being dropped while heated.

Again, I have not used any other clippers before this, but I found that the clippers did not stay cool for very long..but perhaps they stay cool for longer than most clippers? I don't know. I had to pause and let them cool multiple times throughout the grooming process. No complaints on my part..but the dog wasn't too happy to have to come back over and get noosed again.

The clippers come with multiple guards, which was awesome. The #10 blade it comes with is good quality and using that alone will leave 1/16\\" hair on your dog. I used the 1/8\\" guard and it clipped on fine and the cut was even throughout.

The kit also comes with a small tube of clipper oil. All you need to purchase is clipper coolant, grooming shears, some brushes, ear powder, nail clippers/dremel tool, and perhaps an oral hygiene kit to do an entire grooming job (plus the shampoo and tub, obviously). This is a clipper kit only, not a grooming kit..

product_title: Sentry Calming Collar for Cats
review_body:
I have four cats - two males and two females. The males are aggressive with the females and the one female is aggressive with the other female.. I've tried all sorts of treatments, most unsuccessful.

The collars were miracles for the males. The aggressiveness was gone when the boys wore the collars (and actually the spraying the one male cat was doing was lessened and my semi-tame boys were super affectionate) but the collar does nothing for the female. She's still obnoxious to her \\"sister,\\" collar or no collar. I am unsure whether that means the collar is more successful on males than females or it's a crapshoot. Regardless it is worth trying it out. When I first started the collars, I remember it took several days for the aggression to tone down.

However, I do have a caveat since neither boy can wear the collars anymore. Both boys have developed skin eruptions around their neck area where the collar rested... really bad skin eruptions. In the past five years the boys have lived with me, they never had skin problems. I suspect that it is the material the collar is made (a plastic blend?) or maybe it's the formula (you never know what will trigger allergies in humans or animals). I had been using the collars on and off for several weeks at a time, especially when I knew I was taking a trip. The first time it happened, I was out of town for a week and thought the skin irritations were due to stress. I realized this past trip the collar was the only common denominator (darn it, the collars worked too). After removing the collars, the skin is now starting to heal on both cats. It's back to Bach's Rescue Remedy in their food. Note, interesting enough, the sister who also wears the collar, has not gotten a skin irritation. But, the collar doesn't work for her. I keep it on her because she's cute in purple (the color of the collar).

About the collars themselves, the smell is pretty intense when it is taken from the foil-sealed package (It's a note for the humans that may have allergies). I recommend pre-measuring your cats neck and add about two inches (I think those directions are on the package). The collar's rubber/plastic is really hard to adjust, let alone after it is on the cat's neck (I recommend keeping a previously used collar to \\"size\\" the new collar prior to putting it over the cats head, it' easier than trying to figure out the correct length while holding a struggling cat. Just hold the used collar and the new collar side by side and \\"mark\\" the new collar where the clip should be). I kept the collars relatively loose and didn't have a problem with them coming off but you don't want to have it too loose either and 'catch' in the cat's mouth.

review_headline: Fleas'  holding cell - for the tough calls!
review_body: Ok, I'm willing to give this version of Safari's standard single row comb 5 stars but will keep both - the single row ordered by mistake and the double super comb. Let's face it - by the time we have to use one of these to help our cat or dog (or other furry creature) the gross factor is at the bottom of the list. It's fantastic for extraction of the clueless fleas, eggs and random flea 'stuff'. Yes, it does trap a great deal more and it's disgusting. As someone already recommended, use a very thin toothpick to run between the very narrow space and push out the sneaky small guys - some hide and may be mistaken for blood flakes between teeth. I use a small swiss army knife in a slicing motion just in case before washing out. I found that both combs (single and double row) bring out the sadist in me and since some more active fleas jump off quickly I kept several strips of sticky tape which I immediately stuck on top of the up facing side to keep the escapees from flee-ing (can't help myself here).  My poor cat enjoyed the cool weather a bit too long last week and ended up with a flea colony. This was new for us and for an elderly 9 lb feline with renal disease I refuse to subject him to more chemicals than I need to. He's been very understanding about every natural remedy for our surroundings - Diatomaceous Earth sprinkled around (and added to his food in case he licked up some flea larvae) and sulphur (puffed lightly on his fur and added to his food). Note - BOTH human food grade not to be confused with animal feed or pool cleaners! We've even done one of several treatments with Little City Dogs flea killer capsules (for small dogs/cats).  This double tooth comb is a great addition to the seemingly endless battle but a week later we are winning.  Still, this double row brush is a bit too tight pulling even on a short hair soft furred cat so I start off with it and when my patient's had enough, I switch to the single row and we keep going for a while longer. He seems satisfied that the flea search is over and it's just pleasure brushing as far as he's concerned. So, while the double row jobber is awesome, both are a great addition to our beloved Furminator. product_title: GloFish Waterfall Globe with Blue LEDs, 1.8-Gallon
review_headline: Great little fishbowl for a home or office
review_body:
I got this fishbowl for my office, but was worried about 2 things... one I was concerned that it would be too big, and two that the waterfall would be too noisy.

I am very pleased that neither of my concerns came to light. It's a perfect size for a small office (my office is about 10'x15' and has a desk and one set of file drawers). The entire unit is about one foot wide by a little more than a foot high... perfect to fit on a cabinet or medium to large desk. I have it placed on the top of my drawers and it is certainly a attention getter and conversation piece for other co-workers.

I am also very happy that it doesn't make much noise at all. The pump is whisper-quiet and the water only makes a faint rustling noise, a little like a small desk fountain. It's actually very pleasant to hear, not overly loud at all.

The fact that the water is filtered is also great, which is much better for the health and longevity of the fish... downside is that you have to change the filter about once a month, but they are inexpensive and worth it. I was told by the petshop to only start with 2 or 3 fish at first, and then in a couple weeks when the bio is built up in the bowl, I can then add a few more if desired.

So far I have 3 small glofish in it and they are playful and really cool to watch. The LED blacklight really makes them pop, especially in low ambient room lighting. Make sure to get a couple small plastic plants that are made by glofish, as they will also have a florescent look to them and complement the fish nicely. Also remember that it doesn't come with any gravel so you'll have to purchase seperately.

I would definitely recommend this waterfall globe as it is inexpensive, attractive and lots of fun.

Enjoy!

product_title: Betsy Farms Chicken Jerky Dog Treats, 40 oz
review_body:
This exact product is sold at Sam's Club for $14.96 a 40 oz. bag, I purchased 2 bags from Sam's Club and when I arrived home wanted to see what my 2 Cocker Spaniels thought about them, After I opened the bag and pulled a few out, I was immediately taken back by the feel and texture of this product it felt dry and very spongy, I was not impressed at all so I turned the bag over and looked at the ingredients, and noticed that although chicken was an ingredient, it was actually a bunch of processed items pressed together and cut into Jerky like strips!
I decided to let my dogs try these out and make the decision, they both took them out of my hands and went and laid them down and returned to me for something better these treats stayed on the floor uneaten and ended up in the trash.

product_title: ScoopFree Slide Easy-Clean Manual Litter Box
review_body:
There was no way I was going to spend $125+ dollars on a litter box, no matter how much I wanted to eliminate scooping! I was so happy to find this manual model at less than $50.

I had never used crystal litter before and am really sorry I waited so long! I have 2 cats who are 14 years old and didn't do anything special to 'make the transition'. Just threw out the old clay litter box and put this one down.

I did make a raised, covered box for the unit to set in (I have 3 dogs who need to be kept away from the litter). I wanted a slightly larger container for the waste and also had no desire to spend the big money on replacement trays. The disposable trays might be fine if you have one cat, but will not hold even a week's worth of solid waste.

I built a box with a raised platform that the Scoop Free unit sits on. the platform is about 6" off the ground and the area underneath gives me a place to store the unused crystals. The box is tall enough so it acts as a litter box cover as well. I put a couple hinges on the top to easily access the Scoop Free unit I then made a tray out of plexiglass to use in place of the cardboard box refills but added an opening (3"x12") in the front. Underneath the opening is a box lined with a bag so when I use the rake the poops drop into the box. Every couple days I simply tie up the disposal bag, toss it in the trash and put in a new bag liner.

I've found that by doing this, the crystals go MUCH farther. Even with 2 cats, one 4 pound bag lasts a Month. There's never any of the ammonia smell you can get if you skip a day with the clay litter, but I do use my old scoop to mix the crystals around so they dry out a bit. I add about 1/2 cup of clean crystals every other day.

I saw that there are several items available that if combined, would serve a similar purpose as the box I built - but they didn't all quite meet my needs. There is a permanent plastic traywhich is about $35, a raised platform box for $150, the manufacturers cover $45(?). It would have cost me an additional $200+ for the various components, building my own was less than $15.

I've had absolutely no problems as some have described with the rake not catching all the clumps and mixing the crystals around a bit has eliminated any wet spots.

I LOVE THIS LITTER BOX - goodbye clumping clay!

review_headline: As long as you know dry food should supplement a wet diet, this is a good choice for your cats.
review_body:

I also mix it with [[ASIN:B003M5WNKU Hill's Science Diet Mature Adult Hairball Control Dry Cat Food, 15.5-Pound Bag]] and [[ASIN:B003MA8P02 Hill's Science Diet Adult Indoor Dry Cat Food, 15.5-Pound Bag]]. But their primary diet is moist food.

While the old style of thinking was that moist food was bad for cats, the new thinking is that dry food is contributing dramatically to chronic renal failure in cats (the number one cause of illness in domestic cats). So while I buy science diet (the three types mentioned) and provide it to my cats on a free-feed basis, they primarily eat moist food so they are getting something closer to what they would eat in the wild -- almost pure protein and lots of moisture.

I recommend Science Diet as it is one of the better dry foods for cats, but not as a primary diet if you can help it. They really need moist food to help their kidneys function correctly.

Amazon is probably the lowest price you'll find for this -- if you get it delivered on a regular basis (I do every 2 months) and hit the 20% discount for ordering enough on subscribe and save. And it's nice to have it delivered right to the house.

product_title: Aqueon Submersible Aquarium Heaters 50W
review_body:
I run the 300w version. First, I just want to point out that the price for a 300w heater is middle of the road. You have other options from:
[[ASIN:B00513MZ6S ViaAqua 300-Watt Quartz Glass Submersible Heater with Built-In Thermostat]] $14.74!!?? wow! All the way to:
[[ASIN:B004PBCDQE JBJ True Temp Titanium Heating System Kit for Aquariums, 300-watt]] $139.33!!?? wow! :)

My point here is that, at least to some extent, you get what you pay for. I think this one is a good balance of value and reliability.

I have now owned this one for 2 years. The first year I kept a 110g at almost 90 degrees F, ambient temp 72F. During that time it was in the sump and was in a horizontal position. I then moved it to a 55g and keep that tank at 80F, ambient temp 72F. The temp always has been rock solid consistent with little or no fluctuation. Despite the good performance, there have been a few issues.

First, the temperature numbers on the top are meaningless. If you do want to set the temp of the tank you will need a temp gunge so that you can adjust appropriately. [[ASIN:B00DS2NMYI Coralife 00232 Digital Thermometer. Temperature, Indicator, Reader, Digital, Meter, Degrees, Celsius Pet Supplies / Shops]] This make take several days, adjust, wait for a day, check temp, adjust again, and so on. I would rather spend the time to do than than a lot more money on a nicer one, but just FYI.

Second, there is condensation on the inside of the glass now. It has been there for some time and is concerning. However, I have gotten 2 years out of this product. If it did die tmw, that wouldn't bother me. I feel like I have gotten what I paid for. If you buy one, you should keep in mind that it is not going to last a life time.

All in all, I highly recommend for a budget heather. Just take a second to consider whether you may be in the market for something nicer. If so, look elsewhere.

product_title: Marina Power Filter
review_headline: Good Flow. Low Wattage = Low Heat
review_body:
This is the best hang-on filter I've tried in my many years as an aquarium hobbyist. Super slim, low noise, low power, but still has a good amount of water going through the unit. The output comes down a slide with a lip at the bottom, that disperses the current more across the top of the water than in a downward fashion. Seriously, magnificent design. Very well thought out. Uses just 2 Watts of power at full throughput. Which is great for A) low power bills, and B) not adding excess heat to a small tank, especially during hot summer months.

Read the reviews, and I think I can address any possible negatives I might run into. People have said it can hum once it's been on for a while. That is pretty normal for any type of powerhead motor over an extended time, and there are a couple ways to address this. Take it apart, and clean the impeller/impeller housing. This is a common cause of vibration. Also, put a rubber suction cup on the glass behind the motor to absorb vibration. My Marina S10 is currently quiet though, but I'll update if that changes and I have to use my 2 year manufacturers warranty. Worst case scenario (after rma), you could actually replace the motor with a different powerhead.

Why, if you think about it, you could run a small powerhead on a normal undergravel/uplift tube, and disperse its output through the S10 using a piece of tubing. Or just park the S10 on top of an uplift tube.

The filters are small, but like with all hang-on filters, you can use many different types of filter media instead. You could put a small bag of carbon back there. Or chemi beads. Or ceramic canister blocks. It's also easy to cut a sponge a little wider than the filter width in order to get it to stay between the filter supports. Use your imagination.

The disposable filters that are sold for this unit are cheap too, and they work very well. So no problem if you don't want to bother with customization. This is hands down my #1 recommended hang-on aquarium filter.

product_title: SERGEANT S PET PRODUCTS P 1159 Pet Armor Flea and Tick Topical for Cats
review_headline: Don't Trust All the bad reviews
review_body:
So I'm noticing a few different kinds of post, half saying this works the same as other products, and half saying it will kills your cat, because they were told that by a vet. First off, I am a pet specialist, and I am not biased in any way. I believe that most flea topical medications work the same way, because most have the same active ingredients.

First off, only buy a 1 count pack the first time you try this. Cat's can have adverse reactions, same as humans. There are MILLIONS of people who have to switch medications because they are allergic to the first one give, cats are no different. If you have a kitty with bad reactions or sensitive skin, only put a tiny dab on their back between the shoulder blade. Check it every half hour for 12 hours, being careful not to wipe it off with your fingers. If your cat does get a reaction (redness, swelling, broken skin, peeling in the area) use warm water to wipe it off immediately. Pat dry, don't rub.

Second, this will not work instantly! I see so many post saying they put it on their cat an hour ago and the cat still has fleas! REALLY? The way topical medication works is that it absorbs into the skin and is rereleased in the natural oils all over their body. This can take as little as a few hours for some cat, for others a few days. Then the fleas will try to wait it out or run to areas of the cat that don't have medication, or flea from the cat entirely. This means the fleas will get in your funiture, carpet and other soft spots. Make sure you are Vaccuuming daily or even twice daily! Most people don't know this, but you can vaccuum your bed and couch as well. Wash sheets and pillows and blankets twice a week or more and put flea powder in the carpet. Flea powder only cost about $2-$5 in most stores and it's easy to use.

Lastly, people are claiming their vet said not to use this. PetArmor is a private brand that does not distribute to vets offices, meaning that Vets can make money off ofit in any way. Vets want you to bring your pets in for flea dips and buy medication through them. Or, don't mention right away that you used PetArmor, see the different ideas you get as to what is wrong with the cat. Also, vet offices get paid by the companies to promote the medications they sell. Look at the ingredients in PetArmor compared to other topicals. 90% are the same, and the few I saw that weren't the same were natural materials mostly for consistency, color and scent.

So, don't take all reviews as fact. All that I said above is unbiased and true.

As for a review of this product:
I have used this product for many years on many animals. I even use small amounts on Ferrets and Hamsters without any negative results. This product works a little slower than some, but for a third the price, it's worth the extra wait. Make sure you get it on the skin, because it is a thin consistancy and tends to spread out on the fur. It takes about 3 hours to dry, so pat up any areas that may have spilled where the cat might accidentally consume it. Don't bath your cat after this for at least a week, otherwise you might wash out the chemical that kills the fleas.

If you want to wash your cat, to get the process started, wash them with dawn dishsoap BEFORE applying this medicine. Use a Knit or flea come and go through it's fur, making sure to kill the fleas or drop them into boiling hot water to kill them. Dry the cat completely, then apply the medication. Because the cats skin will be dried out, it will actually get their body going and they will start producing natural oils faster.

product_title: CitiKitty "As Seen on Shark Tank" Cat Toilet Training Kit
review_headline: Messy and flimsy (compared to litter kwitter)
review_body:
So I purchased this first because it was cheaper than litter kwitter and now that I've used both, here are the pros/cons of citiKitty ...

Pros:
1) Cheaper
2) Looks closer to the real toilet (color change doesn't confuse kitty)
3) Has 2x more stages (6 stages instead of 3)

Cons:
1) Flimsy and breaks easily. Litter Kwitter is solid plastic, not twistable.
2) Because it is flimsy, you can't use it stand-alone. Like the picture, you need to drop your toilet seat over it or else if your cat weighs more than 10 lbs and tries to sit on it, it will bend. Now if you drop your toilet seat on CitiKitty, first 2 weeks of using it, my cats had poopy scratches all over my toilet seat which would dry in the evening when I came home so I couldn't use the toilet immediately. I had to spray my cleaner, wait for the dry poop stains to soften, then clean, and then use my toilet. It's hard to keep this up for weeks! Litter Kwitter comes with 3 rings PLUS a toilet seat so you can keep yours lifted at all times. So all you have to do is move the kwitter and use your toilet. That easy.
3) Now talking about removing the training toilet and putting it down (so that you can use your toilet), CitiKitty is messy again. CitiKitty is more flat and Litter Kwitter has more of a \\"bowl\\" to it so the litter falls out easily.
4) CitiKitty is non-reusable. Once you cut a hole, you can't stitch it back. There's a 2nd plate you get, but that means you only have 2 shots!
6) Going from one stage to another is difficult and disgusting. The perforations don't break off easily and even when you try cutting the stage off with scissors, it breaks unevenly and the loose litter (even if barely any) splatters all over. It's also easy to get your fingers caught up in sharp edges and bleed.

Overall, cittyKitty has its drawbacks but is an acceptable choice for kittens and young cats that learn quick and aren't too heavy. But if you're cat is old/heavy/picky/slow then go with litter kwitter.

By the next morning we had gotten rid of so many of them that you could definitely see a difference in my dog's mood.  She is so much playful and looks happier than ever. I recommend this product and I will definitely will be purchasing from the seller again.

review_headline: When bulb burns out it is over
review_body:
I have been using this for about a month and loved being able to see what is inside the egg. Fascinating! However, the way this is made you have to cut the end to get the bulb out. Now I cannot find any replacement bulbs for it.

I really do not recommend this unless you just plan to use it a few weeks and throw it away when the bulb burns out.

product_title: Pet Gear Carrier & Car Seat for cats and dogs
review_body: I have a cat that freaks out and hides whenever she sees, hears, or thinks she hears me pulling out the carrier. I bought this one after she had to have her leg amputated and I needed something I could get her into without injuring her. It was perfect. With the large opening I was able to place her in the carrier and zip it up before she realized what was happening. She had plenty of room to move around and I was able to unzip the top to pet her without her trying to get out. She seemed a little calmer in this one versus the old fashioned hard-sided carrier. Kitty weighs 13 pounds and the carrier held her well. The carrier folds down into a small package so it takes up very little space. I wish I had bought it long ago...

review_body: This was a donation for dog that was in a rescue foster home and delivered 12 puppies.  They appreciated it very much

product_title: Paws Aboard Neoprene Doggy Life Jacket
review_body: We have two labrador retrievers that would rather run on the bottom of a lake instead of swim.  Obviously this became a problem as the water got deeper.  These life jackets lift them just enough so they swim properly, as they enter the deeper water.

review_body:
