Our cats really like to drink from the top part, I don't know if that is because it is higher, or because the water is flowing. The fountain is completely silent, also a big change from the last one.
My one concern is that we had the big reservoir bottle before, and this doesn't hold that much water so I am not sure I could leave it unattended for a long weekend or something.

product_title: Whole Life Pet Single Ingredient USA Freeze Dried Beef Filet Treats for Dogs, 4-Ounce
review_body: My GSD has many food allergies, so finding treats she can have is a challenge.  She loves these Whole Life Beef treats and since they are one ingredient (that she can have), it is simple and easy.  These are great for stuffing in her Kong toys, crumbled over her food for variety and added protein and make excellent, not messy training treats!  They come in a wide variety of flavors, so my dog has more than one choice.  They are a bit expensive (price could be lower), but are very light in weight, so they last pretty long.  We will buy these again.

product_title: Van Ness Large Dinner Mat

The mat looked good when it arrived, and it wipes up so easily when the kids overfill the food bowl.

review_headline: Love is hardly the term, but it is a good product

review_body: We have a 6 lb. Yorkie.  To be frank, his penis is too close to his back legs so when the wrap is put on, it puts pressure on his back legs and he can't walk right.  He just sits there.  It is probably good for larger dogs.

product_title: Pet Gear Jogger Pet Stroller for Cats and Dogs
review_body: Arrived promptly and was very easy to assemble.  Fits my 30 pound Welsh Corgi very well.  Nice color, well worth the money to me to be able to take my senior dog with me on walks.

product_title: VETRESOURCES Canine CAS Options - 120 Tablets
review_headline: Life changing for our german shepard mix
review_body: Our ten year old German Shepard mix was a shelter dog and we never saw her mange until a year ago.  She is just the sweetest dog with the best personality and she tried to hide the pain she was in from us.  She also has hip issues. The mange took a toll. After one month on CAS Options, she is acting like herself again, going on ten miles walks happily and running in the backyard with her little sister (a puppy).  I think she'll be on this the rest of her life and we are so blessed to have access to this product.

product_title: OurPets IQ Treat Ball Interactive Food Dispensing Dog Toy
review_headline: Our dogs love it, so we do too.
review_body: We have a highly intelligent shepherd and Shiba Inu mix that needs to be kept focused (or she starts destroying things).  This is one of her favorites.  The center disc allows us to adjust how quickly the kibble will pass from the bottom to the top level then eventually out the outer opening.  Can take her anywhere from 15 minutes to an hour to empty it.  Aside from the rattling, which is less on the carpet, it's a good way to get in a bit of tv.  It is plastic though, so if your dog likes to throw things you might want to keep an eye on it, it's not indestructible. I still give it 2 thumbs up considering it's competition.

product_title: Vet Solutions Aller G3 Omega3 Fatty Acid Liquid (8 oz)
review_body: I bought this for my cat a while back because he scratches a lot and in turn loses some of his fur during the summer months.  The vet suggested something like this, or fish oil as he said it would help his itching as he believed the cat has allergies much like I do during warmer months, and like him, I too get itchy skin.  In any event, the product arrived at the estimated time, and as promised new and with no problems at all.  For the first few days, I would put a small amount in kitty's food, and at first he ate the food with no problem.  I could see in a few days, he was scratching less, and his fur began looking more shiny and healthy. product_title: Elite Little Dog In-Ground Fence
review_headline: Arf Arf We can run free in our yard!
review_body:
We purchased this after examining everything that was available for small dogs. Back around 1997 I installed the heavy Invisible Fence wire around the perimeter of our two acre property for the dogs I had back then. So all I really needed was the transmitter, flags, and collars. The wire seems like such a waste as it'll never get used. And the flags...well...useless.

We have two Havanese puppies and needed small collars. We were pleased with the collar size. When they were 8 lbs the collars seemed a bit big for them, but now at 12 lbs they seem to be no trouble at all for them. As a matter of fact, they eagerly wait for us to put them on because they know it means they get to use the entire property to run and play. Anyone who's seen Havanese in 'run like hell' mode knows how much they enjoy all that running room.

In spite of all the battery complaints we're still on the original batteries. We turn the collars off when they're not on the dogs. Some days they'll wear the collars for 8-10 hours, other days just 2 or 3 hours. They also have a very large fenced-in playpen I built for when we want them contained, but because of the freedom they get with the collars the playpen is mostly used at night when skunks and racoons are out roaming.

I plan to modify the battery holders to use much less expensive aftermarket batteries. My brother-in-law did this to his collars and said it works beautifully. There are YouTube videos explaining how and it's pretty simple. [ UPDATE: Some of those videos go to extremes for what is really a very simple operation. If you examine the battery holder closely you'll see a fine line where a ring of plastic encapsulates the battery. A snip with a pair of small diagonal cutters...the kind used in electronics...and you can peel that ring right off. Smooth it a bit with a file and you're done. Total time...less than a minute. The battery fits tightly, so you'll need a pair of needle nose pliers to remove it. From then on you can use batteries that are 5 for $10 instead of paying $9 for one.]

I didn't use the flags included with the kit. They're even more of a waste than the wire because they can't be used for anything else. They're small and impossible to insert in hard ground. I went to ebay and purchased flags that are the same as came with my Invisible Fence 15 years ago. I used about 180 of them. They're durable and have held up well. I've just started removing every other one and the ones I've pulled are still usable.

Training our pups was too easy. We walked the perimeter with them a few times, telling them 'No' whenever they'd approach a flag. After one of them got shocked and looked at me with a 'what the heck was that' look on his face his sister decided she wasn't going anywhere near those flags even though she's the more adventurous one. After they went off leash and followed me into the vegetable garden that's outside the flags they both learned the lesson and haven't challenged the flags since. However, one time the male did run through the fence while chasing a squirrel. This is when we were training them to pass through the boundary when on leash. He and his sister were barking like fools because he couldn't get back in the yard. He was really upset until I went out and got him. I leashed him, turned off the collar, and then led him on leash back into the yard. The trickiest part of training was teaching them that on leash they could cross the boundary, off leash they could not. My wife walks them nearly every morning and we wanted them to cross the boundary confidently when on leash. We're happy that training is complete and effective.

There's no hassle at all putting the collars on them. As soon as we pick them up they come up to us and sit quietly so they can get their freedom collars. And then it's off to adventuring.

My wife and I get great joy from watching Fred and Ginger run loose in our yard. They can explore in the wooded area, chase squirrels and birds, chase each other, run out to the front to greet visitors and we can be comfortable in the knowledge that they know the boundaries and won't go running off. So far this system has been great for us and my in-laws and we recommend it highly.

product_title: PetSafe Drinkwell Platinum Pet Fountain
review_body:
You'd think our 3 cats had never seen water before. They LOVE to drink out of this fountain. The amount of water that our cats drink is 10-fold what they drank with just a bowl of water on the floor. For humans, the fountain also produces a pleasant water trickle sound effect. It's loud when it first starts running, before the water flow has a chance to even out. But once it runs for a few minutes, the flow smooths out, and it's very quiet.

That being said, we just THREW AWAY our second Platinum because it got warped in the dishwasher. The product description says the cistern and the bowl can both be put in the dishwasher, and that is simply not true. We even ran the dishwasher with no heat dry, and still the cistern was warped by the wash. When the cistern is warped, there is no amount of force that you can use to put the flow regulation cap back on, short of breaking the cap. If the cap is not tight on the cistern, and you put the cistern into the unit anyway, then water will just continuously flow into the bowl, causing it to overflow and make your kitchen a mess.

We elected to go with a different Drinkwell product this time, a metal one, and we will not be putting this one in the dishwasher, not matter what the description says. Hopefully we won't need to buy a third model for awhile.

All in all, it's a nice product, just don't put it in the dishwasher. This is very discouraging, because all of the nooks and crannies make it very hard to clean. It also scums up really quickly, so it has to be cleaned often. This warping is just disappointing.

product_title: vetGuard Plus for Dogs (Small 5-15 LBS) 4 month supply
review_body: We tried this for our 11 lbs poodle mix. That same day he began scratching and biting because his skin had become so irritated. The second time around the scratching and biting continued a couple of hours after applying this treatment. I wanted to save a couple of dollars, but ended up throwing away the product. We will never use vetguard again. Fortunately a good bath washed away the product and relived our dog immediately, but we hope the irritation does not persist.

product_title: Marineland LED Light Hood
review_body:
The hood is a one piece top with hinges that attach to plastic clips which hang on the back of the tank. Several different clip sizes are provided to accommodate different tank dimensions. The first clips I put on the tank weren't quite the right size, and the brittle plastic snapped immediately. I was much more gentle when putting on a second set of clips which happened to better fit my tank, but, alas, it didn't matter. The left clip cracked when a butterfly down the street flapped its wings one too many times. The right clip crumbled when the neighbor's adorable kitten purred too loud. Although in Marineland's defense that little guy has what can only be described as a thunderous purr.

I give this product one star because manufacturer did *not* indicate in the instruction manual that precautions need to be taken to avoid damage to the delicate clips. At least warn us about the potential danger that flea sneezes pose to the structural integrity of this hood. Let us know that that even one errant photon from a rainbow can shred your crappy plastic. With two busted clips the hood became worthless and fell into the fish tank every time I opened it up to feed the fish, change the water, clean the tank, etc. Knowledge is power, and had the appropriate precautions been included in the operating manual I might have extended the useful life of this product by up to 2 or maybe even 3 days.

Back when hinges and clips were working as designed, I couldn't open the lid very far without the LED light strip falling out of its perch. Just a terrible, horrible, awful design. I'm now using a cheap $15 glass top with the salvaged LED bar, and am much happier.

product_title: Dasuquin for Small to Medium Dogs, 84-Count
review_body: I adopted a 7 yr. old Maltese who has luxating patellas on both rear legs.  Over the six years I have had him no vets could suggest anything that could be done for the problem, and his little hippity hop walk had gotten worse and worse until he was hopping with every step.  Then a few months ago a substitute vet gave me Nutramax Dasuquin to try, and within a month the hippity hop had diminished and within two months it was gone!  It was hard to believe! I will keep him on it forever!  (And I will buy it from Amazon, at almost half the cost of what the vet charged.) Tonight I read some of these reviews and found that this med has been around for quite some time.  I am really disappointed that it took so long to learn about it, and I am telling and e-mailing all my friends with dogs to keep it in mind if their dogs ever show signs of any joint problems.

review_body: I purchased this gate for the entry between my living room and kitchen which is 56 inches wide. The gate fits into the opening just fine so this likely would fit the maximum span noted in the product description. The installation was a bit tricky as many other reviewers have mentioned. The paper template included is only accurate for the screw hole placement and the space between the brackets, it's about 1 inch off and it won't work unless you have even floors. My teenager and I figured out an efficient way to install the gate without much of an issue so here's how we did it. 1) we sized the gate to match the width of the opening and inserting the pressure bolts into the ends of the gate; 2) after inserting the plastic foot that goes in the middle of the span we pushed the end of the gate up against the jamb and snapped one of the brackets onto the lower bolt-we marked the screw holes with a sharp object; 3) then we used the paper template by matching the screw holes we marked for the lower bracket with the template and then marked the upper bracket screw holes; 4) we screwed both the upper and lower brackets onto one side of the jamb and placed the gate into the brackets; 5) using a level app on the phone to maintain level we determined where the lower bracket should go and marked the screw holes and repeated step 3 to determine where the top bracket should go. Thankfully it worked the first time. It's not the highest quality metal nor the most decorative but it will do for our purposes. My one complaint is that the pet door does not swing both ways and it's not removable so we'll have to tie it open. My chunky kitty fits through the pet door just fine.

product_title: CitiKitty "As Seen on Shark Tank" Cat Toilet Training Kit
review_headline: Almost worked? Read if you're thinking about buying
review_body:
So I was attracted to the idea of never scooping out litter again, and saving tons of money. I tried training my 1 year old kitty for several months, and eventually had to give up, here's a few reasons why.
I was extra patient with my cat, giving her at least 2 weeks at each stage before moving on to the next. She was scared of the wobbly plastic at first, but soon realized it's actually quite stable. She did great up until the second to last ring. I had to put up with the mess and smell everyone else talked about, but that was tolerable thinking of the litter-free days ahead. I tried to be with her as often I could to catch her when she goes and give her a treat. Here's the catch: because I was doing that, she learned to go only when I'm around (ie. holding it until she can't anymore, then going on my bed) The real problem came when the rings enlarged enough to allow her to go directly in the toilet. Number 1 was a problem because the rim of my toilet was too slippery for her to squat comfortably. Number 2 was a problem because when her poop drops, it creates a splash that sometimes hits her and scares her. Then, the real kicker, I had to go away for 2 weeks before she was completely trained. Even when I tried to restart her program after I came back, all hell had broken loose. She was pooping on the carpet, peeing on my bed... I stuck with it a while longer; she would still go in the toilet if I was watching her, but whenever I'm not around, her favorite spot was on the bathroom floor. I gave up eventually wanting to spare myself the cleaning and knowing I just can't be around 24/7 to train her.
Funny thing is... now I sometimes get lazy about cleaning her litter box, so it ends up pretty stinky. And I've caught her going in the toilet by herself quite a few times. :-/ (I guess the water covering smells better theory is actually true)
So I think verdict is... CityKitty does work... if you have the perfect set of circumstances.
1. Make sure youhave the time to be vigilant around you cat.
2. Double-/triple- estimate how long it would take. It won't hurt to go slow, but as soon as you rush and kitty finds somewhere else to go, there's no going back.
3. Make sure your toilet actually works for your cat. Mine was simply built too angled and slippery for mine. After slipping and falling in once, you can bet she avoided it until the trauma fades.

product_title: Coat Handler Antistatic Detangler Spray 12oz
review_headline: Coat Handler DETANGLER -- I Couldn't be Without It! LOVE!
review_body:
I usually purchase this product from a show dog supply etailer, but I felt I just had to write a review here after reading the 2-star review written below. I was pretty shocked to see that this product didn't work for them. This is my HOLY GRAIL grooming product for my little Shih Tzu. I have used the Coat Handler products for the past 9+ years for her. I do not know what I'd do if they were ever discontinued. Oh YES I do! I'd probably have to shave her BALD! lol

Honestly, without the Detangler (as well as \\"The Conditioner\\" -- gotta love the simplicity of the product names, huh?), her hair would be a matted mess. I use to have her in full show coat, and her hair would literally mat up before my eyes. :/ NOTHING (and I mean N O T H I N G!) could keep her hair mat-free, as this line could (and still does!). I had tried a gazillion other grooming products -- nothing worked! NOTHING could untangle mats as easily, and NOTHING could keep her hair tangle-free between bathings (she's bathed approx every 2 weeks). Of course, you DO have to do daily brushings, especially if you have a dog breed with \\"hair\\" vs \\"fur\\". Lhasas, Shih Tzu, Pekes, Maltese, Yorkies, etc etc and all other \\"drop-coated breeds\\" have \\"hair\\". Some of the breeds are double coated (Shih Tzu, Lhasa, Pekes, etc), whereas others are single-coated (Maltese, Silkies, etc). Double-coated drop-coated breeds will do FABULOUS with this \\"Coat Handler\\" line, as their double-coats are the ones that can really mat up QUICKLY. I wish I had known of this line while I was dealing with my Tzu's \\"pupply blow coat\\" phase. OMG. I thought my hair would go gray overnight. LOL She had the WORST puppy blowcoat phase of any pup I had ever owned. THE worst. :( Even after her puppy blowcoat phase, her hair would mat within hours after a brushing. THEN, I found out about The Coat Handler. My life (and hers!) changed. :) Daily brushings were a breeze! Mats were very few, and when there was a mat issue -- it was simple to brush out with the Detangler. Single coated drop-coated breeds will also love this product, though they may not need as much of the Detangler. As for other types of coats? I really cannot say if these products would work as well for those dogs with \\"fur\\" (GSD, Terriers, etc). I can't see that it would hurt, but perhaps a stronger type product would be needed (fur has more \\"oils\\" and is coarser than the hair of drop coated breeds). As for curly coated breeds? Again, I can't comment, as I only have experience with long-coated breeds. Again, IF you have a long-coated breed, and you have trouble with mats...GET THIS PRODUCT LINE! You will be very thankful, and so will your furbaby. :) Btw, my Tzu is now clipped down on her torso, while her leg furnishing are still full. I kept her topknot length, and kept a bit of her facial furnishings length. I STILL rely on Coat Handler to keep mats at bay. Every now and then I switch \\"shampoos\\", and I may even ADD in a \\"deep conditioner\\" (I LOVE Cindra's Protein Treatment!), BUT I ALWAYS always ALWAAAAAAAAAYS keep using both \\"The Conditioner\\", and \\"The Detangler\\" at EVERY bathtime. And of course, I use The Detangler during daily brushings.

However, there is a method to using these products:
Step 1:
Brush out the hair completely, making sure there are no mats BEFORE you bathe your drop-coated breeds.
I know The Coat Handler states that you do not have to brush first, but I prefer the ease of brushing first to avoid dealing with too many mats while the hair is wet. Trying to untangle a matted drop coated breed is akin to trying to untangle a wet cotton ball, imho. I, for one, do not want to chance that ordeal.

Step 2:
Shampoo, and then rinse thoroughly.

Step 3: Use \\"The Conditioner\\".
I add this to her bath water and let her soak for about 5 minutes. She's so tiny that I use a large plastic office-folder bin/tub as her \\"bathtub\\". :) Perfect for soakings. haha
IF this is the only \\"conditioner\\" I'm going to use for the bathing, I usually just towel dry her, as The Conditioner CAN be used as either a \\"rinse out\\" or a \\"leave in\\" treatment. :)

IF I'm going to also use a DEEP conditioning treatment (ie, Cindra's Protein Reconstructor is AMAZING to soften and silken drop-coats!), I will use the deep conditioner AFTER the shampoo, but BEFORE \\"The Conditioner\\". RINSE out the deep conditioner, then use the Coat Handler \\"Conditioner\\" as a last step \\"leave in treatment\\".

Step 4:
Towel dry. Then, BLOW DRY coat thoroughly, brushing as you dry the coat. IF you encounter any mats, you can mix a few squirts of The Conditioner into a 12oz spray bottle filled with water. Spray the mat, and work the mat loose with your fingers. Then, gently brush (or comb) the mat out. The Conditioner has great \\"slip\\", so most mats come out VERY easlily (IF you have done your work and pre-brushed before you bathe, at least.)

Step 5 -- THIS IS IMPORTANT!
This is the time to apply \\"The DETANGLER\\".
You must do the FIRST application on \\"freshly bathed, and DRIED hair\\". IF you wait a day after bathing, applying The Detangler will only make a mess of things -- it will attract dirt, instead of help repel it, and the hair will mat faster. You CAN still get the mats out by using The Detangler, but you will not be getting the full benefits of the product.

IF you apply The Detangler right after the blow-dry, The Detangler will help to keep hair static free -- resulting in less mats/tangles, and it will help to keep hair cleaner (ie, dirt, leaves, twigs, and all of the other fun stuff that long-coated pups manage to accumulate from potty trips, lol) will brush out with much more ease! :)

____

I do not work for The Coat Handler, but I wish I did! I believe in their product line THAT much!
I use to buy the smaller sized \\"spray bottles\\" of the conditioner and detangler, but I soon began buying the gallonsizes. I NEVER want to run out of either product, but especially not the Detangler! I even keep some spray sizes for travel and as a back up. I'd use these products on my own hair IF I knew they'd be safe on blonde highlights. :)

As for the shampoos (just thought I'd give it a mention here), I use both the \\"15:1\\" (this is a clarifying shampoo, and should be used about every 1 in 8 shampoos, esp if you use any products with \\"siliCONES\\" in them, as those can lead to build-up and cause skin issues), and the \\"5:1\\" (this is the regular \\"maintenance\\" shampoo. I DO use other shampoos on her paws because she has atopic allergies and has to use special treatment shampoos for daily paw washings that treat bacteria and yeast. However, for total-body grooming shampoos, I usually stick to the Coat Handler Maintenance 5:1 shampoo. Every few shampoos, I will ALT with \\"NEEM\\" shampoo, as it helps to repel mosquitos, and other summertime bugs. It's also soothing to the skin. When I use The Coat Handler shampoos, I will often just add a few drops of NEEM OIL to the Coat Handler Conditioner.

I hope this review helps anyone out there who is curious about Coat Handler products.
Not every product line will work on every coat type, but I think that IF you do have a drop-coated breed and are tearing your hair out over mat-issues, you should definitely give these products a try (esp the Conditioner AND the Detangler products).

product_title: SportDOG Brand In-Ground Fence System - Expandable to Contain 100 Acres and Unlimited Dogs - Easy to Install Underground Wire Dog Containment Kit - Waterproof Collar with Tone/Vibration and Shock
review_headline: This system eventually worked with my large stubborn dog.
review_body:
My family was at our wits end with our large dog. Living in a rural area, our dogs in the past have been allowed to roam and drive off the deer and raccoons. But our latest dog had developed a affection for crossing the hill and visiting our neighbors whom own Labradors and became buddies. Unfortunately at some point we got a visit saying our dog had scratched their sons car so we quickly had to cease his roaming behavior. A wireless invisible system did not work as the shock would not slow his running through the fence. We needed a stronger stimulus and this system worked in the end but please read the cons.

Pro - durable collar and unit with a varied selection of modes and strengths for your specific dog.
Enough wire to do all around your home with option to buy more wire to expand.
Can enclose plant beds or water garden ponds inside a perimeter to keep dog out of specific spots. Ours loved to climb in and pull up aquatic plant! Nothing like walking out on the back porch with a coffee and seeing patio covered in dead plants and debris, ugh.

Cons - if you have a quick dog, they can run through fence on rumble and tone mode. I can run through the fence on the widest boundary setting without getting the shock, so you can bet a dog can too. This was how my dog was escaping. He would walk the fence, looked for perceived gap in flags and as soon as he heard the tone and rumble would bolt through. No shock as he cleared the other side. He would also without hesitation chase a deer through fence or chase our neighbor all the way down the gravel road in his truck. He fully grasped the flag meaning from previous wireless collar system. What Fixed this issue for me was turning off vibrate and tone warning and go straight to shock only. As a warning, this is painful setting and hard enough that you can not hold a collar and take the shock. And when he took a hit from the fence, he yelps and retreats to our porch. But this was the last resort before having to keep dog tied out ( and constant barking) or installing dedicated dog fenced area.

Over about three weeks with the silent warning method, i was able to finally be confident with letting him outside on his own. We had to gradually give back his freedom, first being tied up on porch outside. THen minimal time allowed to roam yard supervised for gradually increased lengths of time. He did take new shocks as he tested different sections of fence. But now he has stopped rushing through fence, stopped chasing after neighbors truck, stopped hunting deer ( I've let him out to pee at night and found him at edge of fence barking at a deer on the other side. Before he would blast through and be a hill over) i feel like he is finally a companion that we desired. He is able to exercise and lounge in the grass and run but safely on our property. He can burn off his excess energy and barking has been reduced a great deal where before tie out was inadequate

Conclusion: follow the steps in training your dog. Have patience and be prepared to spend extra time getting it to work with your specific dog. This system Will work for stubborn and large breeds but takes extra work and some hard love. My father was livid when i bought this system after the failed invisible one. But 2 months later it is working and we have peace of mind with our dog. This system scores high for customizable features and layout but i docked one star because of the tone and vibrate feature being longer then shock.fore having to keep dog tied out ( and constant barking) or installing dedicated dog fenced area.

product_title: Nutramax Cosequin DS Chewable Tablets for Dogs
review_body:
Per a vet, most vets prescribe Cosequin early in the life-cycle of a dogs arthritis or other joint issues. As the condition worsens, they switch to Dasaquin. Her point - after a lecture by a noted animal pain specialist - was that dogs should be on BOTH medications because they do different things. Cosequin is a joint lubricant. Dasaquin is an anti-inflammatory.

My dog had been put on all Dasaquin and she recommended using both. I have just started following her recommendation - which involves backing off on my old puppy's dose of Dasaquin, and adding Cosequin. She certainly does not seem less mobile - there might be a slight improvement.

Perhaps someone more knowledgeable in the way these products actually work can correct me if I have been given bad information.

product_title: Pet Qwerks Talking Babble Ball Dog Toy
review_body:
Dear Amazon Shopper,

I like to periodically pick up a toy for my sister's adorable German Shepherd. Normally, I get her something chew-proof, since she tends to chew everything to bits, but since my sister leaves her alone for long tracts of time, I figured I ought to try something that might provide her with a little more stimulation. I noticed the positive reviews for this toy and gave it a shot. Unfortunately, the dog did not seem even remotely interested in it. She tried to chew on it at first, but immediately realized that it was plastic and decided not to bother with it. While it made noise, she kicked it all of one time, recognized that the ball emitted sounds, and then completely ignored it (note that I got the \\"large\\" ball since this Shepherd is 80lbs).

My thoughts on this toy generally are that it is meant for perhaps a different breed of dog. Shepherds are very pack-oriented and like to be included in social activities with their family (which this Shepherd sadly does not get enough of). It also appears that this toy is fairly cheaply constructed and the noise it emits sounds harsh and grating (perhaps why the dog isn't interested in kicking it?). It is also very sensitive. I imagine if the dog glanced at it intensely enough, it would probably go off.

The reason I gave this toy three stars instead of one is that other reviewers seem to have had luck with it. It's not terribly expensive (though for its cheap construction, I don't know that $9 is justified), and if your pet happens to love it, I can see it being a worthwhile investment (though you'll have to get used to constant, annoying sounds). Just know that when you purchase this item, your dog may be completely uninterested, and even if your dog enjoys this toy, at least superficially, it doesn't appear to be designed to hold up for all that long (though I can't comment on that from experience, as my sister's Shepherd hasn't interacted with it to any substantial degree).

Thank you, and if you pull the trigger on this one, I hope it works out.tial degree).

Per their wbsite\\"
Why are the jerky treats made in China?
China is a country where dark meat is more popular due to its inherent fat and flavor. DOGSWELL believes it is less wasteful to obtain our white meat in China where it is abundant, rather than sourcing it domestically, where white meat is less available and held at a premium. Not only do we care about your pet's health by sourcing only the healthiest meat available, we also practice sustainability by reducing as much waste as possible.
2) I used to buy 15oz bags in different flavors for the sake of variety. I noticed that they would get dry and \\"moldy\\" after a while despite the fact that I would seal the packages. I read the bag and saw an expiration date but nothing else. I went on the website and then realized that these treats have to be consumed 1-2 months after opening. Hello?!?! From Dogswell website:
Our resealable bags are designed to lock in freshness and keep air out. Once opened, our jerky treats are best within a 12 month period. VEGGIE LIFE® treats are best consumed within one to two months of opening the bag, as these vegetable/fruit treats are not preserved with artificial preservatives. To retain freshness and prolong shelf life, you may try removing all of the air inside the bag, tightly sealing it and putting it in the refrigerator.

review_headline: Fipronil, the active ingredient is no longer effective on fleas or brown ticks
review_body:
We have been using FrontLine products for years. Where we live with wooded areas and bushes we have a continual battle against fleas and brown ticks. Frontline used to work, but in the past year we have noticed that just one WEEK after using Frontline, the fleas and ticks are back.
Our yard is sprayed against fleas and ticks frequently, the dogs have been treated with the Spot-On type vials of Frontline with a spray for back up. Beds are regularly washed. and yet, still we find fleas on the dogs well within the one month period that the product is supposed to repel these external parasites.
My vet suggested Certifect. We bought $300 worth, We applied Certifect on the 27th of May to 5 of our dogs, by June 7th, the fleas were evident once more.
We tried Vectra 3D on 3 of our other dogs and so far they do not have fleas or ticks.
Fleas and ticks have bu9lt up a resistance to Fipronil. Do not waste your money on any product containing Fipronil. We have tried collars, sprays, spot-on treatments and, being a multi-dog household believe me we WANT a product to be effective. Frontline or Certifect do not do the job. Try Vectra 3D, we shall see at the end of the month if it stays the course.

product_title: Just for Cat Urine Destroyer Cat Remover
review_headline: 6 Cats, 1 corner  -  this stuff works better than anything else I have tried (I've tried a lot)
review_body:
Before anyone on here starts spewing on about animal hoarding or spaying & neutering:
2 cats inherited from deceased best friend and they were already fixed
1 (formerly pregnant & currently 'fixed') female cat inherited from my now deceased mother (the cat gave birth not long after my mother rolled on past her expiration date)
3 male cats (all spawn of the formerly pregnant female & all 'fixed').

I have 6 cats, several litter boxes - one of which is the CatGenie (self flushing and awesome for the fearless few of my mob) - and while most of the time, the cats are all willing to share, they do tend to 'take sides' when they're in their moods. This has led to some problems.

Of the first two cats I inherited, one is a female and she's only a year or two older than the "Mom" cat. The other is an "Old Man" who is fatherly to the other 5 cats and is never easily bothered or upset about anything. He likes the CatGenie if the other litter boxes are not meeting his bathroom preferences.

This product has saved my nostrils from horrifically malodorous carpeting.

The girl cats both assume they are Queen of Mi Casa and tend to get in bad moods when the boys favor one of them over the other. So when one of the 'girls' decided to have a squat in the dining room corner, it was assumed by the majority of the remaining mob that the dining room corner was the place to be. It's hard to say if this was a territorial issue or not. Perhaps it was to begin with, but when the younger boys (Old Man wasn't having any part of the carpet) noticed the new fragrance saturating the dining room corner and spotted a nice healthy steaming pile, they all decided it was just as pleasant as the litter boxes.

While there is some slight lingering odor if you get your face down there close enough for a good long whiff, the fact of the matter is that the carpet and padding are in need of replacement, and this stuff has stopped my cats from having either a wizz or poo on the floor since I used this product. It isn't carpet perfume or an odor masking mess - it is seriously an odor eliminator/minimizer.

It doesn't have a sprayer but I needed to completely saturate a decent area. I saw someone mention a watering can somewhere and this was a good idea. I suppose you could dilute it a little and just slosh it down, but I am clumsy and the thing may have just as likely slipped from my hand and spilled all over just the one spot. My issues were in 3 substantially large spots in that one particular corner.

If you have cats that like to wizz on your bed, then I'm inclined to tell you that your cat just hates your guts. I see that posted a lot, people whining about wee on the bed. Haha, no seriously, I think what cats find enjoyable is when they find something absorbent - be it blankets, carpet (padding underneath), or even on your bed if they're off the litter box for some reason.

I have very good cats. They're all up for a belly rub and most of the time you'll find 3 or more in a heap napping somewhere. A couple of times per year though, they celebrate some sort of top secret feline festivity and will commandeer my bed in order to all nap in a big circle, nose to tail and all facing inward toward one another. They are an unusual bunch in the fact that they are all attention seeking balls of fur. None of them fit the stereotypical 'aloof and independent' description of a cat at all. Then again, they have a strange human room mate so I can't blame them in the slightest for their strangeness.

In any event, I would definitely purchase this product again.

We have four cats at home and this auto cleaner certainly takes away a lot of burden. Now we feel we can't live without it.

The poops are often not picked up by the scoop completely - some break apart or stick to it - and when that happens, during the drying phase you'll get strong unpleasant smells (imagine placing cat poops into an oven and then heat it up nicely...) The manual isn't clear at all on settings - it could be an outdated version and doesn't match the machine exactly. We had to trial and error to figure out how to set for 4 cats and how to know the detergent is running low - none of these is described or at least not precisely in the manual. It also lacks a timer display so to set the start of the 14hr-on-10hr-off cycle, you'll need to manually start it when you want it to start. This could have been set by entering the desired start time if there's a display or option for input. The timer has no internal memory so if there's a short blackout, you'll need to reset the start of the cleaning cycle manually at exactly the time you want it to start. A real hassle - imagine if you want it to start everyday at 5am, then you need to wake up at 5am to manually set it!

This machine is really handy but apparently there's a lot for improvement still. Nonetheless, I couldn't find any other competitive product in the market so this is still my best choice. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend to cat owners.

product_title: Deluxe Quilted and Padded seat cover with Non-Slip Fabric in Seat Area for Pets - One Size Fits All 56"Wx94"L Taupe
review_body: I got this after my dog had an awful, soupy accident in the front seat of his daddy's car.  Needless to say, it was not a pleasant experience, and my worst fear was that the same thing would happen on my perforated leather seats.  I ordered this cover the next day.  So far it has been great!  it is easy to set up with just four clips to hook around the head rests of the front and back seats.  So far, I have not tried any of the other configurations, but I am sure those are just as simple.  The cover works fine in the back seat area of my little station wagon, but it would probably work better in a larger truck or SUV.  For instance, the side flaps don't really fall where they should, and I have to watch so I don't catch them in the door.  My favorite part about this cover, and the reason I got this cover as opposed to others, was for the extra material meant to cover the floor.  This is a great feature, and it also means that I will have plenty of material to cover the area behind the seats in case I need to make room for passengers by moving the dog to the back.  I was also excited to read that the cover is washable; however, before washing it for the first time I realized that it is only hand washable, not machine washable.  Nevertheless, I took my chances and threw it into the washer on its gentlest cycle, sans detergent.  The reason hand washing is recommended, as I learned, is because of the velcro patches on the sides near the corners.  During washing, they fold over and attach to the back lining of the cover and tear it apart.  Luckily, the areas of destruction were small and out of the way.  I don't believe the damage will negatively affect the performance of the cover.  All in all, this is a great product that I highly recommend!

product_title: Precious Cat Dr. Elsey's Ultra Litter Attractant
review_headline: I had so hoped this would work
review_body: I received my Precious Cat Litter Attractant today, and was so excited to try it out.  We got a 15 month old rescue Bengal 3 months ago.  Improper elimination has been a problem from day one.  She is 100% poop perfect in the box, yet she is highly inconsistent about peeing in the boxes...there are 3 litter boxes in our home.  So when the Litter Attractant arrived today, I sprinkled a little bit in two of her boxes, and mixed it in with the litter.  Our kitty sniffed both boxes, and then, in less than five minutes, she had pee'd on the bedroom chair, located BETWEEN the two boxes.  Today was the first time she has voided on furniture.  It has always been the floor.  Now we ARE TRULY at our wit's end.  I'm trying another route.... I've thrown out the new litter that had the Litter Attractant in it, and I've brought in a cup of dirt from the side of our house.  I'm mixing THAT with fresh litter and see what happens.  We walk our cat on a leash nightly and she has a favorite spot she pees outside.  So I've brought the outside in to her.  Praying this will work.  Litter Attractant sure didn't help us....it made things exponentially worse!

product_title: Cherry Blossom 1/2" Adjustable H-Style Cat Harness
review_headline: Instructions say not to use with tie-out.
review_body:
My cat has been using a regular harness with connector straps on both the top and bottom, and although she seems comfortable enough in it I thought this Lupine H harness would feel better on her with one less strap. We're on a top floor where she goes on the porch with a tie-out, but always supervised. However, it says on the paper enclosed with the harness that it should not be used with a tie-out. I'm worried that the design would make it easier for her to strangle if she suddenly got into a bind, and am afraid to use it.

The fabric is also quite stiff, although overall the harness does appear well made, and this Cherry Blossom pattern is pretty and they sell a matching leash.

The fact that this was made in the U.S.A., and apparently by a small company, is a plus.

For walking a cat this harness would probably be fine, but I wish the ad had specified that it is not for use with tie-outs. We don't walk the cat because she stresses from the noise of traffic and there are several cats and dogs unleashed in the neighborhood.

I did try the harness once on the cat, and within 2 minutes it slid down near her belly, and the tie-out became tangled all around her feet. Yes, I had it a bit loose on her, but she wears her regular harness loose for comfort with no problem.

The low review pertains to use with a tie-out, and the insufficient information on the ad for it. If I'd bought it to walk the cat it would have received a higher rating.

product_title: Greenies Dog Treats (Regular, 18 Pack)
review_body: The picture posted here for this product shows a box for a 36-count Regular Size box.  Once you pay and place the order, you will find that an 18-count bag is being sent to you instead.  The picture and the title \\"Regular Size\\" gives you the impression that the Regular Size is referring to the description Greenies uses to match the treat with the size of the dog (again, visible in the picture), but believe it is a shady way for this company to try to get away with a bait and switch scam. product_title: SportDOG Field Trainer for Stubborn Dogs, SD-400S
review_body:
I have a corgi/cattle dog mix. Very high energy with the compulsion to herd everyone around her. I adopted her and have no clue what her past life was like but she is a complete attention hog. She can't get enough. I keep thinking maybe she never got attention before. So what does she do, she attacks anyone walking through the door. She will crowd you and worst of all, jump on you. It was such an issue that it was hard to have people over and hard to take her to the dog park because she would jump all over everyone. I tried every training technique I could find. I took her to basic obedience and even the trainer, with over 20 years experience, was having an issue with her. So I went to my last resort, a training collar.

First thing I have to say is try the collar on yourself. You know your dog. Different dogs, different weights, different personalities, you want to be able to pick a setting that you know will get your dogs attention without freaking the dog out. I tried every setting on this collar and I wouldnt say anything ever hurt but the highest setting sure scared the crap out of me. Its just a really wierd feeling. I am not trying to traumatize my dog so I highly doubt it will ever come to me using the highest setting on her. Follow the manual on how to acclimate your dog to the collar so he/she associates it with a good thing. I did that and my dog actually gets excited when I put the collar on her.

So the results.....amazing. Her jumping has lessened when she doesnt have the collar on and it has stopped when she does. I am hoping to one day not have to use it at all. I paired the first few "shocks" with the beep sound and I only had to "shock" her maybe 4-5 times before the beep is enough to get her to not jump and come to me. She can be off leash anywhere now, I just beep her and she comes running. People can come in my house and she will still crowd them and sit at their feet not letting them move without petting her but at least no one is walking away with scratch marks on their legs anymore. I think this product is more than worth the money. Battery life is good. I can't speak for my dog but she doesn't seem uncomfortable wearing it.

review_headline: Liked it but now a problem

Our doxie has had bouts of pancreatitis so we needed a low fat, good fiber, healthy treat for her. We stopped giving her rawhide years ago so wanted something that could giver her doxie teeth a work out like rawhide. We know giving treats is a \\"people\\" thing but it is still nice to be able to giver her something periodically. But we were so hesitate because of the pancreatitis. Crumps is THE perfect thing for her. We actually cut them in strips (need a tough pair of scissors) and give them to her periodically. She LOVES them !!!!

Well she loved them and still does but we have had to stop giving them to her. We were cutting them into smaller strips and giving the small strip to her periodically. We noticed about 4 a.m. (3 different times) after giving her a strip the evening before she woke us up with an upset tummy. She walked around somewhat uncomfortable like and in 2 cases refused food for about 6 hours and the other time she vomited. Since we have stopped giving them to her this has stopped. product_title: PetSafe Yard & Park Rechargeable Dog Training Collar with Tone and Static Correction, Waterproof, Up to 400 Yards
review_headline: Good collar, but not for all dogs
review_body:
I bough this for a thirty-eight pound beagle with high hopes. My goal was to stop unnecessary barking, jumping up, and running out our front gate. I started him just wearing it turned off-- he was scared. Then I tried to associate the positive tone with treats-- no luck, it just scared him more. So I tried teaching him not run off, thinking if his mind was occupied, he wouldn't be so worried-- that didn't work either, he was still scared, and just ran and hid. Note that I hadn't even shocked him once; just negative tone. It did stop him when he barked too much, even goes through a wall, which is handy. But what I did accomplish wasn't worth having his confidence comepletely shattered. The problem was that he was so scared that he didn't connect the negative tone with bad behavior; it just was scary, and a dog can't learn if he's afraid.

So, yes this is a great shock collar-- it does what is advertised, it has a good range, and the different shock levels are a plus; but it seems some dogs just can't handle it, and no matter how well the collar funtions, it doesn't matter if the dog isn't learning. So if you dog is the type that roles on his back or cowers when you raise your voice (in other words, sensitive dog), this might not have a good effect. However, if you dog doesn't get scared easily (a tough dog) this probably would work well-- thus the three stars.

My advice-- don't fool yourself. If your dog is a wimp (I say that affectionately), pass the shock collars up. It's not worth ruining a dogs confidence just to curb a few bad behaviors.

product_title: Brentwood 4-Inch Gel Memory Foam Orthopedic Dog Bed, 100-Percent Waterproof
review_body:
Purchase: Large size & Chocolate colored bed for 12.5 yr old 3 legged dog.

First Impressions: Literally as soon as I took the bed out of the packaging to put on the floor, she immediately laid down and slept on it the rest of the day! As for sizing, I wasn't sure what to get my dog, she's medium to large size: about 24\\" from base of neck to tail and weighs about 60lbs. I'm glad I got the Large since she does like to 'splay out' entirely on occasion and fits well (with a few inches to spare on every side). When she curls up on the large, there is room for another dog her size or smaller. If I had gotten the medium, she would probably have limbs hanging off if she splayed out, though if she curled into a ball all the time, she would have fit fine on the medium.

About the packaging: it comes in a really long box all rolled up super vacuum sealed down air tight plastic (and taped), so I recommend unrolling it and letting it 'air out' for 10 min or so for the foam to 'fluff up' back to normal. It does stand 4\\" tall when measured and my dog does not 'touch the ground' even when sitting or laying on the foam (so it does hold up well). It also is a bit plastic sounding since it does have the water proof liner, but I'm perfectly okay with that since my dog sometimes gets carried away licking spots on her bed and soaking saliva through (so I'd rather not have her ruin the foam). The cover is fairly easy to get off, a bit tricky getting back on with the foam since it is a tight fit.

Consensus: My dog LOVES her new bed (we've had it for a few weeks now) and even though her favorite spot to relax is on the couch, she now spends significantly more time on her bed than before. Overall I'm VERY happy with this purchase and so is my dog!

product_title: Super Skamper Ramp Pet Safety Pool Exit - for Animals up to 200 lbs
review_headline: Does not work in lakes with a bulkhead
review_body: I bought this product to help our 65 pound lab get in and out of the lake more easily.  Although we have stairs going into the lake, the stairs are narrow and steep and were rarely used by our lab who preferred to climb in and out over the bulkhead (which had rocks for footing on the lakeside going down into the water).  After a weekend of climbing over the bulkhead, our dog would suffer stiff hips and difficulty walking.  The scamper ramp seemed like the ideal solution.  Unfortunately, it was was not.  In fact, it seemed like a poorly make product.  Although easy to assemble, it did not come with the two necessary screws required for installation and the 6 foot rope that accompanied it could have been longer (but that would have been easy enough to change had we decided to keep the skamper ramp).  We found the ramp flimsy, unstable and inappropriate for a 65 pound dog--although the manufacturer claims it is suitable for dogs up to 200 pounds. (It may work for a 15 pound dog.) We tried two installations at different points (next to stairs and parallel to the bulk head as well as perpendicular to the bulk head with rocks underneath attempting to better secure and stabilize the skamper ramp.  Nothing worked.  We thought that had the ramp been longer, wider and heavier, it may have possibly worked for a 65 pound dog.  After our experience, we find it hard to believe that the skamper ramp could work for a 200 pound dog or that it would have worked any better in a swimming pool. The skamper ramp is currently in the box, waiting to be returned.  The only benefit of the skamper ramp is that after trying to coax our dog to use it, she now prefers the steps.

product_title: Elite Sponge Filter
review_body: I didn't buy my filters through Amazon, but at the LFS. I have the double filter in my 55 gallon and the single in a 5 1/2 gallon betta tank. Each works very well. I had occasional problems with water quality in my 55 for a couple years. Adding this filter to supplement my HOB Emperor 400 filter solved that problem. Sponge filters make for great supplement bio-filters and this one does not disappoint. I liked the double enough that when I added the betta tank in my son's room, I bought the single filter for that tank. I was able to take one of the two sponge filters out of the double from my 55 gallon and put it into the smaller tank and then replace it in the 55 with the new single filter. They are interchangeable and allow you to help cycle other tanks more easily, which I think is a great convenience of sponge filters. The only flaw with the single filter is that the only option is to have the filter face out horizontally from the tank wall, which seems to take up a little more room in my small tank. In hindsight, I should have bought another double, which gives the option of using only one or two sponges at the vertical position. Others have complained about noise, and I suppose there is some truth to that. The noise from the pump and then bubble noise inside the tank may annoy some people. After a while I personally just think it becomes \\"white noise\\" which is kind of a good thing in my 2 year old son's room. Others my disagree. Overall, I have been very happy with these filters and would recommend them as supplement filters in larger tanks or the sole filters in smaller tanks.

product_title: Dogswell Vitality Chicken Treats -- 2 oz
review_headline: DO NOT BUY - THIS WILL MAKE YOUR CAT SICK!!
review_body:
I usually don't write reviews but when I read Zach's recent review on Dogswell I just HAD to. If you love your pet PLEASE don't give him/her these treats!

We had a beautiful, strong and healthy, young red ticked Oriental Shorthair Cat named Chopin. He was born November 15, 2009. In July of 2011 he suddenly got very, very sick and nobody knew what was wrong with him, until the vet said that he was poisoned.

Chopin's favorite treats were chicken jerky treats from Vita Kitty - Catswell (same as Dogswell, just for cats) and this was the only thing he would continue to eat when he got sick. We didn't know at that point that the treats made him even more sick. His mom, Wazoo, got sick as well, but she didn't eat as many of these treats and recovered (her kidneys, however, got very much affected and, after a lot of vet visits and pain on her end, died on my birthday, April 19 of this year, 2013). Our other cats - Bubu, Xena and Six-Toes - didn't like the treats, so they didn't get sick.

On August 21, 2011, Chopin passed away in my arms and we were devastated. Shortly after, there was a \\"voluntary pet food recall\\" and we reported Chopin's death to the FDA.

I created a video on YouTube for my little Chopin and a page on Facebook \\"Chopin for Healthy Pet Food\\", which I will continue in order to help pet parents get all the information they need to buy healthy pet food - if I had known that this particular treat was produced in China I would have never bought it in the first place.

If I could have given this treat negative stars I would have.

review_headline: Just does not work well for poodles

The scissors are very thick and do not easily get into small areas. The hair just 'slips' out of the blades and does not cut. The write up on the scissors said they were designed to 'hold' the hair when you made a cut. Nope, does not work on poodles.    UPDATE July 2, 2013:  Mr. Matthew Michel of Scaredy Cut did send me a complimentary second pair to try and see if they worked better. I am sorry to say they did not. So Mr. Michel has refunded my money. His customer service has been exemplary!    What he does not know is that I am getting ready to send him some of my poodles hair (I groomed her a few days ago) for him to try and maybe he can replicate the problem. Perhaps the scissors need adjusting or I am not using them correctly. I have tried cutting with the micro-jagged edge up and then down (turned the scissors over). I also tried them on my Australian Cattle Dog and his hair slipped out of the scissors, too. (Poodles have different texture hair than most dogs.) I really would like to get these to work because they seem to be well made - they just aren't working for me. Others have had great success with them.    UPDATE January 13, 2015: Mr. Michel of Scaredy Cut has continued to solve the poodle hair problem with several more pairs of scissors adjusted differently. They most recent scissors kinda worked, but the poodle hair still just slides out of the scissors. Again, poodles (and other dogs such as Portuguese Water Dogs, Labradoodle, etc.) do not have 'fur' - they have soft hair and they do not shed very much (thus, the need for grooming!). Again, the product works well for others - just not for my poodle. The customer service of Scaredy Cut is exemplary and I am not dissatisfied with the service, nor the product; it is just that the scissors don't work for my dog.

It tells you where they are near but you really don't get an exact address. I was hoping it would tell me something like in the parking lot of a store But instead it just gives a main cross street. I am using that as an example because we took the tracker with us to Home Depot one night to see what it would do. review_headline: Finally, an inexpensive cure to my dog's ear fungus overgrowth and discomfort
review_body:
I have an older female purebred black Labrador, 12 1/2 yrs old named Rose who has really suffered from constant ear infections for many years. I took her to the vet a few years ago about this problem and was advised to have her whole inner ear surgically removed! That is definitely something I would not consider. Surgery cannot be undone and can lead to interference fields in other parts of the body. I don't remember the cost, but it was not cheap. Also got an $80 bill for the useless vet visit. I have been trying other anti-fungals such as coconut oil, tea tree oil, oregano oil, hydrogen peroxide, herbal ear washes, etc. but they were not as comprehensive as the EcoEars. I like that all the ingredients work together to knock out the infection very quickly, within the prescribed 10 days. The first couple days, when I did the application as suggested, I could tell by her reaction, that it was very uncomfortable as it attacked the infection creating maybe a burning sensation inside her ears. We had a fresh snowfall just 2 weeks ago and when I took her outside, she was rolling head first into the snow for some relief with vigorous head shaking to get rid of the fluid. This happened several days in a row, but I could tell it was improving. Each time was less irritating for her. She wanted to get away from me when it was time to clean her ears, but I think she also knew it was helping her ears heal. I used a single paper towel to absorb any excess and to wipe out both ears & then toss...wasn't that messy. Last week, I bought the Wax-Vac ear cleaner from a local Walmart (less than $10) to try to vacuum out any debris and excess moisture. It's not necessarily made for pets, but I think it's beneficial. Rose doesn't mind the gentle suction and even helps cool off her ears internally. I have already recommended EcoEars to several people as it's a terrific product. I only used a small portion of the 8 oz bottle I purchased which is nice because I'll probablyuse it periodically to keep her ears healthy. I think veterinarians should at least know about this as a cure although they would probably up the price. Thank you Enchanted Naturals and Amazon.com for offering this at such a reasonable cost.

P.S. I took my dog off all commercial dogfood 9 mos. ago...had her on the most expensive grain-free brands. I switched her to a raw meat diet which did wonders to clear up her dry itchy skin and all the excessive shedding and dander, plus got rid of the stinky smell and she lost the extra weight! On the high-priced dry, grain-free dogfood, she constantly scratched and bit her hind quarters to relieve the itching. The dry dogfood contributes to drying out their skin, but the raw diet replenishes the fat and oils to stop the shedding, the smell and all the itching. There's a recipe at dinovite.com. I use quinoa instead of white rice because quinoa is not a grain. Also, I throw in tumeric powder (anti-inflammatory) for arthritis, slippery elm bark powder, nettle leaf, granulated garlic, and fennel seed powder...all good for relieving dry, itchy skin. Found that at verialiving.com/whatarelief. Dinovite has great articles & products to help your pets. Dinovite also recommends feeding your dog coldwater fish..i.e. salmon, mackerel & sardines alternately for the healthy Omega-3 oils in their diet. I use the canned versions, even tuna, and she loves it! Rose is healthy and active for her age and now much better since her ears don't bother her. She only has just a little white on her chin so I think she's aging well. I don't buy or feed her any dog snacks either as they are full of junk and many are being recalled off the market with increasing frequency. As a treat, I give her beef soup bones usually boiled for 10-15 minutes. She can chew on those for a long time. She also loves dried roasted seaweed or Nori which is full of vitamins and minerals. I buy it at Safeway or Walmart very inexpensively. Another treat is a couple spoonfuls of coconut oil if its not liquid. I've thought about making my own beef or chicken jerky for her too with a healthy marinade like coconut aminos (found at health food stores) instead of soy sauce.

Hope these suggestions can help you give your dog comfort, well-being and a clean bill of health. So glad I made the changes for Rose. She's much more content. EcoEars was a plus.

Also, although all bully sticks smell, these are the worse smelling bully sticks I've ever come across. The only nice thing is they come in a reusable bag which helps to hold in the smell.

The bag says it contains 50 sticks and although I didn't count the number of sticks I actually weighed them. The total weight of the bag was 14oz. With shipping I paid just under $55. I previously tried another brand on Amazon.com, which I thought was rather expensive until I received them and weighed them. Their 50 thins sticks weighed 1 pound 12 oz, almost twice the weight of these sticks and cost only $80. Additionally the Shadow River lasted twice as long as the ValueBull. The Shadow River sticks were larger in size and smelled a lot better, as far a bully sticks could smell better. They don't come in a reusable bag, which it too bad, but the bag is a thicker mil. So the smell didn't penetrate through the bag.

So far my two dogs have liked all of the sticks I've purchased for them so it comes down to my preference and I would recommend trying these other bully sticks for a better value and quality.

product_title: Marina Power Filter
review_body:
The Marina 210 looks alright from the outset. Well to make a long story short, it broke off on the first day of setting up and so the filter just sat crooked against the tank; furthermore, it made the most annoying noise---of cheap plastic vibrating unceremoniously against glass.

To top it off, I wasn't the only one unhappy. The fish were enveloped in yellowish, cloudy water (usu. two days before my weekly cleaning routine. The flow of water was so weak that it only perturbed about a tenth of the water's surface; thus its filtering capability was so weak I had to up my weekly 15-25% water change to twice a week. (FYI: My bioload includes: 1 dwarf gourami, 1 betta, 2 algae eaters, 2 dwarf catfish bottom feeders, and a nerite snail. Based on that situation I felt the Marina 210 was very inefficient to handle the job.

I do not recommend this product for novice fish owners, unless your bioload is small and you don't want to grow and manage live planted aquariums.

product_title: Purina ONE True Instinct In Gravy Wet Cat Food - (24) 3 oz. Cans
review_body:
I buy this product from amazon on a subscription basis for the convenience- I have four cats and having to patiently scan every can at the local grocery store was getting maddening. I also buy this product because my cats overall like it - and they WILL throw up other name brand canned cat food, including Fancy Feast, Friskies, Nine Lives. I do think there is some slight improvement in quality with this brand . It does not make them sick. I have tried other and natural cat foods in a can from the local boutique pet store- and my cats sometimes eat it and most times just did not. I have tried the canned and near or exactly human-grade cat foods on Amazon- they overall just did not appeal to my cats. for now I am sticking with what seems to work - this canned brand of cat food and Purina Natural dry cat food (in a green bag at most all stores), and sometimes cooked organic chicken, especially for my older male cat who asks for the organic chicken and brightens when I have it in the kitchen. Seriously - he does not do the same with commercially farmed non-organic chicken and I don't know what that is but animals ARE smart.
I really can't say I LOVE this canned cat food but for now it's the best thing going for my treasured felines overall in the canned food department. P.S. Sometimes they don't really eat all of it but they will lick off the gravy consistently. I don't fuss about any waste - sometimes any of us just don't feel like cleaning our plates, us meaning all of us mammals!

product_title: Fluker's Heat Mat for Reptiles and Small Animals, Large (17 x 11 Inches, 20 watt)
review_headline: Not All Materials for a Safe Install, are included !!!!!!!
review_body:
You will find a lot of commentary on this mat, indicating the inadequacies - to no instructions included to install this flimsy plastic strip or \\"frisby\\" type mat. I was expecting the convenience of self adhesive installation, like their competitor's ZooMed heat mat.

The instructions provided indicate: \\"The heat mat should have expanded polystyrene at a minimum of 6mm thick, fixed to the outside surface of the heat mat.\\" WELL - There Isn't any Polystyrene INCLUDED ! Apparently this is a Precaution because the Polystyrene reduces wasted heat energy and will direct heat back into the enclosure. They additionally and strongly indicate: \\"All heaters can be potentially hazardous if misused - Do not take any risks with the lives of animals\\". . . The instructions also read: \\"Ensure that the heat mat is fixed securely to the floor or wall of the cage by securing with good quality adhesive tape. Do not use low tack adhesive tapes such as masking or insulating tape (ALSO NOT INCLUDED) So why in haitis would Fluker's NOT include ALL required Components !!!!!! It has been three days and I have not heard back from Fluker Labs: (800) 735-8537 www.flukerfarms.com - for support. I am Not Having a Good Experience with Flukers and I am resorting to clumsy heat lamps until the science of this install is clear.

review_headline: Just didn't work for our dog

We bought this bark/ training collar to replace a cheaper one that got wet and stopped working. The cheaper worked great up until my son strayed out standard poodle with the hose. This one was much more expensive but it was waterproof and had a auto bark feature that I thought would be a good addition. We received the device and it looked impressive and a sturdy device. We charged it up and put it on our dog. First thing I noticed is the remote controller is complicated to use ( too many settings ) the collar is large and fits a variety of doggy necks but seems extra extra long for even the biggest dog neck. I turned the auto bark feature on but the device goes into 'sleep mode' after 15 or so minutes and if your dog doesn't bark with in that time, you have to use the remote to reactivate or wake it up - so what's the point of auto bark? ... Anyway bottom line is that the device
Seemed to have little or no affect on our dog. We tried it out for a few days and the barking continued. The cheaper one I bought worked much better but isn't waterproof and we have a water dog so I'm shopping around for another one that is waterproof. i may have to spend over $100 which I didn't want to do

I want to add that we got our refund really quick so no problems there:-)

product_title: Harrisons High Potency Fine 5lb …
review_body:
This is one of the best foods you can buy for your domesticated bird. The ingredients are very high quality, certified organic, and very healthy for your bird. I must confess that I do mix this food with Roudybush, another high quality pellet food. I could not be happier with Harrisions than I am - it simply exceeds all of my expectations. Converting your bird to a pellet diet from a seed diet can be somewhat difficult but if you have patience and are consistent it will pay off, and your bird will be healthier. I highly recommend this product for any domesticated bird. Below is the list of ingredients for the Fine - I hope this review helps you to decide if this this product is for you. If you find this product is too costly, and it is not cheap, do check out Roudybush as well, it is cheaper, but is generally considered not quite as good as this diet and it is not organic, but I do feed my birds both of these foods. Also please note this is the 'high potency' forumula, there is also a daily diet that is a bit of a different recepie but Harrison's recommends if you are changing from another food to Harrision's that you use the High Potency for at least the first six months.

Ingredients: *Ground Hulled White Millet (Proso), *Ground Shelled Sunflower Seeds, *Ground Hulless Barley, *Ground Yellow Corn, *Ground Soybeans, *Ground Shelled Peanuts, *Ground Rice, *Ground Green Peas, *Ground Lentils, *Ground Toasted Oat Groats, Chia Seed, *Ground Alfalfa, Calcium Carbonate, Montmorillonite Clay, Spirulina, Ground Dried Sea Kelp, Vitamin E Supplement, Sea Salt, Vitamin A Supplement, Vitamin D3 Supplement, Niacin Supplement, Vitamin B12 Supplement, Riboflavin Supplement, d-Calcium Pantothenate, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, d-Biotin, Thiamine Mononitrate and Sodium Selenite.

*CERTIFIED ORGANIC INGREDIENT

Guaranteed Analysis

Moisture 10.0% max

I wanted to include here a recipe for a fresh diet that a breeder I highly respect gave me just to offer some advice to keep our pet birds healthier - it is not at all related this the product I have reviewed here but it could very well give you some great ideas to get fresh fruits and vegetables into your bird.

All domestic birds, especially parrots, lovebirds, parrotlets, parakeets, canaries, finches, conures, etc, should have fresh fruit and vegetables and they can present a challenge to get them to eat them. Gives this recipe a try Here's a recipe that I make and it took some time for them to get used to it, but now my lovebirds and my parrotlets both eat this when provided. I give it in the morning and remove uneaten food in the evening.
1 apple cored and chopped
1/2 Cup chopped raw broccoli
1 Chopped bell pepper seed included
2 shredded carrots
1/2 Cup chopped greens (bok choy, mustard greens, kale and/or chard)
1/4 Cup frozen corn (can be eliminated if you put slices of raw corn on the cob in treat holders/clips in your cage - all my birds LOVE it and I have had 100% success getting them to eat this)
1/4 Cup frozen peas
1/2 Cup cooked rice (brown or GABA brown rice)
1/2 Cup cooked dried beans (they will need to be soaked overnight for 8 hours)
A handful of blueberries, chopped cherries and chopped seedless grapes
Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl. Place ingredients in an ice cube tray and freeze. Remove frozen cubes and place in plastic bags to store in freezer. Then you can take out the perfect portion on a daily basis . They say 1 cube per bird but you may bind that 1 cube will work well for a pair of birds of if smaller birds, even more. Instead of an ice cube tray I use slider freezer bags and press them flat after I fill them with enough of the mixture and this way I can easily break off appropriate sized pieces. This recipe is variable and you can switch out or add/delete ingredients that you have on hand or what you know your birds already like.

This recipe is in ADDITION to their regular diet of pellets and seeds and not a substitute.

product_title: Pioneer Pet Raindrop Ceramic Drinking Fountain
review_headline: Not perfect, but I like it.
review_body:
After two weeks I decided to write a review. Over all, I am very pleased so far. Price on Amazon and product quality seem quite good. (Sorry for the editing trouble - my smartphone is difficult sometimes.)

I was excited to get the fountain delivered and set it up right away. Being a little cocky, I referred to the instructions only afterward because I wanted to know if I'd ruined it yet. Nope! Very simple. I was thrilled.
The cat was suspicious, however. I ended up leaving the regular water bowl down for him for a few days, then unplugged the fountain for a few days so that he'd try it out. Now he drinks out of it when it is running, but he approaches it cautiously and tests the water with his paw. He will only drink out of the pool. My intention is that he would be encouraged to drink more water, so I hope it helps.
PROTECT YOUR FLOOR - Twice I have found the towel under the fountain soaked, so keep an eye on it. The fountain was not empty and I did not see how the water had spilled (maybe 2 cups worth).
PLEASANT AMBIENT SOUND - It does not disturb me at all. There is little difference in the pump's functioning at its different settings.
PRETTY - Of course, mine is in an awkward place, but practicality is more important to me than decoration. It is a cat bowl with features, not a decorative fountain that the cat drinks out of, in my mind.
INDEED, IT DOES NEED CARE - I find it odd that people would complain about having to fill or clean their fountain. Didn't they clean and fill the water dish before? My cat deserves to be taken care of. Maybe some people want all the benefits of having a pet without really carrying enough to take responsibility for the let's needs. For me it is a very minor labor of love.
