product_title: Prevue Pet Products Tinkle Turf for Small Dog Breeds
review_body:
Like with anything you want to teach your puppy you have to start young! I also ask you ready the entire review as I did tremendous amount of research before purchasing this product and I believe I have solutions to many of the problems people have had in their reviews. I acquired a purebred chocolate lab when she was 8 weeks old. Initially all I had was some generic puppy pads that I had purchased from a local grocery store. I gated her in a small space while I was away (not in a crate) and she was using these for pee and poop. However the pads were a pain to continually clean up and after one or two pee's she was disinterested in using them and would have accidents. At about 10 weeks I had purchased the Tinkle Turf and received it the next day along with the Simple Solution X-LARGE PADS. The idea was that I would use the pads underneath the Tinkle Turk. I tried this combination in the small space while I was gone and it was next to the door when I was at home and while I was asleep there was just a pad next to the bedroom door. This worked beautifully! Eventually I rewarded her for using the Tinkle Turf with more space she could roam within the house. Eventually the Tinkle Turf stays next to the back door to the yard and she has had zero accidents and has free reign to the house. In face when I'm home I keep the back door open (do not have a doggy door) and when she has to go she finds the Tinkle Turf, notices the door is open and just goes outside! I believe the success of this product was small steps and the Simple Solution Training Pads.

The two major problems (and one minor one) I've read is getting the dog to use the Tinkle Turf as well as the smell/cleanliness of the Tinkle Turf itself as well as a flimsy plastic tray. The easiest way to combat both of these problems is the Simple Solution X-Large Pads. When ordering these pads keep in mind they are mad to fit the Tinkle Turk. Don't let this discourage you because when you place the pad in the middle of the Tinkle Turf the pad absorbs all pee from your dog. Additionally the pad also has an attractant that will help aid your dog in using the Tinkle Turf. I suggest that you start our forcing your dog to be in a small space with the Tinkle Turf however not to small (I put mine in the kitchen and allowed my pups to use the hallway has her play area. Then slowly let the area grow. Now, I had nay sayers claiming she wouldn't use it when I moved it to the back door. But dogs are smarter then we give them credit for. All you have to do is show them where its at, their noses will do the rest (that's where the attractant comes in). Then reward your dog with more access to the house and test if they are able to seek out and use the Tinkle Turf.

The second problem is the smell. I change the pad once a day (when I get home for the day) at that time (every other day) I will rinse off the Tinkle Turf. I have a hose in the back yard so I spray it down and let it dry in the Arizona Sunshine however simply hanging it up will just be fine. When you rinse it off you will see that the syntheic grass it self won't retain any liquid. Its the plastic underneath of the Tinkle Turf and the plastic tray that will retain smell. However if you have the Training Pads it not only makes clean up extreamly easy it also prevents any smell that people are worried about.

The third and minor problem is people say the plastic tray breaks easily. I have a lab puppy and she runs and jumps on it, chews on it. Not to mention I initially transferred it everyday from my kitchen to the back door. I don't know what they are doing but I have not had a problem with it.

To sum everything up, I love it. If you train your dog right with it and clean it by a simple rinse (no chemicals) plus the puppy pads. You'll be just fine! My puppy is 4 months old, only uses when she absolutely needs it and we haven't had any accidents. Its made puppy potty training so easy and no headaches!

In my next installment I have a 3 month old Italian Greyhound entering the household and I will be attempting to litter box train him as well as the Tinkle Turf. Look for that review in the next month or so. I hope I've helped you make your decision on purchasing this fantastic item.s!

product_title: Stella & Chewy's Freeze Dried Food for Cat
review_body:
I'm crazy about my cat. No, I don't call her my \\"kid\\" or dress her up in costumes or buy her Martha Stewart bowls... But I do make sure she has the best of everything that she needs to stay healthy. I feed an all-wet diet, including whole raw meat and several brands of canned food. I thought Stella & Chewy's might make a good addition to her food rotation, and I was right!

Pros:

My cat is really, really picky about her wet food. She eats this stuff happily. I was a little worried about spending $25 on ordering something she might not eat, so before I purchased it, I inquired about samples. The S&C's rep said that all samples are given at the retail level and I'd need to attend a demo to get them. The nearest demo location is about half an hour away, so I just went ahead and ordered. Fortunately, it was a hit.

The ingredients are GREAT.

Unless a cat has protein sensitivities, it's a good idea to give as many different protein sources as possible, and most of the S&C's cat foods have at least two. My cat has dry skin and loves chicken, so the salmon and chicken flavor went over well with both of us.

I like the fact that it uses meat ground WITH bone (this is very nutritious!), no \\"byproduct meal,\\" and of course no grains. As an added bonus, it has NO starch! Most wet foods have at least a little starch as a binder. Starch is not bad for cats, per se, as long as you don't give them too much, but it's not ideal. The only valid purpose it serves in cat food is as a binder. Additional starch is really just filler. There's plenty of protein (45%) and a lot of fat (25%). That does seem like a lot of fat, but keep in mind that cats are obligate carnivores - a high-fat diet is actually very appropriate for them. If you want your cat to lose weight, cut the carbs and limit food intake - don't cut the protein or fat! Kitties need lots of both, and S&C's provides plenty.

Raw meat provides maximum nutrition for carnivores. I like to give my kitty as much raw meat as possible. Commercial and homemade ground raw diets don't provide the same dental health benefits as whole raw meat, but as long as it's raw, most of the benefits are still there.

I love to see probiotics in my cat's food! Cats don't produce them the same way humans do. They're designed to get quite a bit of them by eating their prey's digestive system, which contains a lot of probiotics. They also get some by eating grass and other plants. I provide my cat with oat grass, but it's great to have them in her food as well. Food that's sold wet (wet raw, canned, etc.) can't have live cultures on it. Those have to stay dry. The fact that S&C's is freeze-dried means that she can have her probiotics and her wet food, too - I just have to take a couple minutes to rehydrate.

I am always in favor of cat food being wet. Kibble doesn't help their teeth at all, and they really need their diet to be about 70-80% water (see catinfo.org for why your cat should eat wet!). Freeze-dried food is lighter, which makes it cheaper to ship and cheaper to buy, but my cat still gets all her water when I rehydrate the nuggets.

The meat in S&C's is very safe. I always like to see human-grade meat in my cat's diet. It's safer for her and for me. No antibiotics or hormones! And don't worry about things like salmonella hurting your cat - cats aren't nearly as susceptible to the type of bacteria from raw meat that bothers humans. Because it's raw, and because USDA-inspected meat has low sanitation standards to begin with, you will want to wash your hands carefully after handling this food. However, you won't need to worry about the dangers of feeding your pet overseas chicken, and you'll be less likely to come into contact with nasty stuff yourself while handling this product.

All the ingredients come from North America. Also, each batch is tested prior to packaging, and the results are posted on theirwebsite for public viewing. Yay for a company being open about their manufacturing!

Cons:

I do normally like to see a *little* fruit and veggie in there for additional fiber and vitamins, and there weren't even cranberries (to support urinary health) in this product.

It's really, really expensive. Even considering the fact that feeding guidelines are always pretty high regardless of brand (I would only feed my cat half of what S&C's recommends! Holy crap!), I'd still spend around $600 a year feeding my cat if I used S&C's exclusively. Yeah, no. Not happening. However, since I do like this product a lot, I use it for one of her two daily meals about twice a week.

The directions say that it'll take one minute for the nuggets to rehydrate. Nope! It usually takes about two minutes for my cat's food to rehydrate, and that's if I use more water than the directions state and break up the nuggets about halfway through.

Overall, I think this is a great cat food. I wish I could afford to use it a bit more often, but such is life. If you're considering a commercial raw diet, I think this would be a great product to try out. product_title: Amber Technology Adizone C Anti-Inflammatory Pain Reliever for Cats, 1 oz.
review_headline: Worked well for a very old cat
review_body:
I bought this item for a cat that did not have any of the specific diagnosis listed, but is 19 years old and suffers from stiffness and constipation. I called Wolf Creek Ranch, the shipper of this item and was extremely pleased with the additional information she was able to provide.

We were 5 doses into the treatment when the cat began "pooping" daily. Something he had not been able to do for a couple of years. He continues on Lactoluse from the Vet, but it just wasn't working by itself.
This product can lower the cat's blood pressure, so if you notice some wobbles you need to stop using it.
Also, the herbs are preserved in Alcohol. This is a good thing as it is the best preservative for herbs as it preserves the highest potency. Also, don't shake herb mixtures violently like a bottle of ketchup. Just tap it against your palm 5-8 times.

My cat did not like the alcohol taste which is easy to remedy. Take a small Pyrex dish or microwaveable bowl and heat of water. Slosh the water around to heat the bowl. Pour the water out and add Adizone-C to the hot dish and swirl around. The heat causes the majority of the alcohol to burn off. Then, simply give it to your cat with the syringes (love that the included 2 sizes) provided.
You can only use this product for 10 days per label instruction. So for now, we are going to continue using it at a staggered dose.

I gave it just 4 stars instead of 5 because more information could be provided on Amazon. Also, I'd like to see listed a product upsell of some kind to a product that can be used when the 10 day period is successful.

product_title: DOOG Mini Belt, Black
review_headline: One of the smallest walking belt ever
review_body:
I was looking for a small fanny pack, and came across this walkie belt. I LOVE IT. It is very well made, in expensive, and petite. The material is \\"weather proof material on the front = 100% nylon\\", and breathable mesh material on the back. The breathable mesh material would help if you were to wear the belt against your skin. I am going to provide more details since I had a hard time finding someone who can provide me with details of this product:

The belt is elastic and adjustable. It will fit a 22\\" to 37\\" waist UNstretched with an additional 10\\" to 15\\" of comfortable to tighter stretch (20\\" of uncomfortable/choking stretch).

There are 2 zipped pockets:
- One in the front has a slit in the center of the front (right below the DOOG logo) and a 4 and 5/8 inch zipper opening. The dimension of the front pocket is approximately 5.5\\" W x 2.5\\" H x 1\\" D. This is the pocket where you would put the DOOG doggie bags, and pull the bag out from the slit. This belt comes with a pack of 20 doggie bags. It is pretty bulky to carry 20 bags. Unless you have a puppy who loves to poop frequently... I personally only need 1 bag per walk. I recommend removing the pack of poop bags and just carry the number of bags you need. This will give you more pocket room for other things.
- One in the back has a 4.25\\" zipper opening. The dimension of this back pocket is approximately 5.5\\" W x 2.5\\" H with very little to no depth. This pocket is really designed for IDs, credit card, cash, very small set of keys.

The reason why I mentioned the dimensions of the pockets and the zipper openings is because I couldn't get a clear answer on whether my DROID RAZR MAXX (5.15\\" x 2.71\\" x 0.35\\") will fit. I was told that it should from a seller on another site. When I received the items. My phone would not fit if it has the silicon covers on. When I took off the cover, it wouldn't fit in the back pocket where I was hoping to put it, because the zipper opening was not big enough. Then I tried the front pocket. I had to position one end of the phone as far into the pocket as possible and with a slight stretch of the zipper opening, I managed to get the phone in. So, the phone will be in the front pocket without the silicon cover to protect it. If you have smaller cell phones than mine, you will not have problems fitting it in one of the pockets.big enough. Then I tried the front pocket. I had to position one end of the phone as far into the pocket as possible and with a slight stretch of the zipper opening, I managed to get the phone in. So, the phone will be in the front pocket without the silicon cover to protect it. If you have smaller cell phones than mine, you will not have problems fitting it in one of the pockets.

product_title: Poop Bag Shop Dog Waste Bags, 700-Count with Poop Bag Dispenser
review_headline: Why does this come up for biodegradable search
review_body: I have some concerns about this listing. There are a number of poop bags that come up when ypu search for "biodegradable poop bags" that are not biodegradable but this is the only one that comes up for "ASTM D6400," which is the legal standard for bags to be listed as biodegradable in California. And clearly these bags are not biodegradable, much less to ASTM D6400 standard. Nowhere do I see either word on this posting, but it certainly comes up in the search as having it. I think this posting has some meta-tag shenanigans going on. It's bad enough that bag manufacturers were being dishonest for years about their "biodegradable" bags until the state started cracking down, but if they're also messing with search tags, that reprehensible.  Not cool.

product_title: PetSafe Pawz Away Pet Barriers with Adjustable Range, Pet Proofing for Cats and Dogs, Static Stimulation
review_body:
I bought this to try and keep my cat, Kevin, out of a particular room. He keeps marking in that room, only, and I've tried everything to get him to stop, including cleaners, sprays, odor removers, obstacles to block the corner where he pees, and compressed air canisters. I even tried the plug-in stuff that's supposed to simulate cat facial hormones; he peed right on the dispenser. I got this as a second-to last ditch effort to keep him out of the room. I strategically placed the transmitter and put the collar on the Kevin. After a few days I was starting to wonder if it was faulty because pee was still appearing. Then one day I heard a beeping noise and saw that he was approaching the room. I watched eagerly to see his reaction when he got shocked. Instead he sat down about six inches from the transmitter as the beeping continued furiously. I know he was getting the "correction" too, because his back muscles were twitching in time to the beeping. He just didn't care.

The packaging for this product requires nothing short of the Jaws of Life to remove so I don't think I'll be able to return it. Let's hope I'm able to get something for it on eBay.

FYI, the last ditch effort is to shell out around $2K to have a door framed out around the doorway and install French bi-fold doors to close off the room completely. Getting rid of Kevin isn't an option because he's one of the family. He's the member who pees in the corner, but he's one of us, nonetheless.

product_title: TRIXIE Pet Product Baza Cat Trees
review_headline: [Apparently] well-built, attractive, potentially useful cat furniture
review_body:
[Later: While playing with my cats, I placed enough weight on the top of the device to crack the particle-board base (in effect, \\"totaling\\" the Trixie Tree). Still, at its current price (around $30) I can recommend it with the admonition against using excessive weight or force on top. I have since gone to the [[ASIN:B003BYQ12I Armarkat Cat Tree Model A4201]], which is even easier to assemble and provides greater challenges for the cat and more entertainment for their owners (caveat: the contraption threatens to topple over with the bigger cat on top--consider moving up to the next model ($60) for a larger base plate.]

As I saw the price come down on the Trixie Baza Cat Tree, my interest in the product went up. It's not an elaborate multi-platform device, but it's a good first step. One of my two cats can occasionally be found lying on top, while both have shown interest in the scratching posts. It's not exactly a \\"hit,\\" at least after a couple of weeks, but it looks nice, it's very solid without sacrificing comfort or functionality, and it's one of the few cat purchases that wasn't sentenced to the attic after the first several days. When I see a bag of litter going for over $20 (and lasting less than two weeks), I'm all the more sold on this \\"beginner's\\" Cat Tree.

The next question, of course, is: will my cats be sold? Frankly, I'm tired of hearing the quote (attributed to Winston Churchill) to the effect that: 1. Dogs look up to you; 2. pigs look you straight in the eye (given their poor eyesight, I question whether they actually see you--at least before their snouts \\"root\\" you out); 3. it's only cats that look down on you. If true, this 2-story cat tree offers your feline her first step up in the world. Accordingly, the typically proud parent will follow up with ever taller, multi-leveled towers (relocating to a house with higher ceilings, if necessary), until, upon looking up, it's clear to all other cat-lovers that your \\"most special\\" kitty has reached the absolute pinnacle of success (or, if you will, \\"catsess\\"): [[ASIN:B004BA6LSK The Refined Feline Lotus Cat Tower in Espresso]].al\\" kitty has reached the absolute pinnacle of success (or, if you will, \\"catsess\\"): [[ASIN:B004BA6LSK The Refined Feline Lotus Cat Tower in Espresso]].

product_title: KONG Genius Leo Dog Toy, Colors vary
review_headline: Frustrate your dog (in a good way)!
review_body:
I'll start off by saying the only negative I've found: the rubber is too soft. Unlike the traditional ice cream swirl (or dog crap) shaped kong treat toy which is made from more durable rubber, this one is rather soft. Within 2 times of using this treat toy, my dog has managed to bite off chunks of the plastic. Luckily for me, she's trained to not eat things like plastic, rubber, cotton, wood bits, etc. So I don't have the issue of having to supervise, but I can see why other pet owners are concerned.

Aside from the one complaint above, I'm highly impressed with this toy. Within a week of using it, I ordered another one to make it more difficult for my dog. Originally I just used this one alone but she quickly learned to use her teeth and turn it upside down to dispense all the treats from the hole. I'm hoping putting two of these together in the L shape will force her to learn to move the treats to the next part to then turn upside down. We'll see. I'm pretty impressed with this toy!

I did a lot of research into different treat dispensing toys. I would have loved to get a BusterCube but everyone with hardwood floors has said it's a terror due to the amount of noise it creates and that it does scuff up the floors (no thanks!). I would have gotten the rubber BusterCube but the level of difficulty can't be adjusted like with the plastic BusterCube. Anyway, overall I'm really happy with this product. I also bought the Genius Mike but my dog doesn't like it as much because the hole wasn't big enough for her. I ended up having to cut a small bit of the rubber to make it slightly easier for the treat to come out without her having to bite off rubber.

product_title: Outward Hound Pupstop Car Seat Barrier Safety Auto Gear for Dogs
review_headline: Good product, but dogs can still get past it
review_body:
This barrier works well to keep my dogs in the backseat. It is a simple square with straps that attach to your car seats and must be adjusted. It isn't the most well-constructed or high-quality product, but it does the trick. However, when my dogs are distressed and very determined, my smaller dog (20 lbs) is able to squeeze under the barrier. My other small-to-medium sized dog (33 lbs) was able to jump OVER the barrier when he was either distressed or very excited (that happened once or twice, only when the car was parked).

Just to add -- I've tried several different solutions to try to get my dogs to ride peacefully in the car. My biggest problem is that my smaller dog whines incessantly and tries to come to the front seat. I've used a crate (but too much whining and sliding around inside the crate). I have also tried using dog harnesses specifically designed to attach to seatbelts, but those turned out to be dangerous when my dogs were so determined to wriggle out of them that they became a tangled mess of straps and limbs in the backseat, and I had to pull over to disentangle them.

So, overall, this barrier has been the best solution I've found for taking car rides with my dogs.

product_title: OUT! Orange Oxy Stain and Odor Remover, 32 oz, USA Made
review_headline: my new spot cleaner for puppy messes
review_body:
I think more than half of my recent reviews have been about products for cleaning up dog urine! I've tried multiple carpet sprays and this is my current favorite for dog urine. (I have a 5-month-old puppy who is not fully house-trained. Since she weighs 50 pounds, she has a big bladder...)

One thing I like about this spray is the orange scent. It's not overpowering, but it does provide some immediate odor control.

Another thing I like about this product is that it contains hydrogen peroxide, which reacts with biological substances to produce a foam (essentially just bubbles). This means it should be good for cleaning up blood stains, as well. (Before you go thinking the wrong thing, right now my puppy is teething and she therefore bleeds from the mouth occasionally when she loses a puppy tooth.) There's something psychological about the foaming that makes me feel like this product is really cleaning, as opposed to a spray that just sits on the carpet. The presence of the foam helps me to remember where to wipe up after I've let this sit for awhile.

In case you are concerned, this does not appear to bleach carpet. I use it on a fairly dark-colored carpet, and the color has stayed the same, even though the carpet was cheap and I have used the spray in the same area multiple times. (You would still want to test a small area to be safe.) At least with small urine stains, it's pretty good at getting rid of the odor. It seems to work with feces odors and stains, as well.

The reason I took off one star is because of the bottle design -- it is hard to dispense about the last 1/3 using the trigger spray. I have to tilt the bottle to spray onto a horizontal surface (i.e., the floor) and the bottle design is such that the tube inside that picks up liquid is no longer immersed in the liquid when the bottle is tilted and less than 1/3 full. So no liquid comes out. Because the bottle is opaque, you can't manipulate it to make sure the tube is still in the liquid. My solution has been to buy a new bottle, then when it gets low, refill with the leftovers from the first bottle. A pain, to be sure, but it's a good enough product that I will continue to use it.make sure the tube is still in the liquid. product_title: Litter Robot LRII Automatic Self-Cleaning Litter Box
review_headline: Incredibly Easy, and Completely Worth the Price
review_body:
I purchased this litter robot about 5 months ago, and have had no problems at all. I did a lot of research on this product and other similar products when I was in the market for a new litter box, and I am so glad I made the choice to purchase this item. Previously I had a ScoopFree litter box, which worked well when I only had one cat, but with multiple cats the maintenance and cost of the cartridge refills became too high. So I was looking for an automatic box that was easy to maintain and clean, low odor, and cost effective to maintain. At $15 a cartridge for the ScoopFree unit, twice a month, I figured the Litter Robot would pay for itself in less than a year. What I like about this product is the large waste receptacle, which holds enough waste with two cats using it that I can empty it about once or twice a week. I use Worlds Best Cat Litter with the robot which clumps well and doesn't smell too chemical or offensive. It clumps nicely with the way the robot sifts out the waste and stays clumped when I empty the waste receptacle.

Of my two cats, the older one took longer to adapt to the new box. As previously stated, I had an automatic box before, so the sound was not a significant adjustment to either cat. He was more against having to step up so far to get into the box, which was unlike any other box I had owned. While I noticed there are ramps sold separately through Litter Robot, I just used a smaller box to set just under the trigger step, and he uses that to get into the box easier. Both of my cats are larger, about 12 pounds, and they have no problem fitting in the globe.

Lastly, and the part of the product I am most content with is the way it keeps the litter clean. Previously I had issues with one of my cats peeing outside of the box if it wasn't cleaned instantly, a problem for me as she likes to use the litter box to just scratch around multiple times an hour some days. Since this box thoroughly sifts out any waste seven minutes after the step gets triggered, there is always clean litter to use. Since using the Litter Robot I have not had a single instance of either cat peeing outside of the box, and for this alone I would recommend it to anyone.s after the step gets triggered, there is always clean litter to use. product_title: Azodyl (60 Capsules)
review_body:
Do you buy ice cream online? If not, then you probably shouldn't buy this online either. OK, that's not really a fair comparison, but it illustrates the point.

Many other reviewers correctly point out that Azodyl needs to kept cool to be effective. For those of you considering buying this online, you should also consider paying extra (if necessary) for one- or two-day shipping. Another excellent option would be to buy it directly from your vet and take it home immediately. I understand that you're buying it online because it can be half the price (or less) of what your vet charges, but you might want to weigh that cost savings against the risk to your pet's health if you give them a product that has been rendered ineffective by your penny pinching! You've already gone through the process of having the animal diagnosed so that you know it needs Azodyl, you paid for the diagnosis & product, and you take the time to administer it (probably along with other medications and products). My experience has taught me that cats have not evolved with any biologically advantageous mechanisms for taking pills. Kitty hates this part of the day (twice), and I'm not jazzed about spending a half hour every day on the process of administering medicine. You probably aren't, either. So why risk making the whole endeavor pointless?

The companies selling this online probably just shouldn't allow it to be shipped anything but overnight or 2-day, but that's obviously their decision and no one else's.

Having said all that, I need to make sure I also say that I was very pleased with my order from \\"Pet Supplies 4 Less\\". As others have said, it arrived in 2 days (not using Prime) and was well packed in a small Styrofoam ice chest. The bottle felt like it just came out of the refrigerator. However, from now on I'll probably buy it from the vet just to make sure all this trouble and expense is worth it. Oh yeah, and to try to ensure greater longevityand comfort for my pet. Let's not forget that part.

product_title: Pet Naturals Hip & Joint for Cats
review_headline: Very Picky Cat -- These are Palatable!
review_body:
I just received these so I can't comment on product effectiveness but on the fact that my cat will eat them. My cat is beyond picky. Even some human foods don't interest him (bacon, scrambled eggs) but I am breaking up one of these \\"treats\\" and adding it to the small amounts of kibble he eats twice a day.

I had purchased Cosequin from my vet. My cat-sitter used it while I was away and I could tell it helped his hips but he doesn't like it and is no longer eating much of his wet food when this is added.

After reading a lot of reviews for many different joint formulas, I decided to try this one and also thought I might try Nutramax Dasuquin. A reviewer of the latter said her cat liked it better than Cosequin, so if this product fails to deliver, that's my next product to try. With so many good reviews for Pet Naturals I'm hopeful this will be our solution. My main concern was palatability and this one has come through with flying colors!

The pouch is small but being able to try a product for under $7 is great. I wish more suppliers offered cheaper, smaller sizes so you could try the product before making a substantial investment, especially with cats.

review_headline: Build quality is just okay and I'm not really sure what to do with it - too small to hold much

You might get a small ball inside, but I'd doubt it. Certainly, you don't want to be trying to squeeze any decent size \\"dog leavings\\" into the outer compartment of the bag.

Putting my iPhone inside, I really didn't feel like it was too safe, and I figured it should stay either in my pocket or on my waist.

Regarding build quality, it really feels like a pile of velcro with a little snap on the outside. It really doesn't secure well at all.

If you need a small bag to bring along treats or a ball for a walk, I recommend getting yourself a small handbag or fanny pack. I just don't see the point of this bag, and if your dog ever pulls the leash out of your hand, be prepared to see your cell phone go for a walk as well!

product_title: Feeding Tube #5
review_headline: MUST HAVE for emergency care for puppy or kitten
review_body:
These tubes are a requirement if you're breeding your dog or cat. They are professional-medical grade, and in sterile packaging. They arrived must sooner than indicated, which was a blessing because I had a puppy who was fading from diarrhea (MamaDog ate some grass outside and it passed through the milk). I used the tube to administer pedialyte, kaopectate & corn syrup, and then once things had settled down I administered a meal of formula esbilac (sp?). I have no doubt the puppy would have died without this intervention because she was too weak to nurse.

It's easier to tube feed than I thought. Go to YouTube and watch some videos so you know how to measure the length, and how to know you're not in the trachea -> lungs. A very good tip I only saw on ne video is to crimp the tube as you're pulling it out to prevent aspiration into the lungs, since puppies rarely survive a lung infection.

product_title: Purina Pro Plan Dry Cat Food
review_headline: Feed this if you want your cats to get diabetes or die early!
review_body:
PLEASE read the first few main ingredients before buying the product. Do not look at how fancy the wordings look but look at the actual ingredients that your cats will eat. Most of these food contain-

1 - Chicken By-Product Meal -- \\"dry, ground, rendered clean parts of the chicken carcass.\\"
2 - Whole Grain Corn -- grains = high carbs = fat.
3 - Animal Fat (preserved with Mixed Tocopherols and Citric Acid) -- a tocopherol is pretty much a form of vitamin E.
4 - Corn Gluten Meal -- that's a protein corn by-product; it's a little deficient in lysine, so it shouldn't be the only protein source, which it isn't. (Yes, your pet can digest it just fine).
5 - Brewers Rice -- another by-product, leftovers from the milling process.

Please consider Grain-fee food for your cat if you want it to live a longer life because grain-free obviously doesn't contain grains, leftover meats, and the price is almost the same as these cheap 'craps'.

product_title: Multipet Look Who's Talking Duck Dog Toy
review_headline: Our dog loves his friend Ducky so much.
review_body:
Ducky (as we have named this cute fuzzy little thing) makes the most memorable quacking sounds all dogs will love. For our pup, this quacking sound is his warm fuzzy. His very first Ducky made this same sound, but of course we had to put that Ducky away (RIP). Then I came across this miniature sized look a like friend; I had to buy it. Even if it meant the quacking sound may not be the same. I had to because my pup would relentlessly look for Ducky when his cruel mama and dad would mimic the memorable quacking sounds of his dear lost friend. Oh the torture!

To our surprise this Ducky sounds exactly the same. And our dog loves chewing and yelling (err...barking) at his dear old friend again. No other dog can toss up their beloved friend in the air like ours can. No other pup can literally chew out their friend for talking back to him (or quacking I should say). This ducky may not be made of rubber, but he's definitely The One!

review_body: the collar arrived on day of expectation however there are a few things that are quite disappointing about the product. review_headline: Pain in the $#% to put together, but my dog loves it!

He is scared to death of the washing machine (no idea why) so laundry days, he stays outside, on his fancy Coolaroo bed.

I originally purchased a standard coolaroo bed when he was a puppy, and though he loved it, the corners of the bed always came loose, and it is ripped now (after about 2.5 years) This bed is significantly more sturdy than the smaller, cheaper, metal version. I highly recommend this bed to everyone with a giant dog, strong arms, and someone to help them put it together. Good luck!

product_title: Tagg GPS Pet Tracker - Dog and Cat Collar Attachment
review_body:
I have one dog who is a wanderer. I have a large mountain property. When outside, he is usually in a large run with my other dog, but once in a while he breaks out. And I worry when he does. He can easily climb his 6 foot fence whenever the mood strikes him.

So far, he's had two escapes, and I was notified within 10 minutes with the Tagg system. I used my iPad to locate him in less than a minute. I was able to use the TRAIL feature, and saw that he was headed towards home shortly thereafter both times. So I was able to just relax and wait until he came home.

The only thing I'm not crazy about, is that the Home Zone is so large (even if you use the smallest possible diameter circle) , you can't pinpoint exactly where your dog is unless he/she is OUTSIDE the Home Zone. If he was hurt or hung up by the collar on a branch or something INSIDE the Home Zone, it would take quite awhile to find him. But if the Home Zone were much smaller, you would constantly get alerts that your dog was out of the Zone, and then your battery life would decrease significantly.

All in all, Tagg DOES give me peace of mind, and that's exactly why I purchased it. Easy set up. The small monthly fee is worth it to me, and it does come with 3 months monitoring included.
The phone texts do not work for me (I use Straight Talk, seems I'm out of luck as that's not an option in set up..SEE MY UPDATE BELOW, NOW IT WORKS) but with the iPad, I get Push notifications of escapes, and that's fine with me. I also receive emails immediately of escapes.

I am just exploring the Activity monitoring. My dog doesn't have a weight problem, but I can see that it would motivate the owner to increase the dogs activity if weight was an issue.

Some people commented on the unit detaching from the dog's collar easily. The clip it came with seems secure, but I'm not taking any chances. I simply slipped a small rubber band over each \\"wing\\" of the unit, and its on there to stay.

Good purchase, recommend.

Shortly after I published this, Customer service read this review and called me to offer to send a Tracker collar guard, even though am using rubber bands to be sure the unit stays on the collar.. Wow! Great Customer service, I don't think my review had been online for more than 4 hours when they called me.

UPDATE:

Collar still working fine. Battery life is nowhere near what is suggested, but is still absolutely acceptable to me. My dog goes out on his own recognizance about twice a day (otherwise he gets walked with a leash within the Home Zone). I usually press the LOCATE button if he has been gone alone more than about 20 minutes. He us generally somewhere relatively near the house but outside the home zone.
So each day I probably press LOCATE 2 or 3 times while he is out. I generally don't use the TRACK feature, but would if he were \\"really\\" gone for long. I am getting about 4-5 days out of each charge. As I learn to trust the unit and to trust that my dog is coming back on his own, I will probably use the LOCATE feature much less and will get better battery life.

And as an Update to my Update:

Customer support just called ME and has been working behind the scenes to resolve the texting issue with Straight Talk. They fixed it for me (turns out you just have to select Verizon as your carrier) and now I'm all set. Text messages work just fine.

One thing I have to say about this company....OUTSTANDING CUSTOMER SERVICE. When is the last time a CS has worked on something for you behind the scenes, and contacted YOU to let you know they had fixed it without you prompting them to?it, and its on there to stay.

Good purchase, recommend.

review_headline: Feed this if you want your cats to get diabetes or die early!
review_body:
PLEASE read the first few main ingredients before buying the product. Do not look at how fancy the wordings look but look at the actual ingredients that your cats will eat. Most of these food contain-

1 - Chicken By-Product Meal -- \\"dry, ground, rendered clean parts of the chicken carcass.\\"
2 - Whole Grain Corn -- grains = high carbs = fat.
3 - Animal Fat (preserved with Mixed Tocopherols and Citric Acid) -- a tocopherol is pretty much a form of vitamin E.
4 - Corn Gluten Meal -- that's a protein corn by-product; it's a little deficient in lysine, so it shouldn't be the only protein source, which it isn't. (Yes, your pet can digest it just fine).
5 - Brewers Rice -- another by-product, leftovers from the milling process.

Please consider Grain-fee food for your cat if you want it to live a longer life because grain-free obviously doesn't contain grains, leftover meats, and the price is almost the same as these cheap 'craps'.

product_title: Litter Genie Cat Litter Disposal System Refill Cartridge
review_body:

Next on the agenda is that I don't know what the marketing department was smoking when they came up with "cartridge lasts up to two months for one cat". Boy that is some creative marketing. My wife and I are still arguing about it but we *think* we got 5 refills out of the refill cartridge.

Our one big girl kitty can do some major damage on that in about 3 weeks. OK so we get less than HALF the advertised amount.

Side note and not included in the star rating is the fact that the litter genie we purchased will fall apart when you pick it up. There is a snap latch toward the bottom that is "supposed" to latch. Good luck with that. It doesn't engage with the slot at all. We checked the local store and all theirs were just like that. I have some experience with molded parts in consumer electronics and can honestly say these parts have problems and the company just got shipped them out the door. Quality control I think not. Hooray for us!

So all in all while the whole shebang is a great idea the base is poorly executed and the greed glands were on high when they priced the refill cartridges. These are plastic sleeves folks not even zip lock bags. The point is you are paying an enormous amount for a sleeve to carry turds! I figure about $1.25 per time you empty the base. Yee haw!

I will pursue another solution but this will have to do for now. Ironically I sent my wife out to get the competitors model and this is the one she brought home. Our neighbors have another brand and it works MUCH better. Don't know about lifespan of the refills or the price so keep that in mind.

Also keep in mind that you get to tie a knot in the bottom of the bag to start using and a knot in the top of the bag to dispose. If you are a micro knot ninja you may also get more uses per refill. If you are "normal" maybe not so many.

If the base were well made and the bags lasted about twice as long for the money I would have been happy.o start using and a knot in the top of the bag to dispose. If you are a micro knot ninja you may also get more uses per refill. If you are "normal" maybe not so many.

product_title: Rapid Rewards Deluxe Dog Training Bag with Belt by Doggone Good!
review_body:
My husband and are long-time dog owners (35+ years). We recently got a rescue shelter dog that’s unlike any other dog we’ve ever owned in that…well, let’s just say that our new dog doesn't have the world's best manners. Thus, for the first time in our dog-owning lives we have gotten involved with professional dog-training, only to find that dog training is no walk in the park. Right now we are teaching our dog to keep her focus on us--or at this point, at least keep her focus on our hand while we walk around the house by continually giving her treats from that hand. That means we have to carry a steady source of treats on our person, or persons, for periods of time during the day as we go about our other daily business. It's not much fun to be doing chores around the house, only to have your bag of little dog treats spill when you bend down. It's also not much fun to be constantly zipping and unzipping a pouch, inconvenient when you want to deliver that quick-pop-in-the-mouth treat so that the dog associates her good behavior with those yummy treats.

Enter the aptly-named 'Rapid Rewards Deluxe Dog Training Bag’ with its magnetic closing device. I got a red one for myself (nice-looking) and a black one for my husband (macho). Granted, they cost more than other pouches but they are well-made, durable, and attractive as dog pouches go. Inside it has a pocket with a Velcro closure. Outside it has one pocket with Velcro closure, one with zipper closure, and 2 small pockets on either end that are open-topped but tight enough to hold keys or a clicker. I didn’t check to see whether or not they’re waterproof. I might Scotchguard mine.

What I like most about this bag—besides the fact that it’s nice-looking for a dog treat bag-- is the magnetic closure top, which is easy to pop open when you need a treat. However, I do clip a baggie inside it and put the treats in that, both to keep the bag clean and to keep the moist treats from drying out between dog training sessions.

All in all, it’s a nice bag and I’m glad I got the RR Deluxe rather than a less expensive bag.s from drying out between dog training sessions.

product_title: Mighty Massive Dog Toy
review_body:
Thing is, if your dog is intent on ripping a plush toy to shreds and you let him/her chew on it with this intent in mind, you are not likely to find any plush toy on earth that is going to satisfy you for durability. Plush toys are just not going to be able to withstand your dog's singular focus. Our rottweiler loves plush toys but in the act of play chews through most pretty quickly, on the order of hours to days. (We take it away for a while if she's getting too focused on destroying it.) This Mighty Dog Piggie has lasted the longest of any we've had. Sure. Piggie's ears are chewed off and he has a couple holes in him here and there, but this toy is still going after about 3 weeks and we've washed it a couple times. Comes out of the dryer with fur looking like new.

So the reviewers that give this toy a 1, well, I suspect they'd give any plush toy advertising durability a 1. They just have dogs that can't have a plush toy without immediately intently setting about the task of finding a way, any way, to rip it apart. But if your dog likes plush toys, and you can supervise him/her a little to encourage play rather than wanton destruction for destruction's sake, this is not a bad product despite its comparatively steep price. Our dog loves Piggie so much now she sleeps with it under one arm. For us, a month is a pretty good run for a plush toy.

In sum. Plush toys are not tennis balls, or Kongs, or ropes. They simply cannot be made to that level of durability. As stuffies go, Mighty Dog Piggie is pretty dang stong.

review_body:

It is difficult to comb the dog coat, and even harder to use these scissors to cut much of the hair. It takes AGES! The old separate comb and scissors work far quicker and do a better job.

(Re-edit: 4/27/2013 These were my thoughts at the time, but I see now the only reason this purchase was unsatisfactory was due to the smallness of my dogs' bodies! There was only a small patch of flat skin for the comb attachment to pick up hair as the curve of their bodies prevented a good amount of hair to be picked up.)

This item is a good invention and hopefully, the manufacturers will keep going with it until it reaches a more satisfactory level for the smallest of dogs also.

EDIT on my review: April 12, 2013

Thank you Mathew for your comment and offer to help with my dissatisfaction.

I should have added that my Pomeranian dogs are very tiny, one being 3lbs and the other just 5lbs in weight. Perhaps as they are so small, the scissor/comb invention could not work properly on them. I did use the smallest comb provided, but that was still too big for such tinies.

NOTE TO CUSTOMERS:
If you have any doubt about whether this scissor/comb will work on your pet or not, contact the manufacturer, Mathew Michel, who seems very dilligent about after-sales care and giving 100% satisfaction.

UPDATE; APRIL 27TH 2013
Very happy with the after-sales, especially in this instance of my not having 100% satisfaction with their product. My dogs are too tiny for this gadget to work as well as it probably would on a larger dog. When the comb (attached to the scissors) was placed on either dog it always landed on a bit of the curve of their body. If you can picture this it means only a bit of the comb lay flat against the body so was unable to pick up much hair to cut. Perhaps this company will invent the same instrument for very small bodies as that would really help speed up grooming time!

product_title: SureFlap Microchip Cat Door- Brown
review_headline: Good product, some downsides to consider
review_body:
You've seen what's good about this unit. Here are some downsides:

1) The first you'll learn the batteries are dead is Mr. Fluffers will be stuck outside at night. Nothing indicates low battery, and the unit defaults to locked under such circumstances.
2) The unit eats batteries quickly. I recommend getting two sets of rechargeable batteries, keeping one set on the charger. The sanyo eneloop brand works well because the batteries hold a charge for a long time.
3) The unit is poorly insulated, there is always a draft.
4) Our cats actually hate the unit, and much prefer to beg at the door. For the longest time they'd run for the hills when the \\"click\\" of the latch went off.
5) The outside flange is not watertight, and sealing this perfectly appears impossible.
6) The cost of extra tunnels and plastic parts adds to your total bill: you probably need more parts than just this one here for sale.
7) The knob to set cat direction is unlabelled.

But hey, it keeps the 'coons out... and Mr. Fluffers can survive a night or two in the cold every once in a while.

review_body: I purchased this as a last ditch effort to save my husband's cat from being banished from the house due to urinating on my brand new sofa and chair. I ordered 2--one 10x16 to go across the back of the sofa and a smaller one to go across the back of the recliner. They arrived fast! They're simple to put together---you just install the battery in the power pack, then snap the power pack onto the mat. Choose your setting from lo to high (I used high!) and the mat is activated. Now, I have not yet seen the cat get zapped, but she must have been because she has gone from lounging all over the furniture like she owns it to making a W I D E circle around the furniture and not even hopping up for a minute. I am finding no cat hair on the furniture, so this is a good indication that she was zapped and has chosen to avoid having that happen again. I call this a successful diversion and would definitely purchase again and would highly recommend this product. As an added bonus I have enjoyed many moments of amusement when my hubby sits down on the sofa and casually tosses his arm across the back. LOL  He's been zapped four or five times now and each time the kids and I have laughed so hard we cried. FYI.....the people who declared this a "cruel" way to train an animal are likely to have no experience with this mat, in my opinion. Even on the highest setting it isn't a "painful" shock. It's like the well built up, foot shuffling static shock we all had fun with as kids. It uses a 9v battery, so obviously we aren't talking death chamber electrocution here. It's enough, tho and does work as the manufacturer suggests as a deterrent to keep pets (and some husbands) off of the furniture!

review_headline: Beware! Do NOT use these if your pet is elderly or in any weakened condition! It could kill them! There's a SAFER ALTERNATIVE!
review_body:
Hopefully this will help save some pets' lives! (see my original review,(below) about a tragic story of a friend who unwittingly killed his sweet 1 year old cat by using the highly toxic Hartz and Advantage flea killer products on her.)

Update 03/28/14: I used to use these cat flea Shootags with great success until the last ones I bought from Amazon several months ago which didn't work at all.

On their packaging, the manufacturing company, ShooTag says they have a product guarantee and that sometimes the tags are defective, so they suggest calling the company directly to get usage instructions, or, if necessary, a replacement. So I called the company to ask them why my tag might not be working when 3 tags that I'd used in the past had worked great. I had to keep calling them and leaving messages repeatedly until they finally called me back. They said that yes, I had been doing everything correctly and agreed to send me a replacement flea tag for my cat.

That replacement tag finally arrived a couple weeks later and after letting it charge for over a week on my very healthy, young cat (the same cat that the previous tags HAD worked on), I realized that THAT NEW one wasn't working either. I knew it wasn't working because every day I was still combing about 30 new fleas off my cat every time she went out into the yard.

I was beginning to think that the company had started to make the tags weaker so that they would need to be replaced more quickly since I'd never had any problems in the past and I was always using them on the same cat in the same state of great health. Or they may have had to make the tags weaker because they were causing too many animals to get sick from them.

By the way, do NOT use these tags on a cat or any animal that is not in optimal health. I discovered this the hard way when I tried to use the first tag someone gave to me as a gift, on my elderly cat (the cat I had before the one I have now). My 19 year old sweet cat was pretty healthy for her age except for a small tumor which had shown up on her abdomen 3 years before. It wasn't growing at all and the vet agreed that since she was already so old, and the tumor wasn't growing at all, that it was best not to operate on her to remove it since the surgery would probably kill her before the tumor would.

Back then, ShooTag was not including ANY warnings about not using their tags on elderly or sick animals so I had no idea that I would be putting my sweet cat in danger by trying out this new flea tag on her. Frankly, at that time, the company was not even aware that the tags could be dangerous for weakened or elderly animals. I actually alerted them to the fact after my 19 year old cat had such a strong, adverse reaction to the tag. What happened? Well, within 24 hours of putting the ShooTag on my 19 year old cat with the tumor that hadn't grown or changed in over 3 years. that same tumor swelled up to the size of a walnut and burst open. I can only imagine how painful that was for my poor cat. I had to rush her to the vet to get the wound cleaned out and have her put on antibiotics. I immediately realized it was the ShooTag that had almost killed her so I quickly took it off her.
I had already had some reservations about using the tag on her in the first place, knowing that the tag would actually be using her energy to charge itself (I've studied a lot about the science of living energy fields), but I erroneously assumed that the company would have been responsible and tested their tags on a variety of animals prior to selling them, and that they would have included any necessary warnings if the tags were at all potentially dangerous. At that point there were NO warnings whatsoever on their products or website (although now there are). So as soon as her tumor swelled up and burst open, I knew it was because the ShooTag was depleting energy from her energy field which she couldn't afford togive up. The fact that there had been no warning whatsoever on the packaging was extremely irresponsible. Clearly, there had been very insufficient testing done of this product before it was quickly rushed to market. Like I said, the company now DOES warn that you should not use their products on sick or elderly animals because they "do not react well to our product". I'll say!

Anyway, after getting the replacement tag that also did not work (on my new young cat (my older cat has since passed away)), I called the company again, and left a message asking for another replacement since the new one they sent me STILL didn't work. And I called. And I called. And I called, each time leaving a detailed message. But no call back. Ever. They basically just ignored me since they'd already sent me a replacement once. At that point, since it had taken so long to get the replacement tag, I couldn't even get a refund from Amazon since it was past the 30 day deadline. So basically I wasted the money on this dud of a purchase.

I recommend NOT buying ANY tags from this company. I've tried the mosquito and fly repellent tags for humans, also made by this company, and those don't work at all, either!

Save your money and buy something else (but don't get the toxic poisons! (see my original review below to learn why):

Original Review before the company and their products went downhill (2012):

I saw her scratching a lot and thought I'd help her out by combing some of the fleas off of her. If they're scratching and you don't comb any fleas off of them, they may have an allergy to something (like their food, for example))

I was shocked and appalled when I heard this after the fact! product_title: Clevercat Top Entry Litterbox
review_headline: this is what I've been looking for!
review_body:
I have a 2 dog 1 cat household and the dogs love to eat kitty's poo. Baby gates didn't work because my husband always takes them down. Honestly, if I didn't catch the dogs with kitty poo breath, I wouldn't even know that my cat pooped. And the cat litter all over the floor from the front entry box is rather annoying. I am not one to vacuum everyday. So I went in search of a different style of box and found this. It is a bit expensive, yes, and it is a glorified rubbermaid box, but I do believe the lid is much more stable than if you would just cut a hole yourself. Also, the curragated top performs as promised and traps a lot of the litter that would usually end up on the floor. Not perfect, there is still some litter that gets on the floor, but the cat now jumps out to the side, so at least it's not where we walk anymore.

The directions that came with is suggest leaving the lid off of the container for the first day so the cat can get used to it, but our cat wouldn't make the jump over the side and started utilizing other places for relieving herself (not fun!) so we put the lid on the container and barricaded her in the bathroom where her litter box is for a few hours and problem solved! The lesson learned here is know your cat. You may be better off putting the lid on if you think your kitty might be timid about jumping over the side.

Despite the initial use issues, I have been exremely happy with this box. There is far less litter on the floor and the dogs have not figured out how to get to the poo! Success! I would highly recommend this box. It was well worth the price!

product_title: Bags on Board Regular Bag Refill Pack
review_headline: Redesigned bags are terrible--Avoid if you actually need them to work
review_body:
Our two medium-sized dogs, who produce small-to-medium sized piles of dog poop, live without the luxury of a yard and have to do all their business on walks. So we use a lot of these bags, and while they're handy, the redesigned style is awful.

* At least one bag on every roll rips when you tear it off: hope you notice before you wind up with poop on your hands/sidewalk/shoes!
* The top seam is much longer, so they can be incredibly difficult to open on the fly, especially when it's windy or raining, or when you're wearing gloves. So, basically, all of the times that you want them to open easily and quickly so you can just go back inside. Sometimes I give up and use them as a flat protector to pick up pieces and cart them to a nearby dumpster, but again--good luck not getting poop on your hands/sidewalk/shoes!
* The bags don't hold as much as they used to. They contain the 35 lb. dog's poop sufficiently, but the bigger dog often needs two bags. If your dog regularly makes piles larger than a tennis ball, you will have this problem.

We bought the huge box of these and have been using them up, but I cannot wait for them to be gone so we can switch to something else. These are fine if you're going to use them occasionally for a small dog at the park on a dry, sunny afternoon, but for regular daily use in the elements AVOID AVOID AVOID.

-the lights don't stick out too far or obstruct my vision any more than the brim of the hat already does, and they have a really good spread of illumination
-the material is quality- I paid more for a similar hat at my local retail store
-batteries can be replaced, and there are like four of them in there so I'm not worried about doing it soon. common nickle-sized battery
-adjustable
-the button to activate the light is on the left side- great if you are right-handed and have like a dog. I don't have a dog but I guess this is the "dog walking hat" so I will confirm that it would probably be good if you had to like, you know, take your dog outside to use the bathroom and clean up without worrying about handling the flashlight, or worrying about the flashlight accidentally ending up in the bag with the, you know...

Not sure how this holds up in weather but with some Scotchguard I don't see how it would be worse than a regular hat. I would love to see this line of products come out with an officially "weatherized" hat and other gear that has LEDs built in for safety.

This is just the tip of the iceberg as far as this kind of product is concerned and hat's off to Pup.

product_title: Leba III Pet Dental Spray
review_body: I have brushed both dogs' teeth daily (Samoyeds) with Petrodex since they were 8 weeks old --they love it.  My 7 year old male still developed tartar on his back teeth.  My 2 yr old female got tartar on only 4 teeth -- near her salivary ducts -- her tongue is \\"over-sized\\" and she drools a lot.  I noticed improvement in the male within a week or two with subsequent complete removal of tartar. I thought it wasn't working for the female.  But 3 months later I suddenly noticed that the tartar (or stain) was half gone.  Undoubtedly it was disappearing gradually but I couldn't tell until clear white tooth was showing.  A couple of weeks later and it is almost all gone.  A bottle lasted 3 months for 2 dogs with initial treatment at 2 x daily.  Now I spray once daily after brushing and before bed.  I break the rule of not using toothpaste in conjunction with the product -- supposedly it coats the teeth and reduces the effectiveness of Leba III.  I swear by daily brushing. Bottom line -- be patient. It does work.  It's not cheap but it sure beats a vet cleaning/anesthesia/etc. and it preserves their pearly whites.

review_body:

So when I saw this go on sale I quickly nabbed it. I wasn't sure if I should get an egg shape or a ball. I think the egg shape was the best bet. The egg doesn't roll in a straight line. So my cats aren't playing soccer throughout the house with it. I like that the wholes are adjustable for not only the size of kibble you buy but also the difficulty as well. I know the packaging says to start with the largest setting so your cat doesn't get frustrated with it but my kitty quickly caught on and was plowing through the food like there was no tomorrow. So I changed it to the hard setting (1 kernel every 3 rolls or so) and the other 2 caught on shortly after. Granted, the first few days I sprinkled cat nip in the egg with the food to entice them to mess with it but after that they got used to it. My \\"middle child\\" or \\"prissy kitty\\" as she most commonly referred to did stick her nose up at this at first. It wasn't until a week or so later that she realized that \\"this is it\\", we weren't going to be giving her anymore food that she started batting the eggs around.

It may take some coaxing to get your cat to use it but try treats, cat nip or even showing them what to do. Eventually they will figure it out and get the hang of it. It definitely slows down their eating and I've found that food in the egg will last throughout the day whereas the same amount of food in a bowl only lasts minutes.

product_title: PetSafe ScoopFree Ultra Self-Cleaning Cat Litter Box, Covered, Automatic with Disposable Tray, 2 Color Options
review_body:
I adopted my cat in Oct 2010 and since then have absolutely dreaded cleaning the litter box, I love my furry friend but poop is another story. I also dread lugging around multiple 40 LB cat litter containers at the pet store. Before buying the scoop free litter box, I consulted a petco worker about automatic kitty litter cleaners because I really dislike the dust and poop, idea of toxoplasmosis--the whole shabang. I wanted to get the scoopfree litter box with the lid, but the petco lady told me to buy a bag of crystals first and mix it with the old litter so my cat can get used to the crystal litter. Why spend all this money if the cat won't use the crystals?? Good suggestion, so I bought a bag of crystals (significantly cheaper and more lightweight than the regular kitty litter--wish someone had told me about this sooner too). Anyway, over a month, I mixed in his old clumping litter with the crystals. I noticed immediately the crystals really keep the odor down much better than the clumping litter. My cat didn't seem to have any problem with the crystals at all, and the tracking is significantly less too.

After finally finishing all the old litter, I took the plunge to buy the scoop free litter box. It has only been day 1 but
I only wish I had done this sooner!! Not only was I hurting my back lugging around the kitty litter, and then cleaning and replacing the litter (heavy too!!), but also endangering myself in icy parking lots and stairwells between the house and the dumpster! The refill trays are so much lighter to carry and even if I decide to use the forever trays (not sure which to use yet), the crystals are soo much better overall!

On a side note, I am also elated I don't have to scoop litter anymore, and worry about getting toxoplasmosis. As a healthcare worker, getting sick in any way or giving patients anything is a concern. I also want to have kids at some point but don't want to give up my cat. This will make lifeso much easier and healthier too.

When I brought the scoop free litter box home and was setting it up, my cat came over and he knew exactly what it was. Cats aren't stupid like some other mammalian species. I decided since we have already transitioned with the crystals, I moved his kitty litter box away into another room where he can't get to it, and replaced it with the new one entirely. After I showed the litter box to him once, I went downstairs and left him alone, and within less than a minute I heard his thunderpaws galloping down the hallway to the laundry room where we keep the litter box. Within less than 5 minutes of setting up the litter box, he went #1 right away! My cat didn't have any problem transitioning to the litter box. In addition, I am very impressed with the noise level--it is very quite and discreet. I don't see how the noise could bother anyone. My cat probably doesn't even have any idea that it is even automatic and makes noise because I have it on the 20 minute setting. I also like the cat visitor counter. I am looking forward to tracking his whereabouts by making sure he is using the litter box!

I was concerned about the upfront cost because it is a lot of money. But if you add up what I was spending before, this is much more economical. I don't need to buy the right size liners for the litter box($30 every 6 months at least) and for 1.5 months I would spend around $75 at least for the clumping litter. I would put more litter in the box because I hated cleaning it that much. My cat is such a sweetheart and put up with me not scooping for almost 4-5 days sometimes. He deserves a CLEAN litter box so this product is worth the money for me.

I have read some reviews about using a forever litter tray. If I only have to clean it once a month, that might not be a bad deal, and a big bag of crystals could go a long way then. However, with one cat, I am hoping I only need to change the filler once a month. He is a larger cat though but has a good diet of food with no byproducts--mainly Blue Buffalo or Authority, no table food. I will probably stick with the 3-pack and use coupons or find deals through amazon, because I am not interested in fiddling with a permanent box and having to purchase more liners, cat litter and spend more $$. You might find a permanent tray but you still have to waste plastic with a liner so what is the point? I simply won't use something permanent without at least two liners because that is simply unsanitary and I do not have the time to Clorox a tray every few weeks!

I am a little concerned about the litter box smelling so I will definitely give an update on the smell after 3-4 weeks. It seems the reviews are really good for keeping the odor down so I do have my fingers crossed.

Overall, I am thrilled to keep my sweet kitty happy with a clean litter box, and save my own back and money in the process!

With StayAway, it took only three or four blasts of air and the audio alwarm for them to quit
altogether. The highlight, for me, came in the middle of the night when I heard this thing
go off followed by the sound the sulprit knocking things over during a hasty retreat. StayAway
was able to accomplish something that I had been fighting for several years. NOTE: The key is
to place this unit in a way that requires the cat to enter the target field by using simple
barricades (in my case, a roll fo pape towels) to force the culprit to get in the line of fire.

product_title: Marineland Reef Capable LED Light
review_headline: 18"-24" LED: The timer is worth the money
review_body:
I have had this light running for about 9 months on a 10 gallon saltwater aquarium. I couldn't be happier. All of my corals and fish are very happy and healthy with this light. I tend to only run the white light for 5-7 hours a day because the strength of the white light will accelerate algae growth in the tank. The blue light is very bright and gives my corals amazing color at night. The light gets fairly warm when left on for hours at a time. Being able to set the timer and never worry about having to turn on the light is worth the extra cost over the version without the timer. Definitely the most expensive part of my small tank setup but with the extendable arms, I can use this on a larger tank when I upgrade (wouldnt suggest larger than a 30 gallon for this light though)

EDIT: 5/12/14 A WHILE BACK I SPILLED A CUP OF WATER ON THIS LIGHT WHEN DOING A WATER CHANGE ON MY OLD 10 GALLON, RIP MARINELAND LED. LIGHT WORKED AS ADVERTISED UNTIL I SPILLED THE WATER, ALL MY FAULT. I STILL RECOMMEND FOR NANO REEF SETUPS. NOW I USE TAOTRONICS LIGHT PANEL ON MY 65G REEF TANK.

review_headline: Happy Hips Has Been The Best Choice for Our German Shepard
review_body: We have a full-bred Gentle Giant German Shepard who is bred for his size and temper, on a small to large scale, our dog is huge! Prior to getting our dog, we had our coon hound mix who basically can eat anything under the sun and still have tons of vitality. We learned quickly that with our full-bred this was not the case. In his first year of life our German Shepard went from 15 lbs to 90 lbs and the food we fed him prior (high-end Purina) could not support his joints and in the end made him sick, making him loose all of his fur, get numerous infections, and experience terrible joint pain. With research I realized that what I was feeding my dogs was by-product crap so I immediately switched them to Happy Hips and in within days saw tremendous improvement in my German Shepard's coat, immune system, and joints. This brand is hard to find in our area and is only sold in the small bags so we tried the more accessible \\"high-quality\\" brands like Blue Buffalo and Taste of the Wild, but none had shown the results that this brand has and some of them made my dog turn his nose. After a few weeks of being on Blue Buffalo, my dog started to shed fur and have crazy dandruff. He had a vet appointment and our vet asked what happened, when we told her that he was eating Blue Buffalo since it happened, she asked that we immediately put him back on Happy Hips. I'm so glad that I found this on Amazon for such a great price because now I can buy the big bags and have them delivered monthly. For the people who gave this low reviews, they need to keep in mind that each dog differs. Obviously our coon hound mix has a better ability to adapt to all kinds of foods. Full-breds tend to have more allergies and weaker immune systems. I suggest if you haven't tried this food and are on the fence, to give it a try. If my giant German Shepard with every allergy in the world thrives off of it, more than likely your pup will too.

product_title: Exo Terra Sri Lanka Rainforest Terrarium Kit
review_body: I got this after the 10g tank became too small for my gecko. It is nice that it opens in the front. The background is made out of styrofoam. It looks fine, but it has 2 channels that run up the back that are about 2 inches wide for each one. I am guessing this is to run wires up the back without seeing them if you have a heat rock or maybe a waterfall. There is a small gap at the bottom, so my naughty crickets keep disappearing in and crawl up the back. Just when you think your pet has eaten them, you peek behind the background, and they are all hiding back there. I put the black tubes from my cricket keeper in front of the bottom opening and waited until I eventually caught them all. I have reptile carpet at the bottom. Even with some sort of substrate, the crickets can still get behind the background from along the top. Now I will take my gecko out and put him in his old 10 with his bugs for a while. Does anybody know if crickets eat styrofoam? They look like they do. What your crickets eat, end up inside your pet. So ... is this ok? Other than the background with its built in hiding places, I really like it. I just got the tank and background, not the whole kit.

product_title: FURminator deShedding Tool for Cats, 1.75-Inch Edge
review_body:
I was apprehensive when I ordered the product mainly because my cat has short hair and hates to be brushed. I talked myself out of it several times before I ordered it thinking, "How much will it really get out? His fur isn't long and he probably won't let me anywhere near him with it anyways."

It arrived today and I must admit... Boy, was I wrong. I spent about 10 minutes this morning brushing him. At first, he wasn't too happy. As I got used to the brush, he loved it more and more. He purred the whole time and rolled and flipped. I decided to take a break and try again later. I realized I had collected a huge handful of fur from the first session.

This afternoon, I gave it another shot. This time he saw the brush in my hand and came running! I got even more fur off of him this time. All in all, I have enough fur to make a whole new cat.

Something to consider, if your cat is less finicky than mine and you could get away with brushing him on hard flooring- do it. I had to vacuum after because the brush doesn't hold much fur and my birdbrain was rolling around as i brushed him, getting the fur all over the carpet.

Amazing brush.

product_title: Soulistic Good Karma Chicken Dinner in Gravy Cat Food Pouches
review_headline: Finally, a food that works for both of my cats!
review_body:
I have two cats, one who cannot tolerate grains and another who is prone to urinary/kidney problems. With the high quality ingredients and low phosphorus, grain free content of Soulistic, I know that both of my cats can eat this healthfully as their staple food. I try to feed a mostly wet diet, but my cats are very picky about what they will eat. I've spent many many dollars on expensive canned grain free foods and prescription kidney foods from the vet that wind up untouched and in the trash. For me, it's been nearly impossible to feed separate varieties, because they become very curious about what's on the other's plate and will often try to switch foods. Not to mention the fact that my grain-intolerant cat will often turn his nose up at the yucky mush of expensive foods like Wellness, etc. This leads the kidney-afflicted cat to try to eat the grain-free food while the grain-intolerant cat will go for the K/D diet, wich is FULL of grains.

This problem forced me to literally have to watch them eat and redirect them when they attempted the switch, until I found Soulistic. Wow, they BOTH love it...I mean, LOVE IT to the point of licking their plates clean. Plus, I can feed them the same food at the same time, which allows me to maintain my busy schedule without having to be the food monitor.

The food itself actually looks appetizing. The pouches contain shredded chicken that looks like shredded chicken, not some nondescript, smelly mush. It's also less expensive than some of the other high quality, grain free pet foods. Soulistic has definitely been a winner in my household.

review_body:

* All natural snacks developed to help maintain fresh breath
* Made with spearmint, parsley and fennel
* For dogs of all ages and size
* No artificial preservatives
* No wheat, soy, artificial colors or flavors
* Made with spearming (sic), parsley and fennel

Then at the bottom where the ingredients are listed it says:
Ingredients
Whole Wheat Flour, Oatmeal, Wheat Bran, Chicken Fat (preserved with Mixed Tocopherols, a natural source of Vitamin E), Chicken, Cane Molasses, Spearmint, Parsley, Fennel, Eggs, Apples, Carrots, Salt, Mixed Tocopherols (a natural preservative).

product_title: Marineland LED Aquarium Kit
review_headline: decent led aquarium kit, few frills
review_body:
i bought this tank kit from a local petsmart store in february 2012 for $200. got it home, unpacked it and set it up with really no problems at all.

all the hood, filter, and trim parts are plastic. the filter is the bio-wheel penguin 350, which holds a double filter and biowheel setup with adjustable intake. the filter is generally quieter than average for kit systems, and i am very pleased with it so far.

the led lighting comes from two led panels, one on either side of the split-hood. they are removable and come with detachable power cords. they are surprisingly bright, and provide a nice shimmer effect into the tank. however, they do not provide suitable light energy for a planted tank so don't expect to get good plant growth. there is also a night-light setting of a half-dozen blue led's on each panel. the lights do not have a timer option, but instead a 3-way manual switch (white, off, blue) on each panel.

the tank also comes with a generic 200-watt heater and temperature sticker. the heater is not marked in degrees, but that's what the thermometer is for :) they seem to work ok, but i bought a different thermometer to replace the one in the kit. there is also a startup pack that includes a small amount of tropical fish flakes, a net that's far too short to catch bottom-dwelling fish without getting wet up to the elbow, and a small amount of water conditioner. there are no decorations, gravel, air pumps, or other items included.

i am generally satisfied with my purchase. i let the tank cycle for a week before dropping in a couple danios and platies. if i notice any issues with components wearing out early or breaking too easily, i will come back and update this review.

***UPDATE***

after a year, the tank is still holding out very well. nothing has broken or fallen apart, except for the suction cups that were with the heating element. the clips deteriorated and fell apart within a couple months, but i bought some replacements and they've worked just fine. all the led's still work, and the filter is still churning away.

i can definitely say this marineland tank is a keeper.but i bought some replacements and they've worked just fine. all the led's still work, and the filter is still churning away.

i can definitely say this marineland tank is a keeper.
