product_title: KONG Squeezz Ball Dog Toy
review_headline: Great idea, but poorly assembled. Not for vigorous chewers!
review_body:
UPDATE 10/2013 - The replacement toy only lasted a month. Right now, all the Squeezz toys we own have broken at the seams and no longer squeak.

The problem for most customers is that Kong has become a name synonymous with tough dog toys, and the Squeezz line doesn't compare. For a toy to last less than a couple days to a week is a disappointment. Kong should create a different brand for their less sturdy line to protect brand association with tough, high quality toys.

Squeezz is not one of them. Only recommended for gentle chewers. Stick to the original Kongs for aggressive chewing dogs.

------------------------------------------
UPDATE 3/5/13 - I did hear back from the Kong company, and they unfortunately did not have a suggestion for a safe non toxic adhesive to repair the ring seams. I also found out that the Squeezz line of Kong toys does not have the same 30 day guarantee that other Kongs have.

They did replace mine, which was nice - they certainly didn't have to, since I was a little past the warranty period, but I notice the replacement seems to have better looking seams, and the Barkspawn is happy to have his favorite squeaky toy back.

You might want to check for this item locally, and be picky about the condition of the seams on the one you purchase.
-----------------------------
This is the second Kong Squeezz I have purchased, but it's not as durable as the first, the Squeezz Bone. Both have a great loud squeaker embedded in the toy where it cannot easily be removed or destroyed, come in bright colors of translucent plastic, and have a high erratic bounce that the dog loves.

Unlike the Squeezz Bone, the ring is not all that well joined. When I bought it I thought the seams, which are perpendicular to the ring, were not the toughest part. But I bought it because the Bone was so sturdy and still in one piece after years of play. Well, after a about two weeks, the ring gave out at the seams. Once the ring separates, while it might still bounce, the squeak stops, and the squeaker can be destroyed.

This was done to the 'large' (Large is not very large at all) ring by a 5 month old border collie puppy, so I think larger, more dedicated chewers might make short work of those seams as well.

review_body:

product_title: Esky Dog Training Collar Waterproof 330 Yard LCD Backlight Remote Control Dog Training Shock Collar
review_body:
Got this to help my dog learn to not bark in the yard (a shock collar is essential for this!!! because it teaches them to watch their behavior even when they are alone). Even better is the BUZZ feature on these collars. After shocking my dog the first few weeks, i was able to effectively "remind her" with a BUZZ instead of a shock when she misbehaved. This is great because, ideally, you never want to shock the dog you love.

Anyway, this is the cheapest one i found (maybe $40-50? when i bought it), but it functioned perfectly! I have a 70lb dog, and i never, ever needed to shock her above Level 30 to get her attention (level goes up to 100). This shock collar is PLENTY powerful enough if you're concerned about level of shock like me.

I recommend shocking yourself with it on a low setting to understand the level of shock. I found Level 40 to be a lot for Even Myself (175lb man's leg), let along a 70lb dog's neck. Be cautious with level setting.

product_title: Fussie Cat Premium Tuna with Salmon Canned Cat Food - 24 - 2.82-oz. Cans
review_headline: Oh my!  My cats go crazy for Fussie Cat!
review_body:
I decided to try Fussie Cat on a whim ... I'd never heard of it before and it's cute name and packaging caught my eye. I decided to research it a bit before I bought it for my 6 cats and was pleased with what I read.

My 6 cats adore this food - all different flavors of it. I don't know that they have a favorite that I can discern. The top ingredient is Tuna and it's REAL tuna. It's not the rubbery, flaked stuff I see in Fancy Feast that my cats won't touch ... or when they do, they look like they are chewing on rubber bands of something. Fussie Cat is packed in a good amount of water and Aspic (the gelatin and stock combo that helps keep things together). It looks like fresh chunks of tuna. Big enough for my cats to really get their teeth into and feel like a carnivore. They really go nuts for this stuff.

I have a little kitty dealing with some heart issues and kidney failure that requires special care. While he isn't interested in the Kidney RX diets (he says "meh") he is interested in Fussie Cat and will gobble up more of this than any other food. Along with his meds and Subcutaneous fluids he is managing well and getting some zip back in his step.

If you indeed have fussy cats - try this. Much better than some of the store bought brands (even though my cats enjoy Sheba too) i know this is like opening a can of tuna ... but it has all the Taurine and cat essentials. All 6 love Fussie cat.

review_headline: puppy loved it a little too much (didn't hold together very long)
review_body:
The basic idea behind the Chilly Bone is that you soak it with water, freeze it, and then let your dog have at it. Well, I have a teething Rottweiler puppy. She is an absolutely ferocious chewer. I bought the large Chilly Bone thinking the cool temperature would be soothing to her teeth and gums during this stage of her development.

My puppy absolutely loved it, which is why I didn't knock off more stars. However, in under 10 minutes, she had chewed a hole in one end and pulled out a bunch of stuffing. Since I'm afraid she'll swallow the stuffing, I can't let her have the Chilly Bone any more. It's basically $10 down the drain. For what it's worth, it also didn't absorb nearly as much water as I thought it would, based on the weight after soaking.

If you have a dog who is not a big chewer, the Chilly Bone might still work for you. (My last Rottie generally did not pull the stuffing out of toys, for example. However, I am not sure what might be attractive to a dog about vanilla flavoring...)

product_title: Catit Design Senses Food Maze
review_body:
This food maze was a great purchase for our cat! We researched products that would help our cat to eat slower, and this did just the trick! She now takes anywhere from 30 minutes to an hour to eat her meal and she is now able to walk away from her food, which she didn't dare to do before. She seems to enjoy the \\"play\\" behind the food maze as she has to work for her food- more stimulating than just eating out of a bowl.

We have a couple mild complaints about this product:
1) There is a hole in the top of the maze (where you put the cat food in). Our cat has discovered that it is easier to poke her head in and eat from the top instead of working for her food! We put a small bowl up-side-down over the hole and that has eliminated this problem.
2) The maze is light in weight; our cat has been able to knock it over to make the food fall out. I don't think our cat does it on purpose since we put the bowl on top. Last time she knocked it over, the bowl fell, making a crashing noise and scared her out of doing that again. Although, if you have a more daring cat, they may not have a problem with knocking it over! I would suggest maybe gluing the bottom of the maze to a piece of wood so that it is weighed down!

I would recommend this product to any cat owner who's cat eats too fast or is bored with eating out of a bowl!

review_headline: 2 out of 3 of my cats won't eat it
review_body: It's tricky to review this product, since only one of my cats will eat it; fortunately, it's the cat that has the biggest problems with hairballs. I've been using it for a week, and so far no accidents, but she only does it every two weeks or so. Time will tell. In the meantime, I think part of the reason they don't like it is this: first, there is no meat in it at all--just a \\"flavoring\\" agent. Cats are technically carnivores. In nature, they don't eat anything except meat and the occasional grass to help produce hairballs or clean out their stomachs. Aside from that, the ingredients look fine--mostly oils; I'm glad to see it doesn't have corn like pretty much everything else humans and animals consume from a package in the USA. The other reason my cats dislike this is the so-called \\"fun shape\\". It's quite large and difficult to chew, from what I can tell, so the first few times with the other two cats, I ended up with a half-chewed drooly thing on the floor.

product_title: Cardinal Laboratories Botanic Training Rewards Treats for Dogs, Beef, 3.5-Ounce
review_headline: Excellent training reward my dogs love...
review_body:
My dogs (2 Dachshunds, a Chihuahua and a French Bulldog) love these Cardinal Laboratories Pet Botanics Training Rewards beef and brown rice flavor, and their size (1/4 of an inch in diameter and 3/8 of an inch tall) in conjunction with their consistency (neither too moist, nor crumbly) makes them ideal for keeping in your pockets so that they are readily accessible when training your dog.

They are MADE IN THE USA, have only 3 calories per treat, and contain neither soy, corn, nor BHA, BHT, or ethoxyquin (artificial preservatives).

The primary ingredient is Pork Liver. Pork Liver is a nutrient-rich organ which provides your dog with protein, fat and vitamin A. It is also a good source of copper, iron, niacin, phosphorus and zinc. It provides many B vitamins, omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, and essential amino acids. Liver is of great benefit to your dog's health when offered in moderation (too much can lead to a condition called hypervitaminosis A, or an overdose of vitamin A). These little treats are a great way to add the benefits of liver to your dog's diet.

They are also great for crate training, too. Just give them to your dog through the crate door as soon as you put them in and eventually they will associate something good with being crated. Soon enough you can just toss 2 or 3 in the crate when you need to crate them and they will happily go right in. My dogs have their own room that their crates are in. When I open the door to their room they run and get in the crates sometimes quicker than I can put their training rewards in.Iron Oxide (for color), Carrots, Natural Chicken Flavor, Mixed Tocopherols, Cranberry, Peppermint, Chamomile, Rosemary, Dandelion, Tomato, Blueberry

product_title: Thermotex Infrared Large Heated Dog Therapeutic Pet Bed
review_headline: My cats take turns in this bed they love it, we will need another!
review_body:
We have 3 senior cats, one 19 year old has some stiffness and has enjoyed a K&H heated pet bed for years. Lately our other 2 cats have been \\"stealing\\" his heated bed during the chilly winter, so I decided to try this one. I don't know if we will be able to see any therapeutic effects but there is no question that the cats seek out and adore this bed.

Within an hour of receiving the package unwrapping and plugging the bed in on \\"low\\" as the directions specify, one of our cats was in that bed, happy as can be. Those of us with cats know how unusual this is - normally is you buy a new item they will at the very least ignore it a while and if it's an expensive item like this one they may completely reject it. However there was no such period of suspicion with this bed - we've had it for 2 days and the cats take turns in it, the old heated bed is now just the backup. Our 19 year old has been sleeping in it all night, it clearly feels very good to him.

I contacted the company before buying it to ask a few questions and it is good to know that the heating pad can be removed - not only for washing the bed, but it can be used for human IR therapy too. It is the same heat pad they sell for human use. Since I often get a stiff neck, this sounds good to me, though I am not sure if I'll be able to get it away from the cats for long!

PROS: Cats LOVE it! Heater can be used for humans, too.

CONS: It's not very attractive, with the big red logo on the front. I may have to get creative and sew a cover for it.

UPDATE 10-09-13

There is almost never a time when this bed is empty, there is always a cat in it! They adore this bed. I washed it once removing the heater and it washed and dried in the machine on gentle cycles just fine.

review_headline: Very nice jersey for your dog - a better sizing chart would be helpful -- UPDATED 2/20/2013
review_body:
Really nice mesh jersey for your dog -- it is breathable and looks like a pro jersey but for your furry friend. Slightly snug around the front legs and neck, with a drape off the back and belly. I find the fit to be a good feature as your dog won't be tempted to tear at it but is also isn't restricting on the chest/belly which is good for breathing. Lightweight mesh should keep dog cool -- even a furry golden retriever.

One complaint in regards to the Amazon.com listing (please fix this). The main listing for this jersey only shows sizes from XS to Large, with no sizing chart. This implies that large is the biggest size and thus the right one for a large dog. Not true. Large by this product definition would fit a dog 50lbs or less (which are generally considered medium-size dogs -- think cocker spaniel, brittany, toller, etc.) and will not work on a golden retriever (which are commonly considered to be a large dog, with mastiffs and the like considered jumbo or XL).

Had to return my large jersey (fortunately Amazon has a great return policy). Another Amazon search revealed an XL in an separate entry (don't know why this wouldn't be listed altogether) - I have ordered this one and will let you know how it turns out.

UPDATED 2/20/2013 -- Got the XL and its fits PERFECTLY! My dog looks great! Definitely need the XL for the 80-100 lb dogs and it is a snug but good fit for this size, but if yours is bigger (think Mastiff), I'd search for an XXL or Jumbo if they have them.

Dear Amazon: The product has a detailed size chart by breed -- please add this to the website listing as to avoid confusion for future customers.

product_title: Kaytee Hay n Food Bin Feeder with Quick Locks (Colors May Vary)
review_headline: Doesn't work exactly like I hoped
review_body: We chose this feeder after having a plastic bowl that our first guinea pig constantly tipped over, spilling food in his cage.  I liked that it has the clips that you attach to the cage so our new pigs can't tip it over and that does work very effectively.  What doesn't work however is that in order for our pigs to reach their hay, they have to crawl inside the food portion and end up pooping in the food bowl. Our pigs are babies though so maybe once they're a little bigger, they'll be able to reach the hay without climbing in the front part.

product_title: Blue Buffalo Wilderness Grain Free Dry Dog Food, Duck Recipe, 11-Pound Bag
review_headline: Vomiting, hair loss, and rubber chunks!
review_body:
Do you think they have better quality dog food? We have 4 cats. We fed them blue wilderness exclusively for over 2 years thinking it was good. ALL 4 cats had have random bouts of vomiting, ALL 4 cats have been going bald all over. We have thousands in vet bills now. We have found rubber chunks in two different batches, in May 2012 and Jan 2013. We never looked closely at food, these are just the pieces that jumped out at us, therefore, there must of been much more than this. In may 2012, it was hard green chunks, blue's response... a free bag of treats! Thinking it is was a fluke, we inspected next batch closely and then forgot about it. In Jan 2013, found foul smelling white caulk like chunks half way through feeding bag that caused excessive vomiting and more Vet bills with unresolved results.

After last time, we switched to another grain free brand and after month we are seeing hair regrowth and no more vomiting. Dont waste your money on this garbage cat food! It is pollution wrapped in a pretty package.

review_body:

Our puupy sometimes dings the bells when he wants to go outside and not neccessarily neeeds to potty. Although this is annoying its validation that they work for the purpose of him communicatingto us that he wants to get out of the house. Also, if you have kids they might play with the bells and confuse you pup, be sure to let them know they are for the dogs use only.

review_body: The oral chews for dogs are very small and definitely not the same large size I purchased at the VETs.

review_body:
We have a pug with severe allergies, and she has to have a dose of benadryl everyday. Unusually for a pug, she is fairly selective in her eating, so trying to hide it in her food didn't cut it.

With these pill pockets, our pug takes the benadryl without knowing it, she looks forward to them as a treat everyday.

We also order the larger sized pill pockets and split them up into 1/4's making a bag last for a few months rather than order the smaller sized pill pockets. A cost effective way of making the bag go further with a little dog!

review_body: It is kind of strong but my English Bulldog already ripped one of the corners out. I have been using it for two months.

product_title: Guardian Gear Collapsible Dog Crate
review_body: Crate folds easily, great for trips and kitchen \\"bed\\".  The cons I have seen: obviously nothing but a plastic crate will be safe in a car, I have used it in the kitchen as a den for my dog and for a year it's been great.  However, this past week the zipper broke.  There is no way to repair this.  It just simply comes apart.  So for almost $100 I got about a year of use.  I have plastic crates and I have metal folding crates from friends that are at least 40 years old (the crates' age, not the friends').  I would rather spend the money on a crate that will last the lifetime of my pet (or longer) rather than have the lightweight convenience.  Plus you really do need a dog who understands what a crate is.  I had a Min Pin use a fabric crate and he ripped through the door in no time.  My 35lb Miniature Bull Terrier will stay in that same crate (yes, with a huge rip) as long as I have zipped it up.  He could easily walk through the hole.  Also, when I travel to my in laws who have cats, I use a plastic crate to keep her cats safe.  My dog would love to chase and likely injure her cats so a fabric crate just isn't safe for her cats.  Hope my review has been helpful!

While it looka durable, if your dog is a champion chewer like mine, this won't last long. At least with this toy, he is able to destroy each circle separately, and the largest circle does bounce. His jaws finally got tired and we were able to play a little fetch. The treat feature was nice.

review_body:

The flow rate is great, the suction quality is very good, and the size is small enough to fit well without having to move that many decorations.

I knocked it one point because the faucet end will leak over time, and not just where the gaskets are, but a replacement one is cheap.

product_title: Missing Link Ultimate Hip, Joint & Coat Dog Supplement
review_body:
I read the reviews and purchased this product although with some doubt. I did not doubt what the reviewers wrote but doubted that my Dobie would be helped. He was having a very difficut time getting up from his bed or anywhere he chose to lie down. I took him to a vet and he was prescribed glucosamine. This medication made him so sick I thought he was going to die. I took him to a different vet who told me about the hip and joint problem. She replaced the glucosamine with four different prescriptions and he got somewhat better but still had a difficult time getting up.

When I saw the contents of Missing Link Ultimate my first reaction was to decline a purchase because of the glucosamine. But, if it could help I decided to give it a try and would keep the dosage very small. I decided that if I saw any negative reaction to this product at all I would immediately discontinue its use. The recommended dosage for my large Dobie calls for 4 teaspoons. I started off with just one teaspoon. After seeing no ill effects I gradually increased the dosage until I am now at the recommended 4 teaspoons. The results are absolutely amazing. He can get up without the agony he had previously. There are times when he just leaps up with no problem. There are also times when it is obvious that he is not at the top of his game but neither is he in the deplorable condition as before this product was administered.

When your pet is hurting it is a heart-wrenching sight to watch. Although I cannot claim that my Dobie is back to normal at least he is able to get around without experiencing the previous terrible discomfort and agony. I am thankful that this product works for my dog and thankful that it is available. I have seen no ill effects at all from the glucosamine such as he had when it was prescribed. I am now a believer.

product_title: Natural Balance Original Ultra Whole Body Health Dry Dog Food
review_body:
We have been buying Natural Balance products for our three cats and two dogs since 2003. They all love it, and so have we -- we've never had any issues with it before now.

We've always purchased the food from our local Petco, which is a little bit of a drive from our home but we felt it was worth it. When the price for the Natural Balance dog food on Amazon dipped lower than what we were paying at the brick and mortar Petco, we decided to give it a shot, especially since it was available with Prime shipping.

Our first bag was delivered in October 2012 (it was the same \\"kind\\" that we'd purchased from Petco, so there were no changes as far as the type they were used to). The first night after feeding the dog food to our two chihuahuas, they had diarrhea in their crate. This had never happened before and linking it to the food did not cross our minds, we assumed they had gotten into something else. The bathroom issues continued for two weeks, during which time they had two vet visits where no illness was found, but they were put on antidiarrheals. After this two week period the diarrhea subsided and we finished off the rest of the bag without a problem.

I ordered a second bag at the beginning of January 2013. While the bag was en-route, I decided to read the one-star reviews about the product to see what other people have issues with, since we'd never had any (so we thought). I was amazed to read that others were having the same diarrhea problems with their dogs that we'd just had, but since the bag was on its way I figured maybe it was coincidence, since my dogs had finished the bag (over the course of 2.5 months) without further problems. However, the first day we fed them from the new bag the dogs were up all night with more diarrhea in the crate.

As others have stated, I don't know if this is a contamination issue, an old product issue, or what, but I've got the new bag stapled closed and sitting by the front door for a return shipment, and we'll be getting our Natural Balance directly from Petco again.

product_title: Hill's Science Diet Ideal Balance Puppy Chicken and Brown Rice Dinner Dry Dog Food
review_headline: Puppy Chicken and Brown Rice Dinner & Probiotics
review_body:
I had an incident following administration of a heartworm preventive to my dog. Apparently the medication upset the probiotic balance of the intestinal tract and he was not recovering very fast. My vet recommended probiotics and an antibiotic. After 3-4 weeks of unending upset stomach and diarrhea, the vet suggested that I look at food my dog was eating. Well, I did two things: I obtained some stronger and more effective probiotics for my dog, and I switched his food to Hill's Science Diet Ideal Balance Puppy Chicken and Brown Rice Dinner.
I am not sure which regimen did the most good. But I am so satisfied with the results of both that I am afraid to change the food back to what my puppy was eating before he acquired the intestinal upset (much like C. Difficile). I will probably keep him on Science Diet products for the remainder of his life unless I hear of some double blind controlled scientific study that demonstrates there is a foolproof way of treating intestinal upset with another food plus probiotic or food alone.

review_body:

Not so positives:

product_title: Cozy Cabin Pet Car Seat/Carrier
review_body:
I purchased one of these seats listed here in 'Amazon' two years ago right after getting a new little long-legged poodle from our local Humane Society outlet. I wanted a seat that was high enough inside (plus 18-inches) for her to sit down in with her height,(or curl up in the bottom). This seat allows both, and protects the dog fully in case I turn a tight corner or apply the cars brakes quickly.

In assembling the seat, I found that the directions supplied are excellent and well thought out with easy descriptions and useful pictures. I did have some trouble getting the pole top caps into place, but if you do it the way the instructions tell you - eventually it does fit together properly.

The manufacturer could have made all of the side zipper windows (when UN-zipped) drop below the opening. One DOES, and the other doesn't. Also some kind of a covered bolster that velcrod along the back edge underneath to a depth of 3-inches deep in the center would have been nice to make the rear end of the seat equal with the front edge of the car seat so as to make the cage level. (I used some rolled up towles that works instead).

Keep in mind, this seat REQUIRES that you have a head-rest single bar atop of your car seat so that you can wrap the top strap tightly around it to secure the cage. The other strap that that hooks to the diagonal seatbelt works really well to tighten up the cage itself so that the whole cage doesn't side around. Once you get this seat installed -- leave it there, then get yourself another one IF you want to carry your loved one around outside of the car. It's A LOT easier.

Over-all, this \\"Kittywalk\\" product is the BEST seat for the money that you spend and the Security that it provides. I AM VERY HAPPY WITH MINE!

Our dog ended up needed many antibiotics, and the vet did not feel this was an appropriate product to use, despite what the product claims. It was easy to apply, and if your animal needs soothing only I think this would be good, but based on our experience, use caution and talk to your vet first. We switched over to an electric pump you can plug in to your car and it inflated the tires in like two seconds. After putting it together, I put my 23 pound pug in it and took her on a walk. I can tell she really enjoyed the ride. She was wagging her tail the entire time and looking around at the scenery.  She is afraid of heights, so this stroller was perfect because it's closer to the ground and the ride is pretty smooth. The stroller is also very light, so it doesn't feel like you're pushing something super heavy. It's very easy to walk with. We walked a mile with it. The stroller is big enough for two pugs to ride comfortably (maybe three) with plenty of head room (or one Border Collie size dog). There is a good size pocket on the left and right side of the stroller for placing keys, cell phone, treats, etc., etc. in them. There is no water bottle holder, but you might be able to put in one of the pockets. Haven't tried it yet. The inside comes with a little padding on the bottom, but you may add an extra blanket or pad to make it even more comfy for your dog. I really love this stroller. I'm glad I purchased it and I highly recommend it. One more thing, we weren't able to get the handle-break to work. If we had an instructional manual, we'd be able to tell if it needed to be connected to something. But you don't really need the break anyway. The stroller stops when you stop and it only moves when you move it. When I was looking for strollers, I noticed another one from the same company that was red. After reading someone's review about it having a strong chemical smell, I decided to purchase this one instead since no one said this one had it. So I'd just like to say that this one does not have a chemical smell to it.

review_body:
I got my boy at the beginning of December. He came with a brand of cat food I didn't recognize, but fed it to him before I thought to look at the ingredients list. I honestly ended up choosing this at the pet store because it was a few dollars cheaper than Blue Buffalo, but I'm glad I did. After a few weeks of having this out for him to free-feed between his cans of wet food, his energy skyrocketed and his coat is absolutely beautiful. He's sleek, soft, and has more energy than I know what to do with. He was a bit hesitant to eat this at first, but he adjusted and now comes running when he hears me shake the bag. At his check-up a few weeks ago, his vet declared him to be in excellent health. There's more to cat/kitten health than just the food, but it plays a crucial role, especially when they're still growing so much.

The price might be a bit steeper than you'd like, but because it's not stuffed with fillers and has protein, your kitten shouldn't eat nearly as much. I purchased a two-pound bag in mid-December that lasted three-and-a-half weeks. We're now on a five pound bag that's still half full. With his before food, he ate quite often and I had to refill his bowl at least once a day because he was still hungry. With a scoop of this in his bowl, he's content for the whole day with a few mouthfuls left.

product_title: New! Automatic! No Daily Cleaning! No Odor! No Spills! No Work! No Future Costs! Hermetically Sealed! Dog Toilet. Unique one day training
review_headline: The State-of-the-Art potty is the best potty I have ever used with my dog.
review_body: *****The State-of-the-Art potty is the best potty I have ever used with my dog.  I used the artificial potty grass with tray for years and it was very inconvenient and very messy.  My dog uses an indoor potty full-time.  This potty is unique and is great because it is an enclosed unit.  This is an easy device for any dog to use.  I definitely recommend it. *****Please note:  That my dog did not respond to positive reinforcement and the dog trainers did not help because he sees himself as the alpha.  Also, I read many dog books about positive reinforcement training, but their were no treats, rewards...etc... that could ever persuade him to do anything he didn't want to do and that includes using this potty.  So, definitely try the positive reinforcement with this potty as suggested in the comments.  I definitely agree with this.   *****But, for my dog, I had no choice but use this method.  He was raised using the grass potty patches, full-time, but he just didn't want to use this kind of potty.  This is what I had to do to get him to use this potty patch.  Our dog adamantly refused to use the potty.  He even went potty other places in the house versus using this new potty.  He needed to get learn that I am the alpha and I decide what is best for him and us.  It took a whole weekend, but in the end it was worth it.  He was use to the grass and I understood this, but this new grated potty is more convenient and thus better for all concerned.  He is a very stubborn 20 pound little guy named Duke.  Here is what I did:  First, I collected about ½ cup of some pee from the old grass potty and poured it on the new State of the Art potty, so he would smell his own scent on the new potty.  Then, I confined him and myself in the kitchen with the potty, some dog food and lots of water.  I prepared myself to be with him in the kitchen until he used the potty on his own (not easy but worth it for me in the end).  I watched him and after ENOUGH time had passed and I KNEW that he HAD to at least go pee pee..... I set him on the potty.  If he walked away and did not go, I kept setting him there again and again and again (over and over). This is the test, I figured out.  If you let him walk away and he has to go, you lose.  I also ordered him to stay on the potty and go.  Eventually, he did go pee pee.  It wasn't easy and it was a test of wills.  But, since this experience, he also minds me much better.  Of course, he was testing the alpha position that I hold, when he contested my decision to use this new potty.  I didn't have to get angry with him, I just set him on the new potty over and over, then said very sternly, "Duke pee pee right now" and I pointed to the new potty.  Eventually, he did.  Also, if he looked like he was going to go elsewhere in the kitchen, I would pick him up and set him on the potty.  He did pee pee once on the kitchen floor not even close to the potty and I took a rolled up magazine and "lightly" swatted his behind and told him No! No! ...rather sternly.  He understood from this action that it was not okay to pee pee on the floor.  You don't want to be harsh at all because your dog may associate punishment with the potty.  You just want him to understand what you want him to do.  I did the same technique for the poo poo training.  I stayed in the kitchen with him all weekend (except for at night when he slept in a large cage in my bedroom), until he went without my assistance. Also, I would tell him he was a good boy after he did the deed, however, I did not overdo the praise because there was still work to be done.  *****Ok, so it wasn't the easiest weekend for me, but now I reap the rewards.  This is soooo much easier than the grass and tray potty for me.  He now goes to the bathroom on his own and not anywhere else in the house.  But, if he did go in the house again, I would use the rolled up magazine lightly on him and say NO, NO and then set him again on the new potty.  The pee pee goes directlyinto the device and I use a small sandwich baggy to pick up the poop and finish the cleaning with a baby wipe.  If the poop gets into the grates, I lift the grate and clean with another baby wipe.  When I am done cleaning, I set the grate on the device and before snapping shut, I place a large rag over the top of it, so that there is no splattering of the pee.  When the device is full of pee pee, I empty it in the toilet.  This is so much easier and convenient.  Then I put it in the tub and soak it in soapy water using Dawn dish soap for a few hours. Wearing gloves,  I then remove the grates and then clean the entire unit with a large plastic bristle brush with a handle.  I rinse and dry it, put the grates back on and it is ready for reuse.  But, there is one more step that helps minimize any odors.  Before I put the side cap on the unit, I pour about ¼ to ½ cup of Natures Miracle into the device with a measuring cup and then close the side cap.  *****In my experience: This device lasts longer than the grass and tray.  Instead of one day, now I wait about four days to change it out.  Also, I have another clean one waiting to replace it, so there is always one available for my dog to use.  Also, it is easier to clean and takes about half the time to clean as the grass.  Also, there have been no pee pee mishaps.  I don't know how many times in using the grass that the tray of pee pee would spill out on the floor.  Also, the grass tracks.  When Duke would pee, it would take forever to drain through the grass and he would ultimately step back onto it and track the pee through the house.  With this device, the pee drops below the grate and into the drain.  If there is a little on the grates, that is easily remedied if you wipe the grate clean with a dry cloth from time to time.  *****This works for me.  It is a bit more expensive than the grass but has proven worth it.  However, if it had been more expensive than it is, I probably would not have even tried it.  I thinkthat it is priced just right for what it delivers.  The customer service has been wonderful.  And YES, I would recommend this item with the understanding that if you have a dog that won't use it, it may take some time to get your dog used to it and/or trained on it.  But, if my dog, Duke, who is VERY stubborn and strong-willed has learned to use it, I think any dog can be trained to use it by applying one technique or other.  It was worth it to me.  Hope this review is helpful.

product_title: Tetra 25905 Decorative Reptile Filter for Aquariums up to 55 Gallons
review_headline: Low Quality - Not Suitable for Turtles
review_body:
I was so excited to get this for my turtle tank. The idea of combining the basking platform with the filter to free up tank space and give him more room to swim sounded great. Unfortunately, it was neither a good basking platform, nor was it a good filter.

When I got the item in the mail, I opened it up and took it out of the box. Immediately I noticed a piece of the ceramic/resin material the rock is made out of was broken off and laying on the bottom of it. I continued assembly anyways, not thinking that it would be a critical piece (wrong). I am going to blame this broken piece rather than the filter itself, but the water became so dirty I could not see more than an inch into the water. The water was going through where the piece broke off, completely bypassing the filter. I will be returning it for this reason.

Ok, I got a defective item, but even if it worked as a filter, I still would probably only give it 2 stars. The other major problem with it is that there is a max water level marked on the back side of the filter. If you fill the tank up to that level, the top of it is about 2-3 inches out of the water, and nearly impossible for my turtle to climb onto. The walls of the filter are much steeper than you would think by looking at the pictures.

So in the end, I had to put in my old filter and my old basking platform as this item was good for neither of those things.

Pros:
-Looks really nice
-Reasonably priced

Cons:
-Arrived Broken
-Too steep for turtle to climb up
-The slot for the power cord to run out of is aimed out, rather than up, so if you have the filter in the corner against the wall, the power cord will lift the lid up a bit and make the platform wobbly.

product_title: Hill's Science Diet Sensitive Stomach & Skin Dog Food
review_headline: Update - my dog seems to be allergic to the new combined formula
review_body:
I originally bought this food for my dog because of his digestive problems - namely diarrhea and, er, major flatulence issues. Science Diet took care of the problem for months, but I switched to \\"regular\\" food to save a couple of bucks. Mistake. The diarrhea problem was gone, but the other problem remained so it was right back to Science Diet and I'll never switch again. And I don't have to keep opening the windows to air out my house! :)

October 2014 Update: I'm very disappointed with the new combined Sensitive Skin/Sensitive Stomach formula, because my dog seems to be allergic. My dog developed hot spots and his skin was flushed, and my vet assumed it was a food allergy. I didn't believe her, but I put my dog on the (VERY expensive) prescription formula for a week - and my dog was fine. Thinking I was going to disprove my vet's theory, I put my dog back on Sensitive Stomach/Skin - and the itching returned. I couldn't understand why my dog was suddenly having this problem and then I remembered that the formula had changed. This is so frustrating; I thought I had this dog food problem solved.

review_body:

We loved the concept and design, but it did not live up to expectations from the beginning. The leashes constantly tangle - if you catch it quick enough, you could twist your wrist to right them. If you walk at a fast pace (or worse, run) it seems to tangle worse. I used it again this morning and had to stop and literally hang the leash upside down to \\"un-twirl\\" three separate times in 1-1/2 miles. The sides also take turns not retracting, which cause the dogs to get tied up in the extra leash, or for the person walking to trip. Also, the locking mechanism works on both sides simultaneously, which is horrible when one dog needs to get pulled back and the other is right next to you. I should also mention that our dogs are both under 20 lbs, so that should not be an issue. The weight of the handle might be an issue for some, but would be worth it if it worked as advertised.

I will continue to use it because I hate to waste money, but I would not recommend the product.

product_title: Nutramax Cosequin Equine Optimized with MSM, 1400 Gram Container
review_headline: Not quite sure of its effectiveness, but it is more of an added assurance in the form of supplement...
review_body:
I bought this for my father, who owns a dozen or so thoroughbreds.

Honestly, it is difficult to tell for a lay owner to have any noticeable difference that can be traced to this supplement -- just as the physiological effect of glucosamine on human joints has not been clearly demonstrated, given the technical difficulty of measuring bio-availability of the nutrient at relevant areas of the body.

That being said, some other owners that I personally know seem to think that it helps their horses recuperate -- just as men who complain of joint pains sometimes say that taking glucosamine alleviates pain. (This might only be a placebo effect, however.) Despite their tendency to be highly superstitious and fickle in their judgment, I am willing to accept this to a degree.

Remember, apparent "better joint recovery" does not mean that you can expect your horses to race more frequently, etc.; feeding them this supplement should only be a choice of good will toward the animal's long-term well-being.

product_title: Vet's Best Feline Urinary Tract Support Cat Supplements, 60 Chewable Tablets
review_body:
My male cat had a severe UTI that led to a complete blockage and a horrifically painful experience that almost led to his bladder bursting. After a night in the emergency vet clinic and then transferred to my normal vet to be hospitalized for four-five additional days hooked up to a catheter and IV's with a vet bill sitting at about $1000, I was looking for ways to keep from both of us EVER having to go through that fiasco again.

He is on prescription cat food for bladder health, but even on that a few weeks later he began being lethargic and licking incessantly again as well as urinating inappropriately outside his litter box. That is when I started frantically looking for a way to curb what looked like a relapse.

I found this product and had it shipped quickly. I started him on the full dosage recommended on the bottle and after about a week of this schedule he seemed much better. He stopped licking, was more energetic, and started correctly using his litter box without any further incident. I scaled back the dosage to one tablet per day after a couple of weeks, and so far so good and it has been a few months now. He is back to his old self, and he loves the taste.

I break the tablet in half with my hand and simply place it on top of his food. The flavoring they use on the product is desirable to cats and I actually have to feed him locked up so my other cat does not swoop in and snatch up the tablets for herself.

I am hoping this tablet continues to perform as well as it seems to have been doing in order to save me some costly vet bills and him some extreme pain and stress. I will continue to use product.

product_title: PetBuckle Kwik-Connect Tether for the Universal Travel Harness Pet Seat Belt
review_headline: Nice latch to secure dog safety harness
review_body:
I use it with Solvit-Car Safety Harnesses For Dogs, the best car harness around. It is well padded and comfortable for my golden retriever. Very few dogs are restrained in cars, and that is a shame. The Solv-It harness comes with a secure strap that is attached to the lap or shoulder part of a buckled seat belt. It works well but after nearly three years of strain on my seat belt it no longer retracts as snugly as it used to. But I discovered a different type of secure strap this one: the PetBuckle Pet travel Safety Tether. It secures into the LATCH/ISOFIT latches in every car since 2003 designed to secure child safety seats. So by using the PetBuckle I can attach the dog harness to the car without putting constant strain on my rear seat belt because it is secured to the LATCH attachment.

There is one detail I need to clarify. This large strap is supposed to be 30" long. It isn't, at least on its own. The main strap is 25" long. The adapter strap to use it with a seat belt in a car that doesn't have the LATCH connectors. This adapter is about 5" long, so the two pieces together equal about 30". But because I'm securing a large dog with a long spine, the main strap itself was not long enough to give her enough freedom of movement. And because the main reason I bought this strap was to relieve stress on the same outboard seatbelt in the rear of my car I decided to combine the main strap of this product with the 6" or so (adjusted to its shortest length) strap that came along with her Solv-It Car Safety Harness. This product is snapped into the LATCH connector, and it is clicked into the carabiner of the safety harness strap and that is then connected to the safety harness the dog is wearing. This all works together for me. But it is important to keep in mind that the length isn't 30". It may or may not be a concern to you.

My dog can sit, lie down, and put her head out of the window and I know she is safe and secure. And my car's leather upholstery is protected by a cover from wet feet, hair, and mud. I'm a happy girl.

product_title: PetSafe SSSCAT Spray
review_body: I can't begin to describe the level of satisfaction this product has earned in the past few weeks in my household.  For 12 years, I dealt with a cat who would literally NEVER leave the bedroom door at night and frequently scratched and meowed for hours on end.  Since it is impossible to squirt a water gun outside of the door from inside the bedroom, I was desperate to find something I could use to humanely get my animal to GTFA and leave me alone.  I had devised Rube Goldberg-type mechanisms in my mind that would set off a chain reaction which would flip a marble into a pan and spiral it down into a cylinder that would eventually build pressure in a latex balloon filled with compressed helium that would then slowly rise and evoke a hose filled with water from above the doorknob, that would hopefully, hopefully douse my cat's head (I left out the dominoes part).  But alas, my lack of creativity got the best of me, and I just ended up stacking a bevy of pillows outside the door instead.  So then one day, I typed, \\"humane cat repellent\\" into Google, and this device appeared before my eyes.  I ordered it after having read some glowing reviews and after having watched about forty hilarious youtube videos shot by home users.  The day it arrived, I simply popped the sensor on top of the can, turned it on, placed it in from of my door, and went to bed.  About three minutes later, I heard, \\"PPPSSSSTTTT,\\" followed by a flurry of galloping paw noises descending the stairs outside in the hall.  That night and every night hence, when I place the ssscat outside of the door, I hear silence.  Nothing.  Nada.  I would therefore recommend this product to anyone I know who owns a cat dealing with separation or behavior issues.  My only suggestion would be to watch your feet in the morning as you stumble out of the bedroom in a somnambulent stupor.  You are likely to have the ever-loving SH%$ scared out of you!

product_title: 2011 USB Rechargeable LED Dog Collar Black Stars-large 25''(fits 18-23'' Neck)- Red LED
review_body:
I purchased this in November 2011 and am as happy with it today as the day I received it.

Pros:
Night Time Visibility
Easy To Use
Easy To Charge
Multi-Control/Speed Function

Cons:
Not Waterproof
Battery Case Bulky
Lights Do Not Completely Encircle Collar (approx. 80%)
Lights Get Lost In Long Haired Dogs Mane/Ruff

I have two English Shepherds. My one dog is a tri-color with predominately semi-long black hair and, if she is turned with her back toward me, I can not see her from 15 feet away. My other dog is a dark/shaded sable and white with long white hair around his mane/ruff and, if he is turned with his back toward me, I can not see him from 25 feet away. She has the white LEDs, he has the red LEDs, but the white is brighter than the red and it is simply their hair that causes the visibility issues. I can see them mostly fine (and they have several acres they can wander on), it really is only when they're turned just right and hold the position that I lose sight of them.

I like that the collars have not only a multi-control/speed function, but also a separate on/off switch to minimize accidentally turning on when the dogs play together. However, my one dog is 14 1/2 yrs old so they don't play too hard together. The control box really doesn't look sturdy enough to survive the experience of a pair of half-grown pups rough-housing together. But there's no reason one could not just put the collar on for nighttime visibility and leave it off the dog the rest of the time.

The collars themselves look very durable and, after a year of almost constant wear, still look new.

Battery life. During the summer months the LEDs get very little use and so the batteries go a very long time between charges. During the winter months, I use the LEDs for approx. 1 to 1 1/2 hrs a day and usually charge the batteries once a week as a just because. I really don't know how long the batteries will last since the only time I've had them run dry was in the summer (probably from lack of use) and when my male accidentally turned his on at some point and I eventually discovered it when I next went to use it.

What I love most about these collars is that they are rechargeable. I plug them into my computer every now and then and that's it. No buying special (and usually expensive) batteries, no changing batteries with their teeny tiny screws.

All in all, I highly recommend these collars for someone with short-haired dogs who don't like to get wet or rough-house. I recommend these collars to everyone else that pays attention to their dogs while they wear these collars. I also recommend these collars for search & rescue dogs and for people, like me, who have very large yards with no fences.

product_title: Karen Pryor i-Click Dog Training Clicker, 3 Clickers
review_headline: Simple, effective, easy on the ears
review_body:
This is the first clicker I've purchased, so I can't compare its long-term durability to others. I can say that I prefer it over all the clickers I tried out in the pet store (mostly the cheap box-style ones).

The box clickers make a harsh and loud CLICK that I find sort of annoying. This is not necessary. All you need in marker training is a precise and consistent sound the animal can hear (you can pop a Snapple bottle top if you want, or snap your fingers, or use a concise word like \\"yes!\\" as your marker). And since our dogs hear better than us, this clicker is more than sufficiently loud.

Just in testing box clickers a few times each in the store, I found it pretty easy to pinch my finger inside the device when going for a fast click. Perhaps I'm inept, but it seems like a flawed design. The raised-button style of the i-Click makes more sense to me - I keep mine on a wrist band so I don't drop it during training, and it's always easy to grab and click when I need to.

It may cost twice as much as a cheap clicker, but when twice as much means a difference of $1-$2, it's not gonna break the bank. Buy a quality clicker.

However, the couple of reviews stating their dogs broke through the cage are a little severe. If your dog is busting through this cage, a flimsy cage is not the problem. The dog acting out is the problem.
I choose to use the side door that has a 2 inch lip of cage at the bottom, but I found a nice cushion on sale at Ace Hardware to place in the crate that works great. I plan to go to fabric store to cut some fabric panels to hang on sides.
I have a Dachshund and a Beagle that sleep together.
They love the crate.
I would buy it again.

In order to advance my crusade to improve bird nutrition and health I wanted to include here a recipe for a fresh diet that a breeder I highly respect gave me (Thank you Angela) just to offer some advice to keep our pet birds healthier - it is not at all related this the product I have reviewed here but it could very well give you some great ideas to get fresh fruits and vegetables into your bird.

All domestic birds, especially parrots, lovebirds, parrotlets, parakeets, canaries, finches, conures, etc, should have fresh fruit and vegetables and they can present a challenge to get them to eat them. Gives this recipe a try Here's a recipe that I make and it took some time for them to get used to it, but now my lovebirds and my parrotlets both eat this when provided. I give it in the morning and remove uneaten food in the evening.

1 apple cored and chopped
1/2 Cup chopped raw broccoli
1 Chopped bell pepper seed included
2 shredded carrots
1/2 Cup chopped greens (bok choy, mustard greens, kale and/or chard)
1/4 Cup frozen corn (can be eliminated if you put slices of raw corn on the cob in treat holders/clips in your cage - all my birds LOVE it and I have had 100% success getting them to eat this)
1/4 Cup frozen peas
1/2 Cup cooked rice (brown or GABA brown rice)
1/2 Cup cooked dried beans (they will need to be soaked overnight for 8 hours)
A handful of blueberries, chopped cherries and chopped seedless grapes

Mix all ingredients together in a large bowl. Place ingredients in an ice cube tray and freeze. Remove frozen cubes and place in plastic bags to store in freezer. Then you can take out the perfect portion on a daily basis . They say 1 cube per bird but you may find that 1 cube will work well for a pair of birds of if smaller birds, even more. Instead of an ice cube tray I use slider freezer bags and press them flat after I fill them with enough of the mixture which makes freezer storage easy and this way I can easily break off appropriate sized pieces. This recipe is variable and you can switch out or add/delete ingredients that you have on hand or what you know your birds already like.

This recipe is in ADDITION to their regular diet of pellets and seeds and not a substitute.

product_title: SportDOG Brand TEK Series 1.0 GPS Tracking + E-Collar System - 7 Mile Range - Waterproof and Rechargeable - Tone, Vibration, and 99 Levels of Shock - Expandable to Locate and Train up to 12 Dogs
review_body:
I had a spaniel mix who passed away in July. I had considered buying an e-training collar for him, but I was apprehensive. I never did, and truth is, he probably didn't need it. BUT, I have a new dog now (boxer-rhodesian ridgeback mix). I've been leash-walking her daily for the past five months and she gets a decent workout (big hayfield, lots of hills). I couldn't let her off leash because she would simply never come when called. I started investigating e-collars again with the same apprehension. When I saw that manufacturers had integrated GPS with the collars, I was more than interested. I figured even if I didn't use the stimulation, I could at least find my dog if she disappeared into the woods. I went ahead and bought the TEK-V1LT. I used the collar-tracker only for awhile, but basically I was just chasing her all over the park. My dog was very good at obeying commands while on-leash, so I started to use the stimulation buttons simultaneously with the leash corrections. Finally last week I gulped, unhooked the leash and let her rip. She was about 60 yards away (the gps told me that) and I tried the momentary shock button and a loud \\"COME\\". She barely flinched at the stimulation and came directly to me the very first time. I am so happy that I can let her off leash and she runs around like a maniac until I decide it's time for her to move on. I always use the collar's \\"tone\\" function before an electronic correction. She'll obey about 75% of the time only using the tone. It's been 100% success with the stimulation.
I suppose anyone reading this review has already formed an opinion on electronic collars, so let me just describe how well designed this unit is. My dog is extremely active and I have no worries about the ruggedness of the collar. She's been in the water with it, through the woods, jumping obstacles...the works. The GPS locks a signal quickly and the range is beyond what I suppose I'll ever need (specifications state 7 miles!).
The transmitter is a technological work of art. It's intuitive and built to the same standards as the collar. The buttons are very stiff and according to SportDOG they will gradually break in. I personally like the idea of a training transmitter with buttons that would be difficult to activate accidentally. It's easy to toggle between training and tracking mode (push one button). There's a decent level of customization for the buttons; menus are easy to find and navigate; and all the functions seem very logical to me. My only complaint is that the stimulation buttons don't work if the unit is in \\"tracking\\" mode, but it's so easy to switch modes that that's a minor quibble (BTW, the tone button still works in tracking mode).
I bought this unit for one dog; a crazy 11 month old puppy. After successfully using the sportDOG with her, I can imagine how suitable it would be for the owner who trains field dogs. By adding additional collars, you can train and track up to twelve dogs with this thing! I'll never do that (God willing), but judging by the design of the TEK-V1LT, I think it would be easy.

product_title: Just for Cat Urine Destroyer Cat Remover
review_body:
Urine Destroyer is GREAT if it's the only product you use (or at least another enzyme product) first. If you use any other commercial cleaners, they may actually set the uric acid crystals from the urine, as does hot water. Remember that this is a complex bodily fluid made of urea, creatinine, uric acid, sodium and other electrolytes that takes repeated treatments to work to break it down.

1. For fresh stains BLOT up as much as you can (i.e. old towel with plastic bag on top and stand on...plastic bag keeps urine from coming in contact with the bottom of your shoes that you might track on the carpet).

2. SOAK fresh/dry stains (on carpet, down to the pad); BLOT (scrubbing works the urine/uric acid crystals deeper into the carpet fibers). Repeat soak/blot. You can also use hand tool with cool water rinse and suction from steam cleaner.

I used a black light to find spots where my new cat was going, but in addition to finding her new stains, I was shocked to see glowing pale stains from my dog who passed away seven years ago. That carpet gets steam cleaned twice a year...fourteen times! That's how tough urine is! No product will ever remove it 100% but used properly, Urine Destroyer, does it best.

product_title: simpleLEASH - A No Pull Training Simple Leash and Collar
review_body: There are a lot of people on here chastising people for using this product on their dogs. Well let me tell you, I have tried every method with my pit bull mix. I have tried stopping when she pulls, training used successfully on my other dog, gentle lead collars, harnesses, choke collars, you name it I've probably tried it. We went to training classes at petsmart. I tried making her sit when she pulls. I tried almost everything and every method for two years now. Nothing. She has pulled me and made me fall on several occasions just to chase a lizard or a squirrel. She has hurt my neck on several occasions. I'm 115 lbs and she is 65 of pure muscle and excitement. She is stronger than I am and I love her but I needed help. I put this collar on her and all it took were two shocks and she got it. She walks like a perfect angel now. I couldn't believe it. I did try it on myself and will say it's strong even on the low setting. I did not take the decision to buy this collar lightly and it was upsetting to see her jump, but I would buy this again in a heartbeat. Some dogs are more stubborn than others and until you own one you may not understand the degree of difficulty others are experiencing.

product_title: KONG Air Dog Squeaker Dog Toy
review_body:
I bought this at the same time I bought the large Kong squeaker bone toy as an alternate shape to provide variety for my dog. It's constructed the same as the bone toy.

Does your dog destroy most toys? Do you cringe when you purchase a stuffed toy knowing you'll be picking up the shredded parts from the floor the very next day? You may have discovered buying cheap dog toys just isn't a good idea.
If so, this toy may be what you have been searching for. Like most dog owners I was aware of the durability of the hard rubber Kong brand toy. I also found my dog was uninterested in playing with it unless it was stuffed with food or smeared with peanut butter.

Well, this one is different. It's a Kong hard rubber dog toy covered with a durable fabric. It seems the fuzzy fabric surface will keep my dog's interest and keep her chewing it while the sturdy rubber interior keeps the toy from being totally destroyed in the first day. The hollow center make it just soft enough for her to squeeze, while the squeaky noise maker helps to keep her interest. With it's football shape, it works as a retrieval toy too.
Eventually she will tear the fabric completely off. After a longer time, she will even begin to chew the hard rubber into fragments causing me to have to discard the remains of the toy. They are far, far more durable than anything else I've found. It's definitely a value for the money. My dog is a young, 44 pound, Australian Shepherd. This toy is the largest one Kong makes and it's just the right size for her.

They just last longer than any other chew toy I've found.

product_title: PetSafe Busy Buddy Tug-A-Jug Meal Dispensing Dog Toy
review_headline: Kibble size matters, frustration might set in!
review_body:
My dogs have several types of food puzzle balls, and I purchased this one because it had a much larger capacity for kibble. It's not a total bust, but it's probably not a winner for every kind of dog (or every type of food/treat).

PROS:
1. Holds plenty of kibble. I have an XL dog who eats over two cups at a meal and that fits in this thing.
2. More difficult to work than other puzzle balls. This requires the dog to do a lot of "manipulating" of the jug---rolling, flinging in the air, etc.---in order to get the food out. Pulling rope just "closes" the opening so no food comes out. This is a good thing if you want something to really occupy a lot of time with your dog.
3. Stands up so far to three hard chewers.

CONS:
1. Kibble has to be pretty small to work in here. Like the size of a small pearl or a large BB. Weird-shaped kibble also doesn't work well.
2. Dumb dogs can't figure it out. Out of my 3, only the Border Collie really understands what to do to get the food out. The other two lurk around why she works it and try to snatch the food when it comes out.
3. Some dogs might try to just chew the whole rope thing out. When that happens here, I will probably add a small ball into the jug to act as a similar "stopper."
4. If you are really using this as a meal feeder, the dog might get frustrated before he gets all his chow in.

All three dogs do come back to it when it's out with food in it, which is nice because it keeps them quietly occupied for a while. Not bad overall, but depends on the dog and the food!

product_title: TopDog Health GlycanAid HA Factor Joint Formula Supplement for Dogs, 150 Chewable Tablets
review_body:
We operate a small, foster home-based rescue group for dogs. We try to make a difference for dogs that are having a harder time being adopted, whether because of age or health concerns. One of the dogs that came into our rescue in March 2012 was a 7 year-old beagle-mix named Jamaica. She came to us in Saint Paul, MN, from a shelter in Joplin, MO, where she had been passed over for about three months because she had arthritis. We did not realize how severe her arthritis was until the night she arrived at our home. It was immediately obvious that she was significantly affected by her condition - she could not rise and walk without crying. It was very heartbreaking to see that she chose to sleep downstairs, aware from us, because it was closer to the door so she did not have as far to walk when it was time to do her business outside. X-rays showed the extent of her arthritis and the damage done to her hips. Our vet prescribed an anti-inflammatory and recommended that Jamaica be put on a higher dose supplement for her joints. We originally had her on a common supplement that starts with a \\"D\\" and saw no real response in the first four weeks. An internet search pointed me to Dr J's website, where I read about the science and products he offered. We decided to order a bottle of GlycanAid-HC for Jamaica.

Within 2 weeks, we saw an excellent, positive response from the GlycanAid-HC. Since we started using it, Jamaica is a very different dog. She is on only a half dosage of her anti-inflammatory. She does not hesitate to climb the stairs in our 3-story house to follow me as I go about my business. She enjoys her walks. She no longer cries in pain when she rises to walk. Her quality of life is more improved than I could possibly have hoped for, considering the condition she came to us in. She became such an active and integral part of our household, we decided to make her a permanent member and officially adopted her in June.

To be clear, Jamaica's improvement cannot be called a miraculous, full recovery -- she will always suffer from affects of her arthritis -- happily though, she has far more good days than bad days now. The real difference is that even her bad days seem manageable now, and she has a quality of life that gives her reason to wag her tail and look forward her walks and her kooky dances when we come home from work.

Thank you, Dr J and GlycanAid for giving our wonderful girl the ability to enjoy the years she has left with us.

product_title: Tidy Cats Cat Litter, Breeze, Litter Box Kit System, 1 Kit
review_headline: Working well mixed with traditonal litter boxes
review_body: I have too many cats to switch litter boxes \\"cold turkey,\\" so for now I just have one of these which I use alongside other traditional litter boxes.  The good news is that my pickiest cat (that would be the one that colors outside the lines, so to speak) LOVES it.  Bad news is that so far none of them have gone #2 in it, and I've been using it for about two months.  Since none will go #2 in it, I don't have any of the #2 odor issues that other reviewers comment about.  I'm also not sure that all of them have used it - it's being used, but I haven't identified all of the users yet.  My plan is to slowly start replacing traditional boxes with this system and hope for the best because it is so much cleaner and easier to clean than a traditional box.  Even if I can't completely switch over, the convenience just one or two boxes brings is worth the cost.  That's because (for me at least) the worst part of litter box cleaning is the #1 clumps that don't lift easily or otherwise breakup in the box - and dirty the sides of the box - or are HUGE.  That issue is completely eliminated here.  The box stays \\"clean\\" for an entire month.  When it's time to clean it, there isn't any of the messy side residue to scrub off like with a traditional box.  You just wipe it down.  The pad drawer (replace pad weekly) can get a little messy with urine if you let the urine spill over the sides of the pad, but it's still easier to clean up because there is no litter residue down there - just liquid.  Have had a similar problem as other reviewers with broken pellets sticking in the straining grate; would be nice if that could be improved but don't know how they would do it.  Final note: I haven't noticed any urine odor issues with this box, and the only time I've noticed that pellets weren't drying out is at the very end of the month when it's time to switch out the litter anyway (and it was very minor).

product_title: Two 18 x 4 1/2 inch Cat Scratch Guards with Pins ---- THE ORIGINAL CAT SCRATCH GUARD FURNITURE PROTECTOR ---- Love Your Furniture AND Your Cat!
review_headline: Great for corners if you're tired of sticky tape!
review_body:
These scratch guards work especially well if your cat likes to scratch corners (as many cats do). Mine have a fetish for couch corners.

It is made of flexible plastic, so it is a bit trickier to install than the rigid plastic versions I have seen elsewhere. However, the flexibility gives it a much closer fit. Another benefit is that you can cut the guard to size. I needed to shorten it slightly, and it was easy to do. If you have a small hole punch (smaller than the typical US hole punch used for 3-ring binders), you can easily punch a hole for the upholstery tack, but it's probably not necessary.

Please note: if the texture of the upholstery is what attracts your cat, he or she will just move along to a clear area and continue to scratch. These guards are a physical barrier for those places that cats instinctively scratch (scent-mark).

If you need a stronger deterrent, I've had good luck with the sticky-tape. Cats seem to hate it, and they often stay away from the entire piece of furniture once they've had a bad experience. (For a while, at least!).

But if you're tired of having dirty-looking tape on the corners, and tired of walking by furniture and having the tape end up on your pant legs, give these a try!

WOULD NOT USE IN CARGO AREA OF AN AIRPLANE - FOR CARRY-ON ONLY.  IF PLACING A DOG IN A CARGO AREA (WHICH I WOULD NEVER DO) I'D RECOMMEND A STURDY, HARD SIDED CRATE.

product_title: Dogit X-Gear Weather Tech Waterproof Dog Mat, Beige, X-Large
review_body: Mat arrived on time and packaged well.  We've had it for close to a month now and my girl certainly likes it to sit and lie on out on the deck.  She doesn't chew so have not had any problems there.  It has been put down on the deck when the deck has been wet and when my dog has been wet she has laid on it and the mat has dried off fairly quickly.  I like the product and it is light enough to take with you if going somewhere or to put out on the deck and then bring in at night or to place where ever during the day.  I would recommend it.

product_title: HOLIDAY NAUGHTY/NICE T-SHIRT
review_body: I bouught this for my medium sized dog.  It fits him well and he looks great.  The different labels are clever.  One can choose from Nice, Naughty, or the image of a snowflake.  I haven't seen any other clothing like that.  The fabric is much thicker than other dog clothing I've purchased which is great for Winter weather.  I'm satisfied with this purchase.

product_title: ThunderShirt Classic Dog Anxiety Jacket
review_body: Such a smart idea and product! One of my dogs is scared to death of loud noises and thunderstorms and becomes a pacing, panting and quivering mess. During one particularly booming storm, my 5-year old tried to console our dog by completely covering her in a blanket and tucking it around her. She stayed that way for the rest of the storm. I had read about the Thundershirt earlier this year and had forgotten about it until this moment and looked it up. I read the reviews, more positive than not, and decided to try it. Anything to help our dog not be so frightened. Unbelievable! After it arrived, I had her wear it for about 15 minutes to get used it, as suggested by the manufacturer. Didn't bother her a bit and was easy to put on/take off. Was able to test it the next day. As soon as I could hear the distant rumbling, I put the shirt on her. This storm was a doozy with lightening crashing right over the house (we live in the Rocky Mtns if this helps the image). Our dog did great! During the beginning of the storm she was actually pretty relaxed and lounging. Once it got louder, she shook just a little but NOTHING like it would have been without it! Now when it starts to storm, I just pull out the shirt, she knows it's time and comes right to me! She gets a little funny sometimes when traveling in the car and now I have her wear it then, too. It helps! I think she really digs it! I recommend it now to everyone who says their dog is afraid of loud noises, storms, etc. or just plain neurotic and nervous. :)

review_body: This electronic fence is worthless.It doesn't even deserve one star but I had to select at least one to do the review. It doesn't work correctly. review_body: Kong makes durable dog toys that provide fun for our dog, and last a long time. The squeaker stays inside the tennis ball, even with rough treatment from a strong chewer. Safe and entertaining for the dog.

product_title: IRIS Pet Playpen with Door, 24-Inch
review_body: I really wanted this enclosure to work. My 13 yr old dog is now blind and incontinent. I wanted a bigger area that I could put a bed and a pee pad tray into during the day while I'm at work. I read other posts saying that even their active dogs did not move or get out of this enclosure. I did not have that kind of experience. I've looked everywhere for some kind of flooring to attach to this enclosure but, have been unsuccessful.  I liked the size but, it's just too easy for a dog to get out of.

review_body: I love this brush.  I have a Labradoodle with curly hair.  It works great on him and he doesn't seem to mind it at all. product_title: Otomite Plus Ear Mite Treatment (14.7 mL) by VIRBAC
review_headline: This is NOT a toy -this is medication
review_body:
Well, for some reason, this review is asking me to rate this cat toy!
As I write now, this is a listing for Otomite Plus Ear Mite Treatment.

Every cat and dog will have ear mites at some point in their lives. The extent will vary, but it will happen.

We used to use Hartz ear miticide, but after the last time we used it, that was indeed the last time!
It made our cats' ears bright red, hot and they ran around like they were in pain as well.
I think the Hartz quality has fallen so low, it is now off the scale!

One of our cats kept tipping his head to the side, and scratching at his ear. There was nothing
visible to my eye, but mites aren't really visible until they get pretty heavily populated.
So, I was in search of a new ear mite medication.

After a lot of reading and research, I chose this one. It had medication strong enough to kill the pests,
but also had ingredients that would not be quite as harsh on the actual pet. It has lots of warnings on the
bottle that it is veterinarian strength, could be poisonous, etc etc, so do treat it with respect!

It says to clean the outer ear first, then add 2 or 3 drops and massage into the pet's ear(s) until the medicine
gets moved down into the ear canal. This is the first miticide I've ever had that didn't say just drop directly into
the ear canal.

So, I did that - cleaned the outer ear with a damp washcloth, put the drops in, massaged them greatly.
Waited a minute, then took the washcloth and wiped off the back of the ear and outer ear so they would not
ingest much of the medication while cleaning themselves.

I did just the left ear on each cat, to check for any reactions, since this was a new med for us all.
I kept tabs on them, and other than a little warmer than normal, the ears were fine. I checked the next day
as well, to be sure they had not had any negative reactions to it. Everyone was fine, so I did the right ears.

I have to say that I think both cats were happier doing one ear at a time, rather than both. I bet it feels very
strange to have that stuff down in there, and it could definitely affect hearing for a while! Better to give them
one good ear, right?!

So, four days later, there is no need to re-treat. No one is shaking their head, there is no evidence of anything
going on in any ear, and everyone is happy and fine. I can now recommend this one for your cat as well. We have one

product_title: Kirkland Signature Water Resistant 6-Month Flea & Tick Control for Medium Dogs,13-31 Lbs
review_headline: RETURNED FOR REFUND - ITEM PULLED FROM COSTCO
review_body:
I bought this when Costco first started selling it earlier this year before all the awful reviews. I just moved from an area with no fleas to the pacific northwest, so this was my first time dealing with fleas. I used 2 of the 6 doses. Like everyone else said it left an oily spot on my dogs neck, and didn't seem to do anything to help with fleas. I decided to give it one more try, the 2nd time my dog seemed to have an allergic reaction - even a month after applying it, the skin on his neck is really pink and he's constantly scratching till he bleeds slightly. I'm not experimenting with cheaper options next summer and I feel like an awful mom.

Anyway finally got around to returning the box with the remaining 4 doses several months after I originally bought it and without a receipt. Since its Kirkland brand it's obviously from Costco, but they also keep track of your purchases on your Costco card so a receipt isn't necessary. I got a full refund in cash, not store credit.

This makes me wary of Kirkland brand products now. I'm extremely surprised and disappointed they would sell a product this harmful and not even do an official recall. When I asked the guy at customer service if they had a lot of returns, he said yes and they stopped selling it a little while ago. Pulling it from the shelves is NOT a recall. Read the reviews on here and other message boards - enough cats and dogs have had serious medical issues that even ended in death.

product_title: Chuckit! Classic 26M Launcher (Colors Vary)
review_headline: Great addition to tradition brings fruition
review_body:
As a dog owner I would describe myself as a traditionalist. I've never been too interested in what I considered to be unnecessary dog-play products. The most exotic 'toy' I've ever experimented with has been another product whose name rhymes with '[[ASIN:B0002AR0II song]]' (an experience I found satisfactory but not really worth the extra expense). I certainly never thought that I needed an 'extender' for what is perhaps the most routine dog-play activity ever. I didn't know what I was missing.

This thing works great! Not only does it help avoid the inevitable slobber mess on the balls, it is definitely a 'force multiplier', bringing all parties to satisfaction with only a fraction of the usual effort on my behalf. Setting aside the time it took me to learn how to use it properly (just one or two goes before mastery), I have found only two problems with using the product, both of which are probably unique to my situation. First of all, unlike most people I have 1 ball and 2 dogs. It bothers me occasionally but my wife prefers it that way. Second is the question of space. Playing with the product at home exclusively feels a bit cramped but my wife doesn't support my desire to use it elsewhere. She has a litany of arguments against public dog parks which would take too long to describe and isn't relevant here anyway. That's her thing. I personally don't judge those who frequent dog parks (wish I could join you actually).

On the whole I give this product 5 out of 5 stars. If you are someone who normally shy's away from fancy gimmicks but has a high-energy dog that needs regular interactive exercise, this is definitely worth experimenting with. And if you decide to purchase it at a store instead of online, rest assured that the only people who look at you askance will be inexperienced puritans. Anyone who has tried this thing will be giving you a knowing wink.
