product_title: Cedar Chalet Dog House : Size MEDIUM
review_headline: Hope it lasts! * see follow-up comments
review_body:
Comparatively okay for the price from what I have found out there, and there's not a lot.
Wood is a bit brittle and thin, not very sturdy. Doesn't look like cedar wood. Texture is almost like balsa. Has some stain on it that gives the cedar smell and color. Instructions included says do not use a hammer as it will break the wood. Screws that come with the kit are barely long enough, had to use some of my own, longer ones.
Roof is just two wood panels and am not sure if it will last. Floor is slat panels that do not keep anything out. Would prefer a solid floor.
I added a screen on the inside of the vent to keep mesquitoes out. No door, so I plan to add plastic strips like a pet door.
Looks good, but if you are thinking between the medium and large, get the large as the medium is not quite as big as you think. They probably measured the very outside of the wood, untreated pedestals it sits on, which would have added another 2-3\\" each way. I have it up on conc patio blocks so it does not contact directly with ground. If I had it to do again now that I have seen it, I would probably have kept searching for something else or built one myself.

*Has turned out better than previously thought. After about 2 years it seems to have held up fine, doesn't leak and really hasn't shown much age. Actually, the light-weight construction has made it easy to move around.

product_title: PetSafe Wireless Fence Pet Containment System, Covers up to 1/2 Acre, for Dogs over 8 lb., Waterproof Receiver with Tone / Static Correction
review_body: I have spent this weekend trying to establish the boundaries of this system. The first attempt took a little while however we placed the flags as instructed. Fitted the collar to the dog & went outside for the 1st training session. I found it very hard to hear the beeping once the collar was on my dog however I soon realised that even before we were within 2 feet of the flags she was being shocked. I felt terrible. we took the collar off and realised that the boundaries had changed. The instructions say that it can fluctuate however we were never able to get it to beep in the same place twice. Sometimes we would get one beep & it would just stop. We tried to place the transmitter in three different locations today and each gave poor results. There were areas between flags placed 6 feet apart that we never heard a beep and could just keep on walking. I am more than willing to spend the time training my dog but I could not even set the boundaries. We changed the height of the transmitter, moved our car out of the way, moved anything we felt that may be affecting it without success. I am sorry but it did not work well for me. I will be returning the system.

product_title: Stylette; LitterSweep(TM) Ultra Automated Litter System
review_body: I have a Himalayan who is a bit of a snob and one dog that will eat the cats' poo if given a chance.  I think Littersweep is wonderful. It removes the clumps and places it in this receptacle compartment.  It does fill up quickly but I like the idea that it removes it within 30 minutes so it doesn't sit in the box.  Good for both cat and dog.  Also when I have a busy schedule it will sit in the receptacle without it getting smelly.  The bags are hard to find so I stock up when I find them.  So far so good.  We all hope it will continue to work well and will last a long time.

product_title: Ergo Auto Pet Feeder Small 2000Gs
review_body: I have had this product for about a year, and it has saved my sanity. I have to get up at 530 for work, and my cat would wake me up every night at 330 or 4 to be fed and would bug me until I finally got up at 530. Needless to say, I was not happy about missing out on 2 hours of sleep every night. I was at wit's end, but I couldn't free feed him because he is overweight. I really didn't want to have to make a decision between me getting my sleep and him getting fat. So I tried this product. AND I LOVE IT!!!!! Yes, it did not take him long to figure out he can serve himself, but I did an experiment one day. I programmed the feeder to give him the amount I wanted to give him, and let it run naturally through 8 cycles (one day's worth of feedings). Then I simulated a feline paw pulling down extra food after the cycle completes (with my finger) and did that for 8 cycles. Absolutely NO DIFFERENCE in amount of food dispensed. People need to consider....if the cat is pulling down extra food after the cycle stops, it just means that when the auger starts up for the next cycle, there wont be any food right in the end. So it will run for a few seconds without depositing any food into the bowl. The only thing a cat is doing is basically \\"living on credit\\". They're taking food from their next feeding, not giving themselves extra. I challenge anyone who thinks their cat is getting more if they dig it out themselves to do the same experiment I did. All that's happening is that my cat is deciding himself when he eats. If he doesn't want to wait for the 8pm feeding and wants to dig the food out at 630, well, whatever. If anything, this digging out of food might actually cause a cat to lose weight, because when my cat is going for it, he's on his back, his side, rolling back and forth to get just the right angle. Even if he did manage to dig out an extra kibble or  two that he should not have received, I am quite sure that he used up more calories getting the food out than he received from his pilferage. HIGHLY RECOMMEND this product for any person who is tired of being awakened at 2am by a hungry kitty. I have not had any problems with this item and I am admittedly not as good on maintaining it as I should be. When it does finally die, I will splurge on the hundred dollars to get another one. It's well worth getting a full night's sleep and not having a fat cat from free feeding.

product_title: GMI PetShield Mesh Travel Barrier
review_body: Paid $37.99 w/free shipping from Amazon. Was concerned about quality and strength of product for this price, given I have a 75lb boxer that could lay waste to a \\"toy\\" barrier.  Had to seperate him from the backseat where the new baby will ride.  This is plenty strong & installed fairly easily. The only thing is the directions are pretty vague but the pic on the front of the box made sense of all the parts.  Went together well and installed solidly in our Mitsubishi Montero SUV.  Definitely worth the price and I cannot see how it could be made all that much better.  If you can get past the assembly instructions the product is higher quality than the price tag would seem to convey.  Very happy with it.

product_title: CatGenie-Self Washing, Self Flushing Cat Box
review_body: I bought the cat genie in June and I have now returned it within the 90 day period. I did receive a full refund from petnovations. I will try to make this review short and sweet.   *The Cat Genie really does work like it says.  *The Customer support is great.  *They follow through on the 90 day promise.   *It was easy to install.  Those are the positives. Here are the negatives:  *Small bits of poo fall between the hopper and get baked in the drying cycle.   *It is not more sanitary.  *the litter gets everywhere (more than traditional litter).  *It doesn't save money on litter because you have to buy sani solution and pay to flush your toilet up to 4 times a day or however many times you run it.  * Do yourself a favor, go to your bathroom if that is where you plan to have it and look and see if you have an outlet on the wall by the floor. Wait you don't? Join the club! you have to drape the heavy ugly black cord across the bathroom sink and plug it in. What an eye sore.  * The thing is huge! but the space for the cat to go won't hold more than a day's worth of poo so don't plan on leaving or you will have to get someone to come over and check on the cat genie instead of the cat.  * It is kinda noisy  * The biggest problem of all: THE LITTER is non absorbent. Why do cats cover their pee and poo? So that animals won't smell it. Well if the litter isn't absorbant then the pee smell says there until it is ran.     This brings me to the reason I got rid of it. My cat would poop in it reliably but she would only pee in it 2 times a day and then she would go in the sink or the bathtub. If she tried to cover her poop with the litter she would get old urine on her paw and then track it across the house. Hardly more sanitary! My suggestion: get a non clumping, non absorbent, unscented litter. See if they will use that reliably. If they won't then you won't be able to use the cat genie. I had no problems with the operation of the cat genie just with the litter. I didn't have problems with the impeller as some other reviewers have mentioned.

product_title: PetSafe Gentle Spray Bark Collar for Dogs, Citronella, Anti-Bark Device, Water Resistant
review_body: I bought this collar 3 years ago when I first got my dog at 7 months.  She was an abused cocker spaniel left in a pit bull ring as a bait dog.  When she was rescued and given to me she had so many emotional issues (separation anxiety).  When I left for work in the mornings, she would bark and cry ALL DAY LONG until  exactly 1 hour before I came home (My neighbor complained, he worked nights).  This was my last resort as nothing else worked.  When it first squirted at her first bark, she was so cute, she ran around the room looking for the scent.  By the second bark she figured it out.  They say that this is not good for severe anxiety dogs, but it worked wonders.  My neighbor ran into me at the end of the first week and thought I had given my dog away.  I did let her run around without it when I got home. Now its been 3 years since and she is a well adjusted dog, no collar needed after 4 months.  Premier is the best!  Remember: 1) remove the battery or turn off if not using (saves the battery). 2) The collar usually lasts about a year.  My little pup learned how to check the battery by giving a low test bark every time I put it on her.

product_title: Zymox Medicated Rinse 12 oz
review_body: This rinse is a lifesaver. My dog is prone to skin infections due to allergies.  The rinse kills the bacteria and fungus and it leaves my dogs skin and coat moisturized and very soft. It also has a very pleasant aroma. You can use it between shampoo's too. I place a small amount in my hands and rub it into my dogs coat. It leaves his coat soft and does not leave a residue. To top it off the price is right. I am very grateful to have found this product. I also use the shampoo and the ear medication and they all work great. I highly recommend Zymox products.

product_title: Natural Balance Ultra Formula Premium Canned Cat Food Can 24 - 6oz Cans
review_body: I adopted a cat from a rescue shelter and he was underweight, vomiting and had very smelly diarrhea. I purchased Iams and Science diet dry and wet and he barely touched either food. His foster mom said he liked Friskies but I just could not feed my cat a food filled with by products, fillers, and dyes that are not good for cats. I started to research cat diets on line and came across a veteranarian article that recommended Natural Balance as being the best commercial cat food. I ordered a few cases online and hoped that I was not wasting more money on expensive cat food.  Well, my cat gobbled it down the first day. I did not even have to mix it with old food -- he took to it immediately and begs for it several times a day now.  So far he likes the Venison and pea and the Chicken and liver pate. He is gaining weight and has lots of energy and bright clear eyes. Best of all, he has not vomited and his bowel movements are completely normal now. (In fact there is absolutely no smell and miminal waste, I am sure because the food is being digested properly) I am planning on trying other flavor varieties. By contrast, many of her other toys that are about as old (and that she mostly doesn't use as much) have needed sewing, if she still uses them at all. Newer toys have been taken away from her because they were falling apart. I'm very impressed with the quality of this toy.    So: if your dog is a mild to moderate chewer who likes \\"comfort toys\\" (something they can use as a pillow, gnaw on, or get you to play catch with), I totally recommend this Berber Babies green lamb. We'll be buying at least one more for backup, now that we've found them again.

review_body:

Though, while making the switch, I will probably have to supplement it just a little with the cats' old favorites (Fancy Feast fish types) so they make the change-over smoothly.

product_title: Booda Soft Bite Terry Cloth Dog Toy - Pig
review_headline: World's greatest 5-inch tall soft, squeaky pig
review_body:
Objective: To find a toy that my favorite dog, Cindy, will enjoy more than life itself (or at least more than baby carrots).

Materials and methods: This randomized, double-blind study was conducted by purchasing the aforementioned stuffed Booda pig along with one stuffed Air France airplane from Charles de Gaulle airport, Paris ($9.44 US), one small stuffed soccer ball ($5.50), one Booda dog ($3.74), one Kaibab squirrel from the Grand Canyon ($8.95), and one buffalo from Cannon Beach, Oregon ($7.95) and comparing and contrasting Cindy's reaction to each toy. Time spent playing with each toy was analyzed using the Chi square test.

Results: Cindy spent considerably more time playing with the Booda pig than with any other toy (n = 1; P < .005). She enjoyed the softness of the pig's looped, vaguely carpet-like exterior as well as the pleasing tone of the squeaker inside. The basic model comes with a loop of elastic protruding from the top of the pig's head, which she likes to tug. Chasing the pig when it is thrown, squeaking the pig, and laying on her back, putting the pig between her paws, and chewing on the pig's ears have become serious hobbies of hers. When not in play, this Booda pig can be used as a pillow (small) and occasionally as a lumpy security blanket.

Limitations: This is a single case study; more research needs to be done. Also, it is not always cost effective to reproduce this research, given the trips to Western America and Europe required to procure the control toys. Researchers without large amounts of time or energy may feel that this study is \\"trivial,\\" \\"meaningless,\\" or \\"antithetical to the basic tenets of scientific research.\\"

Conclusions: Of all of the toys I've ever purchased for Cindy, either on this continent or in Europe, she only truly, deeply loves the Booda pig. She knows it by name. She loves it like her own offspring. I have no doubt that in the event of quick-spreading fire, Cindy would save the Booda pig long, long before she saved me. It is well worth the price, and I would buy this toy again and again if she, say, happened to destroy the first one I bought her. Which she did. Maybe I'd better order another one now, just to be on the safe side.

product_title: LitterMaid Automatic Litter Box LM920
review_body:
We've had this litterbox for four years now with almost no problems. The only problems we've had have been caused by our own laziness, or mistakes we've made.

1. The cat litter you use is directly proportional to the success of the product. We don't believe in using clay littlers, so even before we got the box, we were using \\"World's Best Cat Litter\\" which you can get on Amazon for a good price. We have two cats, and have NEVER had anything stick to the rake using this litter -- not even when my cat had diarrhea. And we don't use baby oil or cooking spray on the rake. We also have never had \\"flying clumps\\" come out of the box. But our tent flaps would stop it anyway.

2. You still have to pull the bottom out and wash it once a month or so. It's a great unit, but it's not perfect, and in time some stuff will stick to the bottom and impair the rake... but not very often. We only wash ours every month or two. At that time, I also take the hose attachment of my vacuum and vacuum out the tracks of the top part. Works wonders.

3. I'd much rather deal with the soft maintenance issues of this box than spend 5-10 minutes a day raking litter. If you don't want dogs in it, buy the tent. If you don't want to use the cord for aesthetic purposes, use batteries. And I have to say that adding litter to the box is MUCH EASIER than scooping it.

We've had two problems that were our fault. First, we had the unit plugged into a wall switch that was controlled by a light switch. And the light switch accidentally got turned off. Our unit is tented, and we didn't realize it was turned off for several days, which caused a cleaning nightmare

Second, the motor stopped working for a while... but this is because \\"someone\\" (coughhusbandcough) thought it would be a good idea to just let the rake clean up after we discovered that the box hadn't been working for a while again after the light switch was accidentally turned off... again. It was too much for the motor, and rather than burn out, it shut itself off. I called into the customer support, and they helped me to get it working again with some cycling procedure. We still have the same unit, and it works brilliantly with no problems since.

Oh, and two more things:

1. My skittish cat got used to the box rather quickly. I too recommend following the suggestions on the insert to acclimate scaredy cats to the box.

2. I have gotten so used to the noise that I totally sleep through it, and the box is in our bedroom right now (small apartment, don't ask).

product_title: ScoopFree Litter Tray Refills with Premium Blue Crystals - Pack of 6
review_headline: Not Exactly what I expected but better than other litter boxes.

review_body: I think this light is great.  Having dual bulbs really makes the light more even throughout the tank. review_body: I use these as my go-to everyday treats for my two highly active agility shelties.  They love them and they are a good size and do not crumble.
